questions.q: On what do the six rasas rest, according to line 1 of verse 44?
optionExplain: The body is not named in this verse.
Right: षड् द्रव्यमाश्रिताः: the six depend on a dravya.
The doṣas are acted on, not the resting place.
No season is named.
questions.explain: द्रव्यमाश्रिताः = resting in, dependent on a substance.
questions.rule: The six rasas rest in a dravya.

questions.q: Arrange the phrases of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line names Māruta first, then Kapha.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 44 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two lines.
questions.rule: द्रव्यम् = substance; आश्रिताः = resting in; बलावहाः = bringing strength; घ्नन्ति = they destroy.
questions.teaches: द्रव्यम् = substance; आश्रिताः = resting in; बलावहाः = bringing strength; घ्नन्ति = they destroy.

questions.q: Why does the verse print षड् and not षट् before द्रव्यम्?
options: ट् always becomes ड् at the end of a word
The number six is षड् in every position
ट् becomes ड् before the voiced द
It is a misprint for षष्
optionExplain: At the end of a sentence it stays ट्; the change needs a voiced sound after it.
The word is षट्; षड् is a sandhi form.
Right: षट् + द्रव्यम् → षड् द्रव्यम्.
There is no such form; the change is regular.
questions.explain: षड् is षट् changed before the voiced द of द्रव्यम्.
questions.rule: Final voiceless stop + voiced sound → the voiced stop (ट् → ड्).

questions.q: Which doṣa does line 2 say the three rasas beginning with bitter destroy?
optionExplain: Māruta is destroyed by the first rasas, आद्याः.
Pitta is not named in this verse; it is treated in the next.
Neither is named for the bitter group.
Right: त्रयस्तिक्तादयः कफम्.
questions.explain: तिक्तादयः कफं घ्नन्ति: the three starting with bitter destroy Kapha.

questions.q: By the pattern त्रयः + तिक्तादयः → त्रयस्तिक्तादयः, how does रसः + तिक्तः join?
optionExplain: Right: -अः + त becomes -अस् त, as in त्रयस्तिक्तादयः.
-ओ comes before a voiced sound, but त is voiceless.
श् comes before च or छ, not before त.
The visarga does change before त; it is not left as it is.
questions.explain: रसः + तिक्तः → रसस्तिक्तः: the visarga becomes स् before the voiceless त.
questions.teaches: A visarga before a voiceless त becomes स्, as in त्रयः + तिक्त- → त्रयस्तिक्त-.

questions.q: How does line 2 of verse 45 divide a substance (द्रव्य)?
options: Sweet, sour, salty and the rest
Pacifying, provoking, good for the healthy
Hot, cold and neither of these
Light, heavy, soft and the rest
optionExplain: Those are rasas, not the three kinds of dravya.
Right: शमनं कोपनं स्वस्थहितं द्रव्यमिति त्रिधा.
Hot and cold belong to the next verse's vīrya.
The verse does not divide dravya by these.
questions.explain: The verse says a substance is threefold: शमन, कोपन and स्वस्थहित.
questions.rule: द्रव्य is threefold: शमन, कोपन, स्वस्थहित.

questions.q: Arrange the three kinds of substance in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verse gives pacifying, provoking, then good for the healthy.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 45 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the second line and the verb of the first.
questions.rule: शमनम् = pacifying; कोपनम् = provoking; स्वस्थहितम् = good for the healthy; कुर्वते = they make.
questions.teaches: शमनम् = pacifying; कोपनम् = provoking; स्वस्थहितम् = good for the healthy; कुर्वते = they make.

questions.q: Which is the right split of द्रव्यमिति?
optionExplain: मिति is not a word; the म् belongs to द्रव्यम्.
The word द्रव्यम् is neuter and ends in म्, not visarga.
Right: A final म् stays before a vowel and joins it: द्रव्य-म्-इति.
The ending is -म्, not -ए; the join would not give द्रव्यमिति.
questions.explain: द्रव्यमिति = द्रव्यम् + इति ('a substance, thus').
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel: the म् is written with the vowel.

questions.q: Line 1 of verse 45 names tastes that destroy Pitta. Which are they?
optionExplain: Right: named first.
Right: named second.
Right: named third.
Not named in this line; the line says only that 'others' make Pitta.
Not named in this line; the line says only that 'others' make Pitta.
questions.explain: The first line names astringent, bitter and sweet; the others make Pitta.
questions.rule: कषाय-तिक्त-मधुराः destroy Pitta; अन्ये make it.

questions.q: By the pattern स्वस्थहितम् 'good for the healthy', what does रोगिहितम् mean?
options: The sick one who is good
optionExplain: The compound says 'good for', not 'made by'.
हित means good, the opposite of harm.
The compound is not a description of the sick person.
Right: The first member names for whom it is good; रोगिन् means 'sick'.
questions.explain: X-हितम् means good for X, so रोगिहितम् is good for the sick.
questions.teaches: In स्वस्थहितम् the first member names the one for whom it is good; any X-हितम् is read the same way.

questions.q: In verse 46, from what does the twofold vīrya come?
options: The sweet or sour taste of a substance
optionExplain: Right: उष्णशीतगुणोत्कर्षात्: from the excess of the hot or cold quality.
Taste is not given as the basis in this verse.
Ripening belongs to vipāka, not to the basis of vīrya.
Digestion is not mentioned.
questions.explain: उष्ण-शीत-गुण-उत्कर्षात् = from the predominance of the hot or cold quality.
questions.rule: वीर्य: twofold, by the predominance of hot or cold.

questions.q: Arrange the phrases of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line gives the reason first, then 'among these', vīrya, twofold, 'held'.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 46 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two technical terms and two number words.
questions.rule: वीर्यम् = potency; विपाकः = ripening; द्विधा = twofold; त्रिधा = threefold.
questions.teaches: वीर्यम् = potency; विपाकः = ripening; द्विधा = twofold; त्रिधा = threefold.

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुणोत्कर्षात्?
optionExplain: ए before a vowel would give अय्, i.e. गुणयुत्कर्षात्, not गुणोत्कर्षात्.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so गुण + उत्कर्षात् is written गुणोत्कर्षात्.
The word is उत्कर्षात्, with its उ.
गुणो is not a word; the ओ is produced by the join.
questions.explain: गुणोत्कर्षात् = गुण + उत्कर्षात् ('from the excess of the quality').

questions.q: Which pairing of counts does verse 46 give?
optionExplain: This swaps the two.
Vipāka is threefold (त्रिधा).
Right: वीर्यं द्विधा, विपाकः त्रिधा.
Vīrya is twofold (द्विधा).
questions.explain: The first line says vīrya is द्विधा, the second says vipāka is त्रिधा.

questions.q: By the pattern द्विधा and त्रिधा, what does a new word चतुर्धा mean?
optionExplain: An ordinal would be चतुर्थ.
'Times' would be चतुः, as in the number adverbs.
'Of' would be a genitive ending, not -धा.
Right: -धा makes 'in ... ways'; चतुर् is four.
questions.explain: द्वि + धा = twofold, त्रि + धा = threefold, so चतुर् + धा = fourfold.
questions.rule: number + धा = in so many kinds.
questions.teaches: The suffix -धा after a number gives 'so many-fold': द्विधा, त्रिधा, and the same pattern in षोढा, दशधा of verse 39.

questions.q: With the two added and the opposites, how many qualities does verse 47 say there are?
optionExplain: Right: विंशतिः सविपर्ययाः: twenty with their opposites.
Eight are the ones listed in line 1, before the additions.
Ten leaves out the opposites; the verse says twenty with them.
The verse does not give sixteen.
questions.explain: The verse ends with विंशतिः सविपर्ययाः: twenty, with their opposites.

questions.q: Arrange the first six qualities of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line begins with these six; मृदु and स्थिर follow.
questions.rule: गुरु → मन्द → हिम → स्निग्ध → श्लक्ष्ण → सान्द्र → मृदु → स्थिर.

questions.q: Match each quality word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the eight listed qualities.
questions.rule: गुरु = heavy; मन्द = slow; हिम = cold; सान्द्र = dense.
questions.teaches: गुरु = heavy; मन्द = slow; हिम = cold; सान्द्र = dense.

questions.q: ससूक्ष्मविशदा stands for ससूक्ष्मविशदाः. Why is the visarga not written?
options: The visarga is always dropped at the end of a verse line
After आः, before a voiced sound like व, the visarga drops
It is a misprint that should be corrected
The word is a singular that never has a visarga
optionExplain: It is dropped only before a voiced sound, not by line position.
Right: The next word विंशतिः starts with the voiced व.
It is regular sandhi, not a misprint.
It is a plural, in -आः.
questions.explain: ससूक्ष्मविशदाः + विंशतिः → ससूक्ष्मविशदा विंशतिः.

questions.q: The verse names ten qualities. Why does it reach twenty?
options: Each is repeated one more time
Ten more are listed in the next line
Each is taken with its opposite
Two are added to each quality
optionExplain: The word says 'with opposites', not 'repeated'.
No further list of ten follows in this verse.
Right: सविपर्ययाः means 'with their opposites'.
The two added are सूक्ष्म and विशद, once only.
questions.explain: सविपर्ययाः = sa + viparyaya: together with their opposites.

questions.q: By the pattern स + विपर्ययाः 'with their opposites', what does सपुष्पाः mean in a new line?
optionExplain: 'Without' would be अ- or निः-.
स- only says 'with'; it does not say 'many'.
'Of' is a case ending; स- is a prefix.
Right: स- before a noun gives 'with', so स + पुष्प = with flowers.
questions.explain: सपुष्पाः = स + पुष्प with the plural ending, 'with flowers', as सविपर्ययाः is 'with opposites'.
questions.rule: स- + noun = together with that noun.
questions.teaches: The prefix स- means 'with', as in सविपर्ययाः; the same works for any noun.

questions.q: In line 2 of verse 48, what does the vyavāyin quality do?
options: Pervades the whole body and is fit for pāka
Stays in the head alone and is fit for pāka
Pervades the whole body and is unfit for pāka
Pervades the senses and is fit for pāka
optionExplain: Right: व्यवायी देहमखिलं व्याप्य पाकाय कल्पते.
The verse says the whole body, अखिलं देहम्.
It is fit for pāka, कल्पते.
What it pervades is the body (देहम्).
questions.explain: It pervades the whole body and is fit for pāka (ripening, cooking).
questions.rule: व्यवायी: pervades the whole body; fit for pāka.

questions.q: Arrange the phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line runs: vyavāyin, the whole body, having pervaded, fit for pāka.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry both lines.
questions.rule: इन्द्रियार्थाः = objects of the senses; अखिलम् = whole; व्याप्य = having pervaded; पाकाय = for ripening.
questions.teaches: इन्द्रियार्थाः = objects of the senses; अखिलम् = whole; व्याप्य = having pervaded; पाकाय = for ripening.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चापरे?
optionExplain: आपरे is not a word here.
Right: अ + अ join into आ: च + अपरे → चापरे.
परे would mean 'other' only if the अ were not part of अपरे.
चो is not a word; the join of अ and अ gives आ.
questions.explain: चापरे = च ('and') + अपरे ('other').

questions.q: Which of these does line 1 of verse 48 name as other qualities?
optionExplain: Right: objects of the senses.
Right: named in line 1.
Not named in this line.
Not named in this line.
Not named in this line; it belongs to verse 47.
questions.explain: Line 1 names the objects of the senses and vyavāyin, among others.

questions.q: Like व्याप्य 'having pervaded', what does प्रविश्य, from a verb with a prefix, mean?
optionExplain: 'To enter' would be प्रवेष्टुम्.
-य does not make a passive 'been'.
Right: A prefixed verb takes -य for 'having done'; प्र + विश् means enter.
A command would be प्रविशतु.
questions.explain: व्याप्य and प्रविश्य are both absolutives in -य of prefixed verbs.
questions.teaches: After a prefix, 'having done' is -य, not -त्वा: व्याप्य 'having pervaded', प्रविश्य 'having entered'.

questions.q: What does the quality in line 1 of verse 49 loosen?
optionExplain: The doṣas are not mentioned in line 1.
The skin is not mentioned.
Only the bonds of the joints are named.
Right: संधिबन्धान् विमुञ्चति: it looses the bonds of the joints.
questions.explain: विमुञ्चति = looses; संधिबन्धान् = the bonds of the joints.
questions.rule: The quality loosens the bonds of the joints.

questions.q: Arrange the phrases of line 1 in the verse's order (spellings as printed).
questions.explain: The line names the quality, then 'merely by expanding', the bonds, the verb.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are the safe, clear ones of the line.
questions.rule: संधि = joint; बन्ध = bond; विमुञ्चति = looses; एव = merely.
questions.teaches: संधि = joint; बन्ध = bond; विमुञ्चति = looses; एव = merely.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विकषन्नेव (spelling as printed)?
optionExplain: Right: A final न् after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel: विकषन् + एव → विकषन्नेव.
नेव is not a word.
विकषन्न is not a form; the second न् comes from the join.
न्नेव is not a word.
questions.explain: विकषन्नेव = विकषन् (expanding) + एव (merely).
questions.rule: Final न् after a short vowel + vowel → न्न्.

questions.q: According to line 1, how does this quality loosen the bonds?
optionExplain: Nothing in the line speaks of pressing.
Right: एव stresses that expanding alone is enough.
Nothing in the line speaks of drying.
Nothing in the line speaks of cooling.
questions.explain: विकषन्नेव = just by expanding; the bonds of the joints are loosened.

questions.q: By the pattern विकषन् + एव → विकषन्नेव, how does पठन् + एव join?
optionExplain: Without doubling, the join would be wrong.
The न् is not lost.
Right: Final न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel.
ण् is not the nasal of this word.
questions.explain: पठन् + एव → पठन्नेव, the same doubling as in विकषन्नेव.
questions.rule: Short vowel + final न् + vowel → न्न्.
questions.teaches: A final न् after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel: विकषन्नेव, पठन्नेव.

questions.q: Which set does line 1 of verse 50 call the three great qualities?
optionExplain: These three are not named in this verse.
These are qualities of verse 47, not the mahāguṇas.
These are rasas of verse 43.
Right: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति त्रयः प्रोक्ता महागुणाः.
questions.explain: The three great qualities are sattva, rajas and tamas.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Arrange the three great qualities in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verse gives sattva, then rajas, then tamas.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Match each word of verse 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are glossed in the card's rule and English.
questions.rule: महागुण = great quality; त्रयः = three; प्रोक्ताः = called; योग = conjunction.
questions.teaches: महागुण = great quality; त्रयः = three; प्रोक्ताः = called; योग = conjunction.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which is the right split of रजस्तमश्चेति?
optionExplain: Right: The visarga becomes स् before त, श् before च, and च + इति gives चेति.
स्तमः is not a word; the स् is the changed visarga of रजः.
चे is not a word; the ए comes from the join of अ and इ.
The word is इति ('thus'); एति means 'goes'.
questions.explain: रजस्तमश्चेति = रजः + तमः + च + इति.
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्; visarga + च → श्; अ + इ → ए.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which kinds of conjunction does line 2 of verse 50 name?
optionExplain: Right: the first.
Right: the second.
Right: the third.
Not named in this line.
Not named in this line.
questions.explain: The compound हीनमिथ्यातिमात्रकः names deficient, wrong and excessive.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: By the pattern कालार्थकर्मणाम् 'of time, objects and actions', what does गुणकर्मणाम् mean in a new line?
optionExplain: By would need -ऐः or -भिः.
Right: The ending -आम् at the end of the dvandva covers both members.
As subject it would end in -आनि or -आणि.
In would need -सु.
questions.explain: गुण + कर्मन् in a dvandva: the genitive plural -आम् at the end belongs to both, 'of qualities and actions'.
questions.teaches: In a dvandva, the case ending is written once, at the end, and covers every member: कालार्थकर्मणाम् = of time, objects and actions.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: According to verse 51, what is disease (रोग)?
optionExplain: That is अरोगता, freedom from disease.
The verse does not define disease as knowledge.
Right: रोगस्तु दोषवैषम्यम्: disease is imbalance of the doṣas.
No measure is mentioned in the verse.
questions.explain: रोगः = दोषवैषम्यम्, the imbalance of the doṣas.
questions.rule: रोग = दोषों की विषमता; अरोगता = दोषों की समता.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Put the four phrases of verse 51 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The first line gives the sole cause; the second line defines disease, then freedom from disease.
questions.rule: Line 1: सम्यग्योग, the one cause. Line 2: रोग = वैषम्य, then साम्य = अरोगता.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Match each word of verse 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two definitions use opposite words: वैषम्य (imbalance) and साम्य (balance).
questions.teaches: वैषम्य and साम्य are opposites; each is joined to दोष in a compound.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which split of रोगारोग्यैककारणम् is right?
optionExplain: आ + इ would give ए, not ऐ, and इक is not a word of the card.
आ + औ gives औ, not ऐ.
That drops एक, but the card reads it as the sole cause.
Right: आ + ए gives ऐ, so आरोग्य + एक is written आरोग्यैक: the sole cause of disease and health.
questions.explain: रोग + आरोग्य + एक + कारणम् is one compound meaning the sole cause of disease and health.
questions.rule: आ + ए → ऐ; एक = sole; the compound names one cause for both disease and health.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which sentence matches verse 51?
options: Disease is imbalance of the doṣas; freedom from disease is their balance.
Disease is balance of the doṣas; freedom from disease is their imbalance.
Disease is the sole cause of both health and balance of the doṣas.
Freedom from disease is the imbalance of the doṣas, and disease its absence.
optionExplain: Right: This follows रोगस्तु दोषवैषम्यं दोषसाम्यमरोगता.
The two definitions are swapped.
The verse does not say that.
Again swapped, and wrong.
questions.explain: The verse pairs रोग with वैषम्य and अरोगता with साम्य.
questions.rule: वैषम्य = imbalance = रोग; साम्य = balance = अरोगता.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: By the pattern of दोषवैषम्यम्, what would बलवैषम्यम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be बलसाम्यम्.
Right: X-वैषम्यम् is imbalance of X; here X is बल, strength.
The first member is what is imbalanced, not the strength of an imbalance.
Freedom from X is X-रहितता or अ-, not -वैषम्य.
questions.explain: दोष-वैषम्यम् is imbalance of the doṣas, so बल-वैषम्यम् is imbalance of strength.
questions.rule: X-वैषम्यम् = imbalance of X; X-साम्यम् = balance of X.
questions.teaches: A compound X-वैषम्यम् means imbalance of X; X-साम्यम् means balance of X.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Verse 52 divides diseases into two kinds by which division?
optionExplain: That divides the seat (अधिष्ठान), not the diseases.
These are not named in this verse.
Right: निजागन्तुविभागेन: by the division into nija and āgantu.
That divides locality in a later verse.
questions.explain: The two kinds of disease are nija and āgantu.
questions.rule: रोग: निज / आगन्तु. अधिष्ठान: काय / मन.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Put the four phrases of verse 52 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the kinds of disease; line 2 gives the twofold seat.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Match each word of verse 52 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse's two divisions.
questions.rule: निज = one's own; आगन्तु = arriving; अधिष्ठान = seat; मत = held.
questions.teaches: निज and आगन्तु are two opposite words; अधिष्ठान names the seat of the diseases.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which split of कायमनोभेदात् is right?
optionExplain: नोभेदात् is not a word.
मना is not the word on the card; the card has मनः, and मनः + भेदात् gives मनोभेदात्.
The ओ is the changed visarga of मनः, not a word of its own.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant (भ) becomes ओ: मनः + भेदात् gives मनोभेदात्.
questions.explain: कायमनोभेदात् = काय + मनः + भेदात्, from the difference of body and mind.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which are said to be twofold in verse 52?
options: The diseases, by nija and āgantu
The seat (अधिष्ठान), by body and mind
optionExplain: Right: रोगाश्च द्विविधा मताः.
Right: अधिष्ठानमपि द्विधा.
This verse says nothing about the doṣas.
Medicines are not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: Exactly two things are divided: the diseases and their seat.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: How is मनः + विभागेन written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः before the voiced व becomes ओ, as in मनोभेदात्.
A visarga is not left in place before a voiced consonant after अ.
आ does not replace अः here.
The visarga becomes ओ, it is not simply dropped.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives कायमनोभेदात् gives मनोविभागेन.
questions.teaches: The visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant; use it for any new phrase.
questions.section: योग, रोग और रोग के भेद

questions.q: Which two does verse 53 call the doṣas of the mind?
optionExplain: These are not named in this verse.
Right: रजस्तमश्च मनसो द्वौ च दोषावुदाहृतौ.
These are not named in this verse.
Sattva is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The two doṣas of the mind are rajas and tamas.
questions.rule: मन के दोष: रज और तम.

questions.q: Put the three means of examining the patient in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verse lists seeing, then touching, then questioning.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three means plus the verb that governs them.
questions.rule: दर्शन = looking; स्पर्शन = touching; प्रश्न = questioning; परीक्षेत = one should examine.
questions.teaches: The examination uses three means, joined as one compound ending in -ैः (by).

questions.q: Which split of रजस्तमश्च is right?
optionExplain: The स् comes from the visarga of रजः, not from the next word.
श्च is not a word; the श् is the changed visarga of तमः.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, and before च it becomes श्: रजस्तमश्च.
तमः is the word; स्तम is not.
questions.explain: रजस्तमश्च = रजः + तमः + च: rajas and tamas.

questions.q: Which does verse 53 name as means of examining the patient?
optionExplain: Right: दर्शन.
Right: स्पर्शन.
Right: प्रश्न.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse names exactly three means: दर्शन, स्पर्शन, प्रश्न.

questions.q: By the pattern of दर्शनस्पर्शनप्रश्नैः, what does श्रवणदर्शनप्रश्नैः mean?
options: Hearing, looking and questioning together are one thing
optionExplain: All three items are joined; questioning is included.
The ending -ैः is instrumental (by), not genitive (of).
The ending marks the means, not one thing.
Right: A list of nouns joined without ca, ending in the instrumental plural: by each of them.
questions.explain: The new compound is built like the verse's: three nouns, one instrumental plural ending.
questions.rule: A dvandva with -ैः: by A, B and C.
questions.teaches: A list of nouns ending in -ैः means by all of them; the three items are separate means.

questions.q: Verse 54 says locality (देश) is twofold by the difference of which two?
optionExplain: Right: भूमिदेहभेदेन: by the difference of land and body.
Those are two of the means in line 1.
That divides the seat of disease in the previous verse.
Time is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: देशमाहुरिह द्विधा: locality is spoken of as twofold, by land and body.

questions.q: Put the five means of examining the disease in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound lists them in this order.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the glosses of the card; उपशय and आप्ति are left undefined by the verse.
questions.rule: निदान = cause; प्राग्रूप = early sign; लक्षण = characteristic sign; भूमि = land; देह = body.
questions.teaches: Three of the five means have a clear gloss; the other two are only named.

questions.q: Which English line for line 2 is right?
options: Here they speak of locality as threefold, by the difference of land and body.
Here they speak of locality as twofold, by the difference of land and body.
Here they speak of disease as twofold, by the difference of land and body.
Here they speak of locality as twofold, by the difference of land and time.
optionExplain: द्विधा means twofold; the threefold division is the next verse.
Right: This follows भूमिदेहभेदेन देशमाहुरिह द्विधा.
The object is देशम्, locality, not disease.
The second member is देह, body, not time.
questions.explain: द्विधा = in two ways; देशम् = locality; भूमि-देह = land and body.
questions.rule: देश is twofold by भूमि and देह.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five means in line 1?
optionExplain: It is the fourth means named in line 1.
It is the second means named in line 1.
Right: देश is the topic of line 2, not a means of examining the disease.
It is the third means named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 names निदान, प्राग्रूप, लक्षण, उपशय and आप्ति; देश comes in line 2.
questions.rule: Five means in line 1; locality in line 2.

questions.q: By the pattern of भूमिदेहभेदेन, what does बलकालभेदेन mean?
options: By the difference of strength alone
By the sign of strength and time
For the difference of time, with strength
By the difference of strength and time
optionExplain: Both members of the compound count: strength and time.
भेद is difference, not sign.
The ending -एन is instrumental (by).
Right: X-Y-भेदेन means by the difference of X and Y.
questions.explain: The new compound is built like the verse's: two nouns, then भेदेन.
questions.rule: X-Y-भेदेन = by the difference of X and Y.
questions.teaches: X-Y-भेदेन means by the difference between X and Y.

questions.q: Which land-region does verse 55 call vāta-predominant?
optionExplain: Right: जांगलं वातभूयिष्ठम्: the jāṅgala region has vāta predominant.
Anūpa is the region with kapha abundant.
Sādhāraṇa is the region with equal mala.
भूमि is the word for land, not a region name.
questions.explain: जाङ्गल = वातभूयिष्ठ, vāta predominant.
questions.rule: जाङ्गल: वात; अनूप: कफ; साधारण: सम मल.

questions.q: Put the three land-regions in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verse names jāṅgala first, then anūpa, then sādhāraṇa.

questions.q: Match each region of verse 55 to its description.
questions.explain: Each region has one description in the verse.
questions.rule: जाङ्गल = वातभूयिष्ठ; अनूप = कफोल्बण; साधारण = सममल.
questions.teaches: Each region name is matched with the doṣa (or balance) it is described by.

questions.q: Which join gives कफोल्बणम्?
optionExplain: अ + ओ gives औ: that would be कफौल्बणम्.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so कफ + उल्बण is written कफोल्बण.
अ + अ gives आ: that would be कफाल्बणम्.
अ + इ gives ए: that would be कफेल्बणम्.
questions.explain: कफोल्बणम् = कफ + उल्बणम्: with kapha abundant.

questions.q: Which English line for verse 55 is right?
options: Jāṅgala has kapha abundant, anūpa has vāta predominant, sādhāraṇa has equal mala.
Jāṅgala has vāta predominant, anūpa has kapha abundant, sādhāraṇa has vāta abundant.
Jāṅgala has vāta predominant, anūpa has kapha abundant, sādhāraṇa has equal mala.
Jāṅgala has equal mala, anūpa has vāta predominant, sādhāraṇa has kapha abundant.
optionExplain: The first two descriptions are swapped.
Sādhāraṇa has equal mala, not vāta.
Right: This matches the three descriptions in the verse.
Each description is given to the wrong region.
questions.explain: Region, then description: जाङ्गल-वात, अनूप-कफ, साधारण-सम मल.
questions.rule: Keep the three pairs as the verse gives them.

questions.q: By the pattern of वातभूयिष्ठम्, what does पित्तभूयिष्ठम् mean?
optionExplain: भूयिष्ठ means most, predominant, not absent.
The compound describes a thing that has pitta predominant.
Equal is सम, as in सममलम्.
Right: X-भूयिष्ठम् means with X predominant, a bahuvrīhi.
questions.explain: वात-भूयिष्ठम् means with vāta predominant, so पित्त-भूयिष्ठम् is with pitta predominant.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi X-भूयिष्ठम् describes something in which X is predominant.

questions.q: Verse 56 says that, in brief, medicine is of which two kinds?
optionExplain: Right: शोधनं शमनं चेति समासादौषधं द्विधा.
These are named in the next verse as remedies, not as the two kinds.
These are means of examining disease, from verse 54.
These are land-regions from verse 55.
questions.explain: समासात् = in brief; औषधं द्विधा = medicine is twofold: शोधन and शमन.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two statements of the verse.
questions.rule: शोधन = purifying; शमन = pacifying; काल = time; औषध = medicine; समासात् = in brief.

questions.q: Put the four phrases of verse 56 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 describes time; line 2 divides medicine.
questions.rule: Time first (moments, stage, application of medicine), then the two kinds of medicine.
questions.teaches: The verse first says what time is and does, then moves to the division of medicine.

questions.q: Which split of समासादौषधम् is right?
optionExplain: अ + औ would give औ: समासौषधम्, with no द.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: समासात् + औषधम् gives समासादौषधम्.
आ + औ would give औ: समासौषधम्, with no द.
समासात् + ओषधम् would join as समासादोषधम् (ओ); the verse has औ, so the second word is औषधम्.
questions.explain: समासादौषधम् = समासात् + औषधम्: in brief, medicine.
questions.rule: Final त् before a vowel → द्.

questions.q: Which statements does verse 56 make?
options: Time brings about the application of medicine
optionExplain: Right: कालो भेषज्ययोगकृत्.
Right: समासादौषधं द्विधा.
Reversed: शोधन is purifying and शमन is pacifying.
द्विधा is said of medicine, not of time.
questions.explain: Two statements: the role of time, and the twofold medicine.

questions.q: By the pattern of द्विधा (in two ways), what does पञ्चधा mean?
optionExplain: That is द्विधा.
-धा does not make an ordinal.
Right: -धा makes a word meaning in so many ways: द्वि-धा, पञ्च-धा.
-धा is not a locative of a part.
questions.explain: द्वि = two gives द्विधा; पञ्च = five gives पञ्चधा.
questions.rule: Number + धा = in that many ways.
questions.teaches: A number word plus -धा gives in that many ways (द्विधा, त्रिधा, पञ्चधा).

questions.q: Which remedy does verse 57 name first?
optionExplain: Emesis comes third in the list.
Ghee is the fifth item.
Honey is the last item.
Right: बस्तिर्विरेको वमनम्: basti comes first.
questions.explain: The list runs basti, purgation, emesis, then oil, ghee, honey.
questions.rule: बस्ति → विरेक → वमन → तैल → घृत → मधु.

questions.q: Put the six remedies of verse 57 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Three procedures come first; after तथा come oil, ghee and honey.
questions.rule: बस्ति, विरेक, वमन, तथा तैल, घृत, मधु.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the glosses of the card.
questions.rule: बस्ति = enema; विरेक = purgation; वमन = emesis; तैल = oil; घृत = ghee; मधु = honey.
questions.teaches: Names of remedies are only glossed here; no effect or dose is stated by the verse.

questions.q: Which split of बस्तिर्विरेको वमनम् is right?
optionExplain: Right: इः before a voiced व becomes इर्, and अः before व becomes ओ.
The visarga of बस्तिः is not dropped; it becomes र्.
बस्तिर is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
ओवमनम् is not a word; the ओ is the changed visarga of विरेकः.
questions.explain: The visarga changes before a voiced consonant: इः → इर्, अः → ओ.

questions.q: Which are named as remedies in verse 57?
optionExplain: Right: बस्तिः.
Right: वमनम्.
Right: मधु.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse names six remedies: three procedures, and oil, ghee, honey.
questions.rule: बस्ति, विरेक, वमन, तैल, घृत, मधु.

questions.q: By the pattern of शरीरजानाम्, what does मनोजानाम् mean?
options: Of those born in the body
Of those born in the mind
By those born in the mind
Of the mind and the born
optionExplain: That is शरीरजानाम्; here the first member is मनः.
Right: -ज means born; -जानाम् carries the genitive plural ending -नाम्: of those born.
The ending -नाम् is genitive (of), not instrumental (by).
ज is not a separate noun here; it ends the compound.
questions.explain: शरीर-जानाम् = of those born in the body, so मनस्-जानाम् = of those born in the mind.
questions.rule: X-ज = born in/of X; genitive plural -जानाम् = of those born.
questions.teaches: A compound X-ज means born in X; -जानाम् is the genitive plural, of those born.

questions.q: Verse 58 gives the supreme remedy for which doṣas?
optionExplain: The body's doṣas were treated in verse 57.
No such doṣas are mentioned.
Right: मनोदोषौषधं परम्: the supreme remedy for the doṣas of the mind.
Seasons are not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: मनोदोषौषधम् = the remedy for the doṣas of the mind.
questions.rule: मन के दोषों की परम औषध: धी, धैर्य, आत्मादि का ज्ञान.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 58 to its meaning.
pairs: remedy for the doṣas of the mind
questions.explain: Three of these come from line 1 and one from line 2.
questions.rule: धी = intellect; धैर्य = steadiness; मनोदोषौषध = remedy for the mind's doṣas; अध्यायसंग्रह = summary of chapters.

questions.q: Put the four phrases of verse 58 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 names the remedy for the mind's doṣas; line 2 turns to the chapter summary.
questions.rule: First the remedy, then the announcement of the chapter list.
questions.teaches: The verse closes the section on doṣas and remedies and announces the chapter list.

questions.q: Which English line for the second half of verse 58 is right?
options: The summary of the chapters of this treatise has been stated above.
Next, the cure of every disease in this treatise will be stated.
Next, the summary of the doṣas of this treatise will be stated.
Next, the summary of the chapters of this treatise will be stated.
optionExplain: वक्ष्यते is future (will be stated), not past.
अध्यायसंग्रह is a summary of chapters, not a cure.
What is summarised is the chapters (अध्याय), not the doṣas.
Right: This follows तन्त्रस्यास्य परं चातो वक्ष्यतेऽध्यायसंग्रहः.
questions.explain: तन्त्रस्य अस्य = of this treatise; अतः = next; वक्ष्यते = will be stated; अध्यायसंग्रहः = summary of chapters.
questions.rule: वक्ष्यते = will be stated; अध्यायसंग्रह = summary of the chapters.

questions.q: What does वक्ष्यते tell us about the chapter summary?
options: It is being asked by a student
optionExplain: Right: वक्ष्यते is a future passive: it will be told.
A past statement would use a past form.
The word is passive, but it names no questioner.
Nothing in the word forbids it.
questions.explain: The card labels वक्ष्यते as a passive future: the summary of the chapters will be told.

questions.q: How is भविष्यते + अत्र written when joined?
optionExplain: ए + अ does not give ता, and the word अत्र is not changed to व्र.
Right: ए + अ stays ए, and the lost अ is marked by ऽ, as in वक्ष्यतेऽध्याय.
ए + अ does not give आ.
ए before a different vowel may become अय्, but not before अ.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives वक्ष्यतेऽध्यायसंग्रहः gives भविष्यतेऽत्र.
questions.rule: ए + अ → ए, with ऽ for the lost अ.
questions.teaches: Final ए before short अ stays ए and the अ is written as ऽ.

questions.q: What kind of text is verse 59?
optionExplain: No remedy is described.
Disease is defined in verse 51, not here.
Right: The verse has no verb: it lists the titles of chapters.
No instruction is given.
questions.explain: The verse lists chapter titles; it has no verb, so it is translated as a list.
questions.rule: Verse 59: a list of chapter titles, no verb.

questions.q: Put these clear words of verse 59 in their printed order.
questions.explain: दिन and ऋतु are in line 1; द्रव and अन्न are in line 2. Damaged words between them are left out.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are legible and certain.
questions.rule: दिन = day; ऋतु = season; द्रव = liquid; अन्न = food.
questions.teaches: Only the clear words of a damaged list are used for questions.

questions.q: Which split of दिनर्तु is right?
optionExplain: आ + ऋ gives आर्: that would be दिनार्तु.
तु is not part of the word; ऋतु is the second member.
रतु is not a word of the card.
Right: अ + ऋ gives अर्: दिन + ऋतु is written दिनर्तु.
questions.explain: दिन (day) + ऋतु (season) join to दिनर्तु.

questions.q: Which of these words occur in verse 59?
optionExplain: Right: दिनर्तु begins with दिन.
Right: दिनर्तु is दिन + ऋतु joined.
Right: line 2 begins द्रवान्न.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 57.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 60.
questions.explain: The clear words are दिन, ऋतु, द्रव and अन्न.

questions.q: How is वारि + अत्र written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: इ + अ gives य् + अ, as in व्याधि + असम्भवाः → व्याध्यसम्भवाः.
इ + अ does not simply drop the अ.
इ + अ gives य् + अ; ए would come from अ + इ, the other order.
Vowels must join; they are not left apart.
questions.explain: A short इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
questions.teaches: Short इ before a different vowel becomes य्; the second vowel then stands on य्.

questions.q: Which word of verse 60 means great decoctions?
optionExplain: मात्रा means measure.
Right: महा = great, कषाय = decoction: महाकषाय in line 2.
औषध means medicine.
रस means taste.
questions.explain: महाकषाय is a title word in line 2.

questions.q: Put these clear parts of verse 60 in their printed order.
questions.explain: मात्रा and औषधज्ञान are in line 1; महाकषाय and रसभेद are in line 2. Damaged words are left out.
questions.rule: Line 1: मात्रा, औषधज्ञान. Line 2: महाकषाय, रसभेद.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are legible and certain.
questions.rule: मात्रा = measure; अशित = what is eaten; महाकषाय = great decoctions; विविध = various; रस = taste.
questions.teaches: Title words of the list are matched only where the reading is certain.

questions.q: How is अशित + औषध written when joined?
optionExplain: अशितोषध would need अ + उ → ओ; the second word begins with औ (अ + औ → औ), so the join is अशितौषध.
अ + ए would give ऐ; the second word begins with औ.
Right: अ + औ gives औ: अशित + औषध is written अशितौषध.
अ + अ would give आ; औषध begins with औ.
questions.explain: मात्राशितौषधज्ञान contains मात्रा + अशित + औषध + ज्ञान.

questions.q: Which of these words are printed in verse 60?
optionExplain: Right: line 2.
Right: रसभेदकाः.
Right: line 1.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 62.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 61.
questions.explain: Clear words: मात्रा, औषध, ज्ञान, महाकषाय, विविध, द्रव्य, रस.
questions.rule: Check each word against the printed lines.

questions.q: By the pattern of महाकषाय, what does महावन mean?
options: The forest of a great one
optionExplain: महा- does not mean small.
The compound is a simple great + forest.
महा- is not a negation.
Right: महा- means great: महाकषाय is great decoction, so महावन is great forest.
questions.explain: महा before a noun makes it great.
questions.teaches: महा- before a noun means great (महाकषाय, महावन).

questions.q: Which word begins line 2 of verse 61?
optionExplain: Right: Line 2 begins चिकित्सास्नेहस्वेद…
स्नेह comes after चिकित्सा.
दोषादि begins line 1.
भेषजं ends line 1.
questions.explain: चिकित्सा is the first title word of line 2.

questions.q: Put these clear words of line 2 in their printed order.
questions.explain: The doubtful string शुध्यास्थापन sits between स्वेद and नावन and is left out.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are glosses of the card, all from line 2; the verse names them only.
questions.rule: स्नेह = oiling; स्वेद = sweating; चिकित्सा = treatment.
questions.teaches: Procedure names are kept with a literal gloss; the verse gives no detail.

questions.q: What does स्नेहस्वेद mean?
optionExplain: स्वेद, sweating, is the second member.
Right: स्नेह is oiling and स्वेद is sweating; two nouns joined as a pair.
The first member is स्नेह, not चिकित्सा.
स्नेह is oiling, not dryness.
questions.explain: स्नेह (oiling) + स्वेद (sweating) are two procedure names in line 2.

questions.q: Which of these words are printed in verse 61?
optionExplain: Right: line 2.
Right: line 2.
Right: ends line 2.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 57.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 62.
questions.explain: Clear words of line 2: चिकित्सा, स्नेह, स्वेद, नावन.
questions.rule: Check each word against the printed lines.

questions.q: By the pattern of चिकित्सास्नेहस्वेद…, what does तैलघृतमधु mean?
options: The ghee that comes from oil
optionExplain: The items are separate, not one thing of another.
Nothing in the compound negates the items.
Right: A list of nouns with no ca is read as a dvandva: all items together.
The compound names three items, not a source.
questions.explain: Words joined with no ca are read as a list, as the chapter titles here are.
questions.rule: A run of nouns without ca = a dvandva list.
questions.teaches: A run of nouns joined without ca is a dvandva, read as a list of separate items.

questions.q: Line 2 of verse 62 begins with a procedure on what?
optionExplain: The eyes are not named in line 2.
Teeth are not named in this verse.
Skin is not named in this verse.
Right: सिराविधिः: the procedure on the veins.
questions.explain: सिरा-विधिः = procedure on the veins.

questions.q: Put the three title phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 is clear: veins, then dart or foreign body, then operations with blade, caustic and fire.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are words of line 2, which is clear; the damaged line 1 is not used.
questions.rule: सिरा = vein; शल्य = dart or foreign body; शस्त्र = blade; क्षार = caustic; अग्नि = fire.
questions.teaches: Questions use the clear line 2, not the damaged line 1.

questions.q: Which three means does शस्त्रक्षाराग्निकर्मकाः name for operations?
optionExplain: Right: शस्त्र-क्षार-अग्नि: blade, caustic and fire.
The third member is अग्नि, fire.
Smoke is धूम, in line 1; the first member is शस्त्र.
Leeches are जलौकस्, in line 1; the middle member is क्षार.
questions.explain: शस्त्र (blade), क्षार (caustic), अग्नि (fire) + कर्म (operation).
questions.rule: शस्त्र-क्षार-अग्नि कर्म = operations with blade, caustic and fire.

questions.q: Which of these words are printed in verse 62?
optionExplain: Right: शस्त्रक्षाराग्निकर्मकाः in line 2.
Right: line 2.
Right: line 2.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 61.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 57.
questions.explain: Line 2 names शस्त्र, क्षार and अग्नि as the means of the operations.
questions.rule: Check each word against the printed lines.

questions.q: By the pattern of सिराविधिः, what does दन्तविधिः mean?
optionExplain: The first member is the thing acted on.
Right: X-विधिः is a procedure on X, as सिराविधिः is on the veins.
Nothing in the compound negates दन्त.
विधि here is a procedure on X, not a rule given by X.
questions.explain: सिरा-विधिः = procedure on the veins; दन्त-विधिः = procedure on the teeth.
questions.teaches: X-विधिः names a procedure on X; the first member is what is worked on.

questions.q: Which number of chapters does verse 63 open with?
optionExplain: चतुर्दश would be fourteen.
द्वादश is twelve; the verse says forty (चत्वारिंशत्).
Right: चत्वारिंशत् means forty.
षोडश would be sixteen.
questions.explain: चत्वारिंशदिमेऽध्यायाः = these forty chapters.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Put these clear titles of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The fused last title, व्यापच्छरीरजाः, is unclear and is left out.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the glosses of the card.
questions.rule: चत्वारिंशत् = forty; पुत्रार्थ = for a son; अवक्रान्ति = descent; चर्या = conduct.
questions.teaches: Title words are glossed literally; the unit gives no further detail.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: What does गर्भावक्रान्ति mean?
optionExplain: अवक्रान्ति means descent, not death.
No care or mother is in the word.
पुत्र is a separate title word.
Right: गर्भ = embryo, अवक्रान्ति = descent.
questions.explain: गर्भ (embryo) + अवक्रान्ति (descent); आ is from अ + अ.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Which are printed as title words in verse 63?
optionExplain: Right: begins line 2.
Right: line 2.
Right: line 2.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 62.
Not in this verse; it is in verse 59.
questions.explain: Clear title words of line 2: पुत्रार्थ, गर्भावक्रान्ति, चर्या.
questions.rule: Check each word against the printed lines.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How is तत् + च written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् becomes च् before च, as त् + श gives च्छ in व्यापच्छरीरजाः.
त् is not left unchanged before the palatal च.
द् appears before a voiced sound, and च is not voiced.
त् does not turn into श् before च.
questions.explain: The final त् takes the palatal sound of the following च.
questions.teaches: Final त् becomes च् before च (and च्छ before श); use it for any new pair.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Verse 64 gives a number of chapters together with the messenger chapter. Which number?
optionExplain: Sixteen (षोडश) comes later, in verse 66.
Right: सदूता द्वादशाध्याया: twelve chapters with the messenger chapter.
Twenty-four comes in a later unit, not here.
Six is not a number in this verse.
questions.explain: द्वादश = twelve; सदूता = with the messenger (chapter).
questions.rule: Verse 64: twelve chapters including the messenger chapter.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the firm words of the verse; the middle of line 1 is doubtful.
questions.rule: सिरा = veins; मर्म = vital spots; सदूता = with the messenger chapter; निदानम् = the Nidāna; सार्वरोगिकम् = concerning all diseases.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: What does निदानं सार्वरोगिकं say about the Nidāna?
optionExplain: सार्व means 'of all', not one.
सिरा belongs to the earlier list, not to this phrase.
Right: सार्व-रोगिकम् = concerning all diseases.
Twelve counts chapters in the line before, not diseases.
questions.explain: सार्वरोगिकम् (n. nom. sg.) agrees with निदानम्: the Nidāna concerning all diseases.
questions.rule: सार्वरोगिकम् = concerning all diseases; it describes the Nidāna.
questions.teaches: Reading सार्व + रोगिक as 'of all + concerning diseases' gives 'concerning all diseases'.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Which sandhi rule joins द्वादश + अध्यायाः into द्वादशाध्यायाः?
options: इ before a vowel gives य्
optionExplain: There is no इ at this join.
The join has no इ; it is two अ.
There is no visarga at this join.
Right: The final अ of द्वादश and the first अ of अध्यायाः join into long आ.
questions.explain: द्वादश + अध्यायाः → द्वादशाध्यायाः (the printed text has द्वादशाध्याया, the visarga being dropped).
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these words of verse 64 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins with सिरा, मर्म; line 2 runs सदूता द्वादशाध्याया, then निदानं सार्वरोगिकम्.
questions.rule: Order: सिरा, मर्म, सदूता, द्वादशाध्याया, निदानम्.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: A new line says सशिष्यो गुरुः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: Right: स- = with, as in सदूता; सशिष्यः = with pupils.
स- means 'with'; 'without' would be अशिष्यः.
The noun गुरुः is the teacher; the pupils are the 'with' part.
No messenger here; स- does not mean 'of'.
questions.explain: सशिष्यः = स + शिष्य, 'with pupils', the same pattern as सदूता = with the messenger.
questions.rule: स- at the start of a compound = 'with'.
questions.teaches: Prefix स- gives 'with': सदूता = with the messenger; सशिष्यः = with pupils.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: What kind of text is verse 65?
options: A recipe for a medicine with its doses
A list of subjects in the genitive, with no verb
A story about a physician and a patient
A rule for the daily routine of a student
optionExplain: No dose or ingredient appears; the verse only names subjects.
Right: Every member ends in 'of': ज्वर…, मूत्राघात…, उदरस्य.
There is no person or action, only names.
Nothing about conduct; the verse is a list of subjects.
questions.explain: The verse is a genitive list of subjects; there is no verb.
questions.rule: Verse 65: a genitive list without a verb.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These members are kept literal in the card; the disease names that are terms are left out.
questions.rule: ज्वर = fever; असृक् = blood; श्वस = breath; मूत्राघात = urine-obstruction; उदर = abdomen.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: What does the ending of मूत्राघातप्रमेहाणाम् convey?
optionExplain: 'In' would end in -एषु, as in क्षुद्ररोगेषु later.
'By' would end in -ैः; this is not that ending.
Right: -ाणाम् is the genitive plural: 'of'.
'To' would end in -भ्यः; this ending is -ाणाम्.
questions.explain: The list is genitive: ‘of’ each member, as the English line says 'Of fever, … of urinary obstruction and the pramehas'.
questions.teaches: A final -ाम् or -ाणाम् on a list shows the genitive plural: 'of' all its members.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of विद्रध्यादि?
optionExplain: There is no word विद्रध्य here; the base is विद्रधि.
The base ends in short इ, not long ई.
यादि is not a word; the य् comes from the join.
Right: इ before the vowel आ becomes य्: विद्रध्यादि.
questions.explain: विद्रधि + आदि → विद्रध्यादि: 'vidradhi and so on'.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these subjects of verse 65 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: ज्वर opens line 1; line 2 runs मूत्राघात, प्रमेह, विद्रध्यादि, उदरस्य.
questions.rule: Order: ज्वर, मूत्राघात, प्रमेह, विद्रध्यादि, उदर.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: A new list contains the compound कासादि. What does it say?
optionExplain: Right: -आदि = 'and so on', as in यक्ष्मादि and मदादि.
'Without' would need a negative prefix.
-आदि means more items follow.
आदि means beginning, 'and so on', not end.
questions.explain: कास + आदि → कासादि: cough and so on, like मद + आदि → मदादि.
questions.teaches: The member -आदि after a name means 'and so on': यक्ष्मादि, मदादि, so कासादि = cough and so on.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Line 1 of verse 66 ends with the number षोडश. What number is that?
optionExplain: Six would be षट्; षोडश is a different number.
Right: षोडश = sixteen.
Sixty would be षष्टि.
Twelve (द्वादश) was the number in verse 64.
questions.explain: षोडश means sixteen.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are secure in the data.
questions.rule: षोडश = sixteen; चिकित्सा = treatment; ज्वरस्य = of fever; अनिलार्त्तानाम् = of those afflicted by wind; श्वास = laboured breath.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Does verse 66 itself name what is sixteen?
options: No, it gives only the number
optionExplain: The word 'chapter' does not occur in this verse.
No disease count is stated; षोडश stands alone.
Right: The noun counted is not in the verse.
No section word appears with षोडश.
questions.explain: षोडश closes the list but the counted noun is not stated in this unit.
questions.rule: Do not supply a noun for षोडश from outside the verse.
questions.teaches: A number can stand without its noun; a card should say only that the verse gives the number.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: The verse prints वातअस्रस्य unjoined. Joined by sandhi (अ + अ), what does it become?
optionExplain: अ + अ does not give ए.
अ + अ does not give ओ.
The two vowels do not simply drop; they join into आ.
Right: वात + अस्र: अ + अ gives आ.
questions.explain: वात + अस्रस्य → वातास्रस्य; the print leaves the two words unjoined (a possible slip, flagged only as 'possible').
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these words of line 1 of verse 66 in the printed order.
questions.explain: The line reads पांडुकुष्ठानिलार्त्तानां वातअस्रस्य च षोडश.
questions.rule: Order: पांडु, कुष्ठ, अनिलार्त्तानां, वातअस्रस्य, षोडश.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: A new line says श्वासस्य चिकित्सा. What does it say?
optionExplain: Right: X-स्य चिकित्सा = the treatment of X.
Genitive -स्य is 'of', not 'by'.
That would put both words in one case with no 'of'.
Nothing in the words says 'without'.
questions.explain: Like ज्वरस्य चिकित्सा, 'of fever, the treatment'; here श्वासस्य gives 'of laboured breath'.
questions.rule: X-genitive + चिकित्सा = the treatment of X.
questions.teaches: चिकित्सा with a genitive names what is treated: ज्वरस्य चिकित्सा, श्वासस्य चिकित्सा.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: वमौ stands in the locative singular. What does it mean?
optionExplain: 'Of' would be the genitive वमेः.
Right: वमौ = in vomiting (loc. sg.).
'By' would be the instrumental.
The subject (nominative) form would not end in -औ.
questions.explain: वमौ is the locative singular of वमि (vomiting): 'in vomiting'.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are legible and secure.
questions.rule: वमौ = in vomiting; शोफ = swelling; द्वौ द्वौ = two each; विद्रधौ = in vidradhi.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: What does the ending -षु in विसर्पिषु show?
options: Nominative plural: the items as subject
optionExplain: Genitive plural would end in -ाम्.
Instrumental plural would end in -ैः / -भिः.
Right: -षु is the locative plural; the compound lists several items.
Nominative plural would not end in -षु.
questions.explain: गुल्मजठरपाण्डुशोफविसर्पिषु = in gulma, jaṭhara, pāṇḍu, swelling and visarpa.
questions.rule: -षु (loc. pl.) = 'in', over all members of the list.
questions.teaches: A final -षु on a list compound means 'in' all its members.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How is गुल्मजठरपांडुशोफविसर्पिषु read?
options: One disease 'visarpa of the swollen pāṇḍu jaṭhara'
A single word meaning 'having many diseases'
A list with only the last two items
A list of five items joined by 'and'
optionExplain: That would be a tatpuruṣa chain; the gloss gives a list.
Nothing in the gloss says 'having many'.
The locative ending covers all members.
Right: It is a dvandva: gulma, jaṭhara, pāṇḍu, swelling, visarpa.
questions.explain: The data glosses it as a dvandva: 'in gulma, jaṭhara, pāṇḍu, swelling and visarpa'.
questions.rule: Dvandva = an 'and'-list; the final case ending covers all members.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these items of line 2 of verse 67 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads विद्रधौ गुल्मजठरपांडुशोफविसर्पिषु.
questions.rule: Order: विद्रधौ, गुल्म, जठर, पांडु, शोफ, विसर्पिषु.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: वमौ and विद्रधौ end in -औ. By the same pattern, what does ऋषौ mean?
optionExplain: Right: A noun in -इ has locative singular -औ; ऋषौ = in the sage.
The nominative dual of ऋषि is ऋषी, not ऋषौ.
'Of' is the genitive ऋषेः.
'By' is the instrumental ऋषिणा.
questions.explain: -औ here is the locative singular of an -इ noun, like वमौ and विद्रधौ; -औ is not always dual.
questions.teaches: Final -औ can be locative singular: वमौ, विद्रधौ, so ऋषौ = in the sage.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How many chapters does verse 68 state?
optionExplain: Sixteen (षोडश) was in verse 66.
Right: चतुर्विंशतिः = twenty-four.
Twelve (द्वादश) was in verse 64.
Fifty comes in a later verse, not here.
questions.explain: चतुर्विंशतिरध्यायाः = twenty-four chapters.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word or phrase of verse 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the firm words of the verse.
questions.rule: चतुर्विंशतिः = twenty-four; चिकित्सितम् = treatment; अनिलव्याधि = diseases of wind; ततः परम् = after that; कल्पसिद्धिः = Kalpa and Siddhi.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How does the card read the singular कल्पसिद्धिः?
options: As a single section named Siddhi
optionExplain: The gloss reads two names, Kalpa and Siddhi.
Nothing in the verse makes it a medicine.
Right: A dvandva taken as a collective singular.
Twenty-four counts the chapters, not these.
questions.explain: कल्पसिद्धिः is glossed 'Kalpa and Siddhi' (dvandva); the singular is a collective.
questions.rule: A singular dvandva can name a pair taken together.
questions.teaches: A dvandva in the singular can name two things taken together: कल्पसिद्धिः = Kalpa and Siddhi.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How is कल्पसिद्धिस्ततःपरम् split?
optionExplain: स्ततः is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
There is no अ to add; ततः is the word.
The final visarga of the first word and म् of परम् are lost in this split.
Right: Visarga + त becomes स्त: कल्पसिद्धिस्ततः.
questions.explain: Visarga before त joins as स्; so कल्पसिद्धिः + ततः → कल्पसिद्धिस्ततः.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these words of line 1 of verse 68 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads कुष्ठश्वित्रानिलव्याधिवातास्रेषु चिकित्सितम्.
questions.rule: Order: कुष्ठ, श्वित्र, अनिलव्याधि, वातास्रेषु, चिकित्सितम्.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: How is अग्निः + अत्र joined, as चतुर्विंशतिः + अध्यायाः becomes चतुर्विंशतिरध्यायाः?
optionExplain: Right: After इ, visarga before a vowel becomes र्.
Left unjoined; the rule makes visarga र् here.
That changes इ, not the visarga.
स् is for visarga before त, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: The same rule as चतुर्विंशतिः + अध्यायाः → चतुर्विंशतिरध्यायाः.
questions.teaches: Visarga after इ before a vowel becomes र्: अग्निः + अत्र → अग्निरत्र.
questions.section: शारीर, निदान और चिकित्सा के अध्याय

questions.q: Verse 69 opens with the kalpa (preparation) of two things. Which two?
optionExplain: Basti comes later in the verse.
Right: वमेः विरेकस्य: of emesis and of purgation.
Anuvāsa appears only at the end of line 2.
These are named in line 2 and in the third title.
questions.explain: कल्पो वमेर्विरेकस्य = the preparation of emesis and of purgation.
questions.rule: Verse 69 starts with the kalpa of emesis and purgation.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the title list.
questions.rule: कल्पः = preparation; वमेः = of emesis; विरेकस्य = of purgation; सिद्धिः = success; बस्तीनाम् = of the bastis.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: The printed text reads तत्सिद्धि र्बस्तिकल्पना. Where does the र् belong?
options: To बस्तिकल्पना, as its first letter
To neither; it is a different word
To तत्सिद्धिः, as its visarga turned र्
optionExplain: The word is बस्तिकल्पना; it has no initial र्.
र् is the sandhi form of a visarga.
Right: ः before a voiced ब after इ becomes र्.
The र् sits inside this line.
questions.explain: तत्सिद्धिः + बस्तिकल्पना → तत्सिद्धिर्बस्तिकल्पना; the space in the print is misplaced.
questions.rule: Visarga after इ before a voiced consonant → र्.
questions.teaches: Visarga after इ before a voiced consonant becomes र्, joined to the earlier word: तत्सिद्धिर्बस्ति…
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of बस्त्यनुवासयोः?
optionExplain: There is no word बस्त्य.
The base बस्ति has a short इ.
यनुवास is not a word.
Right: इ before अ becomes य्: बस्त्यनुवासयोः.
questions.explain: बस्ति + अनुवासयोः → बस्त्यनुवासयोः: of basti and anuvāsa.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these titles of verse 69 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads कल्पो वमेर्विरेकस्य तत्सिद्धिर्बस्तिकल्पना.
questions.rule: Order: कल्पः, वमेः, विरेकस्य, तत्सिद्धिः, बस्तिकल्पना.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: What does the new compound गुरुशिष्ययोः mean when read as a genitive, like बस्त्यनुवासयोः 'of basti and anuvāsa'?
options: Of the teacher and the pupil
In the teacher and the pupils
Of the teacher who is a pupil
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva with -योः read as genitive dual: of the two.
'In' plural would end in -षु.
A dvandva lists two, not one person.
That would be a nominative form, not -योः.
questions.explain: बस्त्यनुवासयोः is a dvandva with the dual ending -योः (genitive here; -योः can also be locative); गुरुशिष्ययोः works the same way.
questions.rule: Dvandva + -योः = 'of (or in) the two, A and B'; context decides.
questions.teaches: -योः after a dvandva of two names is the genitive (or locative) dual: बस्त्यनुवासयोः = of basti and anuvāsa, गुरुशिष्ययोः = of the teacher and the pupil.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: In द्रव्यकल्पोऽष्टमः, what ordinal does अष्टमः give?
optionExplain: Sixth is षष्ठः.
Right: अष्टमः = eighth.
Fifth is पञ्चमः.
First is प्रथमः.
questions.explain: Dravyakalpa is called the eighth.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are firm or clear in the data.
questions.rule: द्रव्यकल्पः = Dravyakalpa; अष्टमः = eighth; उत्तरम् = Uttara section; बालोपचरणे = in tending of children; निषेधने = in restraint.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: How does द्रव्यकल्पः + अष्टमः become द्रव्यकल्पोऽष्टमः?
optionExplain: After अ the visarga gives ओ, not ए.
The sandhi changes the visarga.
Right: ः → ओ before a voiced sound after अ; अ elided.
That is for अ + अ, but here a visarga is between.
questions.explain: ः + अ after अ → ओ + ऽ (the अ is elided).
questions.rule: After अ, visarga + voiced sound or अ → ओ.
questions.teaches: After अ, a visarga before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped, marked by ऽ.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of बालोपचरणे?
optionExplain: ई before उ would give यु, not ओ.
बालो is the joined form, not a split.
पचरणे is not the second word.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ: बालोपचरणे.
questions.explain: बाल + उपचरणे → बालोपचरणे: in the tending of children.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these parts of line 2 of verse 70 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads बालोपचरणे व्याधिग्रहज्ञाननिषेधने.
questions.rule: Order: बालोपचरणे, व्याधि, ग्रह, ज्ञान, निषेधने.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: How are गृह and उपयोगः joined, as बाल + उपचरणे became बालोपचरणे?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
औ is for अ + ओ / औ.
Dropping the अ is not the rule.
आ is for अ + अ.
questions.explain: गृह + उपयोगः → गृहोपयोगः, the same rule as बालोपचरणे.
questions.teaches: Final अ with initial उ makes ओ: बाल + उपचरणे → बालोपचरणे, गृह + उपयोगः → गृहोपयोगः.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: स्नाने stands in the locative singular. What does it mean?
optionExplain: 'Of' would be the genitive.
Right: स्नाने = in bathing.
'By' would be the instrumental.
The nominative would not end in -ए.
questions.explain: Locative = 'in': in bathing.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are legible and secure.
questions.rule: स्नाने = in bathing; पृथक् = separately; भूते = in bhūta; स्मृतिक्षये = in loss of memory; द्वौ = two.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: In पृथग्ग्रहे, what happens to the final क् of पृथक् before ग्रहे?
optionExplain: A final stop turns voiced before a voiced sound.
ख् is not the voiced partner of क्.
Right: Before a voiced ग्, क् turns to ग्.
The letter changes; it is not dropped.
questions.explain: पृथक् + ग्रहे → पृथग्ग्रहे.
questions.teaches: A final क् becomes ग् before a voiced sound: पृथक् + ग्रहे → पृथग्ग्रहे.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which reading of स्मृतिक्षये is right?
optionExplain: The order of the words would be reversed.
-ए is locative singular; there is no dual.
'From' would be the ablative.
Right: A compound: the loss (क्षय) of memory (स्मृति), in the locative.
questions.explain: The data glosses it 'in loss of memory' (tat-puruṣa, loc. sg.).
questions.rule: Tat-puruṣa: first member depends on the second.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these four items of verse 71 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The order is स्नाने, पृथग्ग्रहे, भूते, (an unclear item), स्मृतिक्षये.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: A new line says धनक्षये. What does it say?
optionExplain: Right: Like स्मृतिक्षये: क्षय of the first word, in the locative.
'By' would be धनक्षयेण.
That would be two words, धने क्षये; here धन depends on क्षय in one compound.
'Of' would be the genitive.
questions.explain: धन + क्षये = in loss of wealth, as स्मृति + क्षये = in loss of memory.
questions.rule: Tat-puruṣa + locative -ए = 'in the X of Y'.
questions.teaches: A tat-puruṣa in the locative reads 'in the Y of X': स्मृतिक्षये, धनक्षये.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: कर्णनासामुखेषु names which three places?
optionExplain: The eye words come before, in the first compound.
Right: कर्ण = ear, नासा = nose, मुख = mouth.
Head and wound are in line 2.
The head (मूर्ध्नि) is separate, in line 2.
questions.explain: कर्णनासामुखेषु = in the ear, nose and mouth.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 72 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are clear in the data.
questions.rule: कर्ण = ear; नासा = nose; मुख = mouth; मूर्ध्नि = in the head; व्रणे = in the wound.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: What does the repeated word pair द्वौ द्वौ mean?
optionExplain: Repeating the number does not make a total.
द्वौ is 'two', not 'again'.
Right: The repeated number is distributive: two for each.
द्वौ is a number, not the names of two organs.
questions.explain: द्वौ द्वौ = two each; the verse leaves open which of the items it covers.
questions.rule: A repeated number = 'two each'; its range here is not stated.
questions.teaches: A repeated number word is distributive: द्वौ द्वौ = two each.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of सद्योभंगे?
optionExplain: Without the visarga there would be no ओ.
आ does not give ओ.
That would be written with ऽ and means 'no breaking'.
Right: ः becomes ओ before a voiced भ after अ.
questions.explain: सद्यः + भंगे → सद्योभंगे: in sudden breaking.
questions.rule: After अ, ः before a voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which of these are named in verse 72?
optionExplain: Right: कर्ण.
Right: मूर्ध्नि.
Right: भगन्दरे.
No tooth appears in the verse.
No tongue appears in the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 names the eye items, ear, nose and mouth; line 2 the head, wound, sudden breaking, bhagandara.
questions.rule: Named: ear, nose, mouth, head, wound, bhagandara; not tooth or tongue.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: What does the new compound हस्तपादमुखेषु mean, like कर्णनासामुखेषु?
options: In the hands, feet and mouth
In the face of hand and foot
Of the hands, feet and mouth
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva with the locative plural -एषु.
That would make a chain, not a list.
'With' would end in -ैः.
'Of' would end in -ाणाम्.
questions.explain: As कर्णनासामुखेषु = in the ear, nose and mouth, so हस्तपादमुखेषु = in the hands, feet and mouth.
questions.teaches: A dvandva ending in -एषु reads 'in A, B and C'.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: What does क्षुद्ररोगेषु mean?
optionExplain: क्षुद्र means small, not great.
Right: क्षुद्र = small, minor; रोगेषु = in diseases.
-एषु is 'in', not 'of'.
-एषु is 'in', not 'by'.
questions.explain: क्षुद्ररोगेषु = in minor diseases.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are clear in the data.
questions.rule: क्षुद्र = minor; गुह्य = hidden; विषे = in poison; भुजगे = in the snake; मूषके = in the rat.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which pair of words stands for 'in the snake and the insect' in line 2?
optionExplain: That is spiders and the rat.
That is 'in poison, two'.
Right: Two locatives, each singular: in the snake, in the insect.
That is the diseases of hidden parts, in line 1.
questions.explain: भुजगे = in the snake; कीटे = in the insect.
questions.teaches: Two singular locatives side by side name two separate items.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of ग्रंथ्यादौ?
optionExplain: There is no word ग्रंथ्य.
The base has a short इ.
यादौ is not a word.
Right: इ before आ becomes य्: ग्रंथ्यादौ.
questions.explain: ग्रंथि + आदौ → ग्रंथ्यादौ: in granthi and so on.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these six items of verse 73 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs ग्रंथ्यादौ, क्षुद्ररोगेषु, गुह्यरोगे, … विषे, … भुजगे, कीटे.
questions.rule: Order: ग्रंथ्यादौ, क्षुद्ररोगेषु, गुह्यरोगे, विषे, भुजगे, कीटे.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: What does the new word अग्न्यादौ mean, as ग्रंथ्यादौ means 'in granthi and so on'?
options: In the fire of the beginning
optionExplain: Right: अग्नि + आदौ: -आदौ = 'in X and so on'.
आदौ is 'and so on' here, not a first fire.
आदि means more items follow.
'Of' would be the genitive.
questions.explain: अग्नि + आदौ → अग्न्यादौ, by the same join as ग्रंथि + आदौ → ग्रंथ्यादौ.
questions.rule: X + आदौ = 'in X and so on'.
questions.teaches: X + आदौ reads 'in X and so on': ग्रंथ्यादौ, अग्न्यादौ.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which word in line 1 of verse 74 means 'chapter'?
optionExplain: विषे means in poison.
Right: अध्यायः = chapter.
रसायने means on rasāyana.
तथा means likewise.
questions.explain: तथाऽध्यायो रसायने = likewise a chapter on rasāyana.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are clear in the data.
questions.rule: विषे = in poison; विषोपयोगे = in the use of poison; रसायने = on rasāyana; वाजीकरणम् = vājīkaraṇa; पञ्चाशः = fiftieth.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Why does उद्दिश्य end in -य and not in -त्वा?
options: The root is a verb of motion
The sentence is in the past
optionExplain: Nothing about motion decides it.
It is an absolutive, 'aiming at'.
Right: With a prefix, the absolutive ends in -य.
Tense does not decide the ending.
questions.explain: उद्दिश्य = ud + √दिश् + य, the absolutive 'aiming at'.
questions.teaches: An absolutive of a prefixed root ends in -य, not -त्वा.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of विषोपयोगे?
optionExplain: विषो is the joined form.
इ before उ would give यु, not ओ.
पयोगे is not the second word.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ: विषोपयोगे.
questions.explain: विष + उपयोगे → विषोपयोगे: in the use of poison.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange these items of verse 74 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives विषे, विषोपयोगे, then the chapter on rasāyana; line 2 begins with वाजीकरणम्.
questions.rule: Order: विषे, विषोपयोगे, अध्यायः, रसायने, वाजीकरणम्.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the correct absolutive (the -त्वा or -य form, meaning having bowed) of √नम् with prefix प्र?
optionExplain: Right: A prefixed root takes -य.
-त्वा is used when there is no prefix.
That is a present participle, not an absolutive.
That is a past participle (bowed), not an absolutive.
questions.explain: प्र + √नम् + य → प्रणम्य, as उद् + √दिश् → उद्दिश्य.
questions.teaches: With a prefix, the absolutive ends in -य: उद्दिश्य, प्रणम्य.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: In how many sthānas (sections) does verse 75 say the work is declared?
optionExplain: Five would be पञ्चभिः.
Right: षड्भिः स्थानैः = by six sections.
Four would be चतुर्भिः.
Eight would be अष्टभिः.
questions.explain: षड्भिः स्थानैः समीरितम् = declared by six sections.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 75 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the numbers and the closing formula.
questions.rule: षड्भिः = by six; स्थानैः = by sections; समीरितम् = declared; प्रथमः = first; नाम = named.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: How does the card read पञ्चाशदध्यायशतम्?
optionExplain: That drops the 'hundred'.
That drops the 'fifty'.
Right: The sum is the natural reading.
Six is the number of sections, not chapters.
questions.explain: पञ्चाशत् + अध्यायशतम् = fifty and a hundred chapters, 150.
questions.rule: The card reads the compound as the sum 150.
questions.teaches: Fifty and a hundred are added: 150 chapters.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Which is the right split of इत्यायुष्कामीयो?
optionExplain: यायुष्कामीय is not a word.
There is no word इत्य.
The word is इति, with short इ.
Right: इ before आ becomes य्; ः becomes ओ.
questions.explain: इति + आयुष्कामीयः → इत्यायुष्कामीयः (and ः → ओ before the next word).
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: Arrange the words of the colophon in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The colophon reads इत्यायुष्कामीयो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः.
questions.rule: Order: इति, आयुष्कामीयः, नाम, प्रथमः, अध्यायः.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: A new colophon ends with नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः. Which chapter is it?
optionExplain: Right: पञ्चमः = fifth, as प्रथमः = first.
First is प्रथमः.
Fiftieth is पञ्चाशः.
No fraction is meant; पञ्चमः is the ordinal.
questions.explain: प्रथमोऽध्यायः means the first chapter; पञ्चमोऽध्यायः means the fifth.
questions.teaches: An ordinal before अध्यायः names the chapter's place: प्रथमः first, पञ्चमः fifth.
questions.section: कल्प, सिद्धि, उत्तर और कुल अध्याय

questions.q: A chapter opens अथातः शिष्योपनयनीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः. What is announced?
options: The pupil's initiation has already been completed
The chapter on the pupil's initiation will be explained
The teacher will now question the pupil
The previous chapter is being closed
optionExplain: Nothing here says it is finished; the verb looks ahead.
Right: व्याख्यास्यामः says 'we shall explain'; the subject is the chapter on the pupil's initiation.
The verb is 'we shall explain', not a question.
The line opens a new chapter.
questions.explain: The line announces that the chapter on the pupil's initiation will now be explained.
questions.rule: अथातः ... अध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the opening to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of the formula and the title word of this chapter.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; अध्यायम् = chapter; शिष्योपनयनीयम् = concerning the pupil's initiation.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: The word for "we shall explain" is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the verb of the announcement: 'we shall explain'.
questions.teaches: The ending -मः marks 'we' (first person plural), and the verb looks ahead: we shall explain.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातः?
optionExplain: अ + इ would join as ए, giving अथेतः.
तः is not a word.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ, so अथ + अतः is written अथातः.
Neither part is a word here.
questions.explain: अथातः = अथ (now) + अतः (therefore).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: अथ + अतः = अथातः.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put the words of the announcement in the order of the line.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, the-initiation-chapter, chapter, we-shall-explain.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented line reads अथातः आहारीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः (आहारीयम् = concerning food). By the same pattern, what is announced?
options: Now, therefore, we shall eat a meal
Now, therefore, the chapter on food is finished
Now, therefore, you will explain the chapter on food
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on food
optionExplain: व्याख्यास्यामः means explaining, and अध्यायम् is a chapter.
The verb is a future 'we shall explain', not a close.
-मः marks 'we', not 'you'.
Right: The pattern is अथातः + title word + अध्यायं + व्याख्यास्यामः; आहारीयम् = concerning food.
questions.explain: आहारीयम् = concerning food; the rest of the formula is unchanged.
questions.rule: अथातः + title word in -ीयम् + अध्यायं + व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain the chapter concerning that subject.
questions.teaches: Chapters open with one fixed pattern: only the title word changes.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: The verse lists three mental gifts. Which three?
optionExplain: Right: धी, स्मृति and पाटव are the three in the verse.
Wealth and fame are not listed.
Anger and pride are not listed.
None of these is listed.
questions.explain: The verse names intellect (धी), memory (स्मृति) and skill (पाटव).
questions.rule: धीस्मृतिपाटवैः = with intellect, memory and skill.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words are mental gifts, two describe the body.
questions.rule: धी = intellect; स्मृति = memory; ऋजु = straight; तनु = thin.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of ऋज्वास्य?
optionExplain: वास्य is not the second word here.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: ऋजु + आस्य = ऋज्वास्य.
ओ + आ would not give ज्वा.
इ + आ would give ज्या (ऋज्यास्य), not ज्वा.
questions.explain: ऋज्वास्य = ऋजु (straight) + आस्य (mouth).
questions.rule: उ + different vowel → व्: ऋजु + आस्य = ऋज्वास्य.
questions.teaches: Before a different vowel, उ turns into व् and the next vowel joins on to it.
