questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: What does the ending -ैः in धीस्मृतिपाटवैः show?
options: Singular 'of': the intellect of one man
Plural 'with': by means of intellect, memory and skill
Plural 'from': coming away from these qualities
optionExplain: It is plural, and not 'of'.
The word names three qualities, and -ैः is not a dual ending here.
Right: -ैः here is the instrumental plural, 'with'.
'From' would be a different ending.
questions.explain: धीस्मृतिपाटवैः = with intellect, memory and skill (instrumental plural).
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put the three mental gifts in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse says intellect, then memory, then skill.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: By the pattern of ऋज्वास्यनासानयनः, whom does a word like दीर्घबाहुः describe?
optionExplain: The compound names the owner, not the arm.
Nothing in the pattern says cutting.
बाहु is an arm, not a road.
Right: Such a compound (bahuvrīhi) names the person who has the features: दीर्घ (long) + बाहु (arm).
questions.explain: A bahuvrīhi like ऋज्वास्यनासानयनः names the one who 'has' these features.
questions.rule: Feature words in a bahuvrīhi describe the person who has them.
questions.teaches: A compound of this kind describes a person by what he has: दीर्घबाहुः = one with long arms.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: How long has this student already lived, according to the verse?
optionExplain: Right: षण्मासानुषितः says he has lived six months.
The verse says six, not three.
A year is not mentioned.
Twelve years is not mentioned.
questions.explain: He is ‘षण्मासानुषितः’: one who has lived six months.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: one who has conquered the pairs of opposites
questions.explain: These four words are the student and his qualities.
questions.rule: ब्रह्मचारी = celibate student; जितद्वन्द्वः = conquered the pairs of opposites; सुचरितः = of good conduct; शक्तः = capable.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: In लज्जाशौचकलान्वितः, what does the ending अन्वितः add to the three nouns?
optionExplain: That is the opposite of अन्वित.
Right: अन्वित means endowed with: modesty, cleanliness and skill belong to him.
Nothing here means fear.
The nouns are what he has, not who teaches him.
questions.explain: लज्जा (modesty), शौच (cleanliness), कला (skill) + अन्वितः = endowed with these.
questions.teaches: A list of nouns followed by अन्वितः names what the person has.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which rendering of the second line is correct?
options: Having lived six years, capable, endowed with modesty, wealth and skill
Having lived six months, unable, endowed with modesty, cleanliness and skill
Having lived six months, capable, endowed with modesty, cleanliness and skill
Having lived six months, capable, endowed with anger, cleanliness and skill
optionExplain: Six months, not years; and wealth is not listed.
शक्तः is capable, not unable.
Right: It follows षण्मासानुषितः शक्तो लज्जाशौचकलान्वितः word for word.
Anger is not listed; modesty is.
questions.explain: The line gives one residence of six months and three gifts: लज्जा, शौच, कला.
questions.rule: Second line = six months resident + capable + modesty, cleanliness, skill.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put these descriptions in the order of the first line.
questions.explain: The first line runs: student, conqueror of opposites, steadfast, well conducted, firm.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: By the pattern of जितद्वन्द्वः, what does an invented word जितक्रोधः describe?
options: One who has lost to anger
optionExplain: जित means conquered, not caused.
The compound describes the person, not the anger.
That would be the opposite.
Right: जित (conquered) + क्रोध (anger), used for the person, like जितद्वन्द्वः.
questions.explain: जितद्वन्द्वः = one who has conquered the pairs; जितक्रोधः works the same way.
questions.rule: जित + noun (as a describing compound) = one who has conquered that.
questions.teaches: जित + a noun describes the person who has conquered it.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Until what point is the pupil to be taught, according to the first line?
options: Until he reaches the end of the treatise, its meaning and its practices
Until he has taught the whole treatise to another pupil
Until the teacher himself grows old and weak
Until he can recite a single chapter from memory
optionExplain: Right: यावदन्तं तन्त्रार्थकर्मणाम् = up to the end of the treatise, meaning and practices.
Teaching others is not mentioned.
Age is not mentioned.
The goal is the end of the whole treatise, not one chapter.
questions.explain: He is taught up to the end of the treatise, its meaning and its practices.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three belong to the first line, the last to the occasions.
questions.rule: शिष्यः = pupil; अध्याप्यः = to be taught; यावदन्तम् = up to the end; राहुदर्शने = at the sight of Rāhu.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाकालविद्युत्स्तनिते?
optionExplain: The next word begins with अकाल (untimely), not आकाल.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: न + अकाल... = नाकाल...
That would drop the negative अ- of अकाल and turn 'untimely' into 'timely'.
लविद्युत्... is not a word.
questions.explain: न (not) + अकाल-विद्युत्-स्तनिते (in untimely lightning and thunder).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: न + अकाल... = नाकाल...
questions.teaches: When न meets a word beginning with अ, the two अ merge into आ.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: What does the ending -णाम् in तन्त्रार्थकर्मणाम् show?
options: Singular 'in': inside one single practice of the treatise
Singular 'by': done by one man through practice
Plural 'to': given to the treatises one by one
optionExplain: It is plural, and 'in' would be a different ending.
It is not an instrumental.
Right: -णाम् here is the genitive plural.
'To' would be a different ending.
questions.explain: तन्त्रार्थकर्मणाम् = of the treatise, its meaning and its practices (three-item reading).
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put the three occasions in the order of the second line.
questions.explain: The line names untimely lightning and thunder first, then an earthquake, then the sight of Rāhu.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: By the pattern of राहुदर्शने, what does an invented चन्द्रदर्शने mean?
options: By the sight of the moon
At the sight of the moon
optionExplain: -ने in this pattern is 'at/in', not 'by'.
दर्शन is sight, not setting.
That would be a genitive.
Right: दर्शने (locative) = at the sight; चन्द्र is the moon.
questions.explain: -दर्शने with the thing seen before it means 'at the sight of' it.
questions.rule: X-दर्शने = at the sight of X.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -दर्शने names the time of seeing something: राहुदर्शने, चन्द्रदर्शने.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: In whose absence should he not recite, according to the first line?
optionExplain: Right: परोक्षे गुरोः = in the absence of the teacher.
The king is not mentioned.
His father is not mentioned.
A patient is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The first line says not in the absence of the teacher (गुरोः परोक्षे).
questions.rule: परोक्षे गुरोः = in the teacher's absence.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words come from the first line and two from the second.
questions.rule: पठेत् = should recite; परोक्षे = in the absence; गुरोः = of the teacher; अतिमन्दम् = too slowly.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of नात्युच्चनीचकैः?
optionExplain: त्युच्च... is not a word.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: अति + उच्च = अत्युच्च; न + अत्यु... = नात्यु...
आति is not the word here; it is अति (too).
अत्य is not a word; the join of अति and उच्च makes अत्युच्च.
questions.explain: नात्युच्चनीचकैः = न (not) + अति (too) + उच्च-नीचकैः (high and low tones).
questions.rule: इ + different vowel → य्: अति + उच्च = अत्युच्च.
questions.teaches: Before a different vowel, इ turns into य्: अति + उच्च = अत्युच्च.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these are named among the manners of reciting in the second line?
options: Tones too high or too low
optionExplain: अतिमन्दम् is named.
अत्युच्चनीचकैः is named.
Walking is not mentioned.
The time of day is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The line names too slowly and tones too high or too low (it also has the doubtful phrase अविच्छिन्नपदम्, left aside).
questions.rule: Named faults: अतिमन्दम् (too slow), अत्युच्च-नीचकैः (too high / too low).
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put these phrases of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The first line gives the tithi, then 'moonless', then 'in the absence', then 'of the teacher', then the verb.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented word लिखेत् is built like पठेत् (from √लिख्, to write). What does it say?
optionExplain: A past form would not end in -एत्.
-एत् is not the future ending.
Right: -एत् is the 'should' ending, as in पठेत्.
That is a plural, and -एत् is singular.
questions.explain: पठेत् and लिखेत् share the -एत् ending: 'he should ...'.
questions.teaches: A verb ending in -एत् is a 'should' form: पठेत्, लिखेत्.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: How should the pupil treat the teacher, according to the first line?
optionExplain: A friend is not mentioned.
A father is not mentioned.
A guest is not mentioned.
Right: राजवत् means 'like a king'.
questions.explain: He should wait upon the teacher like a king (राजवत्).
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two verbs of service and sleep, one of rising, and the comparison.
questions.rule: पर्युपासीत = should attend upon; राजवत् = like a king; शयीत = should lie down; उत्तिष्ठेत = should rise.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: What does -वत् add in राजवत्?
optionExplain: Right: -वत् after a noun makes a word meaning 'like that'.
'From' is a different ending.
'For' is a different ending.
'In' is a different ending.
questions.explain: राजवत् = राज + वत्: like a king.
questions.teaches: -वत् after a noun means 'like' it: राजवत् = like a king.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which pair of times does the second line give the pupil?
options: He lies down before the teacher sleeps and rises after him
He lies down after the teacher sleeps and rises before him
He lies down after the teacher sleeps and rises after him
He lies down before the teacher sleeps and rises before him
optionExplain: This reverses both.
Right: शयीत सुप्त एवास्मिन् (lies down only when he is asleep) and उत्तिष्ठेतास्य पूर्वतः (rises before him) say exactly this.
He rises before the teacher, not after.
He lies down only after the teacher is asleep.
questions.explain: He sleeps only when the teacher has fallen asleep, and rises before him.
questions.rule: After the teacher sleeps; before the teacher rises.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put the pupil's actions in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives service, the comparison, lying down, and then rising.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented line reads शिष्यः गुरुं पितृवत् पर्युपासीत. What does it say?
options: The pupil attended on his father as on a teacher
The father should attend upon the teacher
The pupil should attend upon the teacher as upon a father
The teacher will attend upon the pupil like a father
optionExplain: It is the teacher who is attended upon, and the comparison is a father.
The doer is the pupil.
Right: पितृवत् = like a father; पर्युपासीत = should attend upon.
The pupil attends, not the teacher.
questions.explain: The pattern of राजवत् carries over to other nouns.
questions.rule: noun-वत् + पर्युपासीत = he should attend upon, like that noun.
questions.teaches: -वत् after a noun gives the comparison, and the middle optative -ईत (पर्युपासीत, शयीत) says "should": पितृवत् पर्युपासीत = should attend like a father.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: A good student's speech is described in the second line. Which fits?
optionExplain: Speed and force are not mentioned.
Brevity is not mentioned.
Loudness is not mentioned.
Right: सूनृतः = truthful and pleasant in speech.
questions.explain: सूनृतः means truthful and pleasant in speech.
questions.rule: सूनृतः = truthful and pleasant in speech.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are qualities in the second line.
questions.rule: अभेद्यः = unshakable; अनुद्धतः = not arrogant; सूनृतः = truthful and pleasant in speech; प्रियदर्शनः = pleasant to look at.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of अनुद्धतः?
optionExplain: Right: The negative अ- becomes अन्- before a vowel: अन् + उद्धत = अनुद्धत.
द्धतः is not a word.
नुद्धतः is not a word.
अना- is not the negative prefix here.
questions.explain: अनुद्धतः = अन् (not) + उद्धतः (arrogant): not arrogant.
questions.rule: Negative अ- → अन्- before a vowel: अन् + उद्धत = अनुद्धत.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix अ- takes a न् before a vowel, so अन् + उद्धत joins as अनुद्धत.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: What does न ब्रूयात् convey?
optionExplain: ब्रूयात् is not a past form.
Right: ब्रूयात् is the 'should' form of √ब्रू; with न it forbids.
ब्रूयात् is not a future form.
ब्रूयात् is singular.
questions.explain: न ब्रूयात् केवलं नाम = he should not utter the bare name.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: Put four of the second line's descriptions in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line gives unshakable, not arrogant, (a doubtful word), truthful, pleasant to look at.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: By the pattern of प्रियदर्शनः, an invented word प्रियभाषणः describes whom?
options: One who shows a pleasant face
optionExplain: The compound names the person who has it.
प्रिय is pleasant, not disliked.
Right: प्रिय (pleasant) + भाषण (speech), used for the person, like प्रियदर्शनः.
That would be प्रियमुखः (pleasant-faced), not प्रियभाषणः.
questions.explain: प्रियदर्शनः = pleasant to look at; प्रियभाषणः = pleasant in speech.
questions.rule: प्रिय + noun = one with pleasant [that thing].
questions.teaches: प्रिय + a noun describes the person who has that thing pleasant.
questions.section: गुरु के लक्षण और शिष्य का आचरण

questions.q: How should he tend the helpless and the sick, according to the second line?
optionExplain: A king is the comparison for the teacher, not here.
A stranger is not mentioned.
A master is not mentioned.
Right: पुत्रवत् means 'like a son'.
questions.explain: He should tend them like a son (पुत्रवत् समुपाचरेत्).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three are qualities from the first line; the last is who is tended.
questions.rule: बहुश्रुतः = much learned; कालवेदी = knowing the right time; ज्ञातग्रन्थः = having known the texts; रोगिणः = the sick.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ज्ञातग्रन्थोऽर्थशास्त्रवित्?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ो before अ, and the अ is dropped (ऽ).
ओर्थ... is not a word.
थशास्त्रवित् is not a word.
There is no separate उ in the verse.
questions.explain: ज्ञातग्रन्थः (visarga) + अर्थशास्त्रवित् join as ज्ञातग्रन्थोऽर्थशास्त्रवित्.
questions.rule: -अः + अ- → -ो ऽ-: the visarga turns into ो and the अ of the next word is dropped.
questions.teaches: A final -अः before अ becomes -ो, and the next अ is written as the sign ऽ.

questions.q: Which is the right split of यश्च?
optionExplain: That would join as यशश्च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: यः + च = यश्च; यः is 'who'.
यश् is not a word here.
श्च is not a word.
questions.explain: यश्च = यः (who) + च (and).
questions.rule: visarga + च → श्च: यः + च = यश्च.

questions.q: Put the four qualities of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line gives: much learned, knower of time, knower of texts, knower of the meaning of treatises.

questions.q: By the pattern of कालवेदी, an invented word ऋतुवेदी describes whom?
options: One who is known by the seasons
optionExplain: वेदी is a knower, not a maker.
Nothing in the pattern says fear.
Right: ऋतु (season) + वेदी (knower), like काल + वेदी.
वेदी is the knower, not the known.
questions.explain: कालवेदी = knower of the right time; ऋतुवेदी = knower of the seasons.
questions.rule: noun + वेदी = knower of that noun.
questions.teaches: noun + वेदी describes one who knows it.

questions.q: Who obtains the name 'physician' (bhiṣak), according to the first line?
options: The one who has read the most books
The one chosen by the king
The one who treats the most patients
The one authorised by the teacher
optionExplain: Reading is not the condition named.
The king is not mentioned.
Number of patients is not mentioned.
Right: गुरुणा समनुज्ञातः says he is authorised by the teacher.
questions.explain: He obtains the name when the teacher has authorised him.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make the first line.
questions.rule: गुरुणा = by the teacher; समनुज्ञातः = authorised; अश्नुते = obtains; भिषक्शब्दम् = the name 'physician'.

questions.q: In गुरुणा समनुज्ञातः, who gives the permission, and how can you tell?
options: The pupil: समनुज्ञातः shows he is the giver
The pupil gives it: -णा on गुरुणा shows the giver is the pupil
optionExplain: Right: -णा is the instrumental: the one by whom it is done.
समनुज्ञातः is 'authorised', so the pupil receives it.
गुरुणा names the teacher; -णा is 'by', so the teacher gives it.
-णा is 'by', not 'to'; 'to' would be गुरवे.
questions.explain: The permission comes from the teacher (गुरुणा, 'by the teacher').
questions.rule: -णा / -एन (instrumental) names the one by whom an action is done.
questions.teaches: A noun in the instrumental (-णा, -एन) names the one by whom something is done: 'by'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of यस्तु?
optionExplain: यस् is not the word; it is यः.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: यः + तु = यस्तु.
स्तु is not a word here.
That would be written यस्य तु.
questions.explain: यस्तु = यः (who) + तु (but).
questions.rule: visarga + त → स्त: यः + तु = यस्तु.

questions.q: Put the parts of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: by the teacher, authorised, he, the name 'physician', obtains.

questions.q: An invented phrase reads वैद्येन समनुज्ञातः शिष्यः. By whom is the pupil permitted?
optionExplain: 'For' would be a different ending.
'Of' would be a different ending.
Right: -एन marks the one by whom, as -णा does in गुरुणा.
वैद्येन is not the one permitted.
questions.explain: The instrumental names who gives the permission.
questions.teaches: The instrumental (-णा, -एन) tells you who gives the permission.

questions.q: The man who knows only the treatise reaches a patient. What does the first line say happens?
optionExplain: The verse says the opposite.
Pity is not mentioned.
Anger is not mentioned.
Right: मुह्यति means he becomes bewildered.
questions.explain: Each time he reaches a patient he is bewildered, like a timid man at a battle.
questions.rule: आतुरं प्राप्य मुह्यति = reaching a patient, he is bewildered.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make the comparison and its two sides.
questions.rule: मुह्यति = becomes bewildered; आतुरम् = patient; भीरुः = timid man; आहवम् = battle.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भीरुरिवाहवम्?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after उ turns into र् before a vowel; इव + आहवम् joins as इवाहवम्.
एव would give भीरुरेवाहवम्, and it means 'only', not 'like'.
रिवा and हवम् are not words here.
The last word is आहवम् (battle), not ऊहवम्.
questions.explain: भीरुरिवाहवम् = भीरुः (timid man) + इव (like) + आहवम् (battle).
questions.rule: visarga after उ + vowel → र्; अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: A final visarga after उ becomes र् before a vowel, and अ + आ joins as आ.

questions.q: Why does प्राप्य end in -य and not in -त्वा?
options: Because it is a future form, which always ends in -य
It has the prefix प्र-, so it takes -य
Because the word is repeated as प्राप्य प्राप्य and doubles
Because it is a passive form, which takes -य
optionExplain: It is a 'having done' form, not a future.
Right: A 'having done' word takes -त्वा without a prefix and -य with one.
Repetition does not change the ending; it only means 'each time'.
It is not passive; it is 'having reached'.
questions.explain: प्र + √आप् + -य = प्राप्य, 'having reached'.

questions.q: Put the parts of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: He is bewildered; on reaching a patient each time; like a timid man at a battle.
questions.rule: सः मुह्यति → आतुरं प्राप्य प्राप्य → भीरुः इव आहवम्.

questions.q: To say 'having known' with the prefix वि- on the root √ज्ञा, which form is right?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix.
That is a passive verb, not 'having known'.
Right: With a prefix the 'having done' form ends in -य: वि + ज्ञा → विज्ञाय.
That means one who knows, not 'having known'.
questions.explain: The rule of प्राप्य carries over to other prefixed roots.
questions.teaches: A prefixed root forms its 'having done' word with -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: Which four things about diseases does the second line name?
optionExplain: Price and season are not named.
The name and the spread are not named.
Dose and season are not named.
Right: हेतौ, लिङ्गे, प्रशमने, अपुनर्भवे.
questions.explain: The line names the cause, the sign, the alleviation and the non-recurrence of diseases.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words are all in the 'in' form.
questions.rule: हेतौ = in the cause; लिङ्गे = in the sign; प्रशमने = in the alleviation; अपुनर्भवे = in the non-recurrence.

questions.q: What does -सु show in सत्सु?
options: 'To', singular: given to a good man
optionExplain: Right: -सु is the locative plural ending.
'By' is a different ending.
It is plural, and not 'of'.
It is plural, and not 'to'.
questions.explain: सत्सु = among the good.
questions.teaches: The ending -सु makes a plural word mean 'in' or 'among' the people or things named.

questions.q: What does अपुनर्भवे mean, from its parts?
options: In repeated coming: coming again and again
In a second cause: a different cause
In a sudden start: beginning at once
optionExplain: The negative अ- reverses it.
Right: अ (not) + पुनः (again) + भव (coming to be).
पुनः means again, not second cause.
Nothing in the word means sudden.
questions.explain: अपुनर्भव = a-punar-bhava: no coming again.

questions.q: Put the four topics in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line gives cause, sign, alleviation, non-recurrence.

questions.q: हेतौ (from masculine हेतु) means in the cause. By the same pattern, which form means in the enemy (शत्रु)?
optionExplain: That is 'for the enemy'.
That is 'of the enemy'.
Right: For masculine words in -उ, 'in' ends in -औ: हेतु → हेतौ, शत्रु → शत्रौ.
That is 'the enemy' as object.
questions.explain: The ending of हेतौ carries over to other masculine words in -उ.
questions.teaches: For a masculine word in -उ the 'in' form ends in -औ: हेतौ, शत्रौ.

questions.q: What is said of the physician whose knowledge is fourfold?
options: He must serve a king for life
He should not treat the helpless
He is the youngest of the physicians
He is the best of physicians, worthy of a king
optionExplain: Serving a king for life is not mentioned.
That is not said here.
Age is not mentioned.
Right: राजार्हो भिषक्तमः says exactly this.
questions.explain: The man with fourfold knowledge is best of physicians and worthy of a king.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make the first line.
questions.rule: ज्ञानम् = knowledge; चतुर्विधम् = fourfold; राजार्हः = worthy of a king; भिषक्तमः = best physician.

questions.q: What does -तमः add in भिषक्तमः?
optionExplain: Right: -तम is the superlative: the most excellent.
-तम does not make a diminutive.
-तम does not mean 'without'.
-तम does not mean 'former'.
questions.explain: भिषक्तमः = best physician.
questions.rule: word + -तम = the best of that kind.
questions.teaches: -तम makes a word mean 'the best' of that kind: भिषक्तमः = the best physician.

questions.q: In चतुर्विधम्, what does -विध mean?
optionExplain: विध does not mean time.
Right: चतुर् (four) + विध (kind): fourfold.
विध does not mean cause.
विध does not mean place.
questions.explain: चतुर्विधम् = of four kinds.

questions.q: Put the three things of the second line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line names a weapon, then treatises, then water.

questions.q: By the pattern of चतुर्विधम्, what does an invented षड्विधम् mean?
optionExplain: विध is 'kind', not place.
विध is 'kind', not a repeat.
Right: षट् (six) + विध (kind) = sixfold, as चतुर् (four) + विध = fourfold.
That would be a different word.
questions.explain: The pattern of चतुर्विधम् carries over to other numbers.
questions.teaches: number + विध names how many kinds there are: चतुर्विध = four kinds, षड्विध = six kinds.

questions.q: In the second line the treatise is compared to what?
optionExplain: A mirror is not mentioned.
A road is not mentioned.
A fire is not mentioned.
Right: प्रदीपभूतं शास्त्रम् = the treatise is like a lamp.
questions.explain: The treatise is like a lamp (प्रदीप).
questions.rule: प्रदीपभूतं शास्त्रम् = the treatise is like a lamp.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up the second line's two images.
questions.rule: प्रदीपभूतम् = like a lamp; दर्शनम् = sight; विपुला = wide; मतिः = intellect.

questions.q: By what means is the intellect to be strengthened, and which word shows it?
options: By wide learning: बाहुश्रुत्येन ends in -एन, 'by'
By a king's order: बाहुश्रुत्येन means 'of a king'
For wide learning: बाहुश्रुत्येन ends in a 'for' ending
In wide learning: बाहुश्रुत्येन ends in an 'in' ending
optionExplain: Right: -एन is the instrumental: the means.
बाहुश्रुत्येन is not about a king.
-एन is 'by', not 'for'.
-एन is 'by', not 'in'.
questions.explain: प्रज्ञां बाहुश्रुत्येन बृंहयेत् = strengthen the intellect by wide learning.
questions.teaches: The instrumental (-एन) names the means by which something is done.

questions.q: Which pairing does the second line make?
optionExplain: This swaps them.
Right: प्रदीपभूतं शास्त्रम् and दर्शनं विपुला मतिः.
The line says the intellect is the sight, not a fire.
The line does not equate those.
questions.explain: The treatise is the lamp, and the wide intellect is the sight.

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the second line.
questions.explain: The line gives: like a lamp, the treatise, sight, wide intellect.

questions.q: An invented line reads नौकाभूतः गुरुः. By the pattern of प्रदीपभूतम्, what does it say?
options: The boat is like a teacher
The teacher is like a boat
The teacher has left the boat
optionExplain: -भूत does not make a maker.
The teacher is the one compared.
Right: -भूत after a noun, as in प्रदीपभूतम्, gives 'being like' it.
Nothing here means leaving.
questions.explain: प्रदीपभूतम् = like a lamp; नौकाभूतः = like a boat.
questions.teaches: noun + -भूत makes a comparison: 'being like' it.

questions.q: The verse says that a physician who treats with the two well applied does what?
optionExplain: The verse says he treats (चिकित्सन्); it does not say he avoids patients.
No fee is mentioned in the verse.
He is the one treating (चिकित्सन्), not one who hands over.
Right: चिकित्सन्नापराध्यति: न अपराध्यति, he does not err.
questions.explain: ताभ्यां सुयुक्ताभ्यां चिकित्सन् न अपराध्यति: treating with the two well applied, he does not err.
questions.rule: Well-applied pair + treating: he does not err.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the verse: the verb of line 1 and the three marks of the one who goes in line 2.
questions.rule: अपराध्यति = errs; आहूतः = called; सुवेषः = well dressed; सुनिमित्ततः = on good omens.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads: आहूतएव यो याति, सुवेषः सुनिमित्ततः.
questions.rule: He goes only when called, well dressed, on good omens.
questions.teaches: A relative clause (यः …) can open with its condition first (आहूतएव) and put its verb (याति) after it.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चिकित्सन्नापराध्यति?
optionExplain: Right: न + अ gives ना (अ + अ → आ), so न + अपराध्यति is written नापराध्यति.
ना is not the negative word here; the negative is न.
The participle in the verse is चिकित्सन्, ending in न्.
आपराध्यति is not a word; the verb is अपराध्यति.
questions.explain: The participle चिकित्सन् ends in न्; then comes the negative न, and its अ joins the अ of अपराध्यति to make ना.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say about the one who goes?
optionExplain: Right: आहूतएव.
Right: सुवेषः.
Right: सुनिमित्ततः.
Nothing is said of carrying anything.
The time of going is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The three marks are: called, well dressed, on good omens. Nothing is said of medicines or night.
questions.rule: Marks of the one who goes: called, well dressed, good omens.

questions.q: An invented line says आहूत एव शिष्यो गच्छति. What does it say?
options: The pupil goes though he is not called
The pupil goes only when called
The pupil calls everyone and goes
The pupil is called but never goes
optionExplain: एव means 'only'; it excludes going uncalled.
Right: एव after आहूतः limits the going to when he is called, as in the verse.
आहूतः is 'called', a passive sense, not 'calls'.
गच्छति says he goes.
questions.explain: आहूतः + एव → आहूत एव (the visarga is lost before एव); एव fixes the condition: only when called.
questions.rule: आहूत एव + verb = does it only when called.
questions.teaches: आहूतः (called) with एव (only) makes a condition: he acts only when called.

questions.q: After going to the patient, the physician of this verse sets his mind where?
options: On whatever is nearby in the house
optionExplain: No fee is mentioned.
The king is not in this verse.
Right: न निधत्ते मनः आतुरार्थात् अन्यत्र: he puts his mind nowhere other than the patient's concern.
The verse says nowhere else (अन्यत्र न).
questions.explain: आतुरार्थात् अन्यत्र न: nowhere other than on the patient's concern.
questions.rule: Mind only on the patient's concern.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words from each line: the going and the mind in line 1, the diseases and their examination in line 2.
questions.rule: गत्वा = having gone; मनः = mind; व्याधीन् = diseases; परीक्षते = examines.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: The word for 'mind' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: मनः is the neuter accusative of मनस्, mind: न निधत्ते मनः, he does not place his mind.
questions.teaches: मनः is the thing placed (object of निधत्ते); the verse says it is placed nowhere else than on the patient's concern.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of सम्यग्निदानादिविशेषतः?
optionExplain: सम्यः is not a word; the adverb is सम्यक्.
The last word is विशेषतः, by the particulars, not शेषतः.
यग्निदान is not a word.
Right: Final क् becomes ग् before the voiced न, and निदान + आदि joins as निदानादि.
questions.explain: सम्यक् (properly) + निदान-आदि (beginning with the cause) + विशेषतः (by the particulars).
questions.rule: Final क् → ग् before a voiced consonant: सम्यक् + निदान → सम्यग्निदान.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say the physician does after going?
options: He puts his mind nowhere but on the patient's concern
He examines them by the particulars beginning with the cause
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 2, परीक्षते सम्यक्.
Right: निदानादिविशेषतः.
Taking a gift is a separate rule, in a different unit.
Nothing of the kind is said.
questions.explain: The unit has two statements: the mind kept on the patient's concern, and the proper examination of the diseases by the cause and the rest.
questions.rule: After going: mind on the concern; proper examination of the diseases.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented line says भुक्त्वा शिष्यः पठति. What does it say?
options: The pupil studies, then he eats
The pupil will eat after studying
optionExplain: Right: भुक्त्वा is the 'having done' form, like गत्वा: the eating comes first.
The भुक्त्वा form puts eating first.
The form does not say both go on together.
That would reverse the order.
questions.explain: A word in -त्वा, like गत्वा and भुक्त्वा, names an earlier action by the same doer.
questions.rule: -त्वा form = having done, before the main verb.
questions.teaches: A -त्वा word (गत्वा, भुक्त्वा) means 'having done', an action before the main verb by the same doer.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: What does the physician not make known outside?
options: The medicines he uses for the patient
The fee he has agreed with the patient
The name of his teacher in the craft
optionExplain: No medicines are mentioned in line 1.
Right: गोपनीयां तद्वार्त्तां न प्रकाशयते बहिः: he does not make it known outside.
No fee is mentioned.
No teacher is mentioned.
questions.explain: The object is तद्वार्त्ताम्, his (the patient's) report, qualified by गोपनीयाम्, to be kept secret.
questions.rule: He does not reveal the patient's secret report.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: गोपनीयां च तद्वार्त्तां न प्रकाशयते बहिः.
questions.rule: To be kept secret + his report + does not make known + outside.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up line 1 apart from the particles.
questions.rule: गोपनीयाम् = to be kept secret; वार्त्ताम् = report; प्रकाशयते = makes known; बहिः = outside.
questions.teaches: A word in -अनीय (गोपनीय) is a gerundive: it means 'to be done', here 'to be kept (secret)'.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which word does गोपनीयाम् describe?
optionExplain: That is a verb; an adjective does not describe a verb.
बहिः is an indeclinable word, 'outside'; it has no case to agree with.
Right: Both are feminine accusative singular, so they agree: the report to be kept secret.
That is masculine, in line 2; गोपनीयाम् is feminine.
questions.explain: Agreement of gender, number and case: गोपनीयाम् and वार्त्ताम् are both feminine, accusative, singular.
questions.rule: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender, number and case.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say about the physician?
options: He does not make the secret report known outside
The report he keeps back is called गोपनीय
The report is the patient's own (तद्वार्त्ताम्, his report)
He tells the king the report
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: गोपनीयां … तद्वार्त्ताम्.
Right: तद् points to the patient; the report is his.
Nothing like this is said.
Nothing about writing is said.
questions.explain: Line 1 keeps the patient's secret report from being made known outside; तद्वार्त्ताम् is his report.
questions.rule: Secret report not made known outside; it is the patient's.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented phrase says श्रवणीया कथा. What does it mean?
options: A story that has been heard
optionExplain: Past sense would need a different ending (श्रुत).
The gerundive is passive in sense; the story is what is heard.
श्रवणीया is an adjective of कथा, not a person.
Right: श्रवणीय is a gerundive of √श्रु, 'to be heard', and कथा is feminine like it.
questions.explain: -अनीय gives 'to be …' (गोपनीय = to be kept; श्रवणीय = to be heard).
questions.teaches: A gerundive in -अनीय (गोपनीय, श्रवणीय) means 'to be done' and agrees with its noun.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Who, according to line 1, attains success (सिद्धि)?
options: The physician who knows how to treat
The physician who is wealthy and well known
optionExplain: Right: जानाति चोपचरितुं स वैद्यः सिद्धिमश्नुते: he who knows to treat attains success.
Wealth is not mentioned.
Fame is not mentioned.
Age is not mentioned.
questions.explain: जानाति उपचरितुम्: he knows how to treat; such a physician attains siddhi.
questions.rule: Knows how to treat → attains success.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of line 1 and the object of the new rule in line 2.
questions.rule: सिद्धिम् = success; अश्नुते = attains; जानाति = knows; आमिषम् = gift.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: जानाति चोपचरितुं स वैद्यः सिद्धिमश्नुते.
questions.rule: Knows + to treat + that physician + attains success.
questions.teaches: सः (that) picks up the earlier यः (who): the relative clause ends with 'that physician …'.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाददीतामिषं?
optionExplain: The negative is न; ना here is न + the first आ of आददीत.
Right: न + आ gives ना, and आददीत + आमिषम् joins as आददीतामिषम्: अ + आ → आ each time.
तामिषम् is not a word.
Neither नाद nor दीत is a word of this verse.
questions.explain: न (not) + आददीत (should take) + आमिषम् (gift).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ: न + आददीत → नाददीत.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say?
options: The physician who knows how to treat attains success
He should not take a gift from women
The word for gift in line 2 is आमिषम्
He should take gifts openly from women
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 2.
Right: नाददीतामिषम् = न + आददीत + आमिषम्.
The verse says न आददीत, he should not take.
The verse ties success to knowing how to treat.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives success to the one who knows how to treat; line 2 forbids taking a gift from women.
questions.rule: Success: knows to treat. Rule: no gift from women.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented line says नाचरेत् पापम्. What does it say?
options: One did not do evil in the past
One should do evil if asked
Evil does not come to one
optionExplain: The optative ending -एत् is 'should', not past.
The negative न is in the word.
Right: आचरेत् is an optative, 'should do'; न + आचरेत् gives नाचरेत्.
पापम् is the object of आचरेत्; evil is not the subject.
questions.explain: -एत् is the optative ('should'), as in नाददीत; न + आ → ना.
questions.teaches: The optative (-एत्, -ईत) means 'should'; with न it forbids, and न + आ- joins as ना-.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: In line 1, with women, what does the verse tell the physician to avoid?
optionExplain: Neither speech nor writing is named.
Treating women is not forbidden in the verse.
Neither is named.
Right: नारीभिः रहसि स्थानं परिहासं च वर्जयेत्: avoid staying in private with women and joking.
questions.explain: वर्जयेत् takes two objects: स्थानम् (staying) in private, and परिहासम् (joking), both with women.
questions.rule: Avoid private company and joking with women.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four content words of line 1.
questions.rule: नारीभिः = with women; रहसि = in private; स्थानम् = staying; परिहासम् = joking.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: नारीभिश्च रहसि स्थानं परिहासं च वर्जयेत्.
questions.rule: With women + in private + staying + joking + should avoid.
questions.teaches: The verb वर्जयेत् comes last and governs both objects, and, in this text, the accusatives of line 2 as well.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of नृपसद्वैद्यैर्द्विष्टं?
optionExplain: Right: सत् becomes सद् before the voiced व, and वैद्यैः becomes वैद्यैर् before the voiced द्वि.
द्वैद्यैः is not a word.
The ending is -ऐः (plural 'by'), not the singular वैद्यः.
The participle is द्विष्टम्, hated; विष्टम् would lose the द्.
questions.explain: नृप + सत् + वैद्यैः = by the king and good physicians; द्विष्टम् = hated.
questions.rule: Visarga → र् and त् → द् before voiced consonants.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these does the verse list as things or persons to avoid?
options: A patient hated by the king and good physicians
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 1.
Right: line 2 (the list begins; the verb is understood).
Age is not mentioned in this unit.
Speaking to the king is not mentioned.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives two things to avoid with women; line 2 begins the patients to avoid.
questions.rule: Avoid: private company, joking, and the patient hated by king and good physicians.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented phrase says शिष्यैः पठितं शास्त्रम्. What does it mean?
options: The pupils read by the treatise
The treatise read by the pupils
The treatise to be read by one pupil
The pupils who will read the treatise
optionExplain: The pupils are the doers (शिष्यैः), not the thing read.
Right: शिष्यैः is instrumental plural 'by the pupils', as in वैद्यैः द्विष्टम्, 'hated by the physicians'.
शिष्यैः is plural, and पठितम् is past, not 'to be'.
पठितम् is past, not future.
questions.explain: With a past participle, the instrumental names the doer: 'by whom'.
questions.teaches: A past participle with an instrumental (द्विष्टं वैद्यैः, पठितं शिष्यैः) means 'done by' the instrumental noun.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: The first word of this verse, चण्डम्, describes a person who is what?
optionExplain: Timid is भीरु, the third word of line 1.
Ungrateful is कृतघ्न, the fourth word.
Right: चण्ड means fierce.
Agitated is व्यग्र, in line 2.
questions.explain: The list opens with चण्डम्, fierce; timid and ungrateful come later in the line.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Arrange these items of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: चंडं शोकातुरं भीरुं कृतघ्नं वैद्यमानिनं.
questions.rule: Fierce, stricken with grief, timid, ungrateful, one who thinks himself a physician.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the nine descriptions.
questions.rule: भीरुम् = timid; कृतघ्नम् = ungrateful; व्यग्रम् = agitated; गतायुषम् = whose life has gone.
questions.teaches: All nine words are accusative singular and masculine, the same case and gender as one person.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of हीनोपकरणं?
optionExplain: That would be written हीन उपकरणम् (the visarga drops before उ).
हीनु is not a word; the first member is हीन.
पकरणम् is not a word.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so हीन + उपकरणम् is written हीनोपकरणम्: lacking equipment.
questions.explain: The first member हीन (lacking) joins उपकरण (equipment) by अ + उ → ओ.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: हीन + उपकरण → हीनोपकरण.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which of these are named in the list?
options: One who thinks himself a physician
optionExplain: Right: कृतघ्नम्.
Right: वैद्यमानिनम्.
Right: अविधेयम्.
Greed is not named.
Talkativeness is not named.
questions.explain: The nine items are fixed; greed and talkativeness are not among them.
questions.rule: Ungrateful, self-styled physician, disobedient: yes. Greedy, talkative: no.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented phrase says पण्डितमानिनं शिष्यम्. What does it describe?
options: A pupil who thinks himself learned
A pupil who respects the learned
A learned pupil of a physician
A pupil who is proud of his teacher
optionExplain: Right: -मानिन् after a word means 'thinking oneself that', as in वैद्यमानिनम्.
-मानिन् is about thinking oneself, not respecting others.
वैद्य is not in the phrase; and -मानिन् does not mean 'learned'.
The pride is in himself being learned, not in a teacher.
questions.explain: वैद्यमानिन् = thinking himself a physician; पण्डितमानिन् = thinking himself learned.
questions.rule: X-मानिन् = one who thinks himself X.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -मानिन् means 'one who thinks himself …': वैद्यमानी, पण्डितमानी.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Why, according to the verse, are such physicians to be avoided?
options: They are the forerunners of death
optionExplain: Poverty is not mentioned.
Right: मृत्योः अग्रेसराः हि ते: for they go ahead of death.
Distance is not mentioned.
Age is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The reason is the clause मृत्योरग्रेसरा हि ते: they are indeed the forerunners of death.
questions.rule: Reason: they are forerunners of death.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of both lines: the one who wants to live, and the ones who go ahead of death.
questions.rule: जिजीविषुः = desirous of living; व्याधितः = afflicted with disease; अग्रेसराः = forerunners; मृत्योः = of death.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads: क्रियाविक्रयिणो वैद्यान्मृत्योरग्रेसरा हि ते.
questions.rule: Sellers of treatment + physicians + of death + forerunners + indeed they.
questions.teaches: A short reason clause can close the verse: मृत्योः अग्रेसराः हि ते, 'for they are death's forerunners'.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which is the right split of जिजीविषुर्व्याधितोऽपि?
optionExplain: आधितः is not a word; the word is व्याधितः.
The nominative needs the visarga: व्याधितः; its loss would not give ओऽ.
Right: The visarga becomes र् before the voiced व्, and अः + अ gives ओऽ.
र्व्याधितः is not a word.
questions.explain: जिजीविषुः (desirous of living) + व्याधितः (sick) + अपि (even).
questions.rule: ः → र् before a voiced consonant; अः + अ → ोऽ.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: A sick man who wants to live meets a physician who sells treatment and lacks the earlier qualities. What does the verse say?
options: He should pay him in advance
He should ask the king to choose
optionExplain: The verse calls such physicians forerunners of death.
Paying is not mentioned.
The king is not in this verse.
Right: वैद्यान् … क्रियाविक्रयिणः: such physicians are to be avoided, even by a sick person who wants to live.
questions.explain: The verse bars both marks together: lacking the earlier qualities and selling treatment.
questions.rule: Avoid physicians lacking the qualities and selling treatment.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: An invented phrase says राज्ञः अग्रेसरो दूतः. What does it say?
options: The messenger goes ahead of the king
The king goes ahead of the messenger
The messenger is the king's enemy
The king is the messenger's servant
optionExplain: Right: अग्रेसर is 'going in front', and the genitive names whom he goes ahead of, as मृत्योः अग्रेसराः.
The genitive राज्ञः names the one who is led, not the leader.
Nothing says enemy; अग्रेसर is 'forerunner'.
Nothing says servant.
questions.explain: Genitive + अग्रेसर = forerunner of that person.
questions.rule: X's अग्रेसर = one who goes ahead of X.
questions.teaches: Genitive + अग्रेसर means 'forerunner of': मृत्योरग्रेसराः, राज्ञोऽग्रेसरः.
questions.section: रोगी के प्रति वैद्य का आचरण

questions.q: Which are the four quarters (pāda) of treatment in this verse?
optionExplain: Disease and season are not among the four.
Right: भिषक् द्रव्याणि उपस्थाता रोगी: these are the four.
These are not the four quarters.
Diet, rest and prayer are not named.
questions.explain: The verse lists exactly four and calls them पादचतुष्टयम्, the four quarters of treatment.
questions.rule: Four quarters: physician, medicines, attendant, patient.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four quarters, in the order of line 1.
questions.rule: भिषक् = physician; द्रव्याणि = medicines; उपस्थाता = attendant; रोगी = patient.

questions.q: Arrange the four quarters in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: भिषक् द्रव्याण्युपस्थाता रोगी.
questions.teaches: The order of the quarters (physician, medicines, attendant, patient) is also the order of their qualities in the next two units.

questions.q: Which is the right split of द्रव्याण्युपस्थाता?
optionExplain: अ + उ would give ओ, द्रव्याणोपस्थाता.
The plural of द्रव्य is द्रव्याणि; a visarga ending is not formed.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: द्रव्याणि + उपस्थाता → द्रव्याण्युपस्थाता.
उ + उ would give ऊ, द्रव्याणूपस्थाता.
questions.explain: द्रव्याणि is the neuter nominative plural 'medicines'; its इ becomes य् before उ.

questions.q: A clinic has a skilled physician, medicines and a patient, but nobody to attend. Which quarter is missing?
optionExplain: The clinic has medicines.
The clinic has a physician.
The clinic has a patient.
Right: उपस्थाता is the third quarter; the other three are present.
questions.explain: Of the four named quarters, only the attendant is absent.
questions.rule: The four quarters: physician, medicines, attendant, patient.

questions.q: An invented line says प्रत्येकं तत्त्रिगुणम्, like प्रत्येकं तच्चतुर्गुणम्. What does it say?
options: Each of them has three qualities
All of them together have one quality
Each of them has four qualities
Three of them have no quality
optionExplain: Right: प्रत्येकम् is 'each one'; त्रिगुण is 'having three qualities', as चतुर्गुण is 'four'.
प्रत्येकम् means each, not all together.
त्रि is three; four is चतुर्.
गुण is quality; nothing says none.
questions.explain: A number + गुण names how many qualities something has; प्रत्येकम् spreads it over each item.
questions.rule: प्रत्येकम् + n-गुणम् = each has n qualities.
questions.teaches: प्रत्येकम् = each one; number + गुण (त्रिगुणम्, चतुर्गुणम्) = having that many qualities.

questions.q: Which of these is a quality of the medicine in this verse?
options: One who has seen the work done
optionExplain: Skilled is the physician's quality in line 1.
Right: योग्यमौषधम्: the medicine is suitable.
Pure is the physician's quality in line 1.
That is the physician's quality (दृष्टकर्मा).
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the medicine four qualities; योग्य is the last of them.
questions.rule: Medicine: many preparations, many qualities, well endowed, suitable.

questions.q: Arrange the four qualities of the physician in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: दक्षस्तीर्थात्तशास्त्रार्थो दृष्टकर्मा शुचिर्भिषक्.
questions.rule: Skilled, taken the treatises' meaning from a teacher, has seen the work, pure.

questions.q: Match each quality of the medicine to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four qualities of the medicine, line 2.
questions.rule: बहुकल्पम् = of many preparations; बहुगुणम् = of many qualities; सम्पन्नम् = well endowed; योग्यम् = suitable.
questions.teaches: बहु- + a noun makes a description 'having many …' (बहुकल्प, बहुगुण).

questions.q: Which is the right split of शुचिर्भिषक्?
optionExplain: इषक् is not a word; the word is भिषक्.
र्भिषक् is not a word.
Right: The visarga becomes र् before the voiced भ्.
अभिषक् is not a word.
questions.explain: शुचिः (pure) + भिषक् (physician).

questions.q: A physician is skilled, pure and taught the treatises' meaning by a teacher, but has not seen the work done. Which quality is missing?
optionExplain: He is skilled.
He is pure.
He has this: he learned the meaning from a teacher.
Right: He lacks the quality of one who has seen the work done.
questions.explain: The four qualities are separate; the missing one is दृष्टकर्मा.
questions.rule: Four qualities of the physician: skilled, learned from a teacher, has seen work, pure.

questions.q: An invented phrase says बहुफलं वृक्षम्. What does it describe?
options: A fruit of a big tree
optionExplain: Right: बहु- joined to a noun makes a description 'having many …', as in बहुगुणम्; it agrees with the noun described.
बहु- is 'many', not 'no'.
वृक्षम् is singular; one tree.
फल is inside the description, not a separate noun with वृक्ष as owner.
questions.explain: बहुगुणम् is 'having many qualities'; बहुफलम् is 'having many fruits'.
questions.teaches: बहु- before a noun makes a description 'having many …': बहुकल्पम्, बहुगुणम्, बहुफलम्.

questions.q: In this verse, who is described as devoted (अनुरक्त)?
options: The physician who treats the patient
optionExplain: The physician's qualities were given in the previous unit.
Right: अनुरक्तः … परिचारकः: the attendant is devoted.
The medicine's qualities were given in the previous unit.
The patient's qualities are in line 2: wealthy, obedient and so on.
questions.explain: Line 1 is about the attendant (परिचारकः): devoted, pure, skilled, intelligent.

questions.q: Arrange the four qualities of the attendant in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: अनुरक्तः शुचिर्दक्षो बुद्धिमान्परिचारकः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three qualities of the patient in line 2, and one word from line 1 to keep apart.
questions.rule: आढ्यः = wealthy; भिषग्वश्यः = obedient to the physician; सत्त्ववान् = having mental strength. अनुरक्तः (devoted) belongs to line 1, the attendant.
questions.teaches: First member + वश्य (भिषग्वश्य) means 'under the control of' that first member.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भिषग्वश्यः?
optionExplain: भिषः is not a word.
अश्यः is not a word.
Right: Final क् becomes ग् before the voiced व.
ग्वश्यः is not a word.
questions.explain: भिषक् (physician) + वश्यः (under control): obedient to the physician.
questions.rule: क् → ग् before a voiced consonant.

questions.q: Which qualities does the verse give the patient?
optionExplain: Right: आढ्यः.
Right: भिषग्वश्यः.
Right: सत्त्ववान्.
Devoted is the attendant's quality in line 1.
Intelligent is the attendant's quality in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the patient his qualities; devoted and intelligent are the attendant's.
questions.rule: Patient: wealthy, obedient, ज्ञापक (reading uncertain), mentally strong.

questions.q: An invented phrase says गुरुवश्यः शिष्यः. What does it describe?
options: A teacher obedient to the pupil
A pupil who rules over the teacher
A pupil obedient to the teacher
optionExplain: The first member names who controls: गुरु.
That would be the reverse.
Nothing here says 'without'.
Right: वश्य gives 'under the control of' the first member, as भिषग्वश्यः is under the physician.
questions.explain: Same pattern as भिषग्वश्यः: the first member is the one who has control.
questions.rule: X-वश्य = under the control of X.
questions.teaches: X-वश्य = under X's control, obedient to X (भिषग्वश्यः, गुरुवश्यः).

questions.q: When the physician lacks qualities, what happens to the other quarters?
options: They are replaced by new ones
optionExplain: Right: गुणवन्तोऽप्यनर्थकाः: even though they have qualities, they are useless.
The verse says the opposite: they become useless.
Nothing like this is said.
Replacement is not mentioned.
questions.explain: यद्वैद्ये विगुणे पादा गुणवन्तोऽपि अनर्थकाः: when the physician lacks qualities, the quarters are useless though they have qualities.
questions.rule: Physician without qualities: other quarters useless.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: यद्वैद्ये विगुणे पादा गुणवंतोऽप्यनर्थकाः.
questions.rule: Since in the physician + lacking qualities + the quarters + even qualified + useless.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of line 1 and the verb of line 2.
questions.rule: विगुणे = lacking qualities; गुणवन्तः = having qualities; अनर्थकाः = useless; यापयेत् = may keep going.
questions.teaches: The prefixes वि- and अन- mark lack: विगुण = lacking qualities, अनर्थक = without use.

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुणवंतोऽप्यनर्थकाः?
optionExplain: गुणवान् is the singular; the quarters are plural, गुणवन्तः.
Right: अः + अ gives ोऽ (गुणवन्तोऽपि); अपि + अनर्थकाः → अप्यनर्थकाः (इ before a different vowel becomes य्).
ओपि is not a word.
आपि is not a word; the word is अपि.
questions.explain: गुणवन्तः (having qualities, plural) + अपि (even) + अनर्थकाः (useless).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ोऽ; इ + other vowel → य्.

questions.q: The medicine, attendant and patient are all qualified, but the physician lacks qualities. What does the verse say?
options: The patient alone decides the result
optionExplain: That is the opposite of the verse.
The patient is one of the quarters named useless here.
Right: वैद्ये विगुणे … पादा अनर्थकाः: the other quarters are useless.
The medicine too is one of the quarters, useless without the physician.
questions.explain: The verse says a qualified rest cannot rescue a physician without qualities.
questions.rule: Physician unqualified → qualified other quarters useless.

questions.q: An invented line says सारथौ विगुणे रथोऽनर्थकः. What does it say?
options: The charioteer is useless because the chariot lacks qualities
Though the chariot lacks qualities, the driver is useful
The chariot lacks qualities and so the driver is a fool
When the charioteer lacks qualities, the chariot is useless
optionExplain: The locative phrase is the charioteer lacking qualities.
The locative names the charioteer, not the chariot.
Nothing about a fool is said.
Right: Noun and adjective both in the locative (सारथौ विगुणे) set the condition, as वैद्ये विगुणे.
questions.explain: A noun + adjective in the locative states the condition, 'when X is so': वैद्ये विगुणे.
questions.rule: Locative noun + adjective = when X is so.
questions.teaches: A noun and its adjective both in the locative (वैद्ये विगुणे, सारथौ विगुणे) mean 'when X is so'.

questions.q: In line 1, whom do they know as the chief cause of treatment?
optionExplain: Right: तमेव: him alone, the physician of the previous unit, is the chief cause.
The medicine is only one of the quarters.
The patient is only one of the quarters.
The attendant is only one of the quarters.
questions.explain: Because the physician's lack of qualities makes the other quarters useless, they call him the chief cause.
questions.rule: The physician alone is the chief cause.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads: साध्यः असाध्यः इति व्याधिः द्विधा, तौ तु पुनः द्विधा.
questions.rule: Curable, incurable: thus disease is twofold; those two again twofold.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words of line 1 and two of line 2.
questions.rule: प्रधानम् = chief; कारणम् = cause; साध्यः = curable; असाध्यः = incurable.
questions.teaches: अ- before a word reverses it: साध्य (curable), असाध्य (incurable).

questions.q: Which is the right split of साध्योऽसाध्य इति?
optionExplain: ओसाध्य is not a word.
Right: अः + अ gives ोऽ, and असाध्यः + इति loses its visarga before इ.
The second word has the negative अ-: असाध्यः, incurable.
The disease (व्याधिः) is masculine; असाध्यम् is neuter.
questions.explain: साध्यः (curable) + असाध्यः (incurable) + इति (thus).

questions.q: A learner says: the verse divides disease into curable and incurable, and each is again divided. Is that right?
options: No: it divides disease into curable only, with no second division
No: it divides disease into three
Yes: two, then each of the two again twofold
No: it names the four classes here
optionExplain: Incurable is named too.
The verse says twofold, then twofold again.
Right: व्याधिर्द्विधा, तौ तु पुनर्द्विधा says exactly that.
The four names come in the next unit.
questions.explain: The unit gives the first division and the second division but not the names of the final classes.

questions.q: An invented line says तमेव गुरुं श्रेष्ठं विदुः. What does it say?
options: They know the best teacher but not him
He alone knows the best teacher
They do not know that teacher as the best one
They know that teacher alone as the best
optionExplain: तमेव says him alone, not a different one.
The doer of विदुः is 'they', and the accusatives are what they know.
There is no negative in the line.
Right: विदुः takes two accusatives: 'know X as Y', as तमेव प्रधानं कारणं विदुः.
questions.explain: विदुः + two accusatives = 'they know X as Y'; एव = alone.
questions.rule: विदुः X Y = they know X as Y.
questions.teaches: With विदुः (they know) two accusatives give 'know X as Y'; एव limits it to X alone.

questions.q: Which set names the four classes of disease in this verse?
options: Easily curable, curable with difficulty, to be sustained, no remedy
Easily curable, curable with difficulty, incurable, and quickly fatal
Mild, severe, to be sustained, and one that admits no remedy
Curable, incurable, recent in onset, old in standing
optionExplain: Right: सुसाध्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यः याप्यः अनुपक्रमः: these four.
Only the first two are names in the verse; incurable and fatal are not among the four.
Mild and severe are not named.
Recent and old are not named.
questions.explain: The verse names four: सुसाध्य, कृच्छ्रसाध्य, याप्य, अनुपक्रम.
questions.rule: Four classes: सुसाध्य, कृच्छ्रसाध्य, याप्य, अनुपक्रम.

questions.q: Arrange the four classes in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: सुसाध्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यश्च याप्यो यश्चानुपक्रमः.
questions.rule: Easily curable, curable with difficulty, to be sustained, without remedy.

questions.q: Match each class to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four classes of line 1.
questions.rule: सुसाध्यः = easily curable; कृच्छ्रसाध्यः = curable with difficulty; याप्यः = to be sustained (palliable); अनुपक्रमः = admitting no remedy.
questions.teaches: सु- means 'easily', कृच्छ्र- 'with difficulty': they qualify साध्य (to be accomplished, curable).

questions.q: Which is the right split of यश्चानुपक्रमः?
optionExplain: यत् would not give श्; the word is यः (which).
Right: The visarga becomes श् before च, and च + अ gives चा, since अ + अ → आ.
नुपक्रमः is not a word.
चानुपक्रमः is not a word; and the particle is च.
questions.explain: यः (which) + च (and) + अनुपक्रमः (without remedy).

questions.q: A physician says a disease can only be sustained. Which class name of the verse says this?
optionExplain: That is 'easily curable'.
That is 'curable with difficulty'.
Right: याप्य means to be sustained (palliated).
That is 'admits no remedy'.
questions.explain: याप्यः is the third class, 'to be sustained'.

questions.q: Invented path names: सुगम्यः and कृच्छ्रगम्यः, like सुसाध्यः and कृच्छ्रसाध्यः. What do they mean?
options: Hard to go along with; easy to go along with
Already gone along; not yet gone along
Easy to leave behind; hard to leave behind
Easy to go along; to be gone along with difficulty
optionExplain: The two prefixes are swapped.
Nothing marks past or negative.
गम्य is 'to be gone along', not leaving.
Right: सु- is 'easily' and कृच्छ्र- 'with difficulty', before गम्य, 'to be gone'.
questions.explain: The pattern सु-/कृच्छ्र- + a word 'to be done' gives 'easy to' and 'hard to'.
questions.teaches: सु- (easily) and कृच्छ्र- (with difficulty) before a 'to be done' word grade how hard it is.

questions.q: This verse lists features of an easily curable disease. Which feature would you expect it to give?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says अनुपद्रवः: without complications.
The verse says the opposite: अमर्मगः, not reaching the vital spots.
The verse says the cause is slight (अल्प).
No such signs are listed in this verse.
questions.explain: An easily curable disease is described with slight causes and signs and no complications.
questions.rule: Easily curable: not reaching vital spots, slight cause and signs, no complications.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: when the quarters are well endowed
questions.explain: These four words carry four of the features in the verse.
questions.rule: अमर्मगः = not reaching vital spots; अनुपद्रवः = without complications; अल्प = slight; पादसंपदि = when the quarters are well endowed.

questions.q: How are देश and ऋतु joined in देशर्तु-?
optionExplain: That is the result for अ + अ, not for अ + ऋ.
Right: The final अ of देश with the ऋ of ऋतु becomes अर्, so देश + ऋतु is written देशर्तु.
ए is the result for अ + इ.
ओ is the result for अ + उ.
questions.explain: A short or long अ followed by ऋ becomes अर्: देश + ऋतु = देशर्तु.
questions.teaches: Before the vowel ऋ, a final अ joins it as अर् (देश + ऋतु = देशर्तु).

questions.q: Which is the right split of अमर्मगोऽल्प-?
optionExplain: ल्प is not a word; the ऽ stands for a dropped अ.
Two अ would join as आ (अमर्मगाल्प), not give ओऽ.
Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
A visarga after आ would not give ओ.
questions.explain: अमर्मगः (not reaching the vital spots) and अल्प (slight) are two words.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse give among the features?
optionExplain: Right: अमर्मगः.
Right: अनुपद्रवः.
Right: पादसंपदि.
The verse says the cause is slight.
The verse says पादसंपदि: the quarters are well endowed.
questions.explain: The verse gives no complications, not reaching the vital spots and well-endowed quarters; its causes are slight and the other factors unlike the disease.
questions.rule: Features: अमर्मग, अल्प-हेतु-लक्षण, अनुपद्रव, अतुल्य दूष्य-देश-ऋतु-प्रकृति, पादसंपद्.

questions.q: An invented line calls a disease अनल्पहेतुः, on the pattern of अनुपद्रवः. What does it say of the cause?
optionExplain: That would be अल्प, without the negative prefix.
The word negates 'slight'; it does not speak of knowing.
The word does not speak of effects.
Right: The negative prefix takes अन् before a vowel: अन् + अल्प, 'not slight'.
questions.explain: अनल्प = अन् + अल्प: the negative prefix before a vowel is अन्, as in अन् + उपद्रव = अनुपद्रव.
questions.rule: Negative prefix: अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अन् before a vowel (अनुपद्रव, अनल्प) and अ before a consonant (अमर्मग).

questions.q: In how much time does the verse say the easily curable disease is cured?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says कालेनाल्पेन साध्यते: it is cured in a short time.
That is said of another grade in the next verse.
The verse says it is cured.
No season is named for this.
questions.explain: The last words of the verse, कालेनाल्पेन साध्यते, give a short time.
questions.rule: Easily curable: cured in a short time.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: with a single doṣa and path
questions.explain: These four words describe the disease and its cure.
questions.rule: साध्यते = is cured; एकदोषमार्गः = with a single doṣa and path; सुखोपायः = having easy means; सुखसाध्यः = easy to cure.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'new' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नवः is 'new', one of the features of the easily curable disease.
questions.teaches: नव, 'new', describes the disease as recent: नवः सुखः means 'new and easy'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ग्रहेष्वनुगुणेषु?
optionExplain: नुगुणेषु is not a word.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: ग्रहेषु + अनुगुणेषु → ग्रहेष्वनुगुणेषु.
ग्रहेषो is not a form on the card: the word is the locative plural ग्रहेषु, 'in the planets'.
Again नुगुणेषु is not a word; अनुगुण (favourable) begins with अ.
questions.explain: Both words are locative plural: 'in the planets' and 'favourable', agreeing as 'with the planets favourable'.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The first line gives the planets, then the single doṣa and path, then new, then easy.
questions.rule: Line 1: favourable planets · single doṣa and path · new · easy.

questions.q: An invented word दुःखसाध्यः is built like सुखसाध्यः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: That is सुखसाध्यः.
साध्य is 'to be cured', not 'cured by'.
Right: दुःख- is the opposite of सुख-: 'hard' where सुख- is 'easy'.
Nothing in the word says 'new'.
questions.explain: सुख- gives 'easy' and the opposite दुःख- gives 'hard': सुखसाध्य is easy to cure, दुःखसाध्य hard to cure.
questions.rule: सुख-साध्य = easy to cure; दुःख-साध्य = hard to cure.
questions.teaches: A first member सुख- makes a word 'easy to ...' (सुखसाध्य, सुखोपाय); its opposite दुःख- makes it 'hard to ...'.

questions.q: Compared with the easily curable disease, how much time does this verse give for the kṛcchra disease?
optionExplain: That belongs to the easily curable disease.
The verse gives no such claim.
No length of days is given.
Right: The verse says चिरेण, after a long time.
questions.explain: चिरेण means after a long time; the easily curable disease is cured in a short time.
questions.rule: Kṛcchra: difficult and great means, long time.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the means and the time.
questions.rule: कृच्छ्रैः = difficult; महद्भिः = great; चिरेण = after a long time; शस्त्रादि = surgery and the like.

questions.q: What do the endings of कृच्छ्रैः and उपायैः (-ऐः) show?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural of अ-ending words.
The nominative singular of these words ends in -ः after अ, not -ऐः.
The locative plural ends in -एषु.
The genitive plural ends in -आनाम्.
questions.explain: कृच्छ्रैः उपायैः means 'by difficult means'; the two words agree in case and number.
questions.rule: -ऐः on an अ-ending word = instrumental plural, 'by'.
questions.teaches: The ending -ऐः on a masculine अ-ending word is instrumental plural: 'by ...s' (उपायैः = by means).

questions.q: Which is the right split of महद्भिश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: महद्भिः + च → महद्भिश्च.
महद्भिश is not a word.
भिश्च is not a word; the form is instrumental plural.
questions.explain: महद्भिः is instrumental plural of महत् ('great') and च means 'and'.

questions.q: Reading line 2 with the kṛcchra disease, as the card does, which of these does the verse say?
options: It is cured by difficult and great means
Its means are surgery and the like
It is cured in a short time
It is cured by easy means
optionExplain: Right: कृच्छ्रैरुपायैः ... महद्भिः.
Right: चिरेण.
Right: शस्त्रादिसाधनः.
That is said of the easily curable disease.
The means here are difficult and great.
questions.explain: The verse gives difficult and great means, a long time, and surgery and the like.
questions.rule: Kṛcchra: difficult and great means, long time, surgery and the like.

questions.q: An invented phrase सुखैरुपायैः is built like कृच्छ्रैरुपायैः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: That would be a genitive plural (-आनाम्).
That would be a locative plural (-एषु).
Right: सुखैः is instrumental plural of सुख, 'easy', agreeing with उपायैः.
That would be singular, not -ऐः.
questions.explain: Same ending, same meaning: 'by easy means' (सुखैः + उपायैः, visarga before a vowel becomes र्).
questions.teaches: Two words with the same ending -ऐः agree: सुखैः उपायैः = by easy means, as कृच्छ्रैः उपायैः = by difficult means.

questions.q: By what does the verse say the yāpya disease is kept going?
optionExplain: The verse names wholesome measures (पथ्यैः), not surgery.
Fate is not named in this verse; it names wholesome measures.
A slight cause is what makes it spread in the contrary case.
Right: The verse says पथ्यैः: by wholesome (things).
questions.explain: आयुषः शेषत्वात् पथ्यैः याप्यः: because life remains, it is kept going by wholesome measures.
questions.rule: Yāpya: kept going by wholesome measures.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two halves of the verse.
questions.rule: शेषत्वात् = because of remaining; पथ्यैः = by wholesome things; सुखम् = comfort; प्रतन्यते = is spread out.

questions.q: In शेषत्वात्, what does -त्व make out of the base word शेष (what is left)?
options: A noun of state: being what is left
optionExplain: Right: -त्व makes an abstract noun, and the ending -आत् then gives 'because of'.
-त्व does not make verbs.
A person-word would not end in -त्व.
-त्व has nothing to do with number.
questions.explain: शेषत्वात् = 'because of the state of being a remainder', i.e. because life remains.
questions.teaches: -त्व added to a word makes a noun of state (शेष → शेषत्व), and -आत् on it means 'because of'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पथ्यैर्याप्यः?
optionExplain: That would break याप्य, which begins with य.
Right: A visarga before a voiced consonant such as य becomes र्.
ऐर्याप्यः is not a word.
पथ्यैरि is not a word.
questions.explain: पथ्यैः (by wholesome things) and याप्यः (the yāpya disease) are the two words.

questions.q: What does the verse say in its second line of the yāpya disease?
options: It spreads on account of a slight cause
It is cured in a short time
optionExplain: Right: दत्त्वा सुखम् अल्पम्.
Right: अल्पेन हेतुना प्रतन्यते.
The verse says slight (अल्पम्).
That is said of the easily curable disease.
Surgery is the means of the kṛcchra disease in the previous verse.
questions.explain: The second line gives slight comfort, then spreading on account of a slight cause.
questions.rule: Line 2: slight comfort, then spreading by a slight cause.

questions.q: By the pattern of पथ्यैः (by wholesome things), what would an invented अपथ्यैः mean?
optionExplain: That is पथ्यैः.
A genitive plural would end in -आनाम्.
Right: The negative prefix अ- reverses पथ्य; -ऐः is the instrumental plural.
A locative plural would end in -एषु.
questions.explain: अ + पथ्य = unwholesome; with -ऐः it is 'by unwholesome things'.
questions.rule: अ- + noun = not that noun; -ऐः = by.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix अ- reverses a word (पथ्य → अपथ्य), and -ऐः keeps the instrumental plural 'by ...s'.

questions.q: In the verse's comparison, the patient is held up like one falling. By what?
optionExplain: The verse names the person's fixed lifespan, but not as what holds him up.
Fate is not named in this verse.
Past action is the source of the disease, not the support.
Right: The verse says विष्कम्भैः धार्यते हितैः: held up by wholesome things, as by props.
questions.explain: The comparison is with a falling person or thing held by props; the props are the wholesome things.
questions.rule: Patient held up by wholesome things, like a falling one by props.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the comparison.
questions.rule: रोगः = disease; आतुरः = patient; हितैः = by wholesome things; विष्कम्भैः = by props.

questions.q: In नाशेषताम्, शेष means 'remainder'. What does अशेषता name?
options: The state of having no remainder
The state of having a remainder
optionExplain: Right: अ- negates शेष and -ता makes a noun of state.
The prefix अ- negates; it does not keep the remainder.
-ता makes a noun of state, not a person.
The word has nothing to do with action.
questions.explain: अशेषता = अ + शेष + ता, the state of no remainder, i.e. complete removal; the disease does not reach it.
questions.rule: अ + शेष + ता = state of no remainder.
questions.teaches: Noun of state = word + -ता; with अ- it names the lack: अशेषता, no remainder.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रपतन्निव?
optionExplain: निव is not a word.
Right: An ending -न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel: प्रपतन् + इव → प्रपतन्निव.
The participle ends in -न्, not -न.
न्निव is not a word.
questions.explain: प्रपतन् is a present participle, 'falling', and इव means 'as if'.
questions.rule: -न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say?
options: The disease is born of past action
The person has a fixed lifespan
The disease does not reach the state of no remainder
The disease is wholly removed by wholesome things
The person has no fixed lifespan
optionExplain: Right: कर्मजः.
Right: नियतायुषः.
Right: याति नाशेषताम्.
The verse says it does not reach no-remainder.
The verse says नियतायुः, fixed.
questions.explain: The disease is born of past action, in one of fixed life, and does not reach the state of no remainder.
questions.rule: Karmaja disease, fixed life, never a full removal.

questions.q: An invented sentence says गृहं प्रपतदिव स्तम्भैर्धार्यते. What does it say?
options: The house, once fallen, is rebuilt by pillars
The pillars are falling as if held by the house
The house, as if falling, is held up by pillars
optionExplain: Nothing says it has fallen or is rebuilt.
The instrumental स्तम्भैः marks the pillars as the holders.
Right: प्रपतत् इव is 'as if falling', and स्तम्भैः धार्यते is 'is held up by pillars'.
स्तम्भैः धार्यते says it is held by them.
questions.explain: The same comparison as the verse: something falling, held up by props or pillars.
questions.rule: X प्रपतन् इव Y-भिः धार्यते = X, as if falling, is held up by Y.
questions.teaches: A present participle with इव gives 'as if falling'; the instrumental names what holds it up.

questions.q: How does the verse say the incurable disease is to be treated?
optionExplain: The verse says it goes beyond all treatments, so none is tried first.
The verse says it goes beyond all treatments.
The verse says all treatments are passed over.
Right: The verse says प्रत्याख्येयः and उपेक्ष्यः: to be refused, to be disregarded.
questions.explain: The incurable disease passes beyond all treatments, so it is to be refused and disregarded.
questions.rule: Incurable: beyond all treatments, to be refused, to be disregarded.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four terms carry the verse's teaching.
questions.rule: असाध्यः = incurable; प्रत्याख्येयः = to be refused; उपेक्ष्यः = to be disregarded; क्रियाः सर्वाः = all treatments.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does a word like प्रत्याख्येयः express?
options: What ought to be done to it: 'to be refused'
The one who does it: 'the refuser'
optionExplain: Right: It is a gerundive: it says what should be done to the thing.
That would be a past participle.
That would be an agent noun.
That would be a present participle.
questions.explain: The gerundives प्रत्याख्येयः and उपेक्ष्यः tell what is to be done to the incurable disease.
questions.teaches: A gerundive (प्रत्याख्येय, उपेक्ष्य) says what is to be done to the thing: 'to be refused', 'to be disregarded'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of परोऽसाध्यः?
optionExplain: परो is not the word on the card: the word is परः, and ओऽ comes from अः + अ.
