Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
Two अ would join as आ (परासाध्यः).
परा + असाध्यः would give परासाध्यः, not परोऽसाध्यः.
questions.explain: परः (the other) and असाध्यः (incurable) are two words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The first line names the incurable one, the treatments, 'to be refused' and 'goes beyond'.
questions.rule: Line 1: the other, incurable · all treatments · to be refused · goes beyond.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: On the pattern of तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः, an invented line joins तस्मात् + आतुरः. How is it written?
optionExplain: त् stays त only before a hard consonant, not before a vowel.
The two आ do not stay apart in this way.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel.
न् would come only before a nasal.
questions.explain: Before a vowel the final त् of तस्मात् becomes द्, as in तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: तस्मात् + उपेक्ष्यः = तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः, तस्मात् + आतुरः = तस्मादातुरः.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does the verse say should be done before treatment is begun?
options: Ask the family for a decision
Give up the case at once
optionExplain: The verse puts the examination first (पुरा).
No such step is in the verse.
Giving up is not what the second line says.
Right: The verse says व्याधिं पुरा परीक्ष्य ... ततः क्रियाम्: examine, then begin treatment.
questions.explain: आरभेत ततः क्रियाम्: one begins treatment only then, after the examination.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each member of the first-line compounds to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the features listed in the first line.
questions.rule: भ्रमः = giddiness; मोहः = delusion; अरतिः = unease; रिष्टम् = fatal sign.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: परीक्ष्य comes from परि + ईक्ष्. Why does the 'having examined' form end in -य, not -त्वा?
options: A verb with a prefix takes -य
A verb with a prefix takes -त्वा
optionExplain: Right: The 'having done' form takes -त्वा on a plain verb and -य on a verb with a prefix.
That is the rule for plain verbs, not those with a prefix.
-य marks 'having done', not the future.
-य here marks 'having done'; the verb is active.
questions.explain: परि + ईक्ष् has a prefix (परि), so 'having examined' is परीक्ष्य.
questions.teaches: The 'having done' form is -त्वा after a plain verb and -य after a verb with a prefix (परि + ईक्ष् → परीक्ष्य).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of परीक्ष्यैवम्?
optionExplain: ऐवम् is not a word.
Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ: परीक्ष्य + एवम् → परीक्ष्यैवम्.
वम् is not a word.
परीक्ष्ये is not a form on the card (the word is परीक्ष्य), and ए + ए would not join as ऐ.
questions.explain: परीक्ष्य (having examined) and एवम् (thus) are the two words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: the disease, first, having examined thus, one should begin, then treatment.
questions.rule: Line 2: disease · first · having examined thus · should begin · then treatment.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says रोगं निरीक्ष्य चिकित्सेत्. What does निरीक्ष्य express?
options: While he is looking at it
optionExplain: That would be a present participle.
That would be a gerundive.
Right: निरीक्ष्य is the 'having done' form of a prefixed verb.
That would be a past participle or agent noun.
questions.explain: As in परीक्ष्य ... आरभेत, the action in -य comes first and the main verb follows.
questions.rule: -य form = 'having done', done before the main verb.
questions.teaches: A -य form names an earlier action: रोगं निरीक्ष्य चिकित्सेत्, 'having looked at the disease, one should treat'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What three losses does the verse say the physician would incur otherwise?
optionExplain: These are not named in the verse.
The verse names his own interest, knowledge and fame.
None of these is named.
Right: The verse says स्वार्थविद्यायशोहानिम्: loss of own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.explain: The compound स्वार्थविद्यायशोहानिम् means loss of one's own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.rule: Loss of own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each member of the verse's first compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the compound of the first line.
questions.rule: स्वार्थः = own interest; विद्या = knowledge; यशः = fame; हानिः = loss.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: In अबलिनः, what does the prefix अ- do to बलिन् (a strong one)?
optionExplain: Right: अ- is the negative prefix, so अबलिन् is 'one who is not strong'.
अ- does not make a word stronger.
अ- here is not a tense mark.
अ- carries no number.
questions.explain: संयोगः अबलिनः means 'the combination in a weak person'.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates the word it stands before: बलिन् strong → अबलिन् weak.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of संयोगोऽबलिनः?
optionExplain: That would be 'of the strong', without the dropped अ.
Right: The ऽ marks a dropped अ, so the second word is अबलिनः, 'of the weak'.
Two अ would join as आ; ओऽ comes from a visarga.
A final आ would not give ओऽ.
questions.explain: संयोगः (combination) and अबलिनः (in a weak person).
questions.rule: -अः + अ → ओऽ; the ऽ is the dropped अ.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say?
options: Otherwise the physician would incur loss
The combination of two curable diseases, in a weak person, goes to incurability
Two curable diseases always stay curable
The loss is only possible, not sure
optionExplain: Right: अन्यथा ... हानिम् आप्नुयात्.
Right.
Right: यशोहानिम्.
The verse says even two curable ones can go to incurability.
The verse says ध्रुवम्, surely.
questions.explain: The verse says the loss is sure and names fame; two curable diseases in a weak person can go to incurability.
questions.rule: Sure loss; two curable diseases in a weak person → incurable.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of साध्ययोः, 'of two curable ones', what does an invented रोगयोः संयोगः mean?
optionExplain: -योः is not singular.
-योः is not plural.
Right: -योः is the dual: 'of two'.
रोगयोः names two diseases, not two combinations.
questions.explain: साध्ययोः = of two curable ones; likewise रोगयोः = of two diseases.
questions.teaches: The ending -योः on an अ-ending word is dual (genitive): साध्ययोः 'of two curable ones', रोगयोः 'of two diseases'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse says one meeting is to be known as incurable only. Which meeting?
options: Of a disease and a season
Of a curable disease and a physician
Of a curable and an incurable disease
optionExplain: The verse names the meeting of a curable and an incurable one, not of two curable ones.
No such meeting is named.
No such meeting is named.
Right: The verse says साध्यासाध्यसमागमम्: the meeting of curable and incurable.
questions.explain: The meeting of a curable and an incurable disease is to be known as incurable.
questions.rule: Curable + incurable meeting → know it as incurable.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in the second line.
questions.rule: साध्यः = the curable one; असाध्यः = the incurable one; याति = goes; असाध्यताम् = to incurability.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse's word for 'curability' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: साध्यताम् is साध्य + ता, the state of being curable, here the goal of याति 'goes to'.
questions.teaches: -ता makes a noun of state (साध्य → साध्यता), and याति takes the state it goes to in the accusative.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्वसाध्यताम्?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तु + असाध्यताम् → त्वसाध्यताम्.
त्व is not a word here; तु is the word 'but'.
That drops the negative अ and reverses the sense.
त्वा is not the word before the ending.
questions.explain: तु (but) and असाध्यताम् (to incurability): the curable one but does go to incurability.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A student writes: 'An incurable disease can become curable, but a curable one cannot become incurable.' Which correction matches the verse?
options: Each of the two can become the other
Only the curable can become incurable
Neither of the two can become the other
The sentence is already right as it stands
optionExplain: The verse allows only one direction.
Right: The verse says नासाध्यः साध्यतां याति, साध्यो याति त्वसाध्यताम्.
The curable one does go to incurability.
It reverses the verse.
questions.explain: The verse allows the change only from curable to incurable.
questions.rule: Incurable → curable: never. Curable → incurable: yes.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says न रिक्तः पूर्णतां याति, पूर्णस्तु रिक्ततां याति. What does it say?
options: The empty becomes full, but the full does not become empty
Both the empty and the full become full
The empty does not become full, but the full becomes empty
Neither the empty nor the full changes
optionExplain: The न is on the first half.
The second half has रिक्ततां, 'to emptiness'.
Right: It follows the verse's pattern: न ... याति, X तु ... याति.
The second half says the full does go to emptiness.
questions.explain: As in the verse: one change is denied (न ... याति), the other is affirmed with तु.
questions.rule: न X Y-तां याति, Y तु X-तां याति = X does not become Y, but Y becomes X.
questions.teaches: The pattern 'न A B-तां याति, B तु A-तां याति' gives a one-way rule: A never reaches the state of B, but B does reach the state of A.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse names two things from which diseases pass into another state. Which two?
options: Season, place and the patient's age
Age, sex and the strength of the patient
Mismanagement of the quarters, and fate
optionExplain: These are not named as the causes here.
These are not named in the verse.
These are not named in the verse.
Right: The verse says पादापचारात् दैवात् च.
questions.explain: पादापचारात् (from mismanagement of the quarters) and दैवात् (from fate).
questions.rule: Diseases change state through पाद-अपचार and दैव.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four main words of the first line.
questions.rule: पादापचारात् = from mismanagement of the quarters; दैवात् = from fate; गदाः = diseases; अवस्थान्तरम् = another state.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does the ending -आत् in दैवात् show?
optionExplain: Right: -आत् on an अ-ending word is the ablative: 'from, because of'.
The instrumental singular ends in -एन.
The locative singular ends in -ए.
The accusative singular ends in -म्.
questions.explain: दैवात् and पादापचारात् are both ablative: the sources of the change.
questions.teaches: The ending -आत् on an अ-ending word is the ablative singular: 'from, because of' (दैवात् = from fate).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of यान्त्यवस्थान्तरम्?
optionExplain: वस्थान्तरम् is not a word.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: यान्ति + अवस्थान्तरम् → यान्त्यवस्थान्तरम्.
यान्तु is another verb form ('let them go') and उ would become व्, not य्; the card's word is यान्ति.
That drops the इ of the verb.
questions.explain: यान्ति (they go) and अवस्थान्तरम् (to another state).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's second line (an unfinished sentence) in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: better, the venom of a venomous snake, a blazing fire, or else too.
questions.rule: Line 2: better · snake venom · blazing fire · or else too.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line joins कालात् + च. How is it written?
optionExplain: The two sounds are not left unjoined.
द् is for a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्, as in दैवात् + च → दैवाच्च.
श्च comes from a visarga, not from त्.
questions.explain: The same rule as दैवात् + च = दैवाच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: दैवात् + च = दैवाच्च, कालात् + च = कालाच्च.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The editors mark a verse's Sanskrit as garbled. What is the safest use of its translation?
options: Use it like the translation of a clear verse
Keep the longer of two translations
Always prefer the Hindi over the English
Do not rely on it for any claim
optionExplain: A clear verse has a firm reading; a damaged one does not.
Length does not make a guess right.
Both translations here disagree and are guesses.
Right: A translation of damaged words can only be a guess.
questions.explain: Where the text is damaged, the translation cannot be firmer than the text.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each item to what the card says about it.
pairs: flagged as damaged by the editors
questions.explain: The card gives only what is plain: what is flagged, what disagrees, and which words are unclear.
questions.rule: Both lines are flagged; the book's two translations disagree; line 1 has unclear words रूपेणाञ्जनात् and line 2 has परोक्षभूतवैद्याधर्म.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A sentence begun in verse 36 runs into this damaged unit. Can the unit say what is 'better' than what?
options: No; the objects cannot be recovered
Yes; the English translation says it plainly
Yes; the Hindi translation says it plainly
Yes; the legible words give the whole sentence
optionExplain: Right: The damaged words hide the objects, so the sentence cannot be completed.
The book's English is itself a guess.
The book's Hindi is itself a guess and disagrees with the English.
The legible words are too few to complete it.
questions.explain: The card says the sentence from verse 36 runs into this unit, but what is better than what cannot be recovered.
questions.rule: Do not complete a sentence from a damaged line.
questions.teaches: A sentence that runs into a damaged line is left unfinished: the missing part is not filled in by guessing.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which statement about this unit is safe to learn?
options: The verse lists the duties of a pupil
Both lines are damaged, so no meaning is fixed
The verse gives a clear rule for choosing a teacher
The verse praises refusing every patient
optionExplain: Nothing legible says this.
Right: This is what the card says.
Nothing legible says this.
Nothing legible says this.
questions.explain: The two translations point different ways, so neither can be learnt as the verse's meaning.
questions.rule: Safe: the lines are damaged; no meaning is fixed.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which of these may a student safely do with this unit?
options: Note that the editors flagged both lines
Treat the two translations as guesses
Not quote it as a teaching
Memorise the English as the verse's meaning
Quiz others on what रूपेणाञ्जनात् means
optionExplain: Right: this is a fact about the text.
Right: they disagree.
Right: nothing here is firm.
The English is only a guess.
The word is marked unclear.
questions.explain: The safe uses are facts about the damage; the meaning itself is not known.
questions.rule: Note the damage; do not teach a meaning.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A student meets another garbled line whose two translations disagree. What should a quiz built on it do?
options: Use the translation that fits one's guess
Ask nothing that depends on the damaged words
Teach the damaged words as a rule
optionExplain: A guess does not make a firm reading.
Length is not evidence.
Right: A question can rest only on what is plain.
A rule cannot rest on unclear words.
questions.explain: The same care as here: only the plain facts are used, and the unclear part is left out.
questions.rule: Damaged line: no question, no rule rests on it.
questions.teaches: Where a line is damaged and its translations disagree, a quiz asks nothing that depends on the unclear words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse says the one with his purpose accomplished does what to 'everything' (सर्वम्)?
optionExplain: The verb is अतिवर्त्तते, goes beyond, not give up.
No fear is named.
The verb does not mean collect.
Right: The verse says स सर्वमतिवर्त्तते: he surpasses everything.
questions.explain: अतिवर्त्तते means goes beyond or surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four main words of the line.
questions.rule: वर्त्तते = conducts himself; सिद्धार्थः = with purpose accomplished; सर्वम् = everything; अतिवर्त्तते = surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: In अतिवर्त्तते, what does the prefix अति- add to वर्त्तते, 'conducts himself'?
optionExplain: Right: अति- means beyond or over, so अति + वृत् is 'goes beyond'.
Going back is a different prefix.
Together is another prefix.
Not is अ-, not अति-.
questions.explain: अति + वर्त्तते = goes beyond, which the verse applies to everything.
questions.teaches: The prefix अति- gives 'beyond, over': अति + वर्त्तते = goes beyond, surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of सिद्धार्थः?
optionExplain: The first member is सिद्ध, ending in short अ.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: सिद्ध + अर्थः → सिद्धार्थः.
आर्थः is not a word here.
इ + अ would give सिद्ध्यर्थः.
questions.explain: सिद्ध (accomplished) and अर्थ (purpose): 'one whose purpose is accomplished'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: conducts himself, who, purpose accomplished, he everything, surpasses.
questions.rule: Order: वर्त्तते · यः तु · सिद्धार्थः · सः सर्वम् · अतिवर्त्तते.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: On the pattern of सिद्धार्थः, what does an invented गतभयः mean?
optionExplain: The first member is the participle 'gone', not 'goes to'.
That would be an agent noun.
Right: A past participle plus a noun, as सिद्ध + अर्थ, names a person with that feature.
The compound describes a person.
questions.explain: गत (gone) + भय (fear) = one whose fear has gone, as सिद्ध + अर्थ = one whose purpose is accomplished.
questions.teaches: A past participle followed by a noun can describe a person: सिद्धार्थः 'whose purpose is accomplished', गतभयः 'whose fear has gone'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What name does the closing line give to chapter 2?
optionExplain: The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
Right: The line says इति शिष्योपनयनीयो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः.
questions.explain: The chapter is named शिष्योपनयनीय, 'on the initiation of the student'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in the line.
questions.rule: इति = thus; नाम = named; द्वितीयः = second; शिष्योपनयनीयः = the chapter's name.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायः is the chapter, the unit that the colophon closes.
questions.teaches: अध्यायः, 'chapter', is what the colophon names with its number: द्वितीयः अध्यायः, the second chapter.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of द्वितीयोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
ध्यायः is not a word; the ऽ stands for the dropped अ.
Two अ would join as आ (द्वितीयाध्यायः).
A final आ would not give ओऽ.
questions.explain: द्वितीयः (second) and अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these words of the closing line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: thus, Śiṣyopanayanīya, named, second, chapter.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says इति रसीयो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः (षष्ठ = sixth). What does it say?
options: Thus the fifth chapter, named Rasīya
Thus the sixth chapter, named Rasīya
Thus the sixth verse, named Rasīya
Now the sixth chapter begins, named Rasīya
optionExplain: षष्ठ is sixth, not fifth.
Right: It follows the colophon pattern: इति, the name, नाम, the number, अध्यायः.
अध्यायः is a chapter, not a verse.
इति is 'thus', closing, not 'now'.
questions.explain: The pattern is इति + name + नाम + ordinal + अध्यायः, as in the verse.
questions.rule: इति X नाम N-ः अध्यायः = thus the Nth chapter, named X.
questions.teaches: A colophon reads इति + the name + नाम + the ordinal + अध्यायः: 'thus the ... chapter, named ...'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What is the subject announced in the opening formula of chapter 3?
options: The chapter on the pupil's duty
The chapter on the daily routine
The chapter on the six tastes
optionExplain: That is a different chapter title; not named here.
Not named in this formula.
Right: दिनचर्याध्यायं: the chapter on the daily routine (dinacaryā).
Not named in this formula.
questions.explain: The formula names the daily routine as the subject.
questions.rule: अथातो दिनचर्याध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः: अब दिनचर्या का अध्याय समझाएँगे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the three parts of the formula in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the opening words, then the subject, then the verb.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of the formula to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words give: now, therefore, the chapter on the daily routine, we shall explain.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; दिनचर्याध्याय = chapter on the daily routine; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The formula is made of अथ (now), अतः (therefore), the object, and a future verb in the first person plural.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of अथातो is right?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here; the आ comes from two अ.
आतः is not the word; the card reads अतः, therefore.
That would leave ओ in the middle; the ओ is only the changed visarga.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, and the visarga after अ becomes ओ before the voiced द: अथातो.
questions.explain: अथातः comes from अथ + अतः.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; ः + voiced consonant (after अ) → ओ.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: What does the form व्याख्यास्यामः say about the speaker?
options: You must explain it to us
optionExplain: Right: 1st person plural future: we shall explain.
That would be third person singular, past.
That would be a command to someone else.
That would be singular and present.
questions.explain: The card labels व्याख्यास्यामः as 1 pl. future.
questions.rule: व्याख्यास्यामः = हम समझाएँगे (उत्तम पुरुष, बहुवचन, भविष्यत्).
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of दिनचर्याध्यायम्, what does ऋतुचर्याध्यायम् mean?
options: Chapter on the season of the routine
Chapter on the routine by season
optionExplain: The first member names the subject, not the season of something.
Right: X-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on the routine of X; here X is ऋतु, season.
चर्या is routine, not teaching.
That would be दिनचर्या, with दिन, day.
questions.explain: दिन-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on the daily routine, so ऋतु-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on routine by season.
questions.rule: X-चर्याध्याय = chapter on the routine of X.
questions.teaches: In X-चर्या-अध्याय the first member X says what the routine follows or concerns.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: At what time does verse 2 say a healthy person should rise?
options: At noon, when the sun is high
optionExplain: The verse names no meal time.
Not named in this verse.
Right: ब्राह्मे मुहूर्त्ते उत्तिष्ठेत्: one should rise at the Brāhma muhūrta.
The verse names no such time.
questions.explain: The verse names the Brāhma muhūrta, taken as the pre-dawn period.
questions.rule: स्वस्थ व्यक्ति ब्राह्म मुहूर्त में उठे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: rise, examining digestion. Line 2: for the protection of life, the healthy one voids when the urge has arisen.
questions.rule: उठना → जीर्ण-अजीर्ण का विचार → आयु की रक्षा के लिए → स्वस्थ → वेग होने पर त्याग.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two optative verbs (should rise, should void), one participle (examining) and two nouns for the person.
questions.rule: उत्तिष्ठेत् / समुत्सृजेत् = विधि (should); निरूपयन् = examining; जातवेगः = urge arisen.
questions.teaches: The optative ending -एत् gives 'one should ...'; a participle in -न् says 'doing ... meanwhile'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of रक्षार्थमायुषः is right?
optionExplain: मायुषः is not a word; the म् belongs to अर्थम्.
युषः is not a word here.
That doubles the म्; the म् is single.
Right: The final म् of अर्थम् joins the vowel आ that follows.
questions.explain: रक्षार्थम् (रक्षा-अर्थम्, for the protection) + आयुषः (of life).
questions.rule: म् + स्वर: म् साथ का स्वर पकड़ लेता है: अर्थम् + आयुषः → अर्थमायुषः.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: A healthy person finds the urge has arisen. What does verse 2 say?
options: He should void it, to protect life
He should hold it back, to protect life
He should wait until the evening meal
He should first rise, then forget it
optionExplain: Right: जातवेगः समुत्सृजेत्, रक्षार्थमायुषः.
The verse says to void it, not to hold it back.
No such wait is mentioned.
The verse gives no such instruction.
questions.explain: The verse joins jāta-vega with samutsṛjet: when the urge has arisen, void.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of जीर्णाजीर्णे निरूपयन् (dual objects), what does सुखदुःखे निरूपयन् mean?
optionExplain: The dvandva names both members, सुख and दुःख.
Right: A dual dvandva as object of the participle, as जीर्णाजीर्णे.
निरूपयन् is the one doing the examining, not the object.
The ending -न् is a present participle, not 'having examined'.
questions.explain: Two names joined into one dual word are both objects of 'examining'.
questions.rule: A dvandva in the dual (-ए, neuter) names two things together.
questions.teaches: A dvandva of two items ending in the dual can be the object of a participle: 'examining A and B'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: In verse 3, which direction is faced at night when voiding?
optionExplain: North is the first direction (उदङ्मुखः), not the night one.
East is not named in this verse.
Right: दक्षिणाभिमुखो निशि: facing south at night.
West is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives north first and south for the night.
questions.rule: उदङ्मुख = उत्तर; दक्षिणाभिमुख निशि = रात में दक्षिण.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 3 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the directions; line 2 gives the manner: speech, bowing, covering.
questions.rule: उत्तर → रात में दक्षिण → वाणी का संयम → झुकना → ढका अंग → आवृत.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Both directions are bahuvrīhi compounds ending in -मुख.
questions.rule: उदङ्मुख = north-facing; दक्षिणाभिमुख = south-facing; निशि = रात में.
questions.teaches: A direction word + मुख (or अभिमुख) is a bahuvrīhi: 'one whose face is toward that direction'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of संवीताङ्गोऽवगुण्ठितः is right?
optionExplain: वगुण्ठितः is not a word; the ऽ stands for the अ of अवगुण्ठितः.
The word ends in a visarga, not in long आ.
उवगुण्ठितः is not a word.
Right: अः + अ gives ओ with the avagraha ऽ marking the dropped अ.
questions.explain: संवीताङ्ग + अवगुण्ठित: the visarga turns into ओ, the अ is marked by ऽ.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which describes voiding at night, by verse 3?
options: Facing south, silent, bowed, limbs covered
Facing north, silent, bowed, limbs covered
Facing south, speaking freely, bowed, limbs covered
Facing south, silent, bowed, limbs uncovered
optionExplain: Right: This matches all four points of the verse.
At night the verse says south.
The verse says restraining speech.
The verse says the limbs are covered.
questions.explain: At night: दक्षिणाभिमुख, वाणी रोकी हुई, प्रणत, संवीताङ्ग.
questions.rule: रात में दक्षिण; वाणी संयत; झुका; ढका.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of उदङ्मुखः, what does पश्चिमाभिमुखः mean?
optionExplain: पश्चिम here is a direction word, as in the verse's pattern.
Right: पश्चिम (west) + अभिमुखः (facing): a bahuvrīhi like दक्षिणाभिमुखः.
The compound says whose face is toward the west, not where the face is.
अभिमुख means facing toward.
questions.explain: पश्चिम + अभिमुखः is one whose face is toward the west.
questions.teaches: A direction word + (अभि)मुखः names the person facing that direction; use it for any new direction.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: What does verse 4 say about an urge that has begun to move?
options: Force it out with all effort
Hold it back until a later hour
Let it out, but not with effort
Let it out only after the first meal
optionExplain: That is the opposite of न तु यत्नात् उदीरयेत्.
The verse says to let it out, not hold it.
Right: प्रवर्तयेत्प्रचलितं नतु यत्नादुदीरयेत्.
No such wait is mentioned.
questions.explain: The urge that has started to move is allowed out; forcing it is forbidden.
questions.rule: प्रचलित वेग को निकलने दे; ज़ोर लगाकर न निकाले.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the words of verse 4, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the permitted act and its object, then the forbidden act.
questions.rule: प्रवर्तयेत् प्रचलितम् → न तु यत्नात् उदीरयेत्.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first verb permits, the second forbids (with न तु before it).
questions.rule: प्रवर्तयेत् = let out; प्रचलित = begun to move; यत्न = effort; उदीरयेत् = force out.
questions.teaches: न तु + a verb in -एत् says 'but one should not ...'; the ablative यत्नात् gives the means or manner.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of यत्नादुदीरयेत् is right?
optionExplain: दुदीरयेत् is not a verb of the card.
दीरयेत् is not a word; the verb is उदीरयेत्.
आदुदीरयेत् is not a word either.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a vowel: यत्नादुदीरयेत्.
questions.explain: यत्नात् (with effort) + उदीरयेत् (one should force out).
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 4?
options: Let out what has begun to move
Do not force it out with effort
Force it out so that none remains
What has begun to move should be stopped
optionExplain: Right: प्रवर्तयेत् प्रचलितम्.
Right: न तु यत्नादुदीरयेत्.
The verse forbids forcing.
The verse says to let it out: प्रवर्तयेत्.
questions.explain: Two points are said of the urge itself; line 2 begins a list of places not to void.
questions.rule: वेग: निकलने दे, ज़ोर नहीं; स्थान: अपवित्र आदि वर्जित.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of न तु यत्नादुदीरयेत्, what does न तु बलादुदीरयेत् say?
options: But one should not force it out by strength
But one should force it out by strength
And only strength can let it out
But strength should not be examined
optionExplain: Right: बलात् is ablative (by strength), joined to उदीरयेत् like यत्नात्.
That drops the न; the verse pattern forbids.
The pattern names the means, not a condition.
उदीरयेत् is to force out, not to examine.
questions.explain: बलात् + उदीरयेत् joins as बलादुदीरयेत्; with न तु it is a prohibition.
questions.rule: न तु + ablative + उदीरयेत् = but not by that means.
questions.teaches: A prohibition 'न तु X-आत् उदीरयेत्' forbids forcing something out by the means X.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: In line 2 of verse 5, what does प्रति after the list mean?
optionExplain: प्रति does not mean away.
Right: The card glosses प्रति as toward: न ... प्रति = not toward them.
प्रति does not mean instead of.
प्रति is not a word of company here.
questions.explain: The list in line 2 is followed by प्रति: not toward these.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the first five items of verse 5, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The list begins with a woman, a revered one, a cow, then the sun and the moon.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words are plain nouns in the lists.
questions.rule: वल्मीक = anthill; द्रुम = tree; अर्क = sun; इन्दु = moon; वायु = wind.
questions.teaches: The sun and the moon have several Sanskrit names; here they are अर्क and इन्दु.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which of these is named in line 2 of verse 5?
optionExplain: Not in the clear list of line 2.
Not in the clear list of line 2.
Right: इन्दु is named in line 2.
Not in the clear list of line 2.
questions.explain: इन्दु, the moon, is one of the clear words of line 2.
questions.rule: गो, इन्दु, वल्मीक स्पष्ट शब्द हैं; पर्वत, नदी, दीप सूची में नहीं.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which of these stand in line 2's list under 'not toward' (न … प्रति)?
optionExplain: Right: गो.
Right: अर्क.
द्रुम is in line 1 as a place, not in line 2's list.
वल्मीक is in line 1 as a place, not in line 2's list.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the list under 'not toward'; line 1 gives the places.
questions.rule: पंक्ति २: 'की ओर नहीं' की सूची; पंक्ति १: स्थान.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the verse's pattern, how is न with a word for the moon and प्रति written?
optionExplain: The nominative does not go with प्रति.
The instrumental means 'by the moon', not toward.
The dative means 'for the moon'.
Right: प्रति takes the accusative: इन्दुम् (the card has जलम् + प्रति).
questions.explain: The list word before प्रति stands in the accusative, so इन्दुं प्रति.
questions.teaches: प्रति takes the accusative: न X-म् प्रति = not toward X.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: What does verse 6 say of one who has an urge (वेगितः)?
options: He should not be occupied with other work
He should finish other work first
He should call a physician at once
He should wait for the next day
optionExplain: Right: न वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः स्यात्.
That is the opposite of the line.
No physician is mentioned in this verse.
No such waiting is stated.
questions.explain: वेगित = one who has an urge; अन्यकार्य = engaged in other work; with न: should not be.
questions.rule: वेग हो तो दूसरे कार्य में न लगे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the words of verse 6, line 2 (first half), in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line says: not, one with an urge, engaged in other work, should be.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 6, line 2, to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the plainly readable words of line 2.
questions.rule: वेगित = having an urge; अन्यकार्य = other work; स्यात् = should be; साध्य = curable; आमय = disease.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi such as अन्यकार्यः names the person who has that feature: 'one with other work'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of स्यान्नाजित्वा is right?
optionExplain: न + जित्वा would be नजित्वा; the ा comes from अजित्वा.
Right: त् before न becomes न्; न + अ gives ना: स्यान्नाजित्वा.
That leaves the verb without its final त्.
न्नाजित्वा is not a word.
questions.explain: स्यात् (should be) + न (not) + अजित्वा (without having overcome).
questions.rule: त् + न → न्न; न + अ → ना.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: A person has an urge but starts another task. What does line 2 say?
options: It says he should do the task first
It says the task is a cure for the urge
It says he should not be so occupied
It says nothing about the case
optionExplain: The line forbids it.
No such claim is made.
Right: न वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः स्यात्.
Line 2 states exactly this case.
questions.explain: The case fits the line: one with an urge occupied with other work.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: How is सुप्तः + अपि joined, by the rule of वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः?
optionExplain: The visarga after अ gives ओ, not आ.
A visarga before a vowel after अ is changed, not left.
The अ of अपि is marked by ऽ, not lost.
Right: अः + अ gives ओऽ, as वेगितः + अन्यकार्यः gives वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः.
questions.explain: सुप्तः ends in अः and अपि begins with अ, so the result is सुप्तोऽपि.
questions.teaches: A word ending in अः followed by अ becomes ओऽ; use it for any new word pair.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: With what does verse 7 say the passage is first wiped?
options: Lumps of ash free of splinters
Pieces of cloth that are unspoiled
optionExplain: Right: निःशल्यादुष्टमृत्पिण्डीपरिमृष्टमलायनः.
The verse names earth, not ash.
No cloth is named in the verse.
No leaves are named in the verse.
questions.explain: The wiping is done with unspoiled lumps of earth, free of śalya.
questions.rule: पोंछना: निःशल्य, अदुष्ट मिट्टी के ढेले.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 7 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the wiping with lumps of earth, then the application of waters and earths.
questions.rule: ढेलों से पोंछना → स्वच्छ जल → मिट्टियाँ → उपचार.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words describe the earth, one describes the waters, one is the waters, one is the verb.
questions.rule: निःशल्य = śalya-free; अदुष्ट = unspoiled; शुचि = clean; अप् = water; योजयेत् = apply.
questions.teaches: The prefix नि:/निस् means 'without' and अ- negates: निःशल्य = without splinter, अदुष्ट = not spoiled.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of निःशल्यादुष्ट is right?
optionExplain: That would make the earth spoiled, against the card.
Right: अ + अ gives आ; the earth is free of splinters and unspoiled.
आदुष्ट is not a word of the card.
उष्ट is not a word here.
questions.explain: निःशल्य and अदुष्ट describe the lumps of earth.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: निःशल्य + अदुष्ट → निःशल्यादुष्ट.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: With what does verse 7 say to treat the passage in the end?
optionExplain: Right: शुचिभिः अद्भिः.
Right: मृद्भिः च.
Not named in the verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse names clean waters and earths.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: How is शुचिभिः + गुणैः joined, by the rule seen in शुचिभिरद्भिः?
optionExplain: The visarga is not left standing before a voiced consonant.
स् is for the voiceless sounds like त, not for ग.
Right: After इ a visarga becomes र् before a voiced consonant (here ग).
ओ comes only after अ, not after इ.
questions.explain: शुचिभिः ends in इ + visarga; before ग it becomes र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ becomes र् before a voiced sound; use it for any new instrumental plural.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: What does the cleansing of verse 8 remove?
options: Tears and dirt of the eye
optionExplain: These are in the list of line 2 as things touched.
Tears are in the list of line 2.
Not named in this verse.
Right: लेपगन्धापहं शौचम्: cleansing that removes smear and odour.
questions.explain: The word लेप-गन्ध-अपहम् means removing smear and odour.
questions.rule: शौच: लेप और गन्ध को दूर करे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the items of verse 8, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line begins with having touched, then the list ending with fallen hair and nails.
questions.rule: छूकर → धातु → मल → आँसू → नेत्र → गिरे केश-नख.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three words name the cleansing and what it removes; the last two come from the list of line 2.
questions.rule: लेप = smear; गन्ध = odour; शौच = cleansing; अश्रु = tears; दृश् = eye.

questions.teaches: The first list is of things that go away; the second is of things that come.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 17 say does NOT arise?
optionExplain: Right: It is in the first list, with न भवन्ति.
Appetite is in the list of what arises.
Clearness is in the list of what arises.
Lightness is in the list of what arises.
questions.explain: Dirt, bad taste, tongue odour and mouth-and-teeth troubles are the ones that do not arise.
questions.rule: First list: न भवन्ति; second list: भवन्ति.

questions.q: In verse 17, which verb goes with रुचि, वैशद्य and लघुता?
optionExplain: न भवन्ति goes with the first list.
Right: Right, from the sense (the card's reading): they arise.
Then the verse would contradict itself.
Each list needs a verb, and the card gives one to each.
questions.explain: The card pairs the first verb with the first list and the second verb with the second list.
questions.rule: The pairing of verbs and lists is an inference from the sense.

questions.q: What does the compound शीतोष्णम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be a genitive compound, not a list.
No word for 'without' is present.
Right: A compound of items joined by 'and', like रुचि-वैशद्य-लघुता.
No comparison word is present.
questions.explain: शीत + उष्ण in one word: cold and heat.
questions.rule: A series of items can be packed into one compound meaning A and B (and C).
questions.teaches: A compound can list items in one word, as रुचिवैशद्यलघुता lists appetite, clearness and lightness.

questions.q: Who is told in verse 18 not to chew the stick?
optionExplain: A fracture is not named in the verse.
Leprosy is not named in the verse.
Hiccups are not named in the verse.

questions.explain: The list includes the one with fever (ज्वर).
questions.rule: Named: अजीर्ण, वमथु, श्वास, कास, ज्वर, अर्दित, तृष्णा, आस्यपाक, हृदय-नेत्र-शिर-कर्ण रोग.

questions.q: Put the six troubles of verse 18, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists these six in this order.
questions.rule: अजीर्ण, वमथु, श्वास, कास, ज्वर, अर्दित.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the troubles are plain words.
questions.teaches: The verse names troubles; the card gives each name its plain meaning and no more.

questions.q: Which split of नाद्यात् is right?
optionExplain: Right: न (not) + अद्यात् (should eat): अ + अ gives आ.
A visarga would give नोऽद्यात्.
द्यात् is not a word.
यात् is not the verb here.
questions.explain: न + अद्यात् = नाद्यात्, one should not eat (chew).

questions.q: Which persons does verse 18 name?
options: One with an ailment of the ear
One with pain in the feet
optionExplain: Right: कर्णामयी.
Right: तृष्णा.
A skin trouble is not named in the verse.
Pain in the feet is not named in the verse.
questions.explain: Ear ailment and thirst are both in line 2.
questions.rule: Line 2: तृष्णा, आस्यपाक, हृद्, नेत्र, शिरः, कर्ण.

questions.q: How is न + अस्ति written when joined?
optionExplain: One अ is not simply dropped.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, as in नाद्यात्.
अ + अ does not give ए.
अ + अ does not give ओ.
questions.explain: The rule of न + अद्यात् gives न + अस्ति = नास्ति.
questions.rule: A short अ + a short अ → long आ.
questions.teaches: Two short अ sounds meeting join into long आ.

questions.q: By the card's reading, what is said of sticks born of the plants named in verse 19?
options: They are for the sick only
They are not to be used
optionExplain: The verse begins with a negative, न.
No such limit is stated here.
Right: नैव: nor indeed; the verb is understood from nearby units.
No time of cutting is stated.
questions.explain: The verse opens with नैव, not indeed, so these sticks are not to be used (the verb comes from neighbouring units).
questions.rule: नैव = न + एव; the list continues the prohibition.

questions.q: Put these four names of verse 19, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins with these four names, in this order.

questions.q: Put these four names of verse 19, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 has these names in this order (others stand between).
questions.teaches: Verse 19 gives names in two lines; the names of line 2 begin with बिल्व and end with तिन्दुक.

questions.q: Which split of नैवश्लेष्मातक starts correctly?
optionExplain: व alone is not a word here.
नः + एव would stay apart as न एव, not नैव.
ऐव is not a word of the card.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ: न + एव = नैव.
questions.explain: नैव is न (not) + एव (indeed).

questions.q: Which two names are in verse 19?

Right: line 2.

This is in verse 20.
questions.explain: Verse 19 holds बिभीत and तिन्दुक; शमी and शण are in the next unit.
questions.rule: Names of verse 19 are different from those of verse 20.

questions.q: By the pattern of अरिष्टजान्, what means those born of mud (accusative plural)?
optionExplain: Right: X-जान् means those born of X; X is पङ्क (mud).
That means the muds, not those born of mud.
The जान् part comes last.
That is singular, not plural.
questions.explain: अरिष्ट-जान् = born of ariṣṭa; so पङ्क-जान् = born of mud.
questions.teaches: A compound X-ज means born of X; the case ending follows the last part.

questions.q: What does verse 20 add to the list of verse 19?
optionExplain: No dose is given.
Right: The verse continues the list with names only.
No effect is given.
No season is given.
questions.explain: Verse 20 lists further names such as कोविदार, शमी, गुग्गुलु.
questions.rule: The verse names plants and says nothing about effects or doses.

questions.q: Put the six names of verse 20, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 holds these six names, in this order.
questions.rule: कोविदार, शमी, पीलु, पिप्पल, ऐङ्गुद, गुग्गुलु.

questions.q: Which two names stand in the first line of verse 20?
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 1.

This is in verse 19.
questions.explain: शमी and पीलु are in line 1 of verse 20; शिग्रु and बिल्व belong to verse 19.
questions.rule: Line 1 of verse 20 starts with कोविदार, शमी, पीलु.
questions.teaches: Names of verse 20 are different from those of verse 19; line 1 of verse 20 begins with कोविदार, शमी, पीलु.

questions.q: Which split of पिप्पलैङ्गुद is right?
optionExplain: That would join as पिप्पल्यङ्गुद.
इ + ऐ would give यैङ्गुद.
Right: अ + ऐ gives ऐ: पिप्पल + ऐङ्गुद = पिप्पलैङ्गुद.
That would join as पिप्पलाङ्गुद.
questions.explain: The card's words are पिप्पल and ऐङ्गुद, two names.

questions.q: Put these four names of verse 20, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 holds these four names in this order (मोचक, whose text is damaged, is left out).

questions.q: How is राम + ऐश्वर्यम् written when joined?
optionExplain: अ + ऐ does not give आ.
अ + ऐ does not give ए.
The two words are joined, not left apart.
Right: अ + ऐ gives ऐ, as in पिप्पलैङ्गुद.
questions.explain: The rule of पिप्पल + ऐङ्गुद gives राम + ऐश्वर्यम् = रामैश्वर्यम्.
questions.rule: A short अ before ऐ joins into ऐ.
questions.teaches: A final अ or आ before ऐ joins with it into ऐ.

questions.q: Verse 21 ends by asking one to avoid a pair of what?
optionExplain: Right: पादुके is the dual: a pair of sandals.
No staff is named.
No rope is named.
The teeth are not what is avoided here.
questions.explain: त्यजेत् with पादुके: one should avoid a pair of sandals.

questions.q: Put the seven qualities of verse 21 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The list runs from the three tastes to dry, hollow, and then foul-smelling and slimy.
questions.rule: स्वादु, अम्ल, लवण, शुष्क, सुषिर, पूति, पिच्छिल.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words are the plain qualities of the list.
questions.teaches: The first three words are tastes; शुष्क and सुषिर describe the stick's body.

questions.q: In verse 21, which word is a dual form, meaning a pair?
optionExplain: This is singular, one stick.
Right: -े is the dual ending of the feminine word पादुका.
This is singular.
This is a verb, singular.
questions.explain: पादुके is dual: a pair of sandals.
questions.rule: Dual of feminine -आ nouns ends in -े.

questions.q: Which two qualities are listed in verse 21?
optionExplain: Right: शुष्कम्.
Right: सुषिरम्.
Bent is not in the list.
Very long is not in the list.
questions.explain: शुष्क and सुषिर are both in line 1.
questions.rule: The list has seven qualities, from स्वादु to पिच्छिल.

questions.q: What is the dual of शाला (hall) in the nominative or accusative?
optionExplain: That is the plural.
-औ is the dual of masculine nouns.
Right: Feminine -आ nouns have -े in the dual, like पादुके.
That is the genitive singular.
questions.explain: As पादुका gives पादुके, शाला gives शाले.
questions.teaches: A feminine noun in -आ forms its dual in -े, as पादुके.

questions.q: By verse 22, what fills the mouth when the eyes are sprinkled?
optionExplain: No ghee is mentioned in this verse.
No leaf is mentioned in this verse.
No salt is mentioned in this verse.
Right: तोयपूर्णमुखः: with the mouth full of water.
questions.explain: तोय (water) + पूर्ण (full) + मुख (mouth).
questions.rule: तोयपूर्णमुखः = with the mouth full of water.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 22 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The teeth come first, then the eyes, the water in the mouth, the seasons and the cold water.
questions.rule: Line 1: teeth, morning, eyes. Line 2: water, seasons, cold water.

questions.q: The word for 'summer' in verse 22 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: ग्रीष्म is summer; in ग्रीष्मशरदोः it is joined with शरद् (autumn).
questions.teaches: ग्रीष्म means summer, and शरद् means autumn.

questions.q: Which split of सिञ्चेच्च is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् becomes च् before च.
न् + च would give सिञ्चेंश्च.
श्च is not a word.
A visarga would give सिञ्चेश्च.
questions.explain: सिञ्चेत् (one should sprinkle) + च (and).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 22 to its meaning.
pairs: with the mouth full of water
questions.explain: These five words carry the main facts of the verse.

questions.q: How is भवेत् + च written when joined?
optionExplain: The two words are joined, not left apart.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्, as in सिञ्चेच्च.
द् before च is not the rule.
That would come from a visarga, not from त्.
questions.explain: The rule of सिञ्चेत् + च gives भवेत् + च = भवेच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च turns into च्, giving doubled च्च.

questions.q: Whom does verse 23 begin by bowing to?
optionExplain: They are not named.
The verse names gods and elders.
Right: प्रणम्य देवान्वृद्धांश्च.
They are not named.
questions.explain: Having bowed to the gods (देवान्) and the elders (वृद्धान्).
questions.rule: देवान् and वृद्धान् are the two objects of प्रणम्य.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Put these four words of verse 23, line 1, in the verse's order.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning.

questions.q: Which split of वृद्धांश्च is right?
optionExplain: That would give वृद्धाश्च.
That would give वृद्धाच्च.
वृद्धाम् is not the form; म् + च would give वृद्धां च, with no श्.
Right: Final न् before च becomes ं + श्: वृद्धांश्च.
questions.explain: वृद्धान् (the elders, accusative plural) + च (and).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: The word for 'the gods' in verse 23 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: देवान् = the gods, the object of प्रणम्य.
questions.teaches: देवान् is the accusative plural of देव, the gods.

questions.q: Made like प्रणम्य, which word means having placed down (prefix नि, root क्षिप्)?
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix, the root takes -य, as in प्रणम्य.
A prefixed root does not take -त्वा.
That means to place.
That means he places.
questions.explain: प्र + नम् + य = प्रणम्य; नि + क्षिप् + य = निक्षिप्य.
questions.teaches: A root with a prefix forms 'having done' with -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: Which is said in verse 24 to be beneficial for the eyes?

questions.explain: The sauvīra collyrium is called beneficial for the eyes.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 24, line 1, in the verse's order.

questions.q: Which split of हितमक्ष्णोस्ततो is right?
optionExplain: हितः would join as हितोऽक्ष्णोः.
मक्ष्णोः is not a word.
Right: म् joins the next vowel; the visarga before त becomes स्; ततः before भ becomes ततो.
क्ष्णोः is not a word.
questions.explain: हितम् (beneficial) + अक्ष्णोः (for the eyes) + ततः (then).
questions.rule: म् + vowel joins; ः + त → स्त; अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which verb agrees with the dual subject हस्तौ (two hands)?
optionExplain: That is plural.
That is singular.
That is first person.

questions.explain: लोचने (dual) takes भवतः (dual); हस्तौ takes भवतः too.
questions.teaches: A dual subject takes a dual verb ending in -तः.

questions.q: By verse 25, from what is the danger to the eye especially?

The sun is not named in this verse.

questions.q: Which split of विशेषाच्छ्लेष्मतः is right?
optionExplain: The word is विशेषात्, not विशेषाः; a visarga before श would not give च्छ्.

आच्छ्लेष्मतः is not a word.

questions.explain: विशेषात् (especially) + श्लेष्मतः (from Kapha).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: What does verse 25 say about the three colours?

optionExplain: The verse names no colour.

questions.q: How is तत् + शान्तम् written when joined?
optionExplain: The two words are joined, not left apart.
द् does not come before श् here.
The त् does not turn into श्.
Right: त् before श् becomes च्छ्, as in विशेषाच्छ्लेष्मतः.
questions.explain: The rule of विशेषात् + श्लेष्मतः gives तत् + शान्तम् = तच्छान्तम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् meeting श joins as च्छ.

questions.q: For what purpose does verse 26 say rasāñjana is applied?
optionExplain: Right: स्रावणार्थं रसांजनं: for the purpose of causing discharge.

No such purpose is stated.

questions.q: Which split of सप्तरात्रेऽस्मात्स्रावणार्थम् is right?
optionExplain: That would join as सप्तरात्रास्मात्.
Right: ए + अ gives ए, the अ shown by ऽ.
सप्तरात्रेः is not the form here.
स्मात् is not a word.
questions.explain: सप्तरात्रे + अस्मात् + स्रावणार्थम् (meanings of the first two are open).

questions.q: By verse 26, what comes right after नस्य?

That is in verse 16.
Right: ततो गण्डूषधारणम्: then holding a gaṇḍūṣa.

questions.explain: After nasya, the verse says ततः गण्डूषधारणम्.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: In स्नानं ततो भोजनं ततः शयनम्, which step comes last?

Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as in वासो न.
The visarga becomes ओ; it is not dropped.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives वासो न gives नरो गच्छेत्.
questions.teaches: The visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant; use it for any new phrase.

questions.q: Unit 35 says one should not wear cloth, a flower or sandals in what condition?
options: Not yet washed clean by water
Torn at the edge of the cloth
optionExplain: Washing is not mentioned in the unit.
Tearing is not mentioned in the unit.
Buying is not mentioned in the unit.
Right: अन्येन विधृतम्: worn by another.
questions.explain: The prohibition is of things already worn by another.
questions.rule: Not cloth, flower or sandals worn by another.

questions.q: Put the three things not to wear, as listed in line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads cloth, flower, pair of sandals.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the unit's two sentences.
questions.rule: अन्येन = by another; विधृतम् = worn; उपानहौ = pair of sandals; इच्छन् = desiring.
questions.teaches: उपानहौ is dual (a pair); इच्छन् is a present participle, desiring.

questions.q: Which split of नैव is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए gives ऐ, so न + एव is written नैव: not indeed.
इ + ए would give ये, not ऐ.
व is not a word.
ऐव is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: नैव = न (not) + एव (indeed).

questions.q: Which does the one in line 2 of unit 35 desire?
optionExplain: Right: रुचि.
Right: वैशद्य.
Right: सौगन्ध्य.
Wealth is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: The three desired things are relish, clarity and fragrance.

questions.q: How is सदा + एव (ever, indeed) written when joined?
optionExplain: ए alone would drop the long vowel; the join gives ऐ.
Right: आ + ए gives ऐ, as अ + ए does in नैव.
The two vowels join; they do not stand apart.
ओ comes from अ/आ + उ/ऊ, not from अ/आ + ए.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives नैव gives सदैव.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by ए joins into ऐ; use it for any new phrase.

questions.q: What does line 2 of unit 36 call pleasing and accompanied by pūga-fruit?
optionExplain: Garlands are in unit 34.
Sandals are in unit 35, line 1.
Right: ताम्बूलीनां किसलयं हृद्यं पूगफलान्वितम्.
Warm water is in unit 30.
questions.explain: The leaf is the subject: tender, pleasing, with pūga-fruit.

questions.q: Put the four phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads of the tāmbūlī, tender leaf, pleasing, with pūga-fruit.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 36 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the structure of the unit.
questions.rule: किसलयम् = tender leaf; हृद्यम् = pleasing; अन्वितम् = accompanied by; सह = together with.
questions.teaches: अन्वित at the end of a compound means accompanied by the first part.

questions.q: Which split of पूगफलान्वितम् is right?
optionExplain: इ + अ would give य, not आ.
Neither part is a word.
एन्वितम् is not a word of the card.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so पूगफल + अन्वितम् is written पूगफलान्वितम्.
questions.explain: पूगफलान्वितम् = पूगफल (pūga-fruit) + अन्वितम् (accompanied by).

questions.q: Where does the verb of unit 36 (hold in the mouth) come from?
optionExplain: Right: Unit 36 has no verb; the card notes that 35.2 and 36 form one sentence.
Line 1 has only names and सह.
जयेत् means one should overcome.
आचरेत् means one should practise, and it belongs to unit 31.
questions.explain: 35.2 gives धारयेत्, and unit 36 gives what is held.

questions.q: Which form means accompanied by fruit?
optionExplain: That means devoid of fruit.
Right: X + अन्वितम् means accompanied by X; अ + अ gives आ.
That means without fruit.
That means born of fruit.
questions.explain: The pattern of पूगफलान्वितम् gives फलान्वितम्.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in अन्वित means accompanied by the first member.

questions.q: Unit 37 calls that thing (तत्) what, for the persons it lists?
optionExplain: Unit 38 calls it suitable for other persons.
The unit limits it to the listed persons.
Right: अपथ्यं शोषिणां च तत्: that is unsuitable.
हृद्यम् is said of the leaf in unit 36, not here.
questions.explain: The unit says अपथ्यम्, unsuitable.
questions.rule: तत् = unsuitable for the listed persons.

questions.q: Put the four afflictions of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads poison, fainting, intoxication, and then wasting (śoṣa).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 37 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry line 2.
questions.rule: विष = poison; मूर्च्छा = fainting; मद = intoxication; शोष = wasting.
questions.teaches: These are the afflictions of line 2; the unit gives them as terms, without cause or treatment.

questions.q: Which split of विषमूर्च्छामदार्त्तानाम् is right?
optionExplain: विषम would mean uneven, and ऊर्च्छा is not a word.
आमद is not a word of the card.
Neither of the last two parts is a word.
Right: अ + आ gives आ: मद + आर्त्तानाम् → मदार्त्तानाम्: of those afflicted by poison, fainting, intoxication.
questions.explain: The compound is poison, fainting, intoxication, afflicted.

questions.q: For which persons does unit 37 call that unsuitable?
optionExplain: Right: विष...आर्त्तानाम्.
Right: कुपितचक्षुषाम्.
Right: शोषिणाम्.
Unit 38 calls it suitable for such a person.
questions.explain: Poison, irritated eyes and śoṣa are named in unit 37; the bathed person is in unit 38.
questions.rule: Unit 37: unsuitable for the listed persons; unit 38: suitable after sleep, eating, bathing, vomiting.

questions.q: What does ज्वरार्त्तानाम् (like मदार्त्तानाम्) mean?
optionExplain: Right: X-आर्त्त means afflicted by X, and -आनाम् is the genitive plural.
-आनाम् is the genitive plural, not the instrumental.
-आर्त्त means afflicted, not overcoming.
The compound puts fever first: afflicted by fever.
questions.explain: The pattern of मदार्त्तानाम् gives 'of those afflicted by fever'.
questions.rule: X-आर्त्त + आनाम् = of those afflicted by X.
questions.teaches: X-आर्त्त means afflicted by X; the ending -आनाम् is the genitive plural (of those).

questions.q: For which person does unit 38 call that thing suitable (पथ्यम्)?
options: One who has run a long way
One who has risen from sleep
One who has kept a fast
One who has gone to sleep at night
optionExplain: Running is not mentioned in the unit.
Right: सुप्तोत्थिते: for one who has risen from sleep.
Fasting is not mentioned in the unit.
The unit says risen from sleep.
questions.explain: Unit 38 names four states: risen from sleep, eaten, bathed, vomited.
questions.rule: पथ्य after sleep, eating, bathing, vomiting.

questions.q: Put the four states of the person in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads risen from sleep, eaten, bathed, vomited.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 38 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each state is a locative singular, 'in the case of'.
questions.rule: सुप्तोत्थिते, भुक्ते, स्नाते, वान्ते are four locatives.
questions.teaches: A past participle in the locative, with a noun, means in the case of a person who has done it.

questions.q: Which split of सुप्तोत्थिते is right?
optionExplain: The first part is सुप्त, ending in अ.
ए is not what joins here.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so सुप्त + उत्थिते is written सुप्तोत्थिते: risen from sleep.
ओत्थिते is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: सुप्तोत्थिते = सुप्त (asleep) + उत्थिते (risen).

questions.q: Which are named in line 2 of unit 38?
optionExplain: Right: द्विपत्रम्.
Right: एकं पूगम्.
Right: सचूर्णखदिरम्.
Honey is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: Line 2 names a pair of leaves, one pūga, and powder with khadira.

questions.q: Which phrase means in the case of a person who has gone?
optionExplain: That is accusative: a person who has gone, as an object.
That is nominative: the person who has gone, as subject.
That is dative: for the person gone.
Right: A participle in the locative with a noun in the locative, as भुक्ते मानवे.
questions.explain: The pattern of भुक्ते मानवे gives गते मानवे.
questions.rule: Locative participle + locative noun = in the case of X.
questions.teaches: Participle and noun both in the locative mean in the case of a person who has done it.

questions.q: Line 2 of unit 39 calls even a long life censured when what is lacking?
options: The means are not at hand
Children are not near at hand
Friends are not near at hand
Health is not near at hand
optionExplain: Right: असन्निहितसाधनम्: having no means at hand.
Children are not mentioned in the line.
Friends are not mentioned in the line.
Health is not mentioned in the line.
questions.explain: The line says a long life is censured if the means are not at hand.
questions.rule: दीर्घ आयु also निन्दित without साधन.

questions.q: Put the five parts of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line reads censured, long, even, life, having no means at hand.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: निन्दित = censured; दीर्घ = long; आयुः = life; साधन = means.
questions.teaches: साधन is the means; असन्निहित-साधन is a bahuvrīhi: having no means at hand.

questions.q: Which split of दीर्घमप्यायुः is right?
optionExplain: मप्य is not a word.
Right: म् joins the next vowel, and इ + आ gives या: अपि + आयुः → अप्यायुः.
अप्य is not a word of the card.
यायुः is not a word.
questions.explain: दीर्घमप्यायुः = दीर्घम् (long) + अपि (even) + आयुः (life).

questions.q: The word for 'life' in line 2 of unit 39 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आयुः, the last member of दीर्घमप्यायुः, means life.
questions.teaches: आयुः = life.

questions.q: What does अप्राप्तधनः (like असन्निहितसाधनम्) mean?
options: One who has already obtained wealth
One whose wealth is not obtained
optionExplain: The prefix अ- negates, so it is the opposite.
That would be प्राप्तधनम्.
Right: अ- negates: अप्राप्त + धन, a bahuvrīhi, one whose wealth is not obtained.
No giving is in the word.
questions.explain: असन्निहितसाधनम् = a-sannihita-sādhanam, having no means at hand; अप्राप्तधनः has the same shape.
questions.rule: अ- + participle + noun = one whose X is not ... .
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi with negative अ- describes one whose thing is not present or obtained.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse name for one who desires wealth?
optionExplain: Not named in the verse.
Not named in the verse.
Not named in the verse.
Right: कृषिम् is the first item of the list.
questions.explain: The list begins with कृषिं वणिज्यां गोरक्षाम्: agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping.
questions.rule: धनार्थी resorts to कृषि, वणिज्या, गोरक्षा, a virtuous king.

questions.q: Put the four things to resort to in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping, a virtuous king.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'agriculture' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters)?
questions.explain: कृषिम् (accusative) is the first thing the wealth-seeker resorts to.
questions.teaches: Each item of the list stands in the accusative (कृषिम्, वणिज्याम्, गोरक्षाम्) because it is what one resorts to (संश्रयेत्).

questions.q: Which is the right split of गोरक्षामुपायैः?
optionExplain: Right: Final म् takes the next vowel: म् + उ gives मु.
मुपायैः is not a word.
आमुपायैः is not a word.
A visarga would not turn into म.
questions.explain: गोरक्षाम् (cattle-keeping, accusative) + उपायैः (by means).
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel: the म् joins the vowel (गोरक्षाम् + उपायैः = गोरक्षामुपायैः).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sense of the verse: who, what he does, and the two objects described.
questions.rule: धनार्थी = one desiring wealth; संश्रयेत् = should resort to; गुणिनम् = virtuous; क्रियाम् = activity, occupation.

questions.q: Built like धनार्थी, what does विद्यार्थी mean?
optionExplain: The ending -अर्थी is about wanting, not giving.
Right: -अर्थी at the end of a compound means one who desires the first part.
That would not name a person who wants something.
Nothing in the ending means 'without'.
questions.explain: धन-अर्थी is 'one desiring wealth'; विद्या-अर्थी in the same way is 'one desiring knowledge'.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -अर्थी names the person who desires the first part (धनार्थी, विद्यार्थी).

questions.q: What does मुक्तवेगः say about the person?
options: He is carried by the urges
optionExplain: मुक्त does not mean hidden.
Nothing like this is in the word.
Right: मुक्त = released and वेग = urge.
मुक्त means freed from, not carried by.
questions.explain: मुक्तवेगः is a compound: the one who has released the urges.
questions.rule: मुक्त-वेगः = one who has released the urges.

questions.q: Match each readable word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are readable in the print.
questions.rule: मुक्तवेगः = having released the urges; पाणिना = with the hand; निष्क्रामेत् = should go out; वेग = urge.

questions.q: Which part of this unit does the card mark as unreadable?
optionExplain: This is clear: should go out.
This is clear: with the hand.
This is clear: having released the urges.
Right: गमनखमाहारसमास्त्रियः has no reading.
questions.explain: Only the second word of line 1 is garbled; the card builds on the clear words only.
questions.rule: Where the print is garbled, the card says so and nothing is built on it.
questions.teaches: When a word is garbled in the print, the card marks it and the questions use only the readable words.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निष्क्रामेद्देव-?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् becomes द् before the voiced द: त् + द gives द्द.
A visarga would not give द्द.
That would not end the verb in -एत्.
द्देव is not a word.
questions.explain: निष्क्रामेत् (should go out) + देव- (the first member of the last compound).
questions.rule: त् + voiced consonant → द्: निष्क्रामेत् + देव = निष्क्रामेद्देव.

questions.q: Put these three readable parts in the order of the unit.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins with the released urges; line 2 has the hand and then the going out.

questions.q: Built like मुक्तवेगः, what does मुक्तक्रोधः mean?
options: One who is full of anger
One who has let go of anger
One who is about to be angry
optionExplain: मुक्त means released, not filled.
Right: मुक्त-X at the start of a bahuvrīhi names one who has released X.
A bahuvrīhi names the person, not the anger.
Nothing like 'about to' is in the word.
questions.explain: Like मुक्त-वेगः, one who has released the urges, मुक्त-क्रोधः is one who has released anger.
questions.rule: मुक्त-X = one who has released X.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi that begins with मुक्त names the one who has released the second member (मुक्तवेगः, मुक्तक्रोधः).

questions.q: How far ahead does the verse say one should look while walking?
optionExplain: The verse limits the sight, it does not extend it.
The verse names a measure, a yoke's length, not the ground.
Right: युगमात्रदृक् means looking a yoke's length ahead.
Nothing like this is in the verse.
questions.explain: युगमात्र-दृक् is looking only a yoke's length ahead.
questions.rule: युगमात्रदृक् = looking a yoke's length ahead.

questions.q: Put the three things for the night walk in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the staff, the head-dress and the companion in this order.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्यधिके?
optionExplain: त्यधिके is not a word.
आति is not a word in the verse; the verse has अति.
यधिके is not a word.
Right: अ + अ gives आ in चाति; इ before अ becomes य् in त्यधि.
questions.explain: च (and) + अति (exceedingly) + अधिके (pressing, in a task).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ (च + अति = चाति); इ + अ → य (ति + अधि = त्यधि).
questions.teaches: Two sandhi meet here: अ + अ gives आ, and इ before a different vowel becomes य्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word is a describing word for the walker.
questions.rule: सातपत्रपदत्राणः, युगमात्रदृक्, दंडी and सहायवान् all describe the walker.

questions.q: A task at night is exceedingly pressing. What does the verse give the walker?
options: A lamp, a drum and a dog
A staff alone, going without company
optionExplain: Right: That is line 2.
That is line 1, not the night rule.
None of these is named.
The verse names a companion.
questions.explain: At night, when the business is exceedingly pressing, the verse names a staff, a head-dress and a companion.
questions.rule: रात्रि + अत्यधिक कार्य: दंडी, मौली, सहायवान्.

questions.q: Built like सातपत्र (with an umbrella), what does सपुस्तकः छात्रः mean?
options: A student who gives a book
optionExplain: स- means with, not without.
Right: स- at the start of a bahuvrīhi means 'with'.
A bahuvrīhi describes the person, not a book.
Nothing in स- means giving.
questions.explain: स-पुस्तकः is 'with a book', as सातपत्र is 'with an umbrella'.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi that begins with स- (सातपत्र…) describes someone who has X with him.

questions.q: When does the verse say one should go about covered?
optionExplain: By day the verse says not with the head covered.
Midday is not named in this unit.
Right: रात्रौ पर्यटेत् is paired with प्रावृत्य.
Dawn is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The verse says to go about covered at night, and by day not with the head covered.
questions.rule: रात्रौ प्रावृत्य; अहनि न प्रावृत्य शिरः.

questions.q: Put these phrases of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: having covered, one should roam, at night, not having covered the head, by day.
questions.rule: प्रावृत्य पर्यटेत् · रात्रौ · न प्रावृत्य शिरः · अहनि.

questions.q: Which gives the join in शिरोऽहनि?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give शिरेऽहनि.
आ + अ would give शिराहनि.
हनि is not the word here; the word is अहनि.
Right: अः + अ gives ओ followed by an avagraha (ऽ).
questions.explain: शिरः (head) + अहनि (by day).
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ, before अ, becomes ओ and the following अ is shown by ऽ (शिरः + अहनि = शिरोऽहनि).

questions.q: A translation says: 'At night go about covered; by day, with the head covered.' What is wrong?
options: By day the verse says not
At night the verse says uncovered
The verse speaks of evening, not night
optionExplain: Right: न प्रावृत्य शिरः अहनि.
The verse says covered at night.
पर्यटेत् is a verb of going about.
The word is रात्रौ, at night.
questions.explain: The day rule has न: by day one should not go with the head covered.
questions.rule: अहनि = by day; न प्रावृत्य शिरः = not with the head covered.

questions.q: Which does line 2 of this unit name?
optionExplain: भस्म.
तुष.
अशुचि.
That is in unit 44.
Not named.
questions.explain: Line 2 names ashes, husks and impure things (after the shadows); gravel is in the next unit.

questions.q: Built like प्रावृत्य, which form means having sat down (from उप + विश्)?
optionExplain: -त्वा goes on a verb without a prefix.
Right: A prefixed verb forms its 'having done' word in -य.
This means 'should sit down'.
This means 'sits down'.
questions.explain: प्रावृत्य (प्र + आ + वृ) ends in -य; the prefixed उप + विश् does likewise: उपविश्य.
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य (प्रावृत्य, उपविश्य); a plain verb takes -त्वा.

questions.q: What must one not do to the ground of gravel, clods, offerings and bathing?
optionExplain: The verb is आक्रमेत्, step upon.
Nothing like sweeping is in the verse.
Right: न आक्रमेत् = should not step upon.
Nothing like digging is in the verse.
questions.explain: आक्रमेत् is should step upon, and न forbids it.
questions.rule: न आक्रमेत् = should not step upon.

questions.q: Put the times of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 names midday, the two twilights, night and midnight.

questions.q: In नाक्रमेच्छर्करा-, what happens to the final त् of आक्रमेत् before श?
optionExplain: That is not how this sandhi works.
द् stands before voiced sounds; श is unvoiced.
न् is for a following nasal.
Right: The त् is replaced by च् and the श by छ.
questions.explain: न + आक्रमेत् + शर्करा joins as नाक्रमेच्छर्करा.
questions.teaches: Final त् before श becomes च् and the श becomes छ (आक्रमेत् + शर्करा = आक्रमेच्छर्करा).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the nouns of the unit.
questions.rule: शर्करा = gravel; लोष्ट = clod; बलि = offering; चतुष्पथम् = crossroads.

questions.q: Which times does line 2 name?
optionExplain: मध्याह्ने.
संध्ययोः.
अर्धरात्रे.

Not named.

optionExplain: That drops the long vowel; the two vowels become one long आ.
