questions.rule: आश्वास्य → विदार्य → शिरःकपालान्याहृत्य → शंकुना गृहीत्वा → अपहरेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 106 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Comfort, split open, remove the skull pieces, seize with a hook, draw away.
questions.rule: आश्वास्य, विदार्य, कपाल, शङ्कु, चुबुक, कक्षा.
questions.teaches: A chain of absolutives (-य, -त्वा) ends in one finite verb: ... गृहीत्वा ... अपहरेत्.

questions.q: By the card, how are maṇḍalāgra and aṅguliśastra identified?
options: Probably a round-tipped knife and a finger-knife
Certainly a saw and a pair of forceps
A hook and a peg, both as standard
optionExplain: Right: The data labels both identifications probable.
Neither a saw nor forceps is named; the labels are probable.
The hook (शङ्कु) is a third instrument of the line.
They are translated, with the label probable.
questions.explain: Maṇḍalāgra: probably a round-tipped knife; aṅguliśastra: probably a finger-knife.

questions.q: Which of these places are named with the hook in unit 106?
optionExplain: Right: चुबुके.
Right: उरसि.
No knee is named in unit 106.
Right: कक्षायाम्.
No navel is named in unit 106.
questions.explain: Chin, chest and armpit are named (with the palate, on a flagged reading).

questions.q: By the rule of कपालानि + आहृत्य, how is वारि + आनय (bring water) joined?
optionExplain: ई comes from इ + इ, not from इ + आ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इ + आ → या, as कपालानि + आहृत्य.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + आ.
The इ does not vanish; it becomes य्.
questions.explain: वारि + आनय = वार्यानय, like कपालानि + आहृत्य = कपालान्याहृत्य.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: कपालानि + आहृत्य → कपालान्याहृत्य.

questions.q: By unit 107, what kind of head does this case have?
optionExplain: Size is not named in unit 107.
A head turned aside is a case of unit 102.
Right: अभिन्नशिरसम्: one whose head is unsplit.
The head here is अभिन्न, not split.
questions.explain: The head here is unsplit.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 107 in the line's order.
questions.explain: One whose head is unsplit, or at the akṣikūṭa, at the cheek, or.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 107 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Unsplit head: at the akṣikūṭa or the cheek.
questions.teaches: अभिन्नशिरसम् is a bahuvrīhi: one whose head (शिरस्) is unsplit (अभिन्न = अ + भिन्न).

questions.q: By the card, what is uncertain about गण्ड here?
options: It may mean chin or the palate
It is a word nobody knows
It is a corrected print reading
It may mean cheek or temple
optionExplain: Chin and palate are named in unit 106, not as senses of गण्ड.
गण्ड is a known word; only its exact part is open.
गंडे is printed and kept; only the sense is open.
Right: The data: gaṇḍa = cheek; it can also mean temple.
questions.explain: गण्ड is taken as cheek, though it may also mean the temple.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 107 are right by the card?
options: The line names the hook (शङ्कु) itself
The line says the skull pieces are removed
Akṣikūṭa is probably the eye-socket rim
The head in this case is unsplit
optionExplain: शङ्कु is in unit 106; it is not printed here.
That is unit 106; here the head is unsplit.
Right: the action is not printed.
Right: the data labels it probable.
Right: अभिन्नशिरसम्.
questions.explain: No verb; the head is unsplit; akṣikūṭa is probably the eye-socket rim.

questions.q: अक्षिकूटे and गण्डे are locatives (at). Which form of हस्त means at the hand?
optionExplain: Right: An अ-stem makes its locative singular in -ए, as गण्ड → गण्डे.
-एन is the instrumental: by the hand (as हस्तेन in unit 105).
-अम् is the accusative: the hand as object.
-अस्य is the genitive: of the hand.
questions.explain: हस्त → हस्ते (at the hand), like गण्ड → गण्डे (at the cheek).
questions.teaches: An अ-stem noun makes its locative singular in -ए: गण्डे, अक्षिकूटे (at).

questions.q: By unit 108, what is cut off for one stuck at the shoulder?
options: The arm, at the shoulder region
Nothing; the arm is only pressed
The fingers of the one hand
optionExplain: No cutting at the neck is named in unit 108.
Right: अंसदेशे बाहुं छित्वा: having cut off the arm at the shoulder region.
The unit says the arm is cut off: छित्वा.
No fingers are named in unit 108.
questions.explain: The arm is cut off at the shoulder region.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 108 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Likewise, for one stuck at the shoulder, cutting the arm at the shoulder region; for one swollen like a skin-bag, splitting the wind-filled belly, casting out the intestines, one should extract it when slack.
questions.rule: अंससंसक्तस्य → बाहुं छित्वा → दृतेरिवाध्मातस्य → उदरमवदार्य → निरस्यान्त्राणि → शिथिलीभूतमाहरेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 108 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Stuck at the shoulder: the arm; swollen like a skin-bag: belly and intestines.
questions.rule: अंस, संसक्त, बाहु, दृति, आध्मात, अन्त्र.
questions.teaches: शिथिलीभूत is a cvi form: शिथिल + ई + भूत, 'become slack' (what was not slack).

questions.q: For the one swollen like a skin-bag, what is split open?
options: The head, to take out skull pieces
The shoulder, to free the arm
optionExplain: Skull pieces are removed in unit 106, not here.
No chest is split in unit 108.
Right: वातपूर्णमुदरमवदार्य: having split open the belly full of wind.
The arm is cut off for the shoulder case, not the swollen one.
questions.explain: The belly, full of wind, is split open and the intestines are cast out.

questions.q: By unit 108, when is the swollen one extracted?
options: Only after the arm is cut
optionExplain: It is extracted once slack, after the belly is opened.
The belly is split and the intestines cast out first.
Cutting the arm is the handling of the shoulder case.
Right: शिथिलीभूतमाहरेत्: one should extract (it) when it has become slack.
questions.explain: After the belly is split and the intestines cast out, it is extracted when slack.

questions.q: By the rule of दृतेः + इव, how is मुनेः + आश्रमः (the sage's hermitage) joined?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ए before a voiced sound (here a vowel) becomes र्, as दृतेः + इव.
Only अः and आः lose the visarga before a vowel; after ए it becomes र्.
ऽ marks a lost अ after ए or ओ; here आ follows, after a visarga.
Before a vowel, ः after ए becomes र्; स् comes before त or थ (optionally before स).
questions.explain: मुनेः + आश्रमः = मुनेराश्रमः, like दृतेः + इव = दृतेरिव.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound: दृतेः + इव → दृतेरिव.

questions.q: By unit 109, what is to be broken (दारयित्वा)?
options: The pieces of the skull bones
The bones of the hip region
The arm at the shoulder region
The belly that is full of wind
optionExplain: Removing the skull pieces (शिरःकपाल) is unit 106, not this line.
Right: जघनकपालानि दारयित्वा: having broken the jaghana-kapāla, the hip-region bones.
Cutting the arm at the shoulder is unit 108, not this line.
Splitting the wind-filled belly is unit 108, not this line.
questions.explain: The jaghana-kapāla, the bones of the hip region, are broken.
questions.rule: जघनकपालानि दारयित्वा = having broken the hip-region bones.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 109 in the line's order.
questions.explain: For the one stuck at the hips, the hip-region bones, having broken; thus (the list ends).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 109 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Jaghana is the hip region; its kapāla are its bones; दारयित्वा = having broken them; इति ends the list.
questions.teaches: कपाल = a plate or bone, as in the skull pieces (शिरःकपाल) of unit 106; jaghana-kapāla = the bones of the hip region (probably the pelvic bones).

questions.q: Which split of दारयित्वेति is right?
optionExplain: ए + इ would give दारयित्वयिति or दारयित्व इति, not दारयित्वेति.
दारयित् is not a form; the absolutive ends in -त्वा: दारयित्वा.
Right: आ + इ → ए: दारयित्वा + इति → दारयित्वेति.
अः + इ would drop the visarga and leave a gap: दारयित्व इति.
questions.explain: दारयित्वा (having broken) + इति (thus): आ + इ → ए.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 109 are right by the card?
options: The line has its own verb 'should extract'
इति closes the list of cases
The line names the cutting instrument
Jaghana-kapāla as the pelvic bones is only probable
optionExplain: No: the verb is not printed; it is carried from unit 108.
Right: the data says the closing इति ends the list.
No instrument is named in unit 109.
Right: the data labels it probable.
questions.explain: इति ends the list; the pelvic-bone sense is probable only; the verb comes from unit 108.
questions.rule: जघनकपालानि दारयित्वा इति: no verb, a closing इति.

questions.q: By the rule of दारयित्वेति, how is महा + इन्द्रः (great Indra) joined?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ or आ + ए or ऐ, not + इ.
No short इ results; आ + इ give ए.
The इ is not lost; आ + इ merge into ए.
Right: आ + इ → ए, as दारयित्वा + इति → दारयित्वेति.
questions.explain: महा + इन्द्रः = महेन्द्रः, like दारयित्वा + इति = दारयित्वेति.
questions.teaches: A final आ followed by इ joins as ए: दारयित्वा + इति → दारयित्वेति.

questions.q: By unit 110, what does भवन्ति चात्र introduce?
options: A new chapter of the book
optionExplain: Right: The data: a formula introducing the verses that follow ('verses' understood).
No teacher is named in this formula.
No chapter opens here; the formula introduces lines within this chapter.
The formula names no drug; it only introduces what follows.
questions.explain: It introduces the verses that follow; the noun itself is understood.
questions.rule: भवन्ति च अत्र = and on this there are (verses).

questions.q: In भवन्ति चात्र, which word is understood but not printed?
optionExplain: The verb is printed: भवन्ति.
Right: Right: 'verses' is the usual understood noun; it is not in the Sanskrit.
'And' is printed: च, inside चात्र.
'Here, on this' is printed: अत्र, inside चात्र.
questions.explain: Only the noun 'verses' is supplied; भवन्ति, च and अत्र are all printed.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 110 to its meaning.
questions.explain: भवन्ति = there are; च = and; अत्र = on this.
questions.teaches: भवन्ति is plural, so the understood noun is plural too: (verses).

questions.q: Which split of चात्र is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give चेऽत्र, with ए kept and ऽ.
अः + अ would give चोऽत्र, not चात्र.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.
चा and त्र are not the words; the particle is च and the adverb is अत्र.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 110 are right by the card?
options: The noun 'verses' is understood, not printed
optionExplain: Right: 3rd person plural present of √भू.
No: it only introduces what follows.
Right: the data shows it in brackets.
No: अत्र = here, on this.
questions.explain: A plural verb with an understood plural noun; no teaching of its own.

questions.q: By the rule of चात्र, how is तत्र + अपि (there too) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
The two अ do not shrink to one short अ; they give long आ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अत्र → चात्र.
questions.explain: तत्र + अपि = तत्रापि, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as long आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.

questions.q: By unit 111, whom should one protect from injury?
optionExplain: Right: रक्षेज्जननीं च क्षततः: and one should protect the mother from injury.
The physician is the one who acts; the line protects the mother.
No attendants are named in unit 111.
The stuck limb is cut and removed, not protected.
questions.explain: The mother (जननी) is to be protected from injury.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 111 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Whatever limb, by the power of vāyu, of the fetus gets stuck, piecemeal; having cut that and that, remove it properly, and protect the mother from injury.
questions.rule: यद्यद्वायुवशादंगं → सज्जेद्गर्भस्य खंडशः → तत्तच्छित्वा → हरेत्सम्यग् → रक्षेज्जननीं च क्षततः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 111 to its meaning.
questions.explain: A stuck limb is cut and properly removed, and the mother is guarded from injury.
questions.rule: अङ्ग, सज्जेत्, छित्वा, सम्यक्, जननी, क्षततः.
questions.teaches: यद्यत् ... तत्तत् = whatever ... that and that: each such limb is cut and removed.

questions.q: Which split of तत्तच्छित्वा is right?
optionExplain: त् + च gives च्च: तच्चित्वा, not तच्छित्वा.
Right: त् + छ → च्छ: तत् + छित्वा → तच्छित्वा.
तत्त is not a word; the pronoun तत् is said twice.
ततः before त would give ततस्तत्, not तत्तत्.
questions.explain: तत् तत् (that and that) + छित्वा (having cut; spelling of छित्त्वा): त् + छ → च्छ.

questions.q: A limb of the fetus is stuck by vāyu. What does unit 111 tell the physician?
options: Wait until the vāyu frees the limb
Pull the whole fetus out in one piece
Cut it away, protecting the mother
Leave it be, attend only to the mother
optionExplain: The line does not say to wait; it says to cut and remove.
The line says to cut the stuck limb, not to pull it whole.
Right: तत्तच्छित्वा हरेत् ... रक्षेज्जननीम्: cut, remove, guard the mother.
The limb is to be cut and removed, and the mother guarded.
questions.explain: Cut the stuck limb, remove it properly, and protect the mother from injury.

questions.q: By the rule of रक्षेज्जननीम् (रक्षेत् + जननीम्), how is पठेत् + जनः joined?
optionExplain: Before ज the त् does not stop at द्; it becomes ज्.
त् does not stay unchanged before ज.
ञ् is a nasal; before ज the त् becomes ज्, not a nasal.
Right: त् + ज → ज्ज, as रक्षेत् + जननीम् → रक्षेज्जननीम्.
questions.explain: पठेत् + जनः = पठेज्जनः, like रक्षेत् + जननीम् = रक्षेज्जननीम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before ज becomes ज्: रक्षेत् + जननीम् → रक्षेज्जननीम्.

questions.q: By unit 112, with what is the woman sprinkled?
optionExplain: Right: सिञ्चेदुष्णेन वारिणा: should sprinkle with warm water.
The water is warm (उष्णेन), not cold.
The line names water (वारि), not milk.
Oil and ghee are not named in unit 112.
questions.explain: She is sprinkled with warm water.

questions.q: Put the quarters of the verse in unit 112 in order.
questions.explain: Then the placenta not falling, the physician should make fall as before; and thus her from whom the śalya is drawn out, he should sprinkle with warm water.
questions.rule: अथापतंतीमपरां → पातयेत्पूर्ववद्भिषक् → एवं निर्हृतशल्यां च → सिंचेदुष्णेन वारिणा.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 112 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The physician makes the placenta fall as before, then sprinkles the woman with warm water.
questions.teaches: पातयेत् is the causative of √पत् (fall): 'should make (it) fall'.

questions.q: Which split of पूर्ववद्भिषक् is right?
optionExplain: वद्भिषक् is not a word; the words are पूर्ववत् (as before) and भिषक्.
Right: त् before a voiced sound becomes द्: पूर्ववत् + भिषक् → पूर्ववद्भिषक्.
अः before a voiced sound would give पूर्ववो भिषक्.
A following vowel would give पूर्ववदभिषक्, with अ.
questions.explain: पूर्ववत् (as before) + भिषक् (physician): त् + voiced sound → द्.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 112 are right by the card?
options: The unit names the earlier procedure meant by 'as before'
The unit defines śalya here as the placenta
The one sprinkled is a woman
optionExplain: Right: भिषक् is the nominative subject of पातयेत्.
No: the unit does not say which procedure.
No: śalya is not defined; the context only suggests.
Right: the feminine accusative निर्हृतशल्याम् shows the woman.
questions.explain: The physician acts; the woman (feminine accusative) is sprinkled; 'as before' and śalya stay open.

questions.q: By the rule of सिञ्चेदुष्णेन (सिञ्चेत् + उष्णेन), how is पिबेत् + उदकम् joined?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् does not stay unvoiced; it becomes द्.
The उ of उदकम् stays short; nothing lengthens it.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as सिञ्चेत् + उष्णेन → सिञ्चेदुष्णेन.
च्च arises before च, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: पिबेत् + उदकम् = पिबेदुदकम्, like सिञ्चेत् + उष्णेन = सिञ्चेदुष्णेन.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: सिञ्चेत् + उष्णेन → सिञ्चेदुष्णेन.

questions.q: By unit 113, what is placed in the yoni?
options: A swab of oil or fat
optionExplain: Milk and cloth are not named in unit 113.
No powder or salt is named in unit 113.
The swab is of sneha, not dry; its material is not stated.
Right: योनौ स्नेहपिचुम्: a swab of sneha (oil or fat) in the yoni.
questions.explain: A swab (picu) of sneha (oil or fat).

questions.q: Put the quarters of the verse in unit 113 in order.
questions.explain: One should give, to her whose body is anointed, in the yoni a swab of sneha, then; by that the yoni becomes soft, and her pain subsides.
questions.rule: दद्यादभ्यक्तदेहायै → योनौ स्नेहपिचुं ततः → योनिर्मृदुर्भवेत्तेन → शूलं चास्याः प्रशाम्यति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 113 to its meaning.
questions.explain: After anointing, a swab of sneha makes the yoni soft and the pain subside.
questions.teaches: अभ्यक्तदेहायै is a bahuvrīhi in the dative: 'to her whose body is anointed'.

questions.q: Which split of योनिर्मृदुर्भवेत् is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after इ or उ becomes र् before a voiced sound: योनिर्, मृदुर्.
Long ई and ऊ give no र्; the र् comes from a visarga.
म् before a consonant would be written ं: योनिं मृदुं.
ए and ओ before a consonant stay as they are; no र् would appear.
questions.explain: योनिः (the yoni) + मृदुः (soft) + भवेत् (becomes): इः, उः + voiced sound → इर्, उर्.
questions.rule: इः / उः + voiced sound → इर् / उर्.

questions.q: By unit 113, what two results come from the swab?
options: The placenta falls and fever goes
Soft yoni, and her pain subsides
The fetus turns and comes out
Her skin glows and she gains weight
optionExplain: Neither result is said of the swab in unit 113.
Right: योनिर्मृदुर्भवेत्तेन शूलं चास्याः प्रशाम्यति.
The swab follows delivery; no turning is named.
Skin and weight are not named in unit 113.
questions.explain: By the swab the yoni becomes soft and her pain subsides.

questions.q: By the rule of मृदुर्भवेत् (मृदुः + भवेत्), how is गुरुः + वदति (the teacher speaks) joined?
optionExplain: The visarga drops with lengthening only before र्, not before व.
A visarga becomes श् before च or छ (optionally before श), not before व.
Right: A visarga after उ before a voiced sound becomes र्, as मृदुः + भवेत् → मृदुर्भवेत्.
Before a voiced sound the visarga after उ does not stay; it becomes र्.
questions.explain: गुरुः + वदति = गुरुर्वदति, like मृदुः + भवेत् = मृदुर्भवेत्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound: मृदुः + भवेत् → मृदुर्भवेत्.

questions.q: By unit 114, with what is the powder (चूर्ण) to be taken?
optionExplain: Water is not named in unit 114.
Milk is not named in unit 114.
Honey is not named in unit 114.
Right: चूर्णं स्नेहेन: the powder with sneha, oil or fat.
questions.explain: The powder is given with sneha (oil or fat).

questions.q: Put these pieces of unit 114 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Dīpyaka, ativiṣā, rāsnā (printed रास्त्रा), hiṅgu, elā, the pañcakolakas; powder with sneha, or paste, or decoction; one should make her drink likewise.
questions.rule: दीप्यकातिविषा → रास्त्रा → हिं ग्वेलापंचकोलकान् → चूर्णं स्नेहेन → कल्कं वा काथं वा → पाययेत्तथा.

questions.q: Match each name of unit 114 to the card's identification.
pairs: a group of five (not named here)
questions.explain: Plant names keep the data's labels; pañcakolaka is a group whose members this line does not name.
questions.teaches: Dīpyaka is only probably ajwain; ativiṣā and elā are standard identifications.

questions.q: Which split of दीप्यकातिविषा is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: दीप्यक + अतिविषा → दीप्यकातिविषा.
अः + अ would give दीप्यकोऽतिविषा.
ई + अ would give दीप्यक्यतिविषा.
कातिविषा is not a drug name; the names are दीप्यक and अतिविषा.
questions.explain: दीप्यक + अतिविषा: अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 114 are right by the card?
options: Rāsnā here rests on a conjectural reading
The line names the five members of the pañcakolaka
The line does not say which form is preferred
Dīpyaka as ajwain is a standard identification
optionExplain: Right: printed रास्त्रा is read रास्ना on a conjecture.
No: the five are not named in this line.
Right: powder, paste or decoction, none preferred.
No: the data labels it probable.
questions.explain: Rāsnā is conjectural, the pañcakolaka members are unnamed, no form is preferred, dīpyaka is probable.
questions.rule: Labels and readings exactly as the data gives them.

questions.q: By the rule of चूर्णं स्नेहेन, how is जलम् + पिबेत् (should drink water) written in a sentence?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced sound, not from अम्.
Right: A final म् before a consonant is written ं, as चूर्णम् + स्नेहेन → चूर्णं स्नेहेन.
The म् is not dropped with a lengthened vowel.
The ending is म्, not a visarga.
questions.explain: जलम् + पिबेत् = जलं पिबेत्, like चूर्णम् + स्नेहेन = चूर्णं स्नेहेन.
questions.teaches: Inside a sentence a final म् before a consonant is written as anusvāra: चूर्णं स्नेहेन.

questions.q: By unit 115, which purpose is stated in the line?
optionExplain: Bleeding is not named in unit 115.
Growth of the fetus is not named in unit 115.
Right: वेदनोपशमाय: for the relief of pain.
Sleep is not named in unit 115.
questions.explain: One stated purpose is the relief of pain.
questions.rule: वेदना + उपशमाय = for the relief of pain.

questions.q: Put these pieces of unit 115 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Kaṭukā, ativiṣā, pāṭhā, śāka bark, hiṅgu (printed घिगु), tejanī; and likewise, for the flowing off of the doṣa and for the relief of pain.
questions.rule: कटुकातिविषापाठा → शाकत्वग्घिगु → तेजनीः → तद्वच्च → दोषस्यंदार्थं → वेदनोपशमायच.

questions.q: Match each name of unit 115 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: Each name keeps the data's label; तद्वत् = likewise, in the same way as unit 114.
questions.teaches: Kaṭukā (kutki) is standard; pāṭhā (velvetleaf) is probable; tejanī (not asked) is disputed.

questions.q: Which split of तद्वच्च is right?
optionExplain: तद्व is not a word; the adverb is तद्वत् (likewise).
A visarga before च would give तद्वश्च.
म् before च would be written ं: तद्वं च.
Right: त् + च → च्च: तद्वत् + च → तद्वच्च.
questions.explain: तद्वत् (likewise) + च (and): त् + च → च्च.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 115 are right by the card?
options: The line has its own verb
शाकत्वक् may be one item or two
The line names the doṣa that flows off
हिङ्गु here rests on a conjectural reading
optionExplain: No: 'make her drink' is carried from unit 114.
Right: teak bark, or śāka and tvak; the data leaves it open.
No: the doṣa is not specified.
Right: printed घिगु is read हिङ्गु on a conjecture.
questions.explain: The line has no verb, names no doṣa, and leaves śāka-tvak and hiṅgu open.

questions.q: By the rule of तद्वच्च (तद्वत् + च), how is एतत् + च (and this) joined?
optionExplain: Right: त् + च → च्च, as तद्वत् + च → तद्वच्च.
Before च the त् becomes च्, not द्.
त् does not stay unchanged before च.
श्च comes from a visarga before च, not from त्.
questions.explain: एतत् + च = एतच्च, like तद्वत् + च = तद्वच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: तद्वत् + च → तद्वच्च.

questions.q: By unit 116, what should she drink in the evening (सायम्)?
optionExplain: Milk and ghee are not named in unit 116.
Right: सायं पिबेदरिष्टं च तथा सुकृतमासवम्.
Śirīṣa is unit 117, and there it is for swabs, not a drink.
Water and salt are not named in unit 116.
questions.explain: In the evening: ariṣṭa, and likewise a well-made āsava.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 116 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Thus three nights, seven days; then she should drink sneha alone; in the evening ariṣṭa, and likewise a well-made āsava.
questions.rule: त्रिरात्रमेवं → सप्ताहं → स्नेहमेव ततः पिबेत् → सायं पिबेदरिष्टं च → तथा सुक्कृतमासवं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 116 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two periods, sneha alone, and evening drinks of ariṣṭa and a well-made āsava.
questions.teaches: An accusative of time gives duration: त्रिरात्रम् 'for three nights', सप्ताहम् 'for seven days'.

questions.q: Which split of पिबेदरिष्टम् is right?
optionExplain: पिबेद is not a form; the optative is पिबेत्.
एः before a vowel would give पिबेररिष्टम्, with र्.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: पिबेत् + अरिष्टम् → पिबेदरिष्टम्.
The drink is अरिष्ट; त् + र would not give दर.
questions.explain: पिबेत् (should drink) + अरिष्टम् (ariṣṭa): त् + vowel → द्.

questions.q: A reader takes the two periods of unit 116 as alternatives. What does the card say?
options: Right: वा is printed between them
No: they must add up to ten days
No: the seven days come first
The line has no 'or'; it is open
optionExplain: No वा (or) is printed between the two periods.
Nothing in the line adds the periods together.
The line prints त्रिरात्रम् first, and states no sequence.
Right: The data: no 'or' or 'and'; the relation is not settled.
questions.explain: The two periods stand side by side; whether alternatives or successive is not stated.
questions.rule: त्रिरात्रम् एवम् सप्ताहम्: no वा, no च.

questions.q: By the rule of स्नेहमेव (स्नेहम् + एव), how is फलम् + एव (only the fruit) joined?
optionExplain: Right: A final म् joins the following vowel, as स्नेहम् + एव → स्नेहमेव.
Before a vowel the म् is not written ं; it joins the vowel.
The म् is not dropped before a vowel.
The vowel ए stays ए; nothing makes it ऐ.
questions.explain: फलम् + एव = फलमेव, like स्नेहम् + एव = स्नेहमेव.
questions.rule: म् + vowel → म joined to the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel is joined to it: स्नेहम् + एव → स्नेहमेव.

questions.q: By unit 117, the decoction for the swabs is of which two trees?
optionExplain: Devadāru and candana are not named in unit 117.
Right: शिरीषककुभक्वाथपिचून्: swabs of the decoction of śirīṣa and kakubha.
Kaṭukā and pāṭhā are drugs to drink in unit 115, not these swabs.
Neither tree is named in unit 117.
questions.explain: Śirīṣa (siris) and kakubha (arjuna).

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 117 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Swabs of the śirīṣa-kakubha decoction, and in the yoni one should place; and whatever other complications there may be, those one should treat each by its own.
questions.rule: शिरीषककुभकाथपिचून् → योनौ च निक्षिपेत् → उपद्रवाश्च येऽन्ये स्युः → तान्यथास्वमुपाचरेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 117 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Swabs of the siris-arjuna decoction go in; other complications are treated each by its own.
questions.teaches: यथास्वम् = each according to its own: every complication is treated in its own way.

questions.q: Which split of येऽन्ये is right?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give योऽन्ये.
अ + अ would give यान्ये.
Right: ए + अ → एऽ: the अ of अन्ये is dropped and marked ऽ.
न्ये is not a word; the word is अन्ये (others).
questions.explain: ये (which) + अन्ये (other): ए + अ → एऽ.

questions.q: Another complication arises after all this. What does unit 117 say?
options: Repeat the swabs of śirīṣa and kakubha
Leave it alone; it will pass with time
Give only sneha for seven more days
Treat each according to its own
optionExplain: The swabs are one measure; other complications are treated each by its own.
The line says to treat (उपाचरेत्), not to leave it.
Unit 117 says nothing of sneha or of days.
Right: उपद्रवाश्च येऽन्ये स्युस्तान्यथास्वमुपाचरेत्.
questions.explain: Whatever other complications there are: treat each according to its own.

questions.q: By the rule of उपद्रवाश्च (उपद्रवाः + च), how is बालाः + च (and the children) joined?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as उपद्रवाः + च → उपद्रवाश्च.
आः drops its visarga before a voiced sound or a vowel; before च it becomes श्.
Before च the visarga becomes श्, not स्.
The च stays च; only the visarga changes.
questions.explain: बालाः + च = बालाश्च, like उपद्रवाः + च = उपद्रवाश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: उपद्रवाः + च → उपद्रवाश्च.

questions.q: By unit 118, for how long is the food cooked with Vāta-removing (ones) beneficial?
optionExplain: Seven days (सप्ताहम्) belong to unit 116, not this food.
Right: दशाहं भोजने हितम्: beneficial in the meal for ten days.
Three nights (त्रिरात्रम्) belong to unit 116.
Four months are named in unit 119, not here.
questions.explain: For ten days (दशाहम्).

questions.q: Put these printed pieces of unit 118 in order.
questions.explain: Cooked (mostly) with Vāta-removing (ones), for ten days beneficial in the meal; and rasa for ten days; then (or: excellent) light, (wholesome,) little food.
questions.rule: प्रयो वातहरैः सिद्धं → दशांहं भोजने हितं → रसो दशांहं च → परं → लघुपद्व्याल्पभोजना.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 118 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Food cooked with Vāta-removing (ones) is beneficial in the meal; rasa is also given.
questions.teaches: दशाहम् = दश + अहम्, 'for ten days': the accusative gives the duration.

questions.q: Which split of दशाहम् (printed दशांहं) is right?
optionExplain: म् before a vowel would give दशमहम्.
अः + अ would give दशोऽहम्.
Right: अ + अ → आ: दश (ten) + अहम् (day) → दशाहम्.
हम् is not a word; the word for day is अहन्, here अहम्.
questions.explain: दश (ten) + अहम् (day): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: By unit 118, what is said of the rasa?
options: A meat soup, given for seven days
Forbidden until four months have passed
Given for three nights, then stopped
Ten days; its kind is not stated
optionExplain: The kind is not stated, and the period is ten days.
Nothing forbids it; rasa is given for ten days.
The period named is ten days, not three nights.
Right: रसो दशाहं च: rasa for ten days; the kind is not given.
questions.explain: Rasa is given for ten days; the line does not say which rasa.

questions.q: By the rule of रसो दशाहम् (रसः + दशाहम्), how is नरः + वदति (the man speaks) joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced sound becomes ओ, as रसः + दशाहम् → रसो दशाहम्.
The visarga drops after आः, not after अः; अः becomes ओ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
A visarga becomes श् before च or छ (optionally before श), not before व.
questions.explain: नरः + वदति = नरो वदति, like रसः + दशाहम् = रसो दशाहम्.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: रसः + दशाहम् → रसो दशाहम्.

questions.q: By unit 119, which oil heads the oils she should use?
optionExplain: Sesame oil is not named in unit 119.
Right: बलातैलादिकान्: oils beginning with balā oil.
Castor oil is not named in unit 119.
Mustard oil is not named in unit 119.
questions.explain: Oils beginning with balā oil.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 119 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Intent on sweating and anointing, oils beginning with balā oil she should use; after four months, she, gradually, and pleasant (ones).
questions.rule: स्वेदाभ्यंगपरा → स्नेहान् बलातैलादिकान् → भजेत् → ऊर्ध्वं चतुर्भ्यो मासेभ्यः → सा क्रमेण सुखानि च.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 119 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Intent on sweating and anointing, she uses oils beginning with balā oil.
questions.teaches: -आदिक 'beginning with': बलातैलादिकान् = oils beginning with balā oil; the others are not named.

questions.q: Which split of स्वेदाभ्यङ्ग is right?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give स्वेदोऽभ्यङ्ग.
ए + अ would give स्वेदेऽभ्यङ्ग.
Right: अ + अ → आ: स्वेद + अभ्यङ्ग → स्वेदाभ्यङ्ग.
भ्यङ्ग is not a word; the word is अभ्यङ्ग (anointing).
questions.explain: स्वेद (sweating) + अभ्यङ्ग (anointing): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 119 are right by the card?
options: She should use balā oil only, nothing else
Balā oil is taught later, in units 120 and 121
The second line has no verb of its own
The line states what she does after four months
optionExplain: No: -आदिक means 'beginning with'; other oils are meant.
Right: 120 announces it, 121 gives the recipe.
Right: the data calls it elliptical and incomplete.
No: that line is incomplete; no verb is printed.
questions.explain: Oils beginning with balā oil; its recipe follows; the second line is incomplete.

questions.q: स्वेदाभ्यङ्गपरा is feminine (she, intent on ...). How would a man intent on study, as subject, be said?
optionExplain: -परा is feminine, as in स्वेदाभ्यङ्गपरा; a man needs -परः.
-परम् is neuter, or masculine accusative; the subject needs -परः.
-पराः is plural; one man needs the singular -परः.
Right: The final -पर agrees with the person: masculine nominative singular -परः.
questions.explain: अध्ययनपरः, like स्वेदाभ्यङ्गपरा, but masculine.
questions.rule: -पर at the end of a compound takes the gender, number and case of the person.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -पर ('intent on') agrees with the person: स्वेदाभ्यङ्गपरा (she), अध्ययनपरः (he).

questions.q: By unit 120, what will be taught next?
optionExplain: Right: बलातैलमुपदेक्ष्यामः: we shall teach balā oil.
No ghee is announced in unit 120.
Śirīṣa decoction belongs to unit 117, not this announcement.
Ariṣṭa belongs to unit 116, not this announcement.
questions.explain: Balātaila, the oil of balā.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 120 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Now, balā oil, we shall teach.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 120 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Now we shall teach the oil of balā.
questions.teaches: बलातैल = बला + तैल, the oil of balā (country mallow).

questions.q: What form is उपदेक्ष्यामः?
optionExplain: -स्यामः/-क्ष्यामः is not a present ending, and 'they' would be 3rd person.
Right: The data: 1st person plural future of उप-√दिश्.
An optative 'one should teach' would be उपदिशेत्, not -क्ष्यामः.
-क्ष्यामः marks the future, not the past.
questions.explain: उपदेक्ष्यामः = we shall teach: future, 1st person plural.

questions.q: Where does the book give the recipe that unit 120 announces?
optionExplain: Unit 119 only names balā oil among the oils to use.
The recipe follows at once, in unit 121.
Right: The data: the opening formula of the recipe in card 121.
Unit 116 is about sneha, ariṣṭa and āsava.
questions.explain: The recipe follows in unit 121.
questions.rule: अथ ... उपदेक्ष्यामः → recipe in the next unit.

questions.q: By the pattern of उपदेक्ष्यामः, what does वक्ष्यामः (from √वच्, speak) mean?
optionExplain: That would be a present form, not -क्ष्यामः.
'They will speak' is वक्ष्यन्ति; -मः marks 'we'.
-क्ष्यामः marks the future, not the past.
Right: -क्ष्यामः = future, 1st person plural, as in उपदेक्ष्यामः.
questions.explain: वक्ष्यामः = we shall speak, like उपदेक्ष्यामः = we shall teach.
questions.teaches: The ending -स्यामः (here -क्ष्यामः) makes a future 'we shall': उपदेक्ष्यामः, वक्ष्यामः.

questions.q: By unit 121, how many parts of balā-root decoction are taken?
optionExplain: Right: बलामूलकषायस्य भागाः षट्: six parts.
The line says six (षट्), not four.
The line says six (षट्), not ten.
One part (भागः) is of the yava-kola-kulattha-daśamūla decoction.
questions.explain: Six parts of balā-root decoction, and just as many of milk.

questions.q: Put these steps of the balātaila recipe (unit 121) in the line's order.
questions.explain: Six parts of balā-root decoction; as many of milk; a part of the yava-kola-kulattha-daśamūla decoction; adding the fine powders; preparing slowly on a gentle fire; storing well guarded in a good vessel.
questions.rule: षट् भाग → पयस् → यव... क्वाथ → चूर्ण → मृदु अग्नि → सुभाजन.

questions.q: Match each drug of unit 121 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: Each name keeps the data's label.
questions.teaches: In this recipe each drug keeps its own label: standard, probable, disputed or unidentified.

questions.q: Which split of मृद्वग्निना is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give मृदाग्निना.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: मृदु + अग्निना → मृद्वग्निना.
ओ + अ would give मृदोऽग्निना.
वग्निना is not a word; the word is अग्नि (fire).
questions.explain: मृदु (gentle) + अग्निना (with fire): उ + अ → व.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.

questions.q: Which drugs of unit 121 does the card label 'standard'?
optionExplain: Right: standard.
Right: standard.
No: tagara is disputed.
No: madhuka is probable.
questions.explain: Śatāvarī and kuṣṭha are standard; tagara is disputed; madhuka is probable.

questions.q: By the rule of मृद्वग्निना (मृदु + अग्निना), how is मधु + अत्र (honey here) joined?
optionExplain: उ + अ do not give आ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as मृदु + अग्निना → मृद्वग्निना.
A long ऊ comes from उ + उ.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like मृदु + अग्निना = मृद्वग्निना.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व्: मृदु + अग्निना → मृद्वग्निना.

questions.q: By unit 122, by whom is this king of oils approved?
options: The kings who use it daily
optionExplain: Kings are among the users, not the one who approved it.
Sūtikās are among the users, not the approver.
No preparing physician is named as approver.
Right: भगवतो धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः: approved by the venerable Dhanvantari.
questions.explain: It is approved by the venerable Dhanvantari.

questions.q: Put the four ways of using the oil in unit 122 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Drinking, nasal administration, anointing, enema: पाननावनाभ्यंगबस्तिषु.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 122 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Among the users: the emaciated, women recently delivered, infants, the delicate; nāvana is one way of use.
questions.teaches: The users stand in the genitive plural: कृशानाम्, सूतिकानाम्, शिशूनाम्, 'for the emaciated, ...'.

questions.q: Which split of धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ए before a vowel becomes र्: धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः.
ए + अ would give धन्वन्तरेऽभिमतः.
इः + अ would give धन्वन्तरिरभिमतः, with इ.
भिमत is not a word; the word is अभिमत (approved).
questions.explain: धन्वन्तरेः (of Dhanvantari) + अभिमतः (approved): एः + vowel → एर्.

questions.q: Which persons does unit 122 name among those the oil serves?
optionExplain: No: garbhiṇī is not named in unit 122.
Right: सूतिकानाम्.
Right: शिशूनाम्.
No: wrestlers are not named in unit 122.
questions.explain: Sūtikās and infants are named; pregnant women and wrestlers are not.
questions.rule: सूतिकानाम्, शिशूनाम्: for them it is to be used.

questions.q: By the rule of धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः, how is हरेः + आज्ञा (Hari's command) joined?
optionExplain: After ए the visarga does not drop before a vowel; it becomes र्.
Right: A visarga after ए before a vowel becomes र्, as धन्वन्तरेः + अभिमतः.
य् arises from इ before a vowel, not from एः.
The ए of हरेः does not change to ओ.
questions.explain: हरेः + आज्ञा = हरेराज्ञा, like धन्वन्तरेः + अभिमतः = धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a vowel: धन्वन्तरेः + अभिमतः → धन्वन्तरेरभिमतः.

questions.q: By unit 123, which of these does the oil make increase?
optionExplain: Neither sleep nor body weight is named in unit 123.
Neither is named; unit 123 lists strength, memory, ojas and others.
Right: स्मृति and मेधा are both in the list of what increases.
Neither thirst nor sweating is named in unit 123.
questions.explain: Strength, vigour, memory, understanding, intellect, digestive fire, vīrya and ojas increase.

questions.q: Put these things that increase in the order of unit 123.
questions.explain: Strength, manly vigour, memory, (understanding), intellect, digestive fire, (vīrya), ojas.
questions.rule: बल → पौरुष → स्मृति → मेधा → अग्नि → ओजस्.

questions.q: Match each disorder of unit 123 to its modern name on the card.
questions.explain: The data labels all six identifications standard.
questions.rule: पक्षाघात, आक्षेपक, अर्दित, हिध्मा, श्वास, कास.
questions.teaches: …आदि means 'beginning with': पक्षाघात, आक्षेपक and अर्दित head the list of Vāta disorders; gulma, hiccup, breathlessness and cough follow in the same clause.

questions.q: Which split of printed कासानिवर्त्तंते is right?
optionExplain: अः before a voiced sound gives ओ: that would be कासो निवर्तन्ते.
A final ए stays before a consonant: that would be कासे निवर्तन्ते.
इवर्तन्ते is not a verb; the verb is निवर्तन्ते, they cease.
Right: आः drops its visarga before a voiced sound: कासाः + निवर्तन्ते → कासा निवर्तन्ते.
questions.explain: कासाः (coughs, the end of the compound) + निवर्तन्ते (cease).

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 123 by the card?
options: Ojas and vīrya are among what increases
The line calls gulma and cough Vāta disorders
Facial paralysis is among what ceases
The line gives the dose of the oil
optionExplain: Right: …वीर्योजांसि वर्धन्ते.
They are named in the same clause; the line does not call them Vāta disorders.
Right: अर्दित is in the list that ceases.
No dose is given in unit 123.
questions.explain: Eight things increase; Vāta disorders and four others cease.

questions.q: By the rule of कासाः + निवर्तन्ते, how is देवाः + गच्छन्ति (the gods go) joined?
optionExplain: Right: आः drops its visarga before a voiced sound, as कासाः + निवर्तन्ते.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced sound, not from आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
Before a voiced sound आः does not keep its visarga.
questions.explain: देवाः + गच्छन्ति = देवा गच्छन्ति, like कासाः + निवर्तन्ते = कासा निवर्तन्ते.
questions.teaches: A visarga after आ is dropped before a voiced sound: कासाः + निवर्तन्ते → कासा निवर्तन्ते.

questions.q: By unit 124, how often is it used?
optionExplain: The unit says अहरहः, day after day.
Right: अहरहः = day after day.
No such gap is named; it is used day after day.
No such rule is named; it is used day after day.
questions.explain: It is used day after day.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 124 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Day after day, being used, after six months, the swelling, subsides.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 124 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Used day after day, after six months it reaches subsiding: it subsides.
questions.teaches: प्रशमम् एति, literally 'goes to subsiding', means 'subsides'.

questions.q: Which split of अहरहश्चोपयुज्यमानेन is right?
optionExplain: A final म् before च becomes ं, not श्.
A final ए stays before च; no श् would appear.
Right: Visarga + च → श्च, and अ + उ → ओ: च + उप → चोप.
चो and पयुज्यमानेन are not words; the particle is च.
questions.explain: अहरहः (day after day) + च (and) + उपयुज्यमानेन (being used).
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च; अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 124, when does the subsiding come with daily use?
optionExplain: The unit names months, not days: षण्मास.
The unit names six months, not one.
The unit names months, not years.
Right: षण्मासात्: after (or in) six months.
questions.explain: With daily use, it subsides after six months.

questions.q: By the rule of अहरहः + च, how is रामः + च (and Rāma) joined?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as अहरहः + च → अहरहश्च.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
स् comes before त or थ, not before च.
questions.explain: रामः + च = रामश्च, like अहरहः + च = अहरहश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: अहरहः + च → अहरहश्च.

questions.q: By unit 125, what does the barren woman obtain?
options: A long life free of illness
optionExplain: The unit names a son (पुत्रम्), not a daughter.
Right: पुत्रं गुणवन्तम् … लभते.
Twins are not named; one son (पुत्रम्, singular).
Long life is not named in unit 125.
questions.explain: She obtains a son possessed of good qualities.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 125 in the line's order.
questions.explain: And a barren woman, a son, possessed of good qualities (…), obtains, thus.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 125 to its meaning.
questions.explain: A barren woman obtains a son possessed of good qualities.
questions.teaches: गुणवत् = गुण + -वत् (possessing): possessed of good qualities; its accusative is गुणवन्तम्.

questions.q: Which split of printed लभतइति is right?
optionExplain: अ + इ → ए: that would give लभतेति.
That would give लभन्त इति, with न्.
Right: ए before a vowel becomes अय्; the य् is usually dropped, leaving लभत इति.
आ + इ → ए: that would give लभतेति.
questions.explain: लभते (obtains) + इति (thus): the ए becomes अ before the vowel, and a gap stays.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 125 are right by the card?
options: The printed इच्छ्या is a regular form
लभत is the form of लभते before a vowel
optionExplain: The data says it is not a regular form.
Right: the closing इति marks the end.
The oil is understood, not named.
Right: the data says so.
questions.explain: इति closes the statement, and लभत is लभते before a vowel.

questions.q: By the rule of लभते + इति, how is वने + आस्ते (sits in the forest) joined?
optionExplain: That is अ + आ; a final ए does not simply vanish.
ऽ marks a lost short अ after ए; here आ follows.
य + आ comes from इ + आ, not from ए + आ.
Right: ए before a vowel other than अ becomes अय्, the य् usually dropped: वन आस्ते.
questions.explain: वने + आस्ते = वन आस्ते, like लभते + इति = लभत इति.
questions.teaches: A final ए before a vowel other than अ becomes अय्; the य् is usually dropped, leaving अ and a gap.

questions.q: By unit 126, what does this line do?
options: It leads in to the verses after it
It names the oil's main use
It gives a new remedy for the woman
optionExplain: Right: भवन्ति चात्र: and on this there are (these).
No use is named in unit 126.
The colophon comes in unit 135.
No remedy is named in unit 126.
questions.explain: A standard lead-in formula: and on this matter there are these.

questions.q: Which split of चात्र is right?
optionExplain: Neither चा nor त्र is a word here.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.
ए + अ would give चेऽत्र.
That would be written चत्र, with no आ.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here, in this matter).

questions.q: In unit 126 the word for here, in this matter is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चात्र = च + अत्र; अत्र = here, in this matter.
questions.teaches: अत्र means here; in a text, in this matter.

questions.q: How does unit 126 differ from the units right after it?
options: It is a verse in anuṣṭubh
It is the colophon of the chapter
It is a short prose formula
It is a list of drugs and doses
optionExplain: The data marks unit 126 as prose, not a verse.
The colophon is unit 135.
Right: Unit 126 is prose; units 127 to 134 are verses.
No drug or dose is named in unit 126.
questions.explain: Unit 126 is a prose lead-in; the verses follow.
questions.rule: भवन्ति चात्र: prose formula before verses.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 126 are right by the card?
options: The noun after भवन्ति is printed
The verses it leads in to begin at unit 127
It is a standard lead-in formula
It teaches a remedy of its own
optionExplain: It is not printed and not supplied.
Right: it introduces the verses that follow.
Right: and on this matter there are (these).
It teaches nothing of its own.
questions.explain: A standard lead-in to the verses from unit 127.

questions.q: By the rule of च + अत्र → चात्र, how is तत्र + अपि (even there) joined?
optionExplain: अ + अ does not give ए.
ओऽ comes from अः + अ, not from अ + अ.
य comes from इ before a vowel, not from अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अत्र → चात्र.
questions.explain: तत्र + अपि = तत्रापि, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial अ merge into one long आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.

questions.q: By verse 127, what is the sign that calls for quick action?
optionExplain: Right: कुक्षिः प्रस्पन्दते यदि: if the belly quivers.

Bleeding is not named in verse 127.
Breathing is not named in verse 127.
questions.explain: If the belly quivers, the child is taken out quickly.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 127 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: At the bastidvāra, of her who has perished, if the belly quivers, at the time of birth, then quickly, having split (it) open, one should take out the child.
questions.rule: बस्तिद्वारे → विपन्नायाः → कुक्षिः प्रस्पंदते यदि → जन्मकाले → ततः शीघ्रं → पाटयित्वोद्धरेच्छिशुं.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 127 to its meaning.
questions.explain: If the belly quivers, then quickly, having split (it) open, one should take out the child.
questions.rule: कुक्षि, प्रस्पन्दते, यदि, शीघ्रम्, पाटयित्वा, उद्धरेत्.
questions.teaches: यदि … ततः = if … then: the condition comes first, the action after ततः.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of उद्धरेच्छिशुम् is right?
optionExplain: A visarga before श stays or becomes श्; it never gives च्छ.
Right: त् before श becomes च्, and the श may become छ before a vowel (optional; च्श also correct): उद्धरेच्छिशुम्.
A final म् before a consonant becomes ं: उद्धरें शिशुम्.
छिशुम् is not a word; the word is शिशुम्, the child.
questions.explain: उद्धरेत् (should take out) + शिशुम् (the child).
questions.rule: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which statements about verse 127 are right by the card?
options: The verse says plainly that she has died
The verse explains what bastidvāra is
The action is to be done quickly
The child is taken out after splitting (it) open
optionExplain: Vipanna means ruined or dead; the verse does not say death plainly.
It is not explained; it is read literally.
Right: ततः शीघ्रम्.
Right: पाटयित्वा उद्धरेत् शिशुम्.
questions.explain: Quickly, having split (it) open, one should take out the child.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the pattern of पाटयित्वा उद्धरेत्, what does गत्वा mean in गत्वा पश्येत् (a new example)?
optionExplain: While going would be a present participle such as गच्छन्.
In order to go would be the infinitive गन्तुम्.
Right: -त्वा marks an action done before the main verb, as पाटयित्वा, having split open.
He went would be a past finite verb such as अगच्छत्.
questions.explain: गत्वा पश्येत् = having gone, he should see; like पाटयित्वा उद्धरेत्.
questions.teaches: An absolutive in -त्वा names an action finished before the main verb: पाटयित्वा उद्धरेत्.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 128 and its note, what does each half-verse of this passage give?
options: A sign of a dead fetus
optionExplain: No measure or dose is given in verse 128.
No sign is named; only drugs are listed.
No step of delivery is named in verse 128.
Right: Each half-verse is one combination (yoga) of the seven.
questions.explain: Line 1 is the first combination, line 2 the second.

questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of कृष्णतिलास्ताम्रवल्ली is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: कृष्णतिलास्ताम्रवल्ली.
न् before त gives ंस्त: that would be कृष्णतिलांस्ताम्रवल्ली.
स्ताम्रवल्ली is not a word; the drug is ताम्रवल्ली.
A final म् before a consonant becomes ं: कृष्णतिलं ताम्रवल्ली.
questions.explain: कृष्णतिलाः (black sesame seeds) + ताम्रवल्ली (copper creeper).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which drug of verse 128 belongs to the second combination?

Suradāru is in line 1, the first combination.
The śāka seed is in line 1, the first combination.
questions.explain: Śatāvarī closes line 2, the second combination.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the rule of कृष्णतिलाः + ताम्रवल्ली, how is बालः + तिष्ठति (the boy stands) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
श् comes before च, छ or श, not before त.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, as in कृष्णतिलास्ताम्रवल्ली.
र् comes after vowels other than अ and आ, before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: बालः + तिष्ठति = बालस्तिष्ठति, like कृष्णतिलाः + ताम्रवल्ली.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: कृष्णतिलाः + ताम्रवल्ली → कृष्णतिलास्ताम्रवल्ली.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 129, which drug is named in both of its lines?
optionExplain: Madhuyaṣṭikā is only in line 2.
Vṛkṣadanī is only in line 1.
Padmā is only in line 2.

questions.q: Put these printed words of verse 129 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Vṛkṣadanī, payasyā, (latā), sārivā with utpala; anantā, (sārivā, rāsnā), padmā, madhuyaṣṭikā.

questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 129 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: The labels are the data's: standard or probable.

questions.q: Which split of सोत्पल is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: स + उत्पल → सोत्पल.
अः before a vowel other than अ drops the visarga with a gap: स उत्पल.
A final म् before a vowel joins it: समुत्पल.
त्पल is not a word; the flower is उत्पल.
questions.explain: स (with) + उत्पल (probably blue water lily): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Anantā and sārivā both stand in line 2 of verse 129. How does the card take them here?
options: As a verb and its object
optionExplain: The note takes them as separate here, since both are listed.
Right: Both are listed, so they are taken as separate drugs here.
Both are feminine nouns in the nominative, not a verb.
They are printed as two separate words.

questions.q: By the rule of स + उत्पल → सोत्पल, how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
The अ does not drop; अ and उ merge into ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as स + उत्पल → सोत्पल.
आ comes from अ + अ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like स + उत्पल = सोत्पल.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial उ merge into ओ: स + उत्पल → सोत्पल.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 130, which fat is named in the fifth combination?

No marrow is named in verse 130.
No butter is named in verse 130.

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 2 of verse 130 in the verse's order.

questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 130 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: The labels are the data's: standard or probable.

questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: In बृहतीद्वय, what does द्वय add?
options: Two parts of one bṛhatī plant
A use in the second month
optionExplain: Right: द्वय = a pair: bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī (probable).
द्वय counts the plants, not doses; no dose is given.
The data reads two plants, not two parts of one.
द्वय means a pair; no month is named here.

questions.q: Which statements about verse 130 are right by the card?
options: Ghee belongs to the fifth combination
The milk-yielding trees are named in verse 130
Kṣīri-śuṅga-tvacaḥ can be read two ways
optionExplain: Right: घृतम् is in line 1.

questions.q: By the pattern of बृहतीद्वय, what does नेत्रद्वय (a new example) mean?
optionExplain: The second would be द्वितीय, not द्वय.
Right: -द्वय = a pair: नेत्रद्वय = the two eyes.
द्वय names a pair of things, not a repetition.

questions.q: By verse 131, with what are all these combinations taken?
optionExplain: Honey is not named in verse 131.
Meat soup is not named in verse 131.

questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 1 of verse 131 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Water chestnut, lotus stalk, grape, kaseru, madhuka, sitā: the seventh combination.
questions.rule: शृंगाटकं → बिसं → द्राक्षा → कसेरु → मधुकं → सिता.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 131 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: The labels are the data's: standard or probable.
questions.teaches: सिता literally means 'white'; in drug lists it is usually sugar (probable).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of योगानर्ध (in योगानर्द्धश्लोकसमापनान्) is right?
optionExplain: आः before a vowel drops the visarga and leaves a gap: योगा अर्ध.
इ before अ becomes य्: that would give योगान्यर्ध.
That would give योगमर्ध, with म.
Right: A final न् after a long vowel joins the next vowel unchanged: योगानर्ध.
questions.explain: योगान् (combinations, accusative plural) + अर्धश्लोकसमापनान् (ending at a half-verse).
questions.rule: Final न् (after a long vowel) + vowel → न + vowel.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: What does अर्धश्लोकसमापन tell about each combination?
options: Each is complete within a half-verse
Each is taken for half a month
Each is given at half the usual dose
optionExplain: Right: Each combination fills one half-verse (units 128 to 131).
No half-month is named; श्लोक is a verse.
No dose is given; अर्धश्लोक is a half-verse.
The chapter closes in unit 135, a colophon.
questions.explain: Ardhaśloka-samāpana = ending at a half-verse: one combination per half-verse.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the rule of योगान् + अर्ध, how is देवान् + अर्चति (worships the gods) joined?
optionExplain: न् doubles before a vowel only after a short vowel; here आ is long.
Right: A final न् after a long vowel joins the next vowel unchanged, as योगान् + अर्ध.
That is how आः would join before a vowel, not आन्.
A final न् does not turn into म् before a vowel.
questions.explain: देवान् + अर्चति = देवानर्चति, like योगान् + अर्ध = योगानर्ध.
questions.teaches: A final न् after a long vowel simply joins a following vowel: योगान् + अर्ध → योगानर्ध.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 132, in which months are the combinations applied?
options: Only in the very first month
In the ninth and tenth months
In the seven months, in sequence
In any month, all at once
optionExplain: The verse names seven months, in sequence.
These months come later, with other milks (units 133, 134).
Right: क्रमात् सप्तसु मासेषु: in sequence, in the seven months.
The verse says क्रमात्, in sequence, not all at once.
questions.explain: Seven combinations, applied in sequence over seven months.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put the plants of line 2 of verse 132 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Kapittha, bilva, bṛhatī, paṭola, ikṣu, nidigdhikā.
questions.rule: कपित्थ → बिल्व → बृहती → पटोल → इक्षु → निदिग्धिका.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each plant of verse 132 to the card's identification.
questions.explain: All five identifications are standard in the data.
questions.teaches: Bṛhatī and nidigdhikā are the large and small nightshades (standard).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of पटोलेक्षु is right?
optionExplain: A final म् before a vowel joins it: पटोलमिक्षु.
अः before a vowel other than अ drops the visarga with a gap: पटोल इक्षु.
क्षु is not a word; the plant is इक्षु, sugarcane.
Right: अ + इ → ए: पटोल + इक्षु → पटोलेक्षु.
questions.explain: पटोल (pointed gourd) + इक्षु (sugarcane): अ + इ → ए.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: What does गर्भे स्रवति describe in verse 132?
options: The fetus turned the wrong way
A woman past her tenth month
optionExplain: Right: A locative absolute: with the fetus flowing, probably miscarriage (garbhasrāva, probable).
No turning is named in verse 132.
No tenth month is named in verse 132.
No growth is named in verse 132.
questions.explain: When the fetus is flowing, probably miscarriage, one should apply the combinations.
questions.rule: गर्भे स्रवति = when the fetus flows.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the rule of पटोल + इक्षु → पटोलेक्षु, how is गज + इन्द्रः (lord of elephants) joined?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ + ए or ऐ, not from अ + इ.
Right: अ + इ → ए, as पटोल + इक्षु → पटोलेक्षु.
The अ does not drop; अ and इ merge into ए.
य comes from इ before a vowel, not from अ.
questions.explain: गज + इन्द्रः = गजेन्द्रः, like पटोल + इक्षु = पटोलेक्षु.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial इ merge into ए: पटोल + इक्षु → पटोलेक्षु.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 133, what is boiled with the roots?
optionExplain: No oil is named in verse 133.
No water is named in verse 133.
Right: मूलैः शृतं … क्षीरम्: milk boiled with roots.
No ghee is named in verse 133.
questions.explain: Milk is boiled with the roots.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put the ninth-month drugs of verse 133 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Sārivā, anantā, payasyā, madhuyaṣṭī.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 133 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Milk boiled with roots is used; likewise in the eighth; in the ninth with four drugs.
questions.rule: मूल, शृत, प्रयुञ्जीत, क्षीर, अष्टम, नवम.
questions.teaches: मूलैः शृतम् = boiled with roots: the instrumental names what the milk is boiled with.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of printed तथाऽष्टमे is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give तथेऽष्टमे, with ए kept.
Neither तथ nor ष्टमे is a word here.
ष्टमे is not a word; the word is अष्टमे, in the eighth.
Right: आ + अ → आ; the ऽ printed after आ is a print habit.
questions.explain: तथा (likewise) + अष्टमे (in the eighth): the regular join is तथाष्टमे.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which statements about verse 133 are right by the card?
options: The milk is boiled with roots
The verse states a dose of milk
The ninth month adds sārivā and licorice
optionExplain: Right: मूलैः शृतं क्षीरम्.
No dose is given.
Right: नवमे सारिवा… मधुयष्टिभिः.
Its verb, योजयेत्, comes in unit 134.
questions.explain: Milk boiled with roots; in the ninth, with sārivā, anantā, payasyā and licorice.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the pattern of मूलैः शृतम्, what does पुष्पैः mean in पुष्पैः शृतम् (a new example)?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural of a-stems, as मूलैः, with roots.
Of the flowers would be the genitive पुष्पाणाम्.
In the flowers would be the locative पुष्पेषु.
From a flower would be the ablative पुष्पात्.
questions.explain: पुष्पैः शृतम् = boiled with flowers, like मूलैः शृतम्.
questions.teaches: -ऐः on an a-stem is the instrumental plural, 'with': मूलैः = with roots.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 134, in which month is this milk applied?
optionExplain: The verse says दशमे, the tenth.
Right: दशमे मासि: in the tenth month.
The verse says दशमे, the tenth.
The verse says दशमे, the tenth.
questions.explain: In the tenth month, milk cooked with payasyā is applied.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 134 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: One should apply in the tenth month milk cooked with payasyā, or with licorice, dry ginger and deodar.
questions.rule: योजयेद्दशमेमासि → सिद्धं क्षीरं → पयस्यया → अथवा → यष्टिमधुकनागरामरदारुभिः.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 134 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Milk cooked with payasyā, or with licorice, dry ginger and deodar.
questions.rule: दशम, सिद्ध, क्षीर, अथवा, नागर, अमरदारु.
questions.teaches: मासि, like मासे, means 'in the month': दशमे मासि = in the tenth month.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of योजयेद्दशमे is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after ए before a voiced sound gives र्: योजयेर्दशमे.
A final म् before a consonant becomes ं: योजयें दशमे.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound: योजयेद्दशमे.
द्दशमे is not a word; the word is दशमे, in the tenth.
questions.explain: योजयेत् (should apply) + दशमे (in the tenth).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By verse 134, what is the other choice (अथवा) for the tenth month?
options: Milk boiled with roots of kapittha, bilva and others
Plain milk taken with no drug at all
Ghee cooked with payasyā and white sugar
Milk cooked with licorice, dry ginger and deodar
optionExplain: That is unit 133, milk boiled with roots.
The verse names drugs for the milk.
The verse names milk, not ghee.
Right: अथवा यष्टिमधुकनागरामरदारुभिः.
questions.explain: Or the milk is cooked with licorice, dry ginger and deodar.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the rule of योजयेत् + दशमे, how is भवेत् + धनम् (there should be wealth) joined?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound, as योजयेत् + दशमे.
Before a voiced sound the final त् does not stay unvoiced.
त् may become न् (optionally) only before a nasal; ध is not a nasal.
त् becomes च् before च, छ or श, not before ध.
questions.explain: भवेत् + धनम् = भवेद्धनम्, like योजयेत् + दशमे = योजयेद्दशमे.
questions.teaches: A word-final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound: योजयेत् + दशमे → योजयेद्दशमे.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By unit 135, what is chapter four named?
optionExplain: That is the name of chapter two.
Right: इति गर्भव्यापन्नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
That is the name of chapter one.
That is the oil taught in units 120 to 125, not a chapter name.
questions.explain: The colophon names the chapter Garbhavyāpad, mishap of the fetus.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Put the words of unit 135 in their order.
questions.explain: Thus, Garbhavyāpad, named, fourth, chapter.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Match each word of unit 135 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Thus the fourth chapter, named mishap of the fetus.
questions.teaches: गर्भव्यापद् = गर्भ + व्यापद्: a mishap of the fetus, the theme of the whole chapter.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: Which split of गर्भव्यापन्नाम is right?
optionExplain: अः before a voiced sound gives ओ: गर्भव्यापो नाम.
आ before न stays: गर्भव्यापानाम, with one न.
Right: A final त् before a nasal may become न् (optional; द् is also correct): गर्भव्यापन्नाम.
A final म् before a consonant becomes ं: गर्भव्यापं नाम.
questions.explain: गर्भव्यापत् (mishap of the fetus) + नाम (named): त् + न → न्न (optional; द् is also correct).
questions.rule: त् + nasal → न् (optional; द् is also correct).
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: In unit 135 the word for fourth is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चतुर्थः = fourth; before अध्यायः it is printed चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: चतुर्थ means fourth; ऽ shows the lost अ of अध्यायः.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्थोऽध्यायः, how is पञ्चमः + अध्यायः (the fifth chapter) joined?
optionExplain: आ with a gap comes from आः before a vowel, not from अः.
अः drops its visarga with a gap only before vowels other than अ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and ऽ marks the lost अ, as चतुर्थः + अध्यायः.
questions.explain: पञ्चमः + अध्यायः = पञ्चमोऽध्यायः, like चतुर्थः + अध्यायः = चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the following अ is shown by ऽ: चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
questions.section: मृत माता से शिशु; मासानुसार गर्भस्राव के योग

questions.q: By unit 1, what does this chapter set out to explain?
options: The division of the body into its parts
The mishaps that can occur in pregnancy
The signs that show death is near
The six seasons and their right diet
optionExplain: Right: अङ्गविभागम्: the division (vibhāga) of the parts (aṅga).
Pregnancy mishaps are not the topic named in unit 1.
Signs of death are not the topic named in unit 1.
No season is named; the topic is aṅgavibhāga.
questions.explain: The chapter promises to explain the division of the body's parts.
questions.rule: अङ्गविभागं शारीरं व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain the bodily division of the parts.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Put the words of unit 1 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, the division of the parts, bodily, we shall explain.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अथ अतः opens the chapter; अङ्ग + विभाग = the division of the parts.
questions.teaches: अङ्गविभाग = the division (vibhāga) of the body's parts (aṅga).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Which split of अतोऽंग in unit 1 is right?
optionExplain: अत is not the word; the word is अतः (therefore).
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the second अ is dropped (shown by ऽ).
ङ्ग is not a word; the word is अङ्ग (part).
अतु is not a word, and उ + अ would give व.
questions.explain: अतः (therefore) + अङ्ग (part): अः + अ → ओऽ: अतोऽङ्ग.
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओ, and the अ that follows is dropped (ऽ).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: In अथातोऽंगविभागं, what does the sign ऽ (avagraha) mark?
options: A long vowel to be held
An initial अ dropped after ओ
optionExplain: ऽ does not lengthen a vowel; it marks a dropped अ.
The visarga became ओ; ऽ stands for the lost अ.
Right: अतः + अङ्ग → अतोऽङ्ग: the अ of अङ्ग is dropped.
ऽ is not a pause; it marks a dropped अ.
questions.explain: The avagraha shows that the अ of अङ्ग was dropped after the ओ of अतो.
questions.rule: ओ + अ → ओऽ: the avagraha marks the dropped अ.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By the pattern of व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain), what does वदिष्यामः mean?
optionExplain: -ष्यामः is a future ending, not a past one.
-मः marks the 1st person plural: we, not they.
-मः marks the 1st person plural: we, not you.
Right: -ष्यामः / -स्यामः: future, 1st person plural, as व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.explain: वदिष्यामः = we shall speak, like व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The ending -स्यामः (-ष्यामः) marks the future, 1st person plural: व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 2, which set names the six parts (aṅga) of the body?
options: Head, trunk, two arms, two lower limbs
Head, neck, chest, belly, two feet
Eyes, navel, nose, two feet, and heart
Skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow
optionExplain: Right: शिरोऽन्तराधिद्वौ बाहू सक्थिनी च.
Neck, chest and belly are not named among the six.
Eyes, navel and feet are minor parts (unit 3).
These are not the six aṅgas of unit 2.
questions.explain: Six parts: head, trunk, two arms, two lower limbs.
questions.rule: षडङ्गम्: शिरः, अन्तराधिः, द्वौ बाहू, सक्थिनी.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Put the four names of the six parts of unit 2 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Head, trunk, the two arms, the two lower limbs.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole is body; its six parts are head, trunk, two arms, two lower limbs.
questions.teaches: अन्तराधि = the trunk, the middle part of the body; सक्थि = the lower limb (thigh and leg).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Which split of षडंगं in unit 2 is right?
optionExplain: षड is not the word; the number is षट् (six).
Right: ट् before a vowel becomes ड्: षट् + अङ्गम् → षडङ्गम्.
षः is not a word, and अः + अ would give ओऽ.
षडम् and गम् are not the words; they are षट्, अङ्गम्.
questions.explain: षट् (six) + अङ्गम् (part): ट् + vowel → ड्.
questions.rule: A final ट् becomes ड् before a vowel.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 2?
options: The body is said to have six parts
The eyes are among the six parts
The two lower limbs are among them
The navel is one of the six parts
optionExplain: Right: षडङ्गम्, six parts.

questions.q: By the rule of तत् + च → तच्च, how is एतत् + च (and this) written?
optionExplain: द् comes before a voiced sound; च is unvoiced.

questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Which of these does unit 3 name as a minor part (pratyaṅga)?
optionExplain: The trunk (antarādhi) is one of the six aṅgas, unit 2.
The head is one of the six aṅgas, unit 2.
The arms are among the six aṅgas, unit 2.

questions.explain: The navel is a minor part; head, trunk and arms are main parts.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Put the words of unit 3 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Eyes, navel, nose, feet and so on, but, of this, the minor parts.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The minor parts are the eyes, the navel, the feet and so on.
questions.teaches: प्रत्यङ्ग = a minor or secondary part, as against the six main parts (aṅga).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Which split of त्वस्य in unit 3 is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a vowel becomes व्: तु + अस्य → त्वस्य.

questions.explain: तु (but) + अस्य (of this): उ + अ → व.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: A student calls the eye one of the six aṅgas. By units 2 and 3, what is the correction?
options: The eye is a seventh main aṅga
The eye is a minor part, a pratyaṅga
The eye is one of the great elements
The eye belongs to the two arms

Right: Unit 3 lists नेत्र among the pratyaṅgas.
The eye is listed as a pratyaṅga, not an element.
The eye is listed on its own as a pratyaṅga.
questions.explain: Six main parts in unit 2; the eye is a minor part in unit 3.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By the rule of तु + अस्य → त्वस्य, how is सु + अस्ति (may it be well) written?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
उ + अ does not give a long ऊ.

questions.teaches: Before a different vowel, उ becomes व्: तु + अस्य → त्वस्य.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 4, from what does origination (abhinirvṛtti) come?
options: From the three doṣas in balance
optionExplain: No taste is named in unit 4.
No doṣa is named in unit 4.
The minor parts are named in unit 3, not as a source.

questions.explain: Origination is from the great elements.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Put the five names in the compound of unit 4 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Space, wind, fire, water, earth: the printed order of the compound.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 4 to its meaning.

questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

options: Its -अस् becomes ओ before the voiced ज
The ओ marks the dual of तेजस्

optionExplain: Right: तेजस् + जल: अस् → अः → ओ before a voiced sound.
ओ here is sandhi, not a dual ending.
No lengthening rule applies; अस् → ओ.
Only before a voiced sound; before क, त ... it differs.
questions.explain: तेजस् + जल → तेजोजल: अस् (as visarga) + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 4, what presides over the great elements from which origination comes?
optionExplain: No single guṇa is named as presiding in unit 4.
Right: चेतनाधिष्ठितेभ्यः: presided over by consciousness.
No doṣa is named in unit 4.
The line names cetanā, not manas.
questions.explain: The great elements are presided over by consciousness.
questions.rule: चेतना + अधिष्ठित = presided over by consciousness.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By the rule of तेजस् + जल → तेजोजल, how is मनस् + हर (charming the mind) written?
optionExplain: र् comes after vowels other than अ and आ.
अस् does not become आ before ह.

questions.teaches: A stem in -अस् shows -ओ before a voiced consonant: तेजस् + जल → तेजोजल.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 5, what comes about from the special arrangement of the elements?
options: The six parts and the minor parts of the body
The five marks of the elements, in their order

Likeness or unlikeness of form, voice and so on
optionExplain: The parts are named in units 2 and 3, not here.
The marks are named in unit 11, not here.
The guṇas of the elements come in units 6-10.
Right: सारूप्यमसारूप्यं वा ... निष्पद्यते.
questions.explain: Similarity or dissimilarity of form, size, voice and so on.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Put the qualities of unit 5 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Form, size, unctuousness, lustre, voice (and so on).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The arrangement, through seen and unseen actions, gives graded similarity or dissimilarity.
questions.rule: सन्निवेश, दृष्ट, अदृष्ट, तारतम्य, सारूप्य, स्नेह.
questions.teaches: तारतम्य = gradation in degree; सन्निवेश = arrangement, the way the parts are set together.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: What does the अ- of असारूप्य in unit 5 add to सारूप्य?
options: It makes it past: was similar
optionExplain: Right: अ- (not) + सारूप्य (similarity) = dissimilarity.

अ- negates; it does not strengthen.

questions.rule: अ- before a consonant = not, un-.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Two people differ in voice and lustre. By unit 5, through what power does this come about?
options: Through the guṇa sattva and nothing else

questions.explain: Space is abundant in sattva.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 6 to its meaning.

questions.q: By the rule of बहुलो वायुः, how is रामः + वदति (Rāma speaks) written?

No guṇa is named in unit 8.

बहुलो (बहुलः) is masculine; वनम् is neuter.
Right: Neuter, to agree with वनम्, as बहुलम् with अम्बु.
बहुलेन is instrumental; वनम् is nominative.
questions.explain: वृक्षबहुलं वनम् = a forest abundant in trees: neuter singular, like सत्त्वतमोबहुलम् अम्बु.
questions.rule: The bahuvrīhi agrees with its noun in gender, number and case.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi in -बहुल takes the gender and number of its noun: सत्त्वतमोबहुलम् (n.) अम्बु (n.).
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 10, which guṇa abounds in earth?
optionExplain: Sattva abounds in space (unit 6).
Rajas abounds in wind (unit 7).
Ojas is not a guṇa named in unit 10.
Right: तमोबहुला भूः: earth is abundant in tamas.
questions.explain: Earth is abundant in tamas.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Match each word of unit 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Earth is abundant in tamas.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: By unit 10, earth is abundant in the guṇa ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तमोबहुला भूः: earth is abundant in tamas.
questions.teaches: तमस् = the guṇa of inertia; in a compound before ब it shows तमो.
questions.section: आरंभ: शरीर के अंग व पंचमहाभूत

questions.q: Why is it तमोबहुला and not तमोबहुलो in unit 10?
options: It is feminine, to agree with भूः
It is plural, for many earths
आ is the sandhi of अः before भ
It is neuter, as with अम्बु
optionExplain: Right: भू is feminine; the data marks बहुला f. nom. sg.
भूः is singular; so is बहुला.
