questions.section: मतान्तर: सात त्वचाएँ व उनका प्रमाण

questions.q: What does the name मांसधरा of unit 45 mean?
optionExplain: Blood-bearing is असृग्धरा or रक्तधरा.
Fat-bearing is मेदोधरा (unit 50).
Right: मांस (flesh) + धरा (bearing).
Life-bearing is प्राणधरा (unit 38).
questions.explain: मांसधरा = flesh-bearing.
questions.section: मतान्तर: सात त्वचाएँ व उनका प्रमाण

questions.q: By the pattern of व्रीहिद्वय (a pair of vrīhis), what does नेत्रद्वय mean?
optionExplain: 'Second' would be द्वितीय, not द्वय.
Nothing in नेत्रद्वय names a disease.
द्वय is a pair of the same thing, the eyes.
Right: द्वय = pair, as in व्रीहिद्वय.
questions.explain: नेत्रद्वय = the pair of eyes, like व्रीहिद्वय = a pair of vrīhis.
questions.teaches: -द्वय after a noun means 'a pair of': व्रीहिद्वय = two rice grains.
questions.section: मतान्तर: सात त्वचाएँ व उनका प्रमाण

questions.q: By unit 46, what is it that, so formed, is called kalā?
options: A moisture that stays and is cooked
A bone that grows between joints
A clot of blood under the skin
A hair that grows out of flesh
optionExplain: Right: क्लेदोऽवतिष्ठते ... विपक्वः ... कलासंज्ञः.
No bone is named; the kalā is a moisture (kleda).
No clot is named; the kalā is a moisture.
No hair is named; the kalā is a moisture.
questions.explain: The kleda that stays between the seats and is cooked by the heats is named kalā.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 46 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The moisture that stays ..., cooked by its own heats, covered by snāyu, śleṣman and jarāyu, like heartwood, the essence of the dhātus, with rasa as remainder from smallness, is named kalā.
questions.rule: क्लेदोऽवतिष्ठते → विपक्कः → ...च्छन्नः → काष्ठइव सारो → धातुसारः → कलासंज्ञः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 46 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Moisture, cooked by heats, covered, the essence like heartwood, named kalā.
questions.rule: क्लेद, ऊष्मन्, विपक्व, छन्न, सार, संज्ञा.
questions.teaches: कलासंज्ञः = having the name kalā: संज्ञा = name.

questions.q: Which split of रसशेषोऽल्पत्वात् is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give रसशेषेऽल्पत्वात्, with ए.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the second अ drops, marked ऽ.
ल्पत्वात् is not a word; the word is अल्पत्वात्.
म् before a vowel stays: रसशेषमल्पत्वात्.
questions.explain: रसशेषः (with rasa as remainder) + अल्पत्वात् (from smallness): अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: By unit 46, which cover the moisture that becomes kalā?
optionExplain: Bone is not named among the coverings.
Right: स्नायु is the first of the three.
Hair is not named among the coverings.
Right: श्लेष्म- is the second.
Right: जरायु is the third.
questions.explain: It is covered by snāyu, śleṣman and jarāyu: स्नायुश्लेष्मजरायुच्छन्नः.

questions.q: By the rule of रसशेषोऽल्पत्वात्, how is देवः + अयम् (this is a god) joined?
optionExplain: आ comes from अ + अ with no visarga.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, the अ marked ऽ, as रसशेषः + अल्पत्वात्.
The visarga drops this way before vowels other than अ.
questions.explain: देवः + अयम् = देवोऽयम्, like रसशेषः + अल्पत्वात् = रसशेषोऽल्पत्वात्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after short अ before short अ: अः → ओ and the अ drops (ऽ): रसशेषः + अल्पत्वात् → रसशेषोऽल्पत्वात्.

questions.q: By unit 47, what are the kalās said to be?
options: The roots from which the hairs grow
The seats of all the skin diseases
The paths of food in the belly
Boundaries of the spaces between seats
optionExplain: Hair is not named in unit 47.
Seats of skin diseases belong to the skins (units 35-37).
Food paths are not named in unit 47.
Right: -अन्तरमर्यादाः: boundaries of the spaces between.
questions.explain: The seven kalās are the boundaries of the spaces between the seats.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 47 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Those, the boundaries of the spaces between the seats, are the seven kalās.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 47 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Those seven kalās are the boundaries of the spaces between the seats.
questions.teaches: मर्यादा = boundary, limit: the kalās mark off the spaces between the seats.

questions.q: Why is ताः printed ता before ध्वात्वाशय- in unit 47?
options: After आ, the visarga drops before a voiced sound
After आ, the visarga becomes ओ before ध
The visarga drops before every consonant
optionExplain: Right: ध is voiced, so ताः + ध्वा- → ता ध्वा-.
The singular is सा; the data reads plural ताः.
ओ comes from a visarga after short अ.
Before unvoiced sounds it stays or changes.
questions.explain: ताः + ध्वा... = ता ध्वा...: आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga.

questions.q: Unit 47 names the seven ____ (membrane-like layers). Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सप्त कलाः: the seven kalās.
questions.teaches: कला = a membrane-like layer; there are seven.

questions.q: By the rule of ता ध्वा-, how is अश्वाः + धावन्ति (the horses run) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from a visarga after short अ, not after आ.
Right: आः before the voiced ध loses its visarga, as ताः + ध्वा-.
र् comes after vowels other than अ and आ.
Before a voiced sound the visarga after आ does not stay.
questions.explain: अश्वाः + धावन्ति = अश्वा धावन्ति, like ताः + ध्वा- = ता ध्वा-.
questions.teaches: A visarga after आ is dropped before a voiced sound: ताः + ध्वात्वाशय- → ता ध्वात्वाशय-.

questions.q: By unit 48, what is the first kalā named?
optionExplain: Raktadharā is the second kalā (unit 49).
Medodharā is the third kalā (unit 50).
Right: तासां प्रथमा मांसधरा नाम.
Śleṣmadharā is the fourth kalā (unit 51).
questions.explain: The first kalā is Māṃsadharā.

questions.q: Put the structures spreading in the flesh in unit 48 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Sirā, snāyu, dhamanī, srotas: their networks spread in the flesh.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: In the flesh the networks spread like lotus-fibres and stalks in muddy water.
questions.teaches: प्रतान = a spreading network of tendrils: the vessels and channels spread in the flesh this way.

questions.q: Which split of पंकोदके is right?
optionExplain: अः + उ would give पङ्क उदके, the visarga lost.
दके is not a word; the word is उदके (in water).
ओदक is not a word; water is उदक.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: पङ्क + उदके → पङ्कोदके.
questions.explain: पङ्क (mud) + उदके (in water): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: In the simile of unit 48, what are the networks in the flesh likened to?
options: Lotus-fibres and stalks in muddy water
Roots of a tree deep in the dry ground
Threads of a spider's web on a wall
Cracks that open in earth in summer
optionExplain: Right: भूमाविव पङ्कोदके बिसमृणालानां प्रतानाः.
No tree roots are named; the simile is of lotus.
No web is named; the simile is of lotus.
No cracks are named; the simile is of lotus.
questions.explain: Like the spreading lotus-fibres and stalks in muddy water on the ground.

questions.q: By the rule of पङ्क + उदके, how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as पङ्क + उदके → पङ्कोदके.
अ does not simply vanish before उ; they merge into ओ.
आ comes from अ + अ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like पङ्क + उदके = पङ्कोदके.
questions.teaches: अ + उ join as ओ: पङ्क + उदके → पङ्कोदके.

questions.q: By unit 49, what is the second kalā named?
optionExplain: Medodharā is the third kalā (unit 50).
Pittadharā is the sixth kalā.
Right: द्वितीया रक्तधरा नाम.
Purīṣadharā is the fifth kalā.
questions.explain: The second kalā is Raktadharā, blood-bearing.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 49 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The second, Raktadharā, inside the flesh; in it is blood, especially in sirā, spleen and liver; from a cut the blood flows like milk from a milky tree.
questions.rule: रक्तधरा → मांसस्याभ्यंतरतः → तस्यां शोणितं → विशेषतश्च ... भवति → क्षतात्क्षतजं → वृक्षादिव ... प्रवर्त्तते.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Blood is in it, especially in the spleen and liver; the wound-born blood flows like milk from a milky tree.
questions.teaches: क्षतज = क्षत (wound) + ज (born): a name for blood that flows from a cut.

questions.q: Which split of वृक्षादिव is right?
optionExplain: अः + इ would give वृक्ष इव, with no द्.
दिव is not the word; the particle is इव (like).
म् before a vowel stays: वृक्षमिव.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: वृक्षात् + इव → वृक्षादिव.
questions.explain: वृक्षात् (from a tree) + इव (like): त् + vowel → द्.

questions.q: By unit 49, where especially is the blood?
optionExplain: Right: सिरा- is named first.
The joints are made firm by Kapha (unit 51), not named here.
Right: प्लीह-.
The large bones hold majjā (unit 50).
Right: यकृत्सु.
questions.explain: Especially in the sirā, spleen and liver: विशेषतश्च सिराप्लीहयकृत्सु.

questions.q: By the rule of वृक्षादिव, how is जगत् + ईशः (lord of the world) joined?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as वृक्षात् + इव → वृक्षादिव.
Before a vowel the त् becomes द्; it does not stay.
त् may become न् (optionally) only before a nasal, not before ई.
The long ई of ईशः stays long: -दीशः.
questions.explain: जगत् + ईशः = जगदीशः, like वृक्षात् + इव = वृक्षादिव.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: वृक्षात् + इव → वृक्षादिव.

questions.q: By unit 50, what is the fat in the large bones?
optionExplain: Mastiṣka is its name in the head.
Right: स्थूलास्थिषु तु मज्जा.
Kleda is the moisture of unit 46.
Śleṣman makes the joints firm (unit 51).
questions.explain: In the large bones it is majjā.

questions.q: Put the places of unit 50 in the line's order.
questions.explain: In the belly, in the small bones, in the head, in the large bones.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Fat in the belly and small bones; in the head under the skull; marrow in the large bones.
questions.teaches: The one medas has different names by place: mastiṣka in the head, majjā in the large bones.

questions.q: Which split of मेदोधरा is right?
optionExplain: उधरा is not a word; the word is धरा (bearing).
ए would stay before ध (मेदेधरा); it gives no ओ.
Right: Final -अस् (visarga) becomes ओ before a voiced consonant: मेदोधरा.
म् before a consonant would give मेदंधरा.
questions.explain: मेदस् (fat) + धरा (bearing): -अस् before the voiced ध → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 50, what is this same fat called in the head, covered by the skull?
optionExplain: Majjā is its name in the large bones.
Kleda is the moisture of unit 46.
Śoṇita is the blood of unit 49.
Right: शिरसि कपालप्रतिच्छन्नं मस्तिष्काख्यम्.
questions.explain: In the head, under the skull, it is called mastiṣka.

questions.q: By the rule of मेदस् + धरा → मेदोधरा, how is मनस् + रथ (a wish) joined?
optionExplain: Right: -अस् before the voiced र becomes ओ, as मेदस् + धरा.
आ appears when the visarga after आ drops, not after अ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
The स् does not stay before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: मनस् + रथ = मनोरथ, like मेदस् + धरा = मेदोधरा.
questions.teaches: A final -अस् becomes ओ before a voiced consonant: मेदस् + धरा → मेदोधरा.

questions.q: By unit 51, what is the fourth kalā named?
optionExplain: Purīṣadharā is the fifth kalā.
Right: चतुर्थी श्लेष्मधरा नाम.
Pittadharā is the sixth kalā.
Medodharā is the third kalā (unit 50).
questions.explain: The fourth kalā is Śleṣmadharā.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 51 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The fourth, Śleṣmadharā; joined by the śleṣman, all the joints become firm.
questions.rule: चतुर्थी श्लेष्मधरा नाम → श्लेष्मणाऽऽश्लेषिताः → सर्वसंधयो → दृढा भवंति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Joined by Kapha, all the joints become firm.
questions.teaches: आश्लेषित = joined, clasped: the śleṣman holds the joints together.

questions.q: Which split of श्लेष्मणाऽऽश्लेषिताः is right?
optionExplain: अः + आ would give श्लेष्मण आश्लेषिताः.
इ + आ would give श्लेष्मण्याश्लेषिताः.
Right: आ + आ → आ; the doubled ऽ is a print habit.
ए + आ would give श्लेष्मणयाश्लेषिताः or श्लेष्मण आश्लेषिताः.
questions.explain: श्लेष्मणा (by śleṣman) + आश्लेषिताः (joined): आ + आ → आ.

questions.q: By unit 51, what happens to the joints joined by śleṣman?
optionExplain: The unit says firm (दृढ), not loose.
Fat is the third kalā's (unit 50).
Heat is not named in unit 51.
Right: सर्वसंधयो दृढा भवंति.
questions.explain: All the joints become firm.

questions.q: By the rule of श्लेष्मणा + आश्लेषिताः, how is विद्या + आलयः (school) joined?
optionExplain: Right: आ + आ → आ, as श्लेष्मणा + आश्लेषिताः.
ए comes from अ/आ + इ, not from आ + आ.
औ comes from अ/आ + ओ/औ, not from आ + आ.
No य् arises between आ and आ; they merge into आ.
questions.explain: विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः, like श्लेष्मणा + आश्लेषिताः = श्लेष्मणाऽऽश्लेषिताः.
questions.teaches: Two आ sounds merge into one आ: श्लेष्मणा + आश्लेषिताः → श्लेष्मणाश्लेषिताः (printed with ऽऽ).

questions.q: By unit 52, what is the fifth kalā named?
optionExplain: Pittadharā is the sixth kalā (unit 53).
Right: पंचमी पुरीषधरा नाम.
Śleṣmadharā is the fourth kalā (unit 51).
Śukradharā is the seventh kalā (unit 55).
questions.explain: The fifth kalā is Purīṣadharā, faeces-bearing.

questions.q: Put these printed words of unit 52 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The fifth, named Purīṣadharā; resting on the intestine (and the seats); lying in the unduka within the koṣṭha; the mala; it separates.
questions.rule: पंचमी पुरीषधरानाम → ह्यंत्रामपक्वाशयाश्रिता → कोष्ठांतरुंदुकस्थं → मलं → विभजति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 52 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The fifth kalā, faeces-bearing, resting on the seats, separates the mala in the koṣṭha.
questions.teaches: पुरीषधरा = पुरीष (faeces) + धरा (bearing): the kalā is named for what it holds.

questions.q: Which split of ह्यंत्र... in unit 52 is right?
optionExplain: हि before य stays हि: that would be printed हि यन्त्र.
ए + अ would give हेऽन्त्र, not ह्यन्त्र.
Right: इ before a dissimilar vowel becomes य्: हि + अन्त्र → ह्यन्त्र.
ह्य is not a word, and अ + अ would give ह्यान्त्र.
questions.explain: हि (indeed) + अन्त्र (intestine): इ + अ → य.

questions.q: By unit 52, what does Purīṣadharā do with the mala?
optionExplain: Cooking is said of Pittadharā (unit 53), not of this kalā.
Drying by Pitta's heat is Pittadharā's work (unit 53).
Setting in motion is said of śukra by Śukradharā (unit 55).
Right: मलं विभजति: it separates the mala.
questions.explain: Purīṣadharā separates the mala.

questions.q: By the rule of कोष्ठ + अन्तर् → कोष्ठान्तर्, how is वेद + अन्तः joined?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as कोष्ठ + अन्तर् → कोष्ठान्तर्.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Two short अ sounds merge into a long आ, not a short अ.
questions.explain: वेद + अन्तः = वेदान्तः, like कोष्ठ + अन्तर् = कोष्ठान्तर्.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as long आ: कोष्ठ + अन्तर् → कोष्ठान्तर्.

questions.q: By unit 53, where does Pittadharā lie?
options: Below the opening of the basti
Between the pakva and āma seats
Inside the flesh, with the blood
In the head, under the skull
optionExplain: That is the place of Śukradharā (unit 55).
Right: पक्वामाशयमध्यस्था: in the middle of the pakva and āma seats.
That is Raktadharā, the second kalā (unit 49).
Fat in the head, under the skull, is described with Medodharā (unit 50).
questions.explain: Pittadharā lies between the seats of the digested and the raw.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 53 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The food heading from the āmāśaya to the pakvāśaya; held by force; dried by Pitta's heat; cooked; the cooked released.
questions.rule: अन्नं → बलेन विधार्य्य → पित्ततेजसा शोषयंती → पचति → पक्कं च विमुंचति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: As seat of the inner fire, it holds the food facing the pakvāśaya, dries it, cooks it and releases it.
questions.teaches: अन्तरग्नि = the inner (digestive) fire; Pittadharā is its seat (अधिष्ठान).

questions.q: Which split of पक्वाशयोन्मुखम् is right?
optionExplain: अः before उ drops its visarga: that would give पक्वाशय उन्मुखम्.
न्मुखम् is not a word; the word is उन्मुखम् (facing toward).
Right: अ + उ → ओ: पक्वाशय + उन्मुखम् → पक्वाशयोन्मुखम्.
ए + उ does not give ओ; ए before a vowel becomes अय् (or अ).
questions.explain: पक्वाशय (seat of the digested) + उन्मुखम् (facing toward): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 53, which does Pittadharā do to the food?
options: Separates the waste in the unduka
Dries it by the heat of Pitta
Makes it pervade the whole body
optionExplain: Right: बलेन विधार्य.
That is Purīṣadharā's work (unit 52).
Right: पित्ततेजसा शोषयन्ती.
Pervading the whole body is said of Śukradharā (unit 55).
Right: पक्वं च विमुञ्चति.
questions.explain: It holds the food by force, dries it by Pitta's heat, cooks it and releases the cooked.
questions.rule: बलेन विधार्य, पित्ततेजसा शोषयन्ती पचति, पक्वं च विमुञ्चति.

questions.q: By the rule of पक्वाशय + उन्मुखम्, how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
अ + उ does not give ऊ; ऊ comes from उ + उ.
आ comes from अ + अ, not from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as पक्वाशय + उन्मुखम् → पक्वाशयोन्मुखम्.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like पक्वाशय + उन्मुखम् = पक्वाशयोन्मुखम्.
questions.teaches: अ followed by उ joins as ओ: पक्वाशय + उन्मुखम् → पक्वाशयोन्मुखम्.

questions.q: By unit 54, why does the organ get the name grahaṇī?
options: From its taking up of the food
From its place below the basti
From its holding of the semen
From its being made of fat
optionExplain: Right: अन्नस्य ग्रहणात्: from its taking up of food.
The place below the basti is Śukradharā's (unit 55).
Holding śukra is Śukradharā's work (unit 55).
Fat belongs to Medodharā (unit 50).
questions.explain: It takes up (ग्रहण) food, so it is named grahaṇī.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 54 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Hence, from its taking up of food, again the name grahaṇī; and its strength is Pitta itself, named agni; it keeps the body going.
questions.rule: ग्रहणात् → ग्रहणीसंज्ञा → बलं च तस्याः → पित्तमेव... → शरीरं वर्त्तयति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From taking up food, the name grahaṇī; its strength is Pitta; it keeps the body going.
questions.teaches: ग्रहणी is named from ग्रहण (taking up): the organ that takes up the food.

questions.q: Which split of ततोऽसावन्नस्य is right?
optionExplain: त् before a vowel becomes द्: that would give तदसौ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ; औ before a vowel → आव्.
ततो and असाव are not the words; they are ततः and असौ.
असा and वन्नस्य are not words; the words are असौ and अन्नस्य.
questions.explain: ततः (hence) + असौ (that one) + अन्नस्य (of food).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओऽ; औ + vowel → आव्.

questions.q: By unit 54, what is the strength (बल) of the grahaṇī?
options: Kapha, which holds the joints firm
Vāyu, which carries the food on
Pitta itself, which is named agni
The blood of the liver and spleen
optionExplain: Kapha holding the joints is Śleṣmadharā's (unit 51).
The unit names Pitta, not Vāyu, as its strength.
Right: बलं च तस्याः पित्तमेव अग्न्यभिधानम्.
Blood in the liver and spleen is Raktadharā's (unit 49).
questions.explain: Its strength is Pitta itself, which has the name agni.

questions.q: By the rule of असौ + अन्नस्य → असावन्नस्य, how is तौ + इति (those two, thus) joined?
optionExplain: आय् comes from ऐ before a vowel, not from औ.
अव् comes from ओ; औ gives आव् with a long आ.
औ does not stay unchanged before a vowel inside a sentence.
Right: औ before a vowel becomes आव्, as असौ + अन्नस्य → असावन्नस्य.
questions.explain: तौ + इति = ताविति, like असौ + अन्नस्य = असावन्नस्य.
questions.teaches: औ before a vowel becomes आव्: असौ + अन्नस्य → असावन्नस्य.

questions.q: By unit 55, what does Śukradharā do?
optionExplain: Right: शुक्रं प्रवर्त्तयति.
Kapha in the joints is Śleṣmadharā's (unit 51).
Separating the mala is Purīṣadharā's (unit 52).
Cooking by Pitta's heat is Pittadharā's (unit 53).
questions.explain: Śukradharā sets śukra in motion.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 55 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The seventh, Śukradharā; at two aṅgulas on the right side; and below the basti's opening (bladder, probable); resting on the urinary passage; pervading the whole body; it sets śukra in motion.
questions.rule: नाम → द्व्यंगुले... → बस्तिद्वारस्य चाधो → मूत्रमार्गमाश्रिता → सकलशरीरव्यापिनी → शुक्रं प्रवर्त्तयति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: On the right side, below the basti's opening (bladder, probable), on the urinary passage, pervading the body.
questions.teaches: बस्ति here = the bladder (urinary bladder, probable); बस्तिद्वार = its opening.

questions.q: Which split of चाधो (before मूत्रमार्ग) in unit 55 is right?
optionExplain: चा is not a word; the particle is च (and).
Right: अ + अ → आ, and अः before the voiced consonant म becomes ओ.
म् would not become ओ; it would stay as म् or ं.
ए + अ would give चेऽधः, not चाधः.
questions.explain: च (and) + अधः (below): अ + अ → आ; अधः + मूत्र → अधो मूत्र.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 55, which describe the place of Śukradharā?
options: Above the navel, on the left
Between the āma and pakva seats
optionExplain: Right: दक्षिणे पार्श्वे.
Right: बस्तिद्वारस्य चाधः; basti = bladder, probable.
The unit says the right side, and names no navel.
Right: मूत्रमार्गमाश्रिता.
That is the place of Pittadharā (unit 53).
questions.explain: Right side, below the basti's opening (bladder, probable), resting on the urinary passage.

questions.q: By the rule of द्वि + अङ्गुले → द्व्यङ्गुले, join प्रति + अक्षम्. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma): ____
questions.explain: प्रति + अक्षम् = प्रत्यक्षम्: इ before the dissimilar vowel अ becomes य्, as in द्व्यङ्गुले.
questions.teaches: इ before a dissimilar vowel becomes य्: द्वि + अङ्गुले → द्व्यङ्गुले.

questions.q: By unit 56, what is said of the doṣas, dhātus and malas?
options: They will be stated in the next part
They are the same as the kalās
They are not taught in this book
optionExplain: प्राक् means before, not later.
The line does not equate them with the kalās.
Right: प्रागुदिताः: stated before.
They have been stated before, so they are taught.
questions.explain: They have been stated before (प्राक् उदिताः).

questions.q: Put the three names of unit 56 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The doṣas, the dhātus and the malas have been stated before.

questions.q: Type the word of unit 56 that means 'before', in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma): ____
questions.explain: प्राक् (before) + उदिताः (stated) → प्रागुदिताः.
questions.teaches: प्राक् = before; before a vowel its क् becomes ग्: प्राक् + उदिताः → प्रागुदिताः.

questions.q: Why is दोषाः printed दोषा before धातवः?
options: After आ, the visarga becomes ओ before a voiced ध
दोषा is the feminine singular form
A visarga drops before every consonant of any kind
After आ, the visarga drops before a voiced sound
optionExplain: ओ comes from a visarga after short अ, not after आ.
The data reads दोषाः, masculine nominative plural.
Before unvoiced sounds it stays or changes; it is not dropped.
Right: ध is voiced, so दोषाः → दोषा.
questions.explain: दोषाः + धातवः = दोषा धातवः: आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga.

questions.q: Why does मलाः become मलाश् before च in unit 56?
options: Before च, a visarga becomes श्
Before च, a visarga becomes र्
Before च, a visarga becomes स्
Before च, a visarga becomes ओ
optionExplain: Right: विसर्ग + च → श्च: मलाः + च → मलाश्च.
र् arises after vowels other than अ/आ before voiced sounds; च is unvoiced.
स् arises before त or थ, not before च.
ओ arises from अः before a voiced consonant; च is unvoiced.
questions.explain: मलाः + च = मलाश्च: before च the visarga becomes श्.

questions.q: By the rule of धातवः + मलाः → धातवो मलाः, how is बालः + गच्छति (the boy goes) written?
optionExplain: Dropping the visarga to आ is the rule after आ, not after short अ.
Right: अः before the voiced consonant ग becomes ओ, as धातवः + मलाः.
र् comes after vowels other than अ and आ.
Before a voiced consonant the visarga after अ does not stay.
questions.explain: बालः + गच्छति = बालो गच्छति, like धातवः + मलाः = धातवो मलाः.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: धातवः + मलाः → धातवो मलाः.

questions.q: By unit 57, which of these is one of the five buddhīndriyas?
optionExplain: The hand is an organ of action (unit 58).
The foot is an organ of action (unit 58).
Right: घ्राणं च: smell is the fifth in the list.
The genital organ is an organ of action (unit 58).
questions.explain: The five are śrotra, sparśana, darśana, rasana and ghrāṇa.
questions.rule: श्रोत्रं स्पर्शनं दर्शनं रसनं घ्राणं च.

questions.q: Put the five buddhīndriyas of unit 57 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Hearing, touch, sight, taste, smell.

questions.q: Match each object (viṣaya) of unit 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The objects in order: sound, touch, form, taste, smell.
questions.teaches: विषय = the object of a sense: शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गन्ध.

questions.q: Which split of बुद्धींद्रियाणि is right?
optionExplain: द्रियाणि is not a word; the word is इन्द्रियाणि.
ए + इ does not give ई.
अः + इ would give बुद्ध इन्द्रियाणि.
Right: इ + इ → ई: बुद्धि + इन्द्रियाणि → बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि.
questions.explain: बुद्धि (cognition) + इन्द्रियाणि (sense-organs): इ + इ → ई.

questions.q: A learner lists the objects as शब्द, रूप, स्पर्श, रस, गन्ध. By unit 57, what is wrong?
options: Nothing: it is the printed order
optionExplain: Right: The printed order is शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गन्ध.
रस comes before गन्ध, as the learner has it.
शब्द comes first in the printed list.
The printed order puts स्पर्श before रूप.
questions.explain: The printed order is शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गन्ध.

questions.q: By the rule of बुद्धि + इन्द्रियाणि, how is मुनि + इन्द्रः (chief of sages) joined?
optionExplain: य् arises only before a dissimilar vowel; इ + इ is similar.
Right: इ + इ → ई, as बुद्धि + इन्द्रियाणि → बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + इ.
Two इ sounds make a long ई, not a short इ.
questions.explain: मुनि + इन्द्रः = मुनीन्द्रः, like बुद्धि + इन्द्रियाणि = बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि.
questions.teaches: Two इ sounds join as long ई: बुद्धि + इन्द्रियाणि → बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि.

questions.q: By unit 58, which of these is a karmendriya (organ of action)?
optionExplain: The skin is a seat of a sense-organ of cognition.
The eyes are a seat of a sense-organ of cognition.
Right: पाणि is one of the five organs of action.
The ears are a seat of a sense-organ of cognition.
questions.explain: The hand (पाणि) is an organ of action.

questions.q: Put the seats of the buddhīndriyas in unit 58 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The two ears, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, the two nostrils.

questions.q: Match each organ of action in unit 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five organs of action: anus, genital organ, hand, foot.
questions.teaches: अपायु = anus and उपस्थ = genital organ (both standard).

questions.q: By the data's grammar, which seats in unit 58 are named in the dual?
optionExplain: Feminine nominative singular: one skin.
Right: masculine nominative dual, the two ears.
Feminine nominative singular: one tongue.
Right: neuter nominative dual, the two eyes.
Right: feminine nominative dual, the two nostrils.
questions.explain: कर्णौ, अक्षिणी and नासिके are duals; त्वक् and जिह्वा are singular.

questions.q: Which split of त्वगक्षिणी is right?
optionExplain: त्वग is not the word, and अ + अ would give त्वगाक्षिणी.
क्षिणी is not a word; the word is अक्षिणी (the two eyes).
आ + अ would give त्वचाक्षिणी, with no ग्.
Right: क् at the end of a word becomes ग् before a vowel.
questions.explain: त्वक् (skin) + अक्षिणी (the two eyes): क् → ग् before a vowel.

questions.q: By the rule of त्वक् + अक्षिणी → त्वगक्षिणी, how is दिक् + अन्तः (horizon) joined?
optionExplain: Right: Final क् becomes ग् before a vowel, as त्वक् + अक्षिणी.
Before a vowel the final क् becomes the voiced ग्.
ङ् arises before a nasal, not before a vowel.
The short अ of अन्तः stays short.
questions.explain: दिक् + अन्तः = दिगन्तः, like त्वक् + अक्षिणी = त्वगक्षिणी.
questions.teaches: A word-final क् becomes ग् before a vowel: त्वक् + अक्षिणी → त्वगक्षिणी.

questions.q: By unit 59, why is the mind (manas) beyond the sense-organs?
options: It is joined with no object at all
It lies wholly outside the body
optionExplain: The opposite: it is associated with all objects.
Right: सर्वार्थैरन्वयात्: because of its association with all objects.
The line says nothing of the mind lying outside the body.
Speech is not named as the reason.
questions.explain: The mind is beyond the senses because it is associated with all objects.

questions.q: Put the five purposes of unit 59 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Speaking, discharge, delight, taking, going.

questions.q: Match each word of the second line of unit 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The mind is beyond the senses, from its association with all objects.
questions.teaches: अन्वय = association, connection: the mind is linked with all objects.

questions.q: Which split of अतींद्रियं is right?
optionExplain: त् before a vowel would become द्: अदिन्द्रियम्.
ए + इ does not give ई.
Right: इ + इ → ई: अति + इन्द्रियम् → अतीन्द्रियम्.
द्रियम् is not a word; the word is इन्द्रियम्.
questions.explain: अति (beyond) + इन्द्रियम् (sense-organ): इ + इ → ई.

questions.q: In unit 59, what does आदान, one of the five purposes, mean?
optionExplain: Giving is दान; आ-दान is taking.
Going is गमन, the last purpose.
Speaking is वचन, the first purpose.
Right: आदान = taking, grasping.
questions.explain: आदान = taking.

questions.q: By the rule of सर्वार्थैः + अन्वयात्, how is देवैः + उक्तम् (said by the gods) written?
optionExplain: Right: After ऐ, a visarga becomes र् before a vowel, as सर्वार्थैः + अन्वयात्.
आय् comes from ऐ without a visarga; here the visarga gives र्.
Before a vowel the visarga after ऐ does not stay; it becomes र्.
ओ comes from अ + उ; the word ends in ऐः.
questions.explain: देवैः + उक्तम् = देवैरुक्तम्, like सर्वार्थैः + अन्वयात् = सर्वार्थैरन्वयात्.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ → र् before a vowel or voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: After a vowel other than अ/आ, a visarga becomes र् before a vowel: सर्वार्थैः + अन्वयात् → सर्वार्थैरन्वयात्.

questions.q: By unit 60, through what do the sense-organs engage with their objects?
optionExplain: Pitta's heat cooks the food in unit 53; it is not named here.
Right: तद्योगेन: by union with it, the mind.
Kapha is not named in unit 60.
The seats are listed later (unit 62), not named here.
questions.explain: Union with the mind makes the senses engage with their objects.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 60 in the line's order.
questions.explain: By union with it, and, of the sense-organs, the engagement with objects.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By union with the mind, the sense-organs engage with objects.
questions.teaches: अर्थ here = the object of a sense; अर्थप्रवृत्ति = engagement with objects.

questions.q: Which split of चेंद्रियाणाम् is right?
optionExplain: चे is not a word; the particle is च (and).
एन्द्रियाणाम् is not the word; it is इन्द्रियाणाम्.
Right: अ + इ → ए: च + इन्द्रियाणाम् → चेन्द्रियाणाम्.
च has no visarga; it is an indeclinable.
questions.explain: च (and) + इन्द्रियाणाम् (of the sense-organs): अ + इ → ए.

questions.q: Why is तत् printed तद् in तद्योगेन?
options: त् before the unvoiced य stays त्
त् before य becomes the nasal न्
त् before any consonant becomes द्
त् before the voiced य becomes द्
optionExplain: य is voiced, and the print has द्.
न् may arise (optionally) only before a nasal; य is not a nasal.
Before unvoiced consonants त् stays (आमाशयात्पक्वाशय).
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: तत् + योगेन = तद्योगेन: त् → द् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: By the rule of च + इन्द्रियाणाम् → चेन्द्रियाणाम्, join न + इति. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma): ____
questions.explain: न + इति = नेति: अ + इ → ए, as च + इन्द्रियाणाम् → चेन्द्रियाणाम्.
questions.teaches: अ followed by इ joins as ए: च + इन्द्रियाणाम् → चेन्द्रियाणाम्.

questions.q: By unit 61, the mind has the nature of what?
options: Of the organs of action only
optionExplain: Right: उभयात्मकत्वात्: of the nature of both, cognition and action.
The line says both kinds, not action only.
The line says both kinds, not cognition only.
उभय means both, not neither.
questions.explain: The mind has the nature of both the buddhīndriyas and the karmendriyas.

questions.q: Put the members of the compound of unit 61 in order.
questions.explain: Cognition, action, sense-organ, both, from having the nature.

questions.q: Match each member of unit 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Having the nature of both: cognition and action.
questions.teaches: उभयात्मक = having the nature of both.

questions.q: Which split of ...इन्द्रियोभय... is right?
optionExplain: अः before उ drops its visarga: that would give इन्द्रिय उभय.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: इन्द्रिय + उभय → इन्द्रियोभय.
भय (fear) is not the word; the word is उभय (both).
ए + उ does not give ओ.
questions.explain: इन्द्रिय (sense-organ) + उभय (both): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: What does the ablative ending -त्वात् express in unit 61?
options: A place: in the state of being
A purpose: for the sake of being
A reason: because of its being
A time: at the moment of being
optionExplain: A place would need the locative (-त्वे).
A purpose would need the dative (-त्वाय).
Right: The data: abl. sg.; English 'because of having the nature'.
Time would need the locative, not the ablative.
questions.explain: -त्वात् = because of being: an ablative of reason.

questions.q: By the rule of आत्मकत्वात् + च → आत्मकत्वाच्च, how is तस्मात् + च (and therefore) written?
optionExplain: द् arises before a voiced sound; च is unvoiced.
श् comes from a visarga before च, not from त्.
The final त् is not dropped before च.
Right: त् before च becomes च्, as आत्मकत्वात् + च.
questions.explain: तस्मात् + च = तस्माच्च, like आत्मकत्वात् + च = आत्मकत्वाच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: आत्मकत्वात् + च → आत्मकत्वाच्च.

questions.q: By unit 62, which receptacle comes first in the list of seats?
optionExplain: Right: क्रमादसृक्...: blood comes first.
Urine comes last in the list.
Kapha comes second, after blood.
Vāyu comes sixth, before urine.
questions.explain: The list opens with the receptacle of blood.

questions.q: After असृक् (blood), put the next receptacles of unit 62 in order.
questions.explain: Blood, then Kapha, āma, Pitta, pakva, Vāyu, urine.
questions.rule: कफ → आम → पित्त → पक्व → वायु → मूत्र.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Receptacles of blood, Kapha, the raw, Pitta, the digested, Vāyu and urine.
questions.teaches: आधार = receptacle: each seat is named by what it holds.

questions.q: Which split of कफाम... in unit 62 is right?
optionExplain: कफा and अम are not the words; they are कफ and आम.
Right: अ + आ → आ: कफ + आम → कफाम.
अः before आ drops its visarga: that would give कफ आम.
ए + आ would give कफ आम or कफयाम, not कफाम.
questions.explain: कफ (Kapha) + आम (the raw): अ + आ → आ.

questions.q: A learner places the Pitta seat between Kapha and āma in unit 62's list. What is right?
options: Pitta comes between blood and Kapha
Pitta comes between Vāyu and urine
Pitta comes between āma and pakva
optionExplain: Blood is followed directly by Kapha.
Vāyu is followed directly by urine.
Right: The order is ... आम, पित्त, पक्व ...
Urine closes the list.
questions.explain: āma, then Pitta, then pakva.

questions.q: By the rule of क्रमात् + असृक् → क्रमादसृक्, how is तत् + अपि (that too) joined?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the final त् becomes the voiced द्.
न् arises before a nasal, not before a vowel.
The अ of अपि does not change to ए.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as क्रमात् + असृक्.
questions.explain: तत् + अपि = तदपि, like क्रमात् + असृक् = क्रमादसृक्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: क्रमात् + असृक् → क्रमादसृक्.

questions.q: By unit 63, which seat do women have in addition, as the eighth?
optionExplain: Right: गर्भाशयोऽष्टमः: the womb is the eighth.
The pakva seat is one of the list of unit 62.
The āma seat is one of the list of unit 62.
The urine seat closes the list of unit 62.
questions.explain: In women, the eighth seat is the garbhāśaya.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 63 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of women, of the Pitta and pakva seats, in the middle, the garbhāśaya, the eighth.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of women, in the middle (of the two seats), the womb is the eighth.
questions.teaches: गर्भाशय = गर्भ + आशय: the seat of the embryo, the womb (uterus, standard).

questions.q: Which split of गर्भाशयोऽष्टमः is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give गर्भाशयेऽष्टमः.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: the अ of अष्टमः is dropped (ऽ).
ष्टमः is not a word; the word is अष्टमः (eighth).
अ + अ would give गर्भाशयाष्टमः.
questions.explain: गर्भाशयः (womb) + अष्टमः (eighth): अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: By unit 63, where does the garbhāśaya lie?
options: Between the blood and Kapha seats
Between the Vāyu and urine seats
Between the Pitta and pakva seats
Between the āma and Pitta seats
optionExplain: The line names the Pitta and pakva seats.
The line names the Pitta and pakva seats.
Right: पित्तपक्वाशययोर्मध्ये.
The line names Pitta and pakva, not āma.
questions.explain: The womb lies between the Pitta seat and the pakvāśaya.

questions.q: By the rule of गर्भाशयः + अष्टमः, how is नरः + अयम् (this man) written?
optionExplain: अ + अ → आ holds only without a visarga.
Before short अ the visarga after अ gives ओ, with ऽ.
र् comes after vowels other than अ and आ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ, as गर्भाशयः + अष्टमः → गर्भाशयोऽष्टमः.
questions.explain: नरः + अयम् = नरोऽयम्, like गर्भाशयः + अष्टमः = गर्भाशयोऽष्टमः.
questions.teaches: अः before short अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped (ऽ): गर्भाशयः + अष्टमः → गर्भाशयोऽष्टमः.

questions.q: By unit 64, what are the organs bound in the seats called?
optionExplain: Right: कोष्ठांगानि: the members of the koṣṭha, the trunk.
The organs of action are speech, anus, genital, hand and foot (unit 58).
The seats of the senses are ears, skin, eyes, tongue, nostrils (unit 58).
The seven kalās are another topic (from unit 46).
questions.explain: The organs bound in the seats are the koṣṭhāṅgas, members of the trunk.

questions.q: Put these organs of unit 64 in the line's order (the flagged वक्क is left out).
questions.explain: Heart, liver, spleen, lung, unduka, (kidney), intestine, and so on.
questions.rule: हृदय → यकृत् → प्लीह → फुप्फुस → उंदुक → अंत्र.

questions.q: Match each organ of unit 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the koṣṭhāṅgas with their standard meanings.
questions.teaches: कोष्ठ = the trunk, belly; कोष्ठांग = a member (organ) of the koṣṭha.

questions.q: Which split of कोष्ठांगानि is right?
optionExplain: म् before a vowel stays: that would give कोष्ठमङ्गानि.
Right: अ + अ → आ: कोष्ठ + अङ्गानि → कोष्ठाङ्गानि (printed with ं).
अः + अ gives ओऽ: that would be कोष्ठोऽङ्गानि.
को and ष्ठाङ्गानि are not the words; the words are कोष्ठ, अङ्ग.
questions.explain: कोष्ठ (trunk) + अङ्गानि (members): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which organs does unit 64 name among the koṣṭhāṅgas?
optionExplain: Not in this list; the tongue is a seat of a sense (unit 58).
Right: हृदय comes first.
Not in this list; the eyes are a seat of a sense (unit 58).
Right: प्लीह-.
Right: फुप्फुस-.
questions.explain: Heart, spleen and lung are named; tongue and eye are seats of the senses.

questions.q: By the rule of फुप्फुस + उंदुक → फुप्फुसोंदुक, how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined?
optionExplain: The अ is not dropped; अ + उ merge as ओ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as फुप्फुस + उंदुक → फुप्फुसोंदुक.
व् comes from उ before a vowel, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like फुप्फुस + उंदुक = फुप्फुसोंदुक.
questions.teaches: अ + उ → ओ: फुप्फुस + उंदुक → फुप्फुसोंदुक.

questions.q: By unit 65, which organs arise from the blood?
optionExplain: No bone or joint is named in unit 65.
No eye or ear is named in unit 65.
No hair or nail is named in unit 65.
Right: जायते यकृत्प्लीहा च: the liver and the spleen arise.
questions.explain: From the blood, inflated and cooked, the liver and spleen arise.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 65 in the line's order (the unclear शोणितस्याच्छतो is left out).
questions.explain: There, being inflated by samāna, being cooked by the body's heat, (of blood), arise the liver and spleen.
questions.rule: तत्र → समानेनाध्मायमानस्य → देहोष्मणा पच्यमानस्य → जायते → यकृत्प्लीहा च.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Blood inflated by samāna and cooked by the body's heat: the liver and spleen arise.
questions.teaches: आध्मायमान = being inflated: the present passive participle of आ-√ध्मा.

questions.q: Which split of देहोष्मणा is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ऊ → ओ: देह + ऊष्मणा → देहोष्मणा.
अः before a vowel other than अ loses the visarga: देह ऊष्मणा, no ओ.
ओ before a vowel becomes अव्: that would give देहवूष्मणा.
दे and होष्मणा are not the words; the words are देह, ऊष्मन्.
questions.explain: देह (body) + ऊष्मणा (by the heat): अ + ऊ → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 65, what does the body's heat do to the blood?
optionExplain: Nothing cools it; the heat cooks it (पच्यमान).
Right: पच्यमानस्य: being cooked by the body's heat.
No drying is named; the heat cooks it.
No stopping is named; the heat cooks it.
questions.explain: Samāna inflates the blood; the body's heat cooks it.

questions.q: By the rule of देह + ऊष्मणा → देहोष्मणा, how is जल + ऊर्मिः (a wave of water) joined?
optionExplain: The अ is not dropped; अ + ऊ merge as ओ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + ऊ.
Right: अ + ऊ → ओ, as देह + ऊष्मणा → देहोष्मणा.
व् comes from उ/ऊ before a vowel, not from अ + ऊ.
questions.explain: जल + ऊर्मिः = जलोर्मिः, like देह + ऊष्मणा = देहोष्मणा.
questions.teaches: अ + ऊ → ओ: देह + ऊष्मणा → देहोष्मणा.

questions.q: By unit 66, from what does the lung arise?
options: From the essence of blood and fat
From the essence of blood and flesh
optionExplain: The dregs give the unduka (unit 67), not the lung.
Blood and fat give the kidneys (unit 68).
Blood and flesh give the intestines (unit 69).
Right: रक्तफेनात्: from the froth of blood.
questions.explain: The lung arises from the froth of blood.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the froth of blood, the lung.

questions.q: From the ____ of blood the lung arises (unit 66). Type the Sanskrit word for 'froth' in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: फेन = froth: रक्तफेनात् = from the froth of blood.
questions.teaches: फेन = froth, foam: रक्तफेन = the froth of blood.
questions.rule: रक्त + फेन = the froth of blood.

questions.q: Which split of रक्तफेनात्फुप्फुसं is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् stays before the unvoiced फ; the final म् is printed ं.
त्फुप्फुसम् is not a word; the ablative is रक्तफेनात्.
A visarga gives no त्: that would be रक्तफेनः फुप्फुसम्.
म् before फ would be written ं: रक्तफेनं फुप्फुसम्.
questions.explain: रक्तफेनात् (from the froth of blood) + फुप्फुसम् (lung).
questions.rule: त् stays before an unvoiced consonant such as क, प, फ, स (not before च, छ, श, ट, where it changes).

questions.q: Unit 66 prints no verb. By the data, which verb is understood?
optionExplain: Nothing perishes; the organs arise.
Right: The verb of unit 65 is carried; it is not printed.
No holding is named; the organs arise.
Unit 65 has the participle पच्यमान, not this verb; the carried verb is जायते.
questions.explain: जायते (arises) is carried from unit 65: from the froth of blood the lung arises.
questions.rule: Elliptical line: the verb comes from unit 65.

questions.q: By the -आत् of रक्तफेनात् (from the froth), what does वृक्षात् फलं पतति mean?
options: The fruit falls on the tree
The fruit of the tree falls
The fruit falls from the tree
The tree falls with the fruit
optionExplain: On the tree would be the locative वृक्षे.
Of the tree would be the genitive वृक्षस्य.
Right: -आत् is the ablative: from the tree, as रक्तफेनात् = from the froth.
With would be the instrumental, and the tree is not the subject.
questions.explain: वृक्षात् = from the tree, as रक्तफेनात् = from the froth of blood.
questions.teaches: -आत् is the ablative ending (from) of a-stem nouns: रक्तफेनात् = from the froth of blood.

questions.q: By unit 67, from what does the unduka arise?
options: From the essence of blood and fat
From the essence of Kapha and blood
optionExplain: The froth gives the lung (unit 66).
Blood and fat give the kidneys (unit 68).
Kapha and blood give the heart (unit 73).
Right: रक्तकिट्टात्: from the dregs (kiṭṭa) of blood.
questions.explain: The unduka arises from the dregs of blood.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the dregs of blood, the unduka.

questions.q: What does किट्ट in unit 67 mean?
optionExplain: Right: The data glosses किट्ट as dregs, sediment.
Froth is फेन (unit 66).
The clear essence is प्रसाद (unit 68).
Heat is ऊष्मन् (unit 65).
questions.explain: किट्ट = dregs, sediment.
questions.teaches: किट्ट = dregs, sediment: रक्तकिट्ट = the dregs of blood.

questions.q: Which split of रक्तकिट्टादुंदुकः is right?
optionExplain: दुंदुकः is not the word; the organ is the उंदुक.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्.
अः + उ drops the visarga: that would be रक्तकिट्ट उंदुकः.
म् before a vowel stays: that would be रक्तकिट्टमुंदुकः.
questions.explain: रक्तकिट्टात् (from the dregs of blood) + उंदुकः: त् + vowel → द्.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 67?
options: The unduka comes from the dregs of blood
रक्तकिट्टात् is ablative: from the dregs
The line prints its own verb
optionExplain: No: किट्ट is dregs; froth (फेन) is unit 66.
Right: रक्तकिट्टात् ... उंदुकः.
Right: -आत्, from.
No: 'arises' is carried from unit 65.
questions.explain: From the dregs of blood, the unduka; the verb is carried from unit 65.

questions.q: By the rule of रक्तकिट्टात् + उंदुकः, how is तत् + उदकम् (that water) joined?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् does not stay; it becomes द्.
The द् is not doubled.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्.
The short उ of उदकम् stays short.
questions.explain: तत् + उदकम् = तदुदकम्, like रक्तकिट्टात् + उंदुकः = रक्तकिट्टादुंदुकः.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: रक्तकिट्टात् + उंदुकः → रक्तकिट्टादुंदुकः.

questions.q: By unit 68, from what do the two kidneys arise?
options: From the essence of blood and flesh
From the essence of Kapha and blood
From the essence of blood and fat
optionExplain: Blood and flesh give the intestines (unit 69).
Kapha and blood give the heart (unit 73).
The froth gives the lung (unit 66).
Right: रक्तमेदःप्रसादात्: from the clear essence of blood and fat.
questions.explain: The kidneys arise from the clear essence of blood and fat.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the clear essence of blood and fat, the two kidneys.

questions.q: Why is वृक्कौ in unit 68 read as 'the two kidneys'?
options: -औ of an a-stem noun is the dual
-औ of an a-stem noun is the plural
-औ here is a locative, 'in the kidney'
-औ here is a genitive, 'of the kidney'
optionExplain: Right: The data labels वृक्कौ m. nom. dual: the two kidneys.
The a-stem plural is वृक्काः.
For an a-stem the locative is वृक्के; -औ is locative only for i/u-stems (कुक्षौ).
The genitive is वृक्कस्य.
questions.explain: वृक्कौ = the two kidneys: masculine, nominative, dual.
questions.teaches: वृक्कौ is a masculine dual: the two kidneys.

questions.q: Which split of प्रसादाद्वृक्कौ is right?
optionExplain: द्वृक्कौ is not a word; the word is वृक्कौ.
Right: त् before the voiced व becomes द्.
म् before व would be written ं: प्रसादं वृक्कौ.
अः before a voiced consonant gives ओ: प्रसादो वृक्कौ.
questions.explain: प्रसादात् (from the clear essence) + वृक्कौ: त् + voiced consonant → द्.

questions.q: Which sources does unit 68 name for the kidneys?
optionExplain: Kapha goes with blood for the heart (unit 73), not here.
Right: रक्त-.
Flesh goes with blood for the intestines (unit 69), not here.
Right: मेदः-.
questions.explain: The clear essence of blood and fat: रक्तमेदःप्रसादात्.

questions.q: By the rule of प्रसादात् + वृक्कौ, how is जगत् + गुरुः (teacher of the world) joined?
optionExplain: Before a voiced consonant the त् does not stay.
त् becomes न् (optionally) only before a nasal, not before ग.
Right: त् before the voiced ग becomes द्.
The ग of गुरुः stays ग.
questions.explain: जगत् + गुरुः = जगद्गुरुः, like प्रसादात् + वृक्कौ = प्रसादाद्वृक्कौ.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: प्रसादात् + वृक्कौ → प्रसादाद्वृक्कौ.

questions.q: By unit 69, from what do the intestines arise?
options: From the essence of blood and fat
From the essence of Kapha and blood
From the essence of blood and flesh
optionExplain: Blood and fat give the kidneys (unit 68).
Kapha and blood give the heart (unit 73).
The dregs give the unduka (unit 67).
Right: रक्तमांसप्रसादात्: from the clear essence of blood and flesh.
questions.explain: The intestines arise from the clear essence of blood and flesh.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 69 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Blood, flesh, from the clear essence, the intestines.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the clear essence of blood and flesh, the intestines.
questions.teaches: मांस = flesh: रक्तमांसप्रसाद = the clear essence of blood and flesh.

questions.q: Which split of प्रसादादंत्राणि is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्.
A long आ would stay long: प्रसादादान्त्राणि.
अः + अ gives ओऽ: प्रसादोऽन्त्राणि.
दन्त्राणि is not a word; the word is अन्त्राणि.
questions.explain: प्रसादात् (from the clear essence) + अन्त्राणि (intestines): त् + vowel → द्.

questions.q: What does the ending of अन्त्राणि in unit 69 show?
optionExplain: A neuter dual would be अन्त्रे.
Right: The data labels it n. nom. pl.
The singular would be अन्त्रम्.
That would be अन्त्रैः.
questions.explain: अन्त्राणि is neuter nominative plural: the intestines.

questions.q: By the pattern of रक्तमांस (blood and flesh), what does मातापितरौ mean?
optionExplain: That would be a tatpuruṣa (मातुः पिता); the dual -औ marks two persons.
Nothing here means 'like'.
Right: A dvandva: both members joined by 'and', like रक्त and मांस.
Nothing here means 'without'.
questions.explain: मातापितरौ = mother and father, as रक्तमांस = blood and flesh.
questions.teaches: A dvandva joins its members with 'and': रक्तमांस = blood and flesh.

questions.q: By unit 70, how long are the intestines in men?
optionExplain: The line has त्रि (three), not seven.
Three vyāmas is the women's length (unit 71).
The line has त्रि (three), not eight.
Right: सार्द्धत्रिव्यामानि: three and a half vyāmas.
questions.explain: In men the intestines are three and a half vyāmas.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 70 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Those (are) three and a half vyāmas, of men.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Those intestines are three and a half arm-spans in men.
questions.teaches: व्याम = the span of the outstretched arms, a measure of length.

questions.q: In unit 70, to what does तानि (those, neuter plural) point?
optionExplain: Right: अन्त्राणि is neuter plural, like तानि; the data names it the antecedent.
वृक्कौ is masculine dual; it would need तौ.
हृदयम् is singular and comes later.
फुप्फुसम् is singular; it would need तत्.
questions.explain: तानि = those intestines (अन्त्राणि, unit 69).
questions.rule: A pronoun agrees in gender and number with what it points to.

questions.q: A student renders unit 70 as: Those are three and a half vyāmas in women. Which word is wrong?
optionExplain: त्रि is three: right.
Right: पुंसाम् is of men; women come in unit 71.
सार्ध, with a half: right.
तानि, those: right.
questions.explain: Those (intestines) are three and a half vyāmas in men.

questions.q: By सार्द्धत्रि (three and a half), what does सार्धद्वि mean?
optionExplain: द्वि is two, so the whole is two and a half.
सार्ध means with a half, not half of.
Right: सार्ध + द्वि: two with a half more.
सार्ध adds a half to two.
questions.explain: सार्धद्वि = two and a half, as सार्धत्रि = three and a half.
questions.rule: सार्ध + number = that number and a half.
questions.teaches: सार्ध (with a half) before a number adds a half: सार्धत्रि = three and a half.

questions.q: By unit 71, how long are the intestines in women?
optionExplain: That is the men's length (unit 70).
The line has त्रि, three.
The line has त्रि, three.
Right: त्रिव्यामानि: three vyāmas.
questions.explain: In women the intestines are three vyāmas.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three vyāmas, in women.

questions.q: Unit 71 prints no noun. By the data, what does it measure?
optionExplain: Right: तानि (the intestines) is carried from unit 70.
The kidneys get no length; तानि of unit 70 is carried.
Unit 75 comes later and gives no length.
The heart comes later and gives no length.
questions.explain: The intestines (तानि of unit 70) are understood.
questions.rule: Elliptical line: the noun comes from unit 70.
questions.teaches: An elliptical line carries its noun and verb from the line before: तानि of unit 70.

questions.q: What does the ending of स्त्रीणाम् in unit 71 show?
optionExplain: That would be स्त्रियाः.
Right: The data labels it f. gen. pl.
That would be स्त्रीभिः.
That would be स्त्रियः.
questions.explain: स्त्रीणाम् = of women: genitive plural.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 71?
options: The women's length is three and a half vyāmas
The noun measured is printed in this line
The women's length is three vyāmas
optionExplain: No: सार्ध is not in this line; that is the men's length (unit 70).
No: तानि (the intestines) is carried from unit 70.
Right: त्रिव्यामानि.
Right: f. gen. pl.
questions.explain: In women, three vyāmas; the noun is carried from unit 70.

questions.q: By त्रिव्यामानि, where त्रि counts the vyāmas, what does पञ्च वर्षाणि mean?
optionExplain: The fifth would be पञ्चमम्.
Nothing here means each.
Right: पञ्च counts the years, as त्रि counts the vyāmas.
No men are named; पञ्च counts the years.
questions.explain: पञ्च वर्षाणि = five years, as त्रिव्यामानि = three vyāmas.
questions.rule: A number before a noun counts it.
questions.teaches: A number before a noun counts it: त्रिव्यामानि = three vyāmas.

questions.q: By unit 72, with what is the blood joined?
optionExplain: No water is named in unit 72.
No milk or honey is named in unit 72.
No food is named in unit 72.
Right: अनिलयोगात्: from union with anila, Vāyu.
questions.explain: The blood is joined with Vāyu (anila).

questions.q: Match each part of unit 72 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the union of blood with Vāyu.

questions.q: What does अनिल in unit 72 mean?
optionExplain: Right: The data glosses अनिल as Vāyu (wind).
That is देहोष्मन् (unit 65).
Water is जल or उदक.
Earth is पृथ्वी.
questions.explain: अनिल = Vāyu, the wind.
questions.teaches: अनिल = Vāyu, wind: अनिलयोग = union with Vāyu.

questions.q: Which split of रक्तस्यानिल is right?
optionExplain: निल is not a word, and no long आ would come.
Right: अ + अ → आ: रक्तस्य + अनिल → रक्तस्यानिल.
ए + अ would give रक्तस्येऽनिल.
स्यानिल is not a word; the genitive is रक्तस्य.
questions.explain: रक्तस्य (of blood) + अनिल (Vāyu): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 72?
options: The line prints its own verb
The blood is joined with Kapha
optionExplain: Right: रक्तस्य अनिलयोगात्.
No: 'arises' is carried from unit 65.
No: अनिल is Vāyu, not Kapha (कफ).
Right: -आत्, from.
questions.explain: From the union of blood with Vāyu; the last word is unclear and the verb is carried.

questions.q: By the rule of रक्तस्य + अनिल, how is सूर्य + अस्तः (sunset) joined?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as रक्तस्य + अनिल → रक्तस्यानिल.
The avagraha marks an अ dropped after ए or ओ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + अस्तः = सूर्यास्तः, like रक्तस्य + अनिल = रक्तस्यानिल.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as आ: रक्तस्य + अनिल → रक्तस्यानिल.

questions.q: By unit 73, from what does the heart arise?
options: From the essence of blood and fat
From the essence of blood and flesh
From the essence of Kapha and blood
optionExplain: Blood and fat give the kidneys (unit 68).
Blood and flesh give the intestines (unit 69).
The dregs give the unduka (unit 67).
Right: श्लेष्मरक्तप्रसादात्: from the clear essence of Kapha and blood.
questions.explain: The heart arises from the clear essence of Kapha and blood.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 73 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The heart, moreover, arises from the clear essence of Kapha and blood; like a lotus bud, hollow, face downward.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The heart arises; it is like a lotus bud, hollow, with its face downward.
questions.teaches: पद्मकोशसंकाश = resembling a lotus bud (lotus, Nelumbo nucifera: standard).

questions.q: Which split of अधोमुखं is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः + a voiced consonant (म) → ओ.
अः + उ drops the visarga (अध उमुखम्), and उमुख is not a word.
म् before म would be written ं or म्म्: अधंमुखम्.
ओमुख is not a word, and ओ + ओ would give अवो.
questions.explain: अधः (downward) + मुखम् (face): अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ (अः + अ → ओऽ).

questions.q: Which describe the heart in unit 73?
optionExplain: Right: सुषिरम्.
The heart is hollow (सुषिर).
Right: पद्मकोशसंकाशम्.
Right: अधोमुखम्.
अधोमुख: downward, not upward.
questions.explain: Like a lotus bud, hollow, face downward.

questions.q: By the rule of अधः + मुखम् → अधोमुखम्, how is मनः + रथः (wish) joined?
optionExplain: After अ the visarga is not simply dropped before र.
Right: अः + a voiced consonant (र) → ओ.
The avagraha marks a dropped अ; रथः begins with र.
आ does not come from अः before र.
questions.explain: मनः + रथः = मनोरथः, like अधः + मुखम् = अधोमुखम्.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: अधः + मुखम् → अधोमुखम्.

questions.q: By unit 74, the heart is especially the seat of what?
optionExplain: No bone is named; it is the seat of cetanā.
No hunger or thirst is named in unit 74.
Right: चेतनायाः स्थानम्: the seat of consciousness.
No urine is named in unit 74; the heart is the seat of cetanā.
questions.explain: The heart is especially the seat of consciousness.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 74 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Seat of consciousness and of the states that follow it; on its left spleen and lung; on the right liver and kloman.
questions.rule: ...स्थानं → ...चेतनानुगानां → तस्य वामपार्श्वे → प्लीहा फुप्फुसश्च → दक्षिणतो → यकृत्क्लोमंच.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The seat of consciousness; organs on the left and on the right.
questions.teaches: वाम = left; दक्षिणतः = on the right: the two sides of the heart.

questions.q: Why is दक्षिणतः printed दक्षिणतो before यकृत् in unit 74?
options: अः becomes ओ before every consonant
दक्षिणतो is a new word, 'of the south'
After अ the visarga drops before य
अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant
optionExplain: Not before an unvoiced one: फुप्फुसः + च → फुप्फुसश्च, here.
The data reads दक्षिणतः, on the right.
After अ, before a voiced consonant, it gives ओ; it is not just dropped.
Right: य is voiced: दक्षिणतः + यकृत् → दक्षिणतो यकृत्.
questions.explain: दक्षिणतः + यकृत् = दक्षिणतो यकृत्: अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Picture the heart. By unit 74, which pair lies on its right side?
optionExplain: Right: दक्षिणतो यकृत्क्लोमं च: on the right, the liver and the kloman.
They are on the left (वामपार्श्वे).
The spleen is on the left.
The lung is on the left.
questions.explain: Left: spleen and lung. Right: liver and kloman.
questions.rule: तस्य वामपार्श्वे प्लीहा फुप्फुसश्च दक्षिणतो यकृत्क्लोमंच.

questions.q: By the rule of फुप्फुसः + च → फुप्फुसश्च, how is रामः + च (and Rāma) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes before a voiced consonant; च is unvoiced.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्.
The visarga is not dropped before च.
Before च the visarga becomes श्, not स्.
questions.explain: रामः + च = रामश्च, like फुप्फुसः + च = फुप्फुसश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: फुप्फुसः + च → फुप्फुसश्च.

questions.q: By unit 75, from what do the sense-organs arise?
options: The froth and the dregs of the blood
The essence of the blood and the fat alone
The essence of channels and great elements
The essence of the blood and the flesh alone
optionExplain: Froth and dregs give the lung and the unduka (units 66-67).
Blood and fat give the kidneys (unit 68).
Right: स्रोतसां महाभूतानां च प्रसादात्: from their clear essence.
Blood and flesh give the intestines (unit 69).
questions.explain: The sense-organs arise from the clear essence of the channels and the great elements.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 75 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Likewise, of the channels carrying Kapha and blood, and of the great elements, from the clear essence, the sense-organs.
questions.rule: तथा → कफरक्तवाहिनां → स्रोतसां → महाभूतानां च → प्रसादात् → इंद्रियाणि.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 75 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the clear essence of the channels and the great elements, the sense-organs.
questions.teaches: स्रोतस् = channel; कफरक्तवाहिन् = carrying Kapha and blood.

questions.q: By unit 75, what do the channels named there carry?
optionExplain: Neither Vāyu nor Pitta is named in unit 75.
Neither is named in unit 75.
Neither is named in unit 75.
Right: कफरक्तवाहिनाम्: carrying Kapha and blood.
questions.explain: The channels of unit 75 carry Kapha and blood.

questions.q: Which sources does unit 75 name for the sense-organs?
optionExplain: Right: कफरक्तवाहिनां स्रोतसाम्.
The mind is not named in unit 75.
Right: महाभूतानाम्.
No bone is named in unit 75.
questions.explain: Two sources: the channels carrying Kapha and blood, and the great elements.

questions.q: By the pattern of कफरक्तवाहिन् (carrying Kapha and blood), what does जलवाहिनी नदी mean?
options: A river carried by the water
optionExplain: Right: -वाहिन्/-वाहिनी = carrying; the first member is what is carried.
The first member is what is carried, not the carrier.
नदी is the noun described; जलवाहिनी describes it.
Nothing here means without.
questions.explain: जलवाहिनी नदी = a river carrying water, as कफरक्तवाहिन् = carrying Kapha and blood.
questions.teaches: -वाहिन् (carrying) after a noun names what is carried: कफरक्तवाहिन् = carrying Kapha and blood.

questions.q: By unit 76, from what does the white circle of the eye arise?
options: From the clear essence of Kapha
From the froth of the blood
From the clear essence of the flesh
optionExplain: The black circle comes from blood (unit 77), not the white.
Right: श्लेष्मणः प्रसादात्: from the clear essence of Kapha.
The froth gives the lung (unit 66).
Flesh with blood gives the intestines (unit 69).
questions.explain: The white circle arises from the clear essence of Kapha.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 76 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Among these too, in the eye, of Kapha, from the clear essence, the white circle; that is father-born.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 76 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the clear essence of Kapha, the white circle; it is born from the father.
questions.teaches: पितृज = पितृ (father) + ज (born): born from the father.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of प्रसादाच्छुक्लमंडलं is right?
optionExplain: च्छुक्ल is not a word; the ablative is प्रसादात्.
छुक्ल is not a word; the word is शुक्ल, white.
Right: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ).
A visarga gives no च्छ: that would be प्रसादः शुक्ल...
questions.explain: प्रसादात् (from the clear essence) + शुक्लमण्डलम् (white circle).
questions.rule: त् + श → च्छ when श is followed by a vowel or semivowel (optional; च्श also correct).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 76, from which parent is the white circle born?
optionExplain: The black circle is the mother-born one (unit 77).
The circle of sight has the nature of both (unit 77).
पितृज: it is born from the father.
Right: तत्पितृजम्: that is born from the father.
questions.explain: The white circle is pitṛja, born from the father.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of तेषु + अपि → तेष्वपि, how is मधु + अरिः (foe of Madhu) joined?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: मधु + अरिः → मध्वरिः.
ओ does not come from उ + अ.
The उ itself becomes व्; it does not stay.
The short अ of अरिः stays short.
questions.explain: मधु + अरिः = मध्वरिः, like तेषु + अपि = तेष्वपि.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तेषु + अपि → तेष्वपि.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 77, from what does the kṛṣṇa-maṇḍala (black circle) of the eye come?
optionExplain: Fat is not named in unit 77; the black circle comes from blood.
Right: असृजः कृष्णमंडलम्: the black circle comes from blood.
Bone is not named in unit 77; the black circle comes from blood.
Marrow is not named in unit 77; the black circle comes from blood.
questions.explain: The kṛṣṇa-maṇḍala comes from blood and is mother-born.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 77 in the line's order.
questions.explain: From blood the black circle; that is mother-born; in the middle the circle of sight; that has the nature of both.
questions.rule: असृजः कृष्णमंडलं → तन्मातृजं → मध्ये दृष्टिमंडलं → तदुभयात्मकं.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 77 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From blood the black circle, mother-born; in the middle the circle of sight, of both natures.
questions.teaches: मातृज = मातृ (mother) + ज (born): born from the mother; उभयात्मक = having the nature of both.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of तन्मातृजं in unit 77 is right?
optionExplain: म् + म would give तम्मातृजम् or तंमातृजम्, and the data reads तत् (that, neuter).
तन्मा and तृजम् are not words; the words are तत् and मातृजम्.
Right: त् before the nasal म is written न् here (optional; द् is also correct): तत् + मातृजम् → तन्मातृजम्.
तन्म and आतृजम् are not words; the words are तत् and मातृजम्.
questions.explain: तत् (that) + मातृजम् (mother-born): before म the त् appears as न् (optional; द् is also correct).
questions.rule: तत् + मातृजम् → तन्मातृजम् (optional; द् is also correct).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 77?
options: The circle of sight lies at the outer edge
The black circle comes from blood
The black circle is born from the mother
The circle of sight is born from the mother only
optionExplain: It lies in the middle: मध्ये दृष्टिमंडलम्.
Right: असृजः कृष्णमंडलम्.
Right: तन्मातृजम्.
It has the nature of both: तदुभयात्मकम्.
questions.explain: From blood the black circle, mother-born; the circle of sight in the middle has the nature of both.
questions.rule: असृजः कृष्णमंडलं तन्मातृजं मध्ये दृष्टिमंडलं तदुभयात्मकम्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of तदुभयात्मकं (तत् + उभय...), how is एतत् + उक्तम् (this is said) joined?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the final त् does not stay unvoiced; it becomes द्.
न् is not taken before a vowel; त् becomes द्.
उ does not change to ओ here; only त् changes to द्.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as तत् + उभयात्मकम् → तदुभयात्मकम्.
questions.explain: एतत् + उक्तम् = एतदुक्तम्, like तत् + उभयात्मकम् = तदुभयात्मकम्.
questions.rule: A final त् before a vowel → द्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: तत् + उभयात्मकम् → तदुभयात्मकम्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 78, what are the five things named in this line?
options: The five seats of the senses
The five layers of the skin
optionExplain: Right: पंच मंडलानि: the five maṇḍalas (circles).
The seats of the senses are another topic; this line names maṇḍalas.
The skin's layers are another topic; this line names maṇḍalas.
The organs of action are another topic; this line names maṇḍalas.
questions.explain: The line names the five maṇḍalas (circles) of the eye.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put the five maṇḍalas of unit 78 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Eyelashes, eyelid, white, black, sight.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each maṇḍala of unit 78 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The five maṇḍalas: eyelashes, eyelid, white, black, sight.
questions.teaches: पक्ष्म = eyelashes and वर्त्म = eyelid are counted as maṇḍalas too, beside the white, black and sight circles.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which of these are among the five maṇḍalas of unit 78?
optionExplain: Right: the second maṇḍala.
Not a maṇḍala in unit 78; the outer corner is named in unit 80.
Not a maṇḍala; the six paṭalas are a separate count (unit 82).
Right: the fourth maṇḍala.
questions.explain: The five are pakṣma, vartma, śukla, kṛṣṇa and dṛṣṭi.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 78, which maṇḍala is named right after वर्त्म (eyelid)?
optionExplain: दृष्टि comes last, after कृष्ण.
Right: The order is पक्ष्म, वर्त्म, शुक्ल, कृष्ण, दृष्टि.
कृष्ण comes after शुक्ल, not straight after वर्त्म.
पक्ष्म comes first, before वर्त्म.
questions.explain: After the eyelid comes the white circle, then the black, then sight.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: In unit 78, दृष्टि before the following आ is written दृष्ट्या... By that rule, how is इति + आह (thus he says) joined?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + आ.
The इ does not drop; it becomes य्.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + आह → इत्याह.
The इ does not lengthen; it becomes य् before आ.
questions.explain: इति + आह = इत्याह, as दृष्टि + आ... → दृष्ट्या...
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्: दृष्टि + आ... → दृष्ट्या...
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 79, how many are the junctions (sandhi) of the maṇḍalas?
optionExplain: The line says चत्वारः, four.
Five is the count of the maṇḍalas, not of their junctions.
The line says चत्वारः, four.
Right: तत्संधयश्चत्वारः: their junctions are four.
questions.explain: The junctions of the five maṇḍalas are four.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each part of unit 79 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Their junctions are four.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Their junctions are four: तत्सन्धयः ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चत्वारः = four (masculine, agreeing with सन्धयः).
questions.teaches: चत्वारः = four, masculine nominative plural, agreeing with सन्धयः (junctions).
questions.rule: तत्सन्धयः चत्वारः = their junctions are four.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of सन्धयश्चत्वारः is right?
optionExplain: Right: The visarga before च becomes श्: सन्धयः + चत्वारः → सन्धयश्चत्वारः.
श्चत्वारः is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga of सन्धयः.
सन्धयो is not the word here; ओ comes from अः only before a voiced consonant (or before अ).
अश्चत्वारः is not a word, and the form is सन्धयः, the plural.
questions.explain: सन्धयः (junctions) + चत्वारः (four): ः before च → श्.
questions.rule: Visarga before च or छ → श्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: In unit 79, what does तत् in तत्सन्धयः refer to?
options: The six paṭalas (layers) of the eye
The five maṇḍalas of the eye
The two corners of the eye
optionExplain: The paṭalas come later, in unit 82; tat- points back to the maṇḍalas.
Right: The data: tat- refers to the five maṇḍalas of unit 78.
The corners are named in unit 80; tat- points back to the maṇḍalas.
Those are another topic; tat- points back to the maṇḍalas.
questions.explain: Their junctions = the junctions of the five maṇḍalas.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of सन्धयश्चत्वारः, how is रामः + चलति (Rāma moves) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः only before a voiced consonant (or before अ); च is unvoiced.
Before च the visarga becomes श्, not स्.
Right: The visarga before च becomes श्, as सन्धयः + चत्वारः.
Before च the visarga is not dropped; it becomes श्.
questions.explain: रामः + चलति = रामश्चलति, like सन्धयः + चत्वारः = सन्धयश्चत्वारः.
questions.rule: Visarga before च or छ → श्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: सन्धयः + चत्वारः → सन्धयश्चत्वारः.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 80, which two places does the line name with its two?
options: At the upper and the lower eyelids
At the root and the tip of the tongue
At the two ears and the two nostrils
At the apāṅga and the kanīna
optionExplain: The line names the apāṅga and kanīna, not the eyelids.
The tongue is not named; the line names the eye's corners.
Ears and nostrils are not named; the line names the eye's corners.
Right: चापांगकनीनयोः: at the outer corner and (probably) the inner corner.
questions.explain: Two are placed at the apāṅga and the kanīna.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 80 to its meaning.
pairs: inner corner or pupil (sense not firm)
questions.explain: And two, at the outer corner and (probably) the inner corner.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: च + अपाङ्ग is joined as ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: च + अपाङ्ग = चापाङ्ग: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as long आ: च + अपाङ्ग → चापाङ्ग.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of चापांग in unit 80 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: च (and) + अपाङ्ग (outer corner).
चाप (bow) and अङ्ग give no sense here, and the line then loses its च (and).
ए + अ would give चेऽपाङ्ग, with ए kept and ऽ.
चा and पाङ्ग are not words; the words are च and अपाङ्ग.
questions.explain: च (and) + अपाङ्ग (outer corner of the eye) = चापाङ्ग.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which statements about unit 80 are right by the card?
options: The noun counted is named in this unit
Apāṅga is the outer corner of the eye
Two are placed at the apāṅga and kanīna
optionExplain: The data: the noun counted is not stated here.
Kanīna is probably the inner corner; the sense is not firm.
Right: so the data glosses it.
Right: द्वौ च अपाङ्गकनीनयोः.
questions.explain: Two at the apāṅga (outer corner) and kanīna (probably inner corner); the noun is not named here.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of चापांग (च + अपाङ्ग), how is च + अपि (and also) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अपाङ्ग → चापाङ्ग.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
The avagraha marks an अ dropped after ए or ओ, not after अ.
questions.explain: च + अपि = चापि, like च + अपाङ्ग = चापाङ्ग.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as long आ: च + अपाङ्ग → चापाङ्ग.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: What does इति do in unit 81 (इति ते षट्)?
options: It sums up a count: thus
It opens a new list: namely
optionExplain: इति does not ask here; it closes the count.
No cause is given; इति closes the count.
Right: इति ते षट्: thus these are six.
No new list follows in this unit; इति closes the count.
questions.explain: इति = thus: it rounds off the count.
questions.rule: इति ते षट् = thus these are six.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 81 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Thus these are six.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Thus these are six: इति ते ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: षट् = six.
questions.teaches: षट् = six; इति ते षट् = thus these are six.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: One word of this translation of unit 81 is wrong: Thus these are seven. Which?
optionExplain: इति = thus: right.
ते = they, these: right.
The copula 'are' is understood: right.
Right: षट् is six, not seven.
questions.explain: इति ते षट् = thus these are six.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: In unit 81, to what does ते (they) point?
options: To items counted earlier, unnamed here
To the six paṭalas named in this unit
To the five maṇḍalas of unit 78
To the two eyelids of unit 83
optionExplain: Right: The data: te points back to the items counted before.
No paṭala is named in unit 81; they come in unit 82.
Five is not six; ते points to the six items counted earlier.
Those come later; ते points back to earlier items.
questions.explain: ते points back to the items counted earlier; this unit names none.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the use of ते in unit 81 (they, masc. nom. pl.), what does ते वृक्षाः mean (वृक्ष = tree)?
optionExplain: That would need the genitive वृक्षस्य; ते वृक्षाः is nominative plural.
Right: ते, masc. nom. pl., goes with the masc. nom. pl. वृक्षाः: these (those) trees.
That would need the instrumental वृक्षेण; ते वृक्षाः is nominative plural.
One tree would be सः वृक्षः; ते वृक्षाः is plural.
questions.explain: ते वृक्षाः = these (those) trees, like ते in इति ते षट्.
questions.teaches: ते is the masculine nominative plural of तत्: they, these, those.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 82, what are said to be six?
optionExplain: The eyelids are two, named in unit 83; this line counts six paṭalas.
The binding strands come in unit 85; this line counts paṭalas.
Right: षट् च पटलानि: and six paṭalas (layers).
The circles (maṇḍala) are five, in unit 78; this line counts paṭalas.
questions.explain: Unit 82 counts six paṭalas, layers.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And six layers.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: And six layers: षट् च ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पटलानि = layers (neuter nominative plural of पटल).
questions.teaches: पटलानि = layers, neuter nominative plural of पटल.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Why does षट् stay unchanged before च in unit 82?
options: ट् never changes in any sandhi
The print leaves out a due sandhi
च always makes the sound before it voiced
च is unvoiced, so ट् stays as it is
optionExplain: It does: before a vowel or a voiced non-nasal consonant ट् becomes ड् (षडङ्ग).
No sandhi is due; ट् stays before the unvoiced च.
च is unvoiced; it does not make ट् voiced.
Right: ट् would become ड् only before a vowel or a voiced non-nasal consonant.
