questions.explain: Before the unvoiced च, ट् stays: षट् च.
questions.rule: ट् stays before an unvoiced consonant; it becomes ड् before a vowel or a voiced non-nasal consonant.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the card, whose layers are the six paṭalas, and does the line say so?
options: The eye's; known from the context
The eye's; the line names the eye
The skin's; the line names the skin
The heart's; known from the context
optionExplain: Right: The data: of the eye, from the context; the eye is not named in this line.
The line does not name the eye; the context shows it.
The skin is not named; the context is the eye.
The context of these units is the eye, not the heart.
questions.explain: The six paṭalas are the eye's layers by context; the line names no organ.
questions.rule: षट् च पटलानि (the eye from context).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule behind षट् च, how is षट् + अङ्गानि (six limbs) joined, the next word starting with a vowel?
optionExplain: Before a vowel ट् does not stay unvoiced; it becomes ड्.
Right: Before a vowel ट् becomes ड्; before the unvoiced च it stayed ट्.
The vowel अ does not lengthen; only ट् changes to ड्.
ण् is not taken before a vowel; ट् becomes ड्.
questions.explain: षट् + अङ्गानि = षडङ्गानि; षट् + च = षट् च.
questions.rule: ट् before a vowel or a voiced non-nasal consonant → ड्; before an unvoiced sound it stays.
questions.teaches: A final ट् stays before an unvoiced sound (षट् च) and becomes ड् before a vowel or a voiced non-nasal consonant (षडङ्गानि).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 83, what two things are named?
optionExplain: Nostrils are not named in unit 83; it names eyelids.
Ears are not named in unit 83; it names eyelids.
Right: द्वे वर्त्मनी: two vartmans, eyelids.
Testes are not named in unit 83; it names eyelids.
questions.explain: Unit 83 names two vartmans, the eyelids.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which statements about unit 83 are right by the card?
options: The line has its own verb
The line names the eye itself
optionExplain: Right: so in the eye section (standard).
No verb is stated; the copula is understood.
Right: the data notes the sense path.
The eye is not named in this line.
questions.explain: Two eyelids; vartman also means path; no verb; the eye is not named.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Two eyelids: द्वे ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: वर्त्मनी = two eyelids (neuter nominative dual of वर्त्मन्).
questions.teaches: वर्त्मनी is the neuter nominative dual of वर्त्मन् (eyelid).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Why is the number word द्वे, not द्वौ, in unit 83?
options: द्वे is the plural form of the word two
द्वे is the masculine dual of the word two
द्वे means second here, not the number two
वर्त्मन् is neuter; द्वे is the neuter dual
optionExplain: द्वि is dual by nature; द्वे is a dual form, not a plural.
The masculine dual is द्वौ; द्वे is neuter or feminine.
Second is द्वितीय; द्वे is the number two.
Right: द्वे is the neuter (or feminine) dual of द्वि; द्वौ is masculine.
questions.explain: द्वे agrees with the neuter वर्त्मनी; with a masculine noun it would be द्वौ.
questions.rule: द्वि: masc. du. द्वौ; neut./fem. du. द्वे.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: In unit 83, why is वर्त्मन् read as eyelid and not as path?
options: It stands in the section on the eye
The line itself says नेत्र (the eye)
A dual can only ever mean eyelids
optionExplain: Right: The data: vartman = eyelid in the eye section (standard).
It does mean path elsewhere; the context decides.
The line names no organ; the context decides.
Number does not decide the sense; the context does.
questions.explain: The eye section makes वर्त्मन् the eyelid here.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By द्वे वर्त्मनी (neuter dual), how is two fruits said, फल being neuter?
optionExplain: द्वौ and -औ are masculine dual forms; फल is neuter.
Right: Neuter dual: द्वे with फले, as द्वे with वर्त्मनी.
फलानि is plural; two needs the dual फले.
द्वौ is masculine; with the neuter फले the number is द्वे.
questions.explain: द्वे फले = two fruits, like द्वे वर्त्मनी = two eyelids.
questions.rule: Neuter nominative dual: द्वे + noun in the dual.
questions.teaches: With a neuter noun, two is द्वे and the noun takes the dual: द्वे वर्त्मनी, द्वे फले.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 84, what is named as the third?
optionExplain: Bone is named fourth: चतुर्थम् अस्थि.
Blood is not named in unit 84.
Right: तृतीयं मेदः: the third is fat.
Skin is not named in unit 84.
questions.explain: The third is medas, fat; the fourth is bone.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 84 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Flesh; third, fat; fourth, bone.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 84 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Third fat, fourth bone; their thickness is by a fifth part of sight (kept literal).
questions.teaches: तृतीय = third, चतुर्थ = fourth: ordinal numbers that agree with the unnamed noun (neuter here).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of चतुर्थमस्थि in unit 84 is right?
optionExplain: मस्थि is not a word; the word is अस्थि (bone).
अः + अ would give चतुर्थोऽस्थि; the data reads चतुर्थम्.
चतुर्थम and स्थि are not words; the words are चतुर्थम् and अस्थि.
Right: म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it: चतुर्थम् + अस्थि → चतुर्थमस्थि.
questions.explain: चतुर्थम् (fourth) + अस्थि (bone) = चतुर्थमस्थि.
questions.rule: Final म् before a vowel → stays म्, joined to the vowel.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which statements about unit 84 are right by the card?
options: The noun counted is printed in the line
दृष्टेः पञ्चमांशेन has a settled meaning
The reading of the first part is not settled
optionExplain: The data: the noun is not stated (probably paṭala).
Right: चतुर्थम् अस्थि.
The data keeps it literal and does not interpret it.
Right: the data calls it hard and not settled.
questions.explain: Fat third, bone fourth are sure; the first part and the fifth-part phrase are not settled.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्थमस्थि, how is फलम् + अस्ति (there is a fruit) joined?
optionExplain: Right: म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it, as चतुर्थम् + अस्थि.
Anusvāra stands for म् only before a consonant, not before a vowel.
The म् is not lost; it stays before the vowel.
The vowel अ does not lengthen; the म् joins it.
questions.explain: फलम् + अस्ति = फलमस्ति, like चतुर्थम् + अस्थि = चतुर्थमस्थि.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → म् joined to the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it: चतुर्थम् + अस्थि → चतुर्थमस्थि.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 85, of what nature are the binding strands?
optionExplain: That is the list for the testes in unit 89, not the binding strands.
Right: सिराकंडरामेदःकफात्मकाः: having the nature of these four.
Skin and bone are not in the list; it is sirā, kaṇḍarā, fat, Kapha.
Vāta, Pitta and blood are not in the list of unit 85.
questions.explain: The four binding strands have the nature of sirā, kaṇḍarā, medas and Kapha.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put the four natures of the binding strands in the line's order.
questions.explain: Sirā, kaṇḍarā, medas, Kapha.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 85 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four binding strands having the nature of sirā, kaṇḍarā, fat and Kapha.
questions.teaches: -आत्मक at the end of a compound = having the nature of, consisting of: सिरा...कफात्मक.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of बन्धनगुणास्तु is right?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give गुणोऽस्तु, and अस्तु (let it be) does not fit.
स्तु is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
Right: The visarga before त becomes स्: गुणाः + तु → गुणास्तु.
आस्तु is not a word; the word is the particle तु.
questions.explain: बन्धनगुणाः (binding strands) + तु (however): ः before त → स्.
questions.rule: Visarga before त or थ → स्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which of these are among the four natures of the binding strands in unit 85?
optionExplain: Flesh is not in the list of unit 85.
Bone is not in the list of unit 85.
Right: the first of the four.
Right: the fourth of the four.
questions.explain: The four are sirā, kaṇḍarā, medas and Kapha.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of गुणास्तु, how is देवाः + तत्र (the gods there) joined?
optionExplain: आः drops its visarga only before a voiced sound; त is unvoiced.
श् is taken before च or छ, not before त.
आ does not change to ओ; only the visarga changes.
Right: The visarga before त becomes स्, as गुणाः + तु → गुणास्तु.
questions.explain: देवाः + तत्र = देवास्तत्र, like गुणाः + तु = गुणास्तु.
questions.rule: Visarga before त or थ → स्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: बन्धनगुणाः + तु → बन्धनगुणास्तु.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 86, what is the binder of all joints?
optionExplain: Right: श्लेष्मा ... सर्वसन्धिबन्धनम्: Kapha binds all joints.
Vāta is not named in unit 86; it names śleṣman.
Pitta is not named in unit 86; it names śleṣman.
Blood is not named in unit 86; it names śleṣman.
questions.explain: Śleṣman (Kapha) is the chief binder of all joints.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 86 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Śleṣman however, the highest, binder of all joints, thus said, before.
questions.rule: श्लेष्मा तु → परं → सर्वसंधिबंधनम् → इत्युक्तं → प्राक्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 86 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Śleṣman is the binder of all joints; thus it was said before.
questions.rule: श्लेष्मन्, सर्व, सन्धि, बन्धन, उक्त, प्राक्.
questions.teaches: श्लेष्मन् is another name of Kapha; सन्धि here is a joint of the body.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of इत्युक्तं in unit 86 is right?
optionExplain: इति + युक्तम् would be written इति युक्तम्, with no य् from sandhi.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + उक्तम् → इत्युक्तम्.
इत्य is not a word; the particle is इति.
इतः + य would give इतो युक्तम्, and युक्तम् (joined) does not fit.
questions.explain: इति (thus) + उक्तम् (said): इ + उ → यु.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 86, how is this statement about śleṣman presented?
options: As said here the first time
As the view of other teachers
optionExplain: प्राक् shows it was said before, not first here.
उक्तं प्राक् looks back, not forward.
Right: इत्युक्तं प्राक्: thus it was said before.
No other teachers are named; it was said before.
questions.explain: The line recalls an earlier statement: thus it was said before.
questions.rule: इति उक्तं प्राक् = thus it was said before.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of इत्युक्तम् (इति + उक्तम्), how is प्रति + उत्तरम् (a reply) joined?
optionExplain: उ does not change to ओ; only इ changes to य्.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from इ + उ.
ए comes from अ + इ; here इ becomes य्.
Right: इ before उ becomes य्, as इति + उक्तम् → इत्युक्तम्.
questions.explain: प्रति + उत्तरम् = प्रत्युत्तरम्, like इति + उक्तम् = इत्युक्तम्.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + उक्तम् → इत्युक्तम्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 87, through union with what does the eye's tejas become fit for its work?
options: The cool water of the eye
The blood of the black circle
optionExplain: Right: बाह्यतेजसा स्वयोनिना योगात्: through union with the outer tejas.
No water is named in unit 87; the union is with the outer tejas.
Kapha is not named in unit 87; the union is with the outer tejas.
Blood is not named in unit 87; the union is with the outer tejas.
questions.explain: The eye's tejas works through union with the outer tejas, its own source.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 87 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The tejas in the eye, with the outer tejas its own source, through union, like a weapon with a stone, becomes fit; through excess it is harmed.
questions.rule: नेत्राश्रितं तु तेजो → बाह्यतेजसा स्वयोनिना → योगाच्छस्त्रमिवाश्मना → कर्मण्यं भवति → अतियोगादुपहन्यते.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 87 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Union with the outer tejas makes it fit, like a weapon with a stone; excess harms it.
questions.rule: बाह्य, स्वयोनि, शस्त्र, अश्मन्, कर्मण्य, उपहन्यते.
questions.teaches: योग = union; अतियोग = excessive union: the same contact that helps, in excess, harms.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of योगाच्छस्त्रम् in unit 87 is right?
optionExplain: A visarga before श would give योगाः शस्त्रम् or योगाश्शस्त्रम्, not च्छ.
Right: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ): योगाच्छस्त्रम्.
म् before श would give योगं शस्त्रम्, not च्छ.
छस्त्रम् is not a word; the word is शस्त्रम् (weapon).
questions.explain: योगात् (through union) + शस्त्रम् (weapon) = योगाच्छस्त्रम्.
questions.rule: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ).
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which statements about unit 87 are right by the card?
options: The eye's tejas rests in the eye
The stone is known to be a whetstone
Union with the outer tejas makes it fit
optionExplain: Right: नेत्राश्रितं तेजः.
The data: probably a whetstone, but the Sanskrit says only stone.
Right: अतियोगादुपहन्यते.
Right: बाह्यतेजसा ... योगात् कर्मण्यं भवति.
questions.explain: Union with its source makes the eye's tejas fit; excess harms it; the stone is only a stone.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of योगाच्छस्त्रम्, how is तत् + शरीरम् (that body) usually written?
optionExplain: द् is taken before a voiced sound; श is unvoiced.
Before श the त् does not stay; it becomes च्.
Right: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ), as in योगात् + शस्त्रम्.
श् comes from a visarga, not from त्.
questions.explain: तत् + शरीरम् = तच्छरीरम्, like योगात् + शस्त्रम् = योगाच्छस्त्रम्.
questions.rule: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ).
questions.teaches: त् + श → च्श, optionally च्छ before a vowel or semivowel (the print has च्छ): योगात् + शस्त्रम् → योगाच्छस्त्रम्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 88, why does the tejas not abandon its fiery nature in water?
options: Because it stays far from all water
Because Kapha shields it from water
Because the mind keeps it burning
optionExplain: It is even in the midst of water: अम्भोमध्यगमपि.
Kapha is not named in unit 88; the cause is vīrya.
The mind is not named in unit 88; the cause is vīrya.
Right: वीर्योत्कर्षात्: because of the excellence of its potency.
questions.explain: Its potency (vīrya) is so strong that it keeps its fiery nature.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 88 in the line's order.
questions.explain: And that, like lightning, and like the vaḍavāmukha, even in the midst of water, from the excellence of vīrya, does not abandon its fiery nature.
questions.rule: तच्च → वैद्युतवत् → वडवामुखवत् च → अम्भोमध्यगम् अपि → वीर्योत्कर्षात् → तेजस्त्वं न जहाति.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 88 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Like lightning and the submarine fire, even in water it keeps its fire by the strength of its vīrya.
questions.teaches: -वत् = like: वैद्युतवत् = like lightning, वडवामुखवत् = like the submarine fire.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of वीर्योत्कर्षात् in unit 88 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: वीर्य + उत्कर्षात् → वीर्योत्कर्षात्.
अः before उ loses its visarga and the vowels stay apart: वीर्य उत्कर्षात्.
त्कर्षात् is not a word; the word is उत्कर्षात् (from excellence).
ओत्कर्षात् is not a word, and अ + ओ would give औ.
questions.explain: वीर्य (potency) + उत्कर्षात् (from the excellence): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 88, what do lightning and the vaḍavāmukha share with the eye's tejas?
options: Water puts them out at once
They burn only in dry places
They give light only by day
optionExplain: The point is the opposite: they keep their fire in water.
Right: Like them, even in the midst of water, it does not abandon its fiery nature.
They are fires in the midst of water: अम्भोमध्यगम् अपि.
Day and night are not named in unit 88.
questions.explain: Lightning, the submarine fire and the eye's tejas: fire that keeps its nature amid water.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of वीर्योत्कर्षात् (वीर्य + उत्कर्षात्), how is हित + उपदेशः (good advice) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as वीर्य + उत्कर्षात् → वीर्योत्कर्षात्.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: हित + उपदेशः = हितोपदेशः, like वीर्य + उत्कर्षात् = वीर्योत्कर्षात्.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by उ joins as ओ: वीर्य + उत्कर्षात् → वीर्योत्कर्षात्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 89, from the clear essence of what does the tongue arise?
optionExplain: That longer list, with fat, is for the testes.
None of these is named for the tongue in unit 89.
Fat is not in the tongue's list; flesh and blood are.
Right: मांसासृक्कफप्रसादात् जिह्वा जायते.
questions.explain: The tongue arises from the prasāda of flesh, blood and Kapha.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Put the four sources of the testes in unit 89 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Flesh, blood, Kapha, fat.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 89 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the clear essence of flesh, blood and Kapha the tongue arises; with fat added, the testes.
questions.rule: मांस, असृज्, प्रसाद, जिह्वा, वृषण, जायते.
questions.teaches: प्रसाद = the clear, finest part of a substance; organs are said to arise from the prasāda of tissues.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 89, which source is in the testes' list but not in the tongue's?
optionExplain: Right: The testes' list adds मेदः: मांसासृक्कफमेदःप्रसादात्.
Flesh is in both lists.
Blood is in both lists.
Kapha is in both lists.
questions.explain: The only difference between the two lists is fat (medas).
questions.rule: जिह्वा: मांस, असृक्, कफ · वृषणौ: + मेदस्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: Which split of वृषणाविति in unit 89 is right?
optionExplain: विति is not a word; the व् comes from the औ of वृषणौ.
Right: औ before a vowel becomes आव्: वृषणौ + इति → वृषणाविति.
अः + इ would give वृषण इति, and the data reads the dual वृषणौ.
म् + इ would give वृषणमिति, with म्, not व्.
questions.explain: वृषणौ (the two testes) + इति (thus): औ + vowel → आव्.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By the rule of वृषणाविति, how is बालौ + इति (the two boys, thus) joined in one word?
optionExplain: औ is not kept before a vowel; it becomes आव्.
ए comes from अ/आ + इ; here the vowel is औ.
Right: औ before a vowel becomes आव्, as वृषणौ + इति → वृषणाविति.
औ gives आव् with long आ; अव् comes from ओ.
questions.explain: बालौ + इति = बालाविति, like वृषणौ + इति = वृषणाविति.
questions.teaches: A final औ before a vowel becomes आव्: वृषणौ + इति → वृषणाविति.
questions.section: नेत्र की रचना; जिह्वा व वृषण

questions.q: By unit 90, how many seats of life (prāṇāyatana) are there?
optionExplain: Seven is the number of the first ones called mahāmarma in unit 91, not of all the seats.
Sixteen is the count of the kaṇḍarās in unit 92.
Fourteen is the count of the bone assemblages in unit 98.
Right: दश प्राणायतनानि: ten seats of life.
questions.explain: The line opens: दश प्राणायतनानि, ten seats of life.
questions.rule: दश प्राणायतनानि = ten seats of life.

questions.q: Put the first six seats of life of unit 90 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Head, tongue-binding, throat, heart, navel, bladder; then gūda, śukra, ojas and blood follow.
questions.rule: मूर्धा → जिह्वाबन्धन → कण्ठ → हृदय → नाभि → बस्ति.

questions.q: Match each seat of life of unit 90 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the ten seats: head, navel, bladder, gūda (anus, rectum), śukra (semen).
questions.teaches: प्राणायतन = प्राण (life) + आयतन (seat, abode): a seat of life.

questions.q: Which split of नाभिर्बस्तिर्गूदः is right?
optionExplain: Right: Each visarga after इ becomes र् before the voiced consonants ब and ग.
A long ई before a consonant gives no र्; the र् shows a visarga after short इ.
र्बस्तिः is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga of the word before.
अस्ति is not one of the seats, and no ब would appear from इ + अ.
questions.explain: नाभिः (navel) + बस्तिः (bladder) + गूदः (anus): इः + voiced consonant → इर्.

questions.q: Which of these does unit 90 name among the ten seats of life?
optionExplain: Right: रक्तम् is the last of the ten.
The liver is not in the list of unit 90.
Right: नाभिः is the fifth of the ten.
The kidney is not in the list of unit 90.
questions.explain: The ten are head, tongue-binding, throat, heart, navel, bladder, gūda, śukra, ojas and blood.
questions.rule: मूर्धा जिह्वाबन्धनं कण्ठो हृदयं नाभिर्बस्तिर्गूदः शुक्रमोजो रक्तम्.

questions.q: By the rule of नाभिर्बस्तिः, how is अग्निः + दहति (fire burns) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from इः.
Right: A visarga after इ before a voiced consonant becomes र्, as नाभिः + बस्तिः.
द is voiced; before it the visarga after इ becomes र्, not श्.
Before a voiced consonant the visarga after इ does not stay; it becomes र्.
questions.explain: अग्निः + दहति = अग्निर्दहति, like नाभिः + बस्तिः = नाभिर्बस्तिः.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound: नाभिः + बस्तिः → नाभिर्बस्तिः.

questions.q: By unit 91, what are the first seven of the ten called?
optionExplain: The kaṇḍarās are counted in unit 92; they are not these seven.
The jālas are described in unit 93.
Right: महामर्मसंज्ञानि: named mahāmarma.
The sīvanīs are counted in unit 96.
questions.explain: The first seven are named mahāmarma.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 91 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of these, the first seven, again, are named mahāmarma.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 91 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of these, the first seven, again, are named mahāmarma.
questions.teaches: -संज्ञ at the end of a compound means 'having the name': महामर्मसंज्ञानि = named mahāmarma.

questions.q: Which split of एषामाद्यानि is right?
optionExplain: माद्यानि is not the word; the word is आद्यानि (first).
म् + अ would give एषामद्यानि, with a short अ, not मा.
एषामा is not a form; the pronoun is एषाम् (of these).
Right: The final म् simply joins the following vowel: एषाम् + आद्यानि → एषामाद्यानि.
questions.explain: एषाम् (of these) + आद्यानि (first): म् + आ → मा.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → the म् joins the vowel.

questions.q: By unit 91, what does एषाम् (of these) refer to?
options: The ten seats of life of unit 90
The fourteen bone groups of unit 98
optionExplain: Right: Right after the ten seats of life: of these, the first seven.
The kaṇḍarās come after unit 91, not before it.
The sīvanīs come later, in unit 96.
The bone groups come later, in unit 98.
questions.explain: एषाम् points back to the ten prāṇāyatanas just listed in unit 90.
questions.rule: एषाम् = of these (the ten of unit 90).

questions.q: By the rule of एषामाद्यानि, how is फलम् + अस्ति (there is a fruit) joined?
optionExplain: The anusvāra stands for म् only before a consonant, not before a vowel.
Right: Final म् joins the following vowel, as एषाम् + आद्यानि.
म् + अ keeps the short अ; nothing lengthens it.
ओऽ comes from अः + अ, not from अम् + अ.
questions.explain: फलम् + अस्ति = फलमस्ति, like एषाम् + आद्यानि = एषामाद्यानि.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → the म् joins the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel is not changed; it joins that vowel: एषाम् + आद्यानि → एषामाद्यानि.

questions.q: By unit 92, how many kaṇḍarās (large tendons) are there?
optionExplain: Fourteen is the count of the bone assemblages in unit 98.
Six is the count of the kūrcas in unit 94.
Right: षोडश कण्डराः: sixteen kaṇḍarās.
Seven is the count of the sīvanīs in unit 96.
questions.explain: The line opens: षोडश कण्डराः, sixteen kaṇḍarās.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 92 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Sixteen kaṇḍarās; of them, two each in the hands and feet; four, separately, in the neck and the back.
questions.rule: षोडश कंडराः → तासां → द्वे द्वे करचरणेषु → चतस्रः पृथक → ग्रीवापृष्ठयोः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 92 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two each in the hands and feet; four, separately, in the neck and the back.
questions.teaches: करचरणेषु is a dvandva in the locative plural: in the hands and feet.

questions.q: In unit 92, what does the repeated द्वे द्वे express?
options: Two in all, for hands and feet
Two in the hands, two in the neck
Twice as many as in the back
Two each, in every hand and foot
optionExplain: Repeating the numeral gives 'two each', not one total of two.
द्वे द्वे goes with करचरणेषु; the neck has its own number, four.
No comparison with the back is made; द्वे द्वे means two each.
Right: A repeated numeral is distributive: two each.
questions.explain: द्वे द्वे करचरणेषु = two each in the hands and feet.

questions.q: By unit 92, where are the four (चतस्रः) kaṇḍarās placed?
options: In the neck and the back
In the hands and the feet
In the head and the tongue
In the ankle and the wrist
optionExplain: Right: चतस्रः पृथक् ग्रीवापृष्ठयोः: four, separately, in the neck and the back.
The hands and feet have two each (द्वे द्वे).
The head and tongue are places of the sīvanīs in unit 96.
The ankle and wrist are places of the jālas in unit 93.
questions.explain: Four, separately, are in the neck and the back.

questions.q: By the pattern of द्वे द्वे, what does a new example पञ्च पञ्च फलानि ददाति mean?
options: He gives fifty fruits in all
He gives five fruits to each
He gives only five fruits once
He gives the fifth fruit only
optionExplain: Repeating पञ्च does not make fifty; that would be पञ्चाशत्.
Right: A repeated numeral is distributive, as द्वे द्वे = two each.
The repetition adds 'each'; it does not stress 'only once'.
The fifth would be the ordinal पञ्चम, not the repeated पञ्च.
questions.explain: पञ्च पञ्च = five each, like द्वे द्वे = two each.
questions.teaches: A numeral said twice is distributive: द्वे द्वे करचरणेषु = two each in the hands and feet.

questions.q: By unit 93, where are the jālas (nets) situated?
options: At the neck and the back
At the head and the tongue
At the ankle and the wrist
At the knee and the groin
optionExplain: The neck and back hold the four kaṇḍarās of unit 92.
The head and tongue hold sīvanīs in unit 96.
Right: गुल्फे मणिबन्धे च: at the ankle and the wrist.
The knee and groin are places of bone groups in unit 98.
questions.explain: The jālas lie at the ankle and the wrist.

questions.q: Put the four sources of the jālas in the order of मांससिरास्नाय्वस्थिजानि.
questions.explain: Born of flesh, vessel, snāyu and bone.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 93 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Nets at the ankle and wrist, lying mutually latticed.
questions.teaches: गवाक्षित = made like a gavākṣa (window lattice): interlaced.

questions.q: In unit 93, what does परस्परगवाक्षितानि say about the jālas?
options: They lie apart and never touch
They are hollow like a lotus bud
They bind the muscles to the spine
They lie interlaced like a lattice
optionExplain: परस्पर (mutually) with गवाक्षित means they are interwoven.
The lotus-bud likeness is said of the heart in unit 73.
Binding the muscles is the work of the flesh-cords in unit 95.
Right: गवाक्षित = made like a window lattice; परस्पर = mutually.
questions.explain: The jālas are situated mutually latticed, i.e. interlaced.

questions.q: Which does unit 93 name as sources of the jālas?
optionExplain: Fat is not among the four sources of unit 93.
Right: मांस is the first of the four.
Skin is not among the four sources of unit 93.
Right: अस्थि is the last of the four.
questions.explain: The four sources are flesh, vessel, snāyu and bone.

questions.q: By the rule of स्नायु + अस्थि → स्नाय्वस्थि, how is मधु + अत्र (honey here) joined?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as स्नायु + अस्थि.
उ + उ would give ऊ; here a different vowel, अ, follows.
ओऽ needs a word ending in ओ or अः; मधु ends in उ.
The अ of अत्र is not simply lost; उ + अ gives व.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like स्नायु + अस्थि = स्नाय्वस्थि.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: स्नायु + अस्थि → स्नाय्वस्थि.

questions.q: By unit 94, how many kūrcas are there?
optionExplain: Ten is the count of the seats of life in unit 90.
Right: षट् कूर्चाः: six kūrcas.
Seven is the count of the sīvanīs in unit 96.
Sixteen is the count of the kaṇḍarās and of the jālas.
questions.explain: The line opens: षट्, six.

questions.q: Put the places of the kūrcas in the order of हस्तपादग्रीवामेढ्रेषु.
questions.explain: In the hands, feet, neck and meḍhra.

questions.q: Match each place of unit 94 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The kūrcas are in the hands, feet, neck and meḍhra (penis, standard).
questions.teaches: मेढ्र = penis (standard); unit 96 uses मेहन for the same organ.

questions.q: In unit 94, what does the ending -एषु of ...मेढ्रेषु show?
optionExplain: The genitive plural of an अ-stem ends in -आणाम्/-आनाम्, not -एषु.
The nominative plural of an अ-stem ends in -आः or -आणि, not -एषु.
Right: -एषु is the locative plural of an अ-stem: in the hands, feet, neck, meḍhra.
The instrumental plural of an अ-stem ends in -ऐः, not -एषु.
questions.explain: हस्तपादग्रीवामेढ्रेषु = in the hands, feet, neck and meḍhra.

questions.q: Which place is NOT among the kūrca places of unit 94?
optionExplain: ग्रीवा, the neck, is named.
पाद, the foot, is named.
हस्त, the hand, is named.
Right: The head is not named in unit 94.
questions.explain: Unit 94 names hands, feet, neck and meḍhra; the head is not one of them.

questions.q: By the rule of कूर्चाः + हस्त..., how is अश्वाः + धावन्ति (horses run) joined?
optionExplain: Right: आः drops its visarga before a voiced consonant, as कूर्चाः + हस्त...
ओ comes from अः, not from आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
Before a voiced consonant the visarga after आ does not stay; it drops.
questions.explain: अश्वाः + धावन्ति = अश्वा धावन्ति, like कूर्चाः + हस्त... = कूर्चा हस्त...
questions.teaches: After आ, a visarga drops before a voiced consonant: कूर्चाः + हस्त... → कूर्चा हस्त...

questions.q: By unit 95, what are the flesh-cords for?
options: For moving the tongue and eyes
optionExplain: Carrying Kapha and blood is said of channels (srotas) in unit 75.
Right: पेशीनिबन्धनार्थे: for the purpose of binding the peśīs (muscles).
No movement of tongue or eyes is named in unit 95.
No bones of the head are named in unit 95.
questions.explain: They are there for binding the muscles.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 95 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Four flesh-cords, on both sides of the spine, for binding the muscles; of them two outer, and two inside.
questions.rule: चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः → पृष्ठवंशमुभयतः → पेशीनिबंधनार्थे → तासां द्वे बाह्ये → द्वे चाभ्यंतरस्थिते.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 95 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four cords on both sides of the spine bind the muscles; two are outer.
questions.teaches: उभयतः (on both sides) takes the accusative: पृष्ठवंशम् उभयतः = on both sides of the spine.

questions.q: Which split of चाभ्यंतरस्थिते is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give चेऽभ्यन्तर, with ए kept and ऽ.
च has no visarga, and अः + अ would give चोऽभ्यन्तर.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अभ्यन्तर → चाभ्यन्तर.
भ्यन्तर is not a word; the word is अभ्यन्तर (inner).
questions.explain: च (and) + अभ्यन्तरस्थिते (situated inside): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: By unit 95, how are the four cords divided?
options: Two on the neck, two on the back
optionExplain: Neck and back are the places of four kaṇḍarās in unit 92.
The line says two and two: द्वे ... द्वे.
Two are outer (बाह्ये); they lie on both sides of the spine.
Right: तासां द्वे बाह्ये द्वे चाभ्यन्तरस्थिते.
questions.explain: Of them, two are outer and two are situated inside.

questions.q: By the rule of चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः, how is बालः + गच्छति (the boy goes) joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as चतस्रः + मांस...
The visarga drops this way after आः, but बालः ends in अः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
Before a voiced consonant the visarga after अ does not stay; अः becomes ओ.
questions.explain: बालः + गच्छति = बालो गच्छति, like चतस्रः + मांसरज्जवः = चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: चतस्रः + मांसरज्जवः → चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः.

questions.q: By unit 96, how many sīvanīs (seams) are in the head?
optionExplain: Seven is the total of all the sīvanīs, not those in the head.
Right: ताः पञ्च शिरसि: of them five in the head.
One each is in the tongue and the mehana, not in the head.
The line says पञ्च, five, for the head.
questions.explain: Five of the seven are in the head.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 96 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Seven sīvanīs; of them five in the head; in the tongue and the mehana, one each.
questions.rule: सप्त सीवन्यः → ताः पंच शिरसि → जिव्हामेहनयोः → एकैका.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 96 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Seven seams: five in the head, one each in the tongue and the mehana.
questions.teaches: एकैका = एक + एक → एकैक (अ + ए → ऐ), in the feminine एकैका to agree with सीवनी: 'one each'.

questions.q: Which split of जिव्हामेहनयोरेकैका (जिह्वामेहनयोरेकैका) is right?
optionExplain: रेकैका is not a word; the word is एकैका (one each).
-योर is not an ending; the locative dual ending is -योः.
Right: A visarga after ओ becomes र् before a vowel: -योः + ए → -योरे.
औ + ए would give -यावेकैका, with आव्, not -योरे.
questions.explain: जिह्वामेहनयोः (in the tongue and the mehana) + एकैका (one each).

questions.q: In unit 96, five sīvanīs are in the head: पंच ____. Type the printed word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पंच शिरसि: five in the head (शिरसि, locative of शिरस्).
questions.teaches: शिरसि is the locative singular of शिरस् (head): 'in the head'.

questions.q: By the rule of एक + एक → एकैक (in एकैका), how is तत्र + एव (there indeed) joined?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + ए.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + ए.
The ए is not lost; अ + ए gives ऐ.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as एक + एक → एकैक.
questions.explain: तत्र + एव = तत्रैव, like एक + एक = एकैक (एकैका).
questions.teaches: अ followed by ए joins as ऐ: एक + एक → एकैक, feminine एकैका.

questions.q: By unit 97, with what is something to be avoided?
optionExplain: Right: शस्त्रेण: with the śastra (blade, surgical instrument).
No fire or cautery is named in unit 97.
No hand or pressing is named in unit 97.
No oil or rubbing is named in unit 97.
questions.explain: It is to be avoided with the śastra, the blade.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 97 in the line's order.
questions.explain: And to be avoided with the blade.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 97 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And to be avoided with the śastra.
questions.teaches: परिहार्य is a gerundive of परि-√हृ: 'to be avoided'.

questions.q: Which split of परिहार्य्याश्च is right?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the word is च (and).
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: परिहार्याः + च → परिहार्याश्च (the print doubles the य).
अः + च would give परिहार्यश्च, with a short अ, not या.
ए before च stays ए: परिहार्ये च, with no श्.
questions.explain: परिहार्याः (to be avoided) + च (and): ः + च → श्च.

questions.q: In unit 97, what case is शस्त्रेण, and what sense does it give?
optionExplain: The ablative would be शस्त्रात्.
The locative would be शस्त्रे.
Right: -एण is the instrumental singular of an अ-stem: with the blade.
The genitive would be शस्त्रस्य.
questions.explain: शस्त्रेण = with the śastra: instrumental singular.
questions.rule: -एण (after र/ष) = instrumental singular of an अ-stem.

questions.q: By the rule of परिहार्याश्च, how is देवाः + च (and the gods) joined?
optionExplain: The visarga does not drop before च; it becomes श्.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ, and only before voiced sounds.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant; च is voiceless and देवाः ends in आः.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as परिहार्याः + च.
questions.explain: देवाः + च = देवाश्च, like परिहार्याः + च = परिहार्याश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: परिहार्याः + च → परिहार्याश्च.

questions.q: By unit 98, how many asthi-saṃghātas (bone assemblages) are there?
optionExplain: Right: चतुर्दश अस्थिसंघाताः: fourteen bone assemblages.
Sixteen is the count of the kaṇḍarās and of the jālas.
Eighteen is the total of the sīmantas in unit 99.
Seven is the count of the sīvanīs in unit 96.
questions.explain: The line opens: चतुर्दश, fourteen.

questions.q: Put the places of unit 98 in the order of गुल्फजानुवंक्षणमणिबंधकूर्परकक्षासु.
questions.explain: Ankle, knee, groin, wrist, elbow, armpit.
questions.rule: गुल्फ → जानु → वंक्षण → मणिबंध → कूर्पर → कक्षा.

questions.q: Match each place of unit 98 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sure places: ankle, knee, groin, wrist, elbow and armpit.
questions.teaches: अस्थिसंघात = अस्थि (bone) + संघात (assemblage, group): a group of bones.

questions.q: Which split of चतुर्दशास्थिसंघाताः is right?
optionExplain: स्थिसंघाताः is not a word; the word is अस्थिसंघाताः.
Right: अ + अ → आ: चतुर्दश + अस्थि → चतुर्दशास्थि.
ए + अ would give चतुर्दशेऽस्थि, with ए kept and ऽ.
अः + अ would give चतुर्दशोऽस्थि, with ओऽ.
questions.explain: चतुर्दश (fourteen) + अस्थिसंघाताः (bone assemblages): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which places does the sure part of unit 98 name for the bone assemblages?
optionExplain: Right: जानु is the second place.
The navel is not named in unit 98.
The neck is not named in unit 98.
Right: कूर्पर is the fifth place.
questions.explain: The sure places are ankle, knee, groin, wrist, elbow and armpit.

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्दश + अस्थि → चतुर्दशास्थि, how is अत्र + अपि (here too) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as चतुर्दश + अस्थि.
The two अ merge into a long आ; neither is simply lost.
questions.explain: अत्र + अपि = अत्रापि, like चतुर्दश + अस्थि = चतुर्दशास्थि.
questions.teaches: A short अ followed by a short अ joins as long आ: चतुर्दश + अस्थि → चतुर्दशास्थि.

questions.q: By unit 99, what total of sīmantas does the line give?
optionExplain: Fourteen is the count of the bone assemblages in unit 98.
Sixteen is the count of the kaṇḍarās and of the jālas.
Seven is the count of the sīvanīs in unit 96.
Right: इत्यष्टादश: thus eighteen.
questions.explain: The line ends: इति अष्टादश, thus eighteen.

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 99 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Likewise the sīmantas; they, however, five in the head; thus eighteen.
questions.rule: तद्वत्सीमंताः → ते तु → पंच शिरसि → इति → अष्टादश.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 99 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Likewise the sīmantas; they, however, are five in the head: thus eighteen.
questions.teaches: तद्वत् = तत् + वत्, 'like that, likewise': त् becomes द् before the voiced व.

questions.q: Which split of शिरसीत्यष्टादश is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ + इ → ई (शिरसीति), then इ + अ → य (इत्यष्टादश).
ति is not a word; the particle is इति.
इत्य is not a word; the particle is इति.
यष्टादश is not a word; the number is अष्टादश.
questions.explain: शिरसि (in the head) + इति (thus) + अष्टादश (eighteen).
questions.rule: इ + इ → ई; इ + a different vowel → य्.

questions.q: In unit 99 the sīmantas in the head are ____ (five). Type the number word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: ते तु पञ्च शिरसि: they, however, are five in the head.
questions.teaches: पञ्च (printed पंच) = five.

questions.q: By the rule of इति + अष्टादश → इत्यष्टादश, how is इति + अपि (thus too) joined?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as इति + अष्टादश.
ई comes from इ + इ; here अ follows.
इ becomes य्, not अय्; अय् comes from ए before a vowel.
questions.explain: इति + अपि = इत्यपि, like इति + अष्टादश = इत्यष्टादश.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + अष्टादश → इत्यष्टादश.

questions.q: By unit 100, how many bones are counted in all?
optionExplain: The excess is sixty (षष्ठ्या), not six.
The hundreds are three (त्रीणि), not two.
Right: त्रीणि षष्ठ्याधिकानि अस्थिशतानि: three hundred, exceeding by sixty.
The excess is sixty, not sixteen (षोडश).
questions.explain: 300 exceeding by 60 = 360.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Put the words of unit 100 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Three, by sixty, exceeding, hundreds of bones.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Match each word of unit 100 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three hundreds of bones, exceeding by sixty.
questions.teaches: A number with -अधिक is added to the hundreds: त्रीणि ... अधिकानि शतानि = three hundred plus.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Which split of अधिकान्यस्थिशतानि is right?
optionExplain: अधिकान्य is not a form; the word is अधिकानि.
ए + अ would give अधिकानेऽस्थि, with ए kept and ऽ.
यस्थि is not a word; the word is अस्थि (bone).
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: अधिकानि + अस्थि → अधिकान्यस्थि.
questions.explain: अधिकानि (exceeding) + अस्थिशतानि (hundreds of bones): इ + अ → य.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: In unit 100, what does अधिकानि tell about the sixty?
options: Sixty is added to three hundred
Sixty is taken away from three hundred
Three hundred is multiplied by sixty
Sixty bones are left out of the count
optionExplain: Right: अधिक = exceeding: three hundred, and sixty more.
अधिक means in excess, not less.
Nothing is multiplied; sixty is the excess.
Nothing is left out; the sixty are counted in.
questions.explain: Three hundred exceeding by sixty: 300 + 60.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: By the pattern of unit 100, what does a new example द्वे दशाधिके शते mean?
optionExplain: अधिक adds the ten; it does not take it away.
Right: द्वे शते = two hundreds; दशाधिके = exceeding by ten.
The ten is added to the hundreds, not multiplied.
The excess is दश, ten, not twenty.
questions.explain: द्वे दशाधिके शते = 200 + 10 = 210, like त्रीणि षष्ठ्याधिकानि शतानि = 360.
questions.rule: N शतानि with M-अधिक = N hundred + M.
questions.teaches: Hundreds with an -अधिक word add that number: त्रीणि षष्ठ्याऽधिकानि अस्थिशतानि = 360 bones.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: By unit 101, how many bones are in the head (मूर्धन्)?
optionExplain: That is the number given for the limbs (शाखा).
Sixty is the excess over three hundred in unit 100.
Right: शतं मूर्ध्नि: a hundred in the head.
That is the total of all the bones in unit 100.
questions.explain: शतं मूर्ध्नि: a hundred in the head.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Put these printed phrases of unit 101 in the line's order.
questions.explain: And of them: a hundred and forty in the limbs; a hundred and twenty in the trunk (probable); a hundred in the head.
questions.rule: तेषां च → त्वारिंशच्छतं शाखासु → स विंशशत मंतराधौ → शतं मूर्द्ध्नीति.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Match each word of unit 101 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The bones in the limbs, the trunk and the head; a hundred in the head, thus.
questions.teaches: शाखा, literally 'branch', names the limbs: शाखासु = in the limbs.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: Which split of मूर्द्ध्नीति (मूर्ध्नीति) is right?
optionExplain: ति is not a word; the particle is इति.
ए before इ would give मूर्ध्न इति (or मूर्ध्नयिति), not ई.
अः before इ drops the visarga: मूर्ध्न इति, with no ई.
Right: इ + इ → ई: मूर्ध्नि + इति → मूर्ध्नीति.
questions.explain: मूर्ध्नि (in the head) + इति (thus): इ + इ → ई.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: By unit 101, of what are these counts a division?
options: Of the fourteen bone groups of unit 98
Of the sixteen jālas of unit 93
Of the seven sīvanīs of unit 96
optionExplain: Right: तेषाम् (of them) points back to the bones just counted; the counts here run to hundreds (शतं मूर्ध्नि).
The bone groups are fourteen in all; these counts run to hundreds.
The jālas are sixteen in all; these counts run to hundreds.
The sīvanīs are seven in all; these counts run to hundreds.
questions.explain: तेषाम् points back to the 360 bones of unit 100.
questions.rule: तेषाम् = of them (the bones of unit 100).
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: संख्या, शाखाओं व पसलियों में

questions.q: By the rule of मूर्ध्नि + इति, how is अस्ति + इति (‘is’, thus) joined?
optionExplain: इ becomes य् only before a different vowel; here इ meets इ.

अष्टाव is the plain word for eight

The word is अष्टौ; अष्टाव् is its form before a vowel.

questions.q: By the rule of अष्टावुरसि, how is तौ + इति (those two, thus) written when joined?

औ before a vowel does not swallow the vowel; it becomes आव्.
questions.explain: तौ + इति = ताविति, like अष्टौ + उरसि = अष्टावुरसि.
questions.teaches: औ before a vowel becomes आव्: अष्टौ + उरसि → अष्टावुरसि.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: शेष स्थान व पाँच प्रकार

questions.q: भगे and त्रिके share the ending -ए. What does it mean in unit 109?
optionExplain: Right: The data: both are loc. sg., 'in the bhaga, in the trika'.
The instrumental of an अ-stem ends in -एन, not -ए.
The ablative of an अ-stem ends in -आत्, not -ए.
The genitive of an अ-stem ends in -अस्य, not -ए.
questions.explain: -ए here is the locative: in the bhaga, in the trika.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: शेष स्थान व पाँच प्रकार

questions.q: By the rule of एक + एकम्, how is न + एव (not at all) written when joined?

Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as एक + एकम् → एकैकम्.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + ए.

questions.explain: न + एव = नैव, like एक + एकम् = एकैकम्.
questions.teaches: Short अ before ए joins as ऐ: एक + एकम् → एकैकम्.
questions.section: अस्थियाँ: शेष स्थान व पाँच प्रकार

questions.q: By unit 167, where are twelve snāyus counted?
options: In the upper and lower lips
In the upper and lower gums
In the two jaws and the neck
In the tongue and the palate
optionExplain: The lips (ओष्ठ) are not named in unit 167.
Right: उत्तराधरेषु दंतमांसेषु: in the upper and lower gums.
The jaws come in unit 165; unit 167 names the gums.
The tongue comes in unit 166; unit 167 names the gums.
questions.explain: Twelve in the upper and lower gums.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 167 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Twelve, in the upper and lower gums.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Match each word of unit 167 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Twelve in the upper and lower gums.
questions.teaches: दन्तमांस = 'tooth-flesh', the gums; उत्तर and अधर here mean upper and lower.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Which split of द्वादशोत्तर in unit 167 is right?
optionExplain: द्वादशो is not the number; the word is द्वादश (twelve).
ओत्तर is not a word; the word is उत्तर (upper).
Right: अ + उ → ओ: द्वादश + उत्तर → द्वादशोत्तर.
A visarga after अ drops before उ: that gives द्वादश उत्तर, two words.
questions.explain: द्वादश (twelve) + उत्तर (upper): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: By unit 167, what does दन्तमांस literally mean?
optionExplain: मांस is flesh, not root or socket.
दन्त is tooth, not lip.
दन्त is tooth and मांस is flesh, not bone.
Right: दन्त (tooth) + मांस (flesh): the gums.
questions.explain: दन्तमांस = tooth-flesh = the gums.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: By the pattern of दन्तमांसेषु (in the gums, from दन्तमांस), how is in the houses said from गृह?
optionExplain: Right: An अ-stem takes -एषु for 'in' (plural): दन्तमांस → दन्तमांसेषु, गृह → गृहेषु.
गृहे is the locative singular, 'in the house'.
गृहाणि is the nominative or accusative plural.
गृहैः is the instrumental plural, 'by the houses'.
questions.explain: गृहेषु = in the houses, like दन्तमांसेषु = in the gums.
questions.teaches: दन्तमांसेषु is the locative plural of an अ-stem: -एषु means 'in' (many).
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: By unit 168, how many snāyus are counted in the head?
optionExplain: Twelve is the count for the gums (unit 167).
Right: षण्मूर्द्धनि: six in the head.
Five is the count for the tongue (unit 166).
षट् is six; sixty would be षष्टि.
questions.explain: Six in the head.
questions.rule: षट् = six; मूर्धनि = in the head.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Match each part of unit 168 to its meaning.
questions.explain: षट् + मूर्धनि = षण्मूर्धनि: six in the head.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: In unit 168 the plain number word hidden in षण्- is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: षट् = six; before मूर्धनि it is written षण्.
questions.teaches: षट् = six; ट् before a nasal may become ण्.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Which split of षण्मूर्द्धनि in unit 168 is right?
optionExplain: षष्टि is sixty, and no ष्टि is printed; the data reads six, षट्.
र्धनि is not a word; the word is मूर्धनि (in the head).
Right: ट् before the nasal म is written ण् here: षट् + मूर्धनि → षण्मूर्धनि.
षण is not the number word; six is षट्.
questions.explain: षट् (six) + मूर्धनि (in the head).
questions.rule: ट् + म → ण्म (optional nasal before a nasal).
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: Why is मूर्धनि printed मूर्द्धनि in unit 168?
options: A dual form, meaning in the two heads
A different word, meaning in the neck
A sandhi change caused by the six
A print habit of doubling द after र
optionExplain: The data reads a locative singular, मूर्धनि.
The data reads मूर्धन्, the head.
The six changes only its own ट्; the द्द is a print habit.
Right: The note: doubled -rdd- is a print habit, normalised to मूर्धनि.
questions.explain: मूर्द्धनि = मूर्धनि; the doubled द is a habit of this print.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: By the rule of षण्मूर्धनि (ट् before म written ण्), what number stands in षण्मुखः (six-faced), a new example?
optionExplain: Right: षण्- before मुख is षट् with ट् written ण् before the nasal म.
Sixty would be षष्टि, not षण्-.
Sixteen is षोडश, not षण्-.
Five is पञ्च, not षण्-.
questions.explain: षण्मुखः = षट् + मुख: six-faced.
questions.teaches: Before a nasal such as म, a final ट् may become ण्: षट् + मूर्धनि → षण्मूर्धनि.
questions.section: स्नायु: धड़, गर्दन व सिर में

questions.q: By unit 169, what are the large round snāyus called?
optionExplain: Tendrilled is said of those in the limbs and joints.
Right: महास्नावानि तु वृत्तानि तानि कण्डरासंज्ञानि: called kaṇḍarā.
Hollow ones are named in unit 170, not here.
Broad ones are named in unit 171, not here.
questions.explain: The large round ones are called kaṇḍarā (probably tendons).

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 169 in the lines' order.
questions.explain: Among these, in the limbs and joints: tendrilled; but the large ones, round, are called kaṇḍarā.
questions.rule: शाखासु संधिषु च → प्रतानवंति → महास्नावानि तु → वृत्तानि तानि → कंडरासंज्ञानि.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 169 to its meaning.
questions.explain: In the limbs and joints: tendrilled; the large round ones: kaṇḍarā.
questions.teaches: प्रतानवत् = having tendrils, spreading in branches; कण्डरा is probably a tendon.

questions.q: Which pairing of place or shape and kind is right by unit 169?
optionExplain: Kaṇḍarā is the name of the large round ones.
The large round ones are called kaṇḍarā.
Right: शाखासु संधिषु च प्रतानवंति.
Unit 169 does not call them broad.
questions.explain: Limbs and joints → tendrilled; large and round → kaṇḍarā.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 169?
options: It compares the snāyus to a creeper
Those in the limbs and joints are tendrilled
Here snāva names a thing other than snāyu
The large round ones are called kaṇḍarā
optionExplain: The note: the Sanskrit gives no comparison with a creeper.
Right: शाखासु संधिषु च प्रतानवंति.
The note: snāva is a variant of snāyu.
Right: वृत्तानि तानि कण्डरासंज्ञानि.
questions.explain: Tendrilled in the limbs and joints; the large round ones are kaṇḍarā.

questions.q: By the pattern of महास्नाव (large sinew), what does महावृक्षः mean in a new example?
optionExplain: महा- means large, not small.
महा- is not a plural; the compound is one tree.
Nothing in महा- means root.
Right: महा- at the start of a karmadhāraya = large: महा + स्नाव = large sinew.
questions.explain: महावृक्षः = a large tree, as महास्नाव = a large sinew.
questions.rule: महत् → महा- in a karmadhāraya: large X.
questions.teaches: In महास्नाव, महा- (from महत्, large) describes the sinew: a karmadhāraya, 'large sinew'.

questions.q: By unit 170, what kind of snāyu is in the bladder and the intestines?
optionExplain: Right: सुषिराणि: hollow ones.
Broad ones are in unit 171, in other places.
Round ones are the kaṇḍarās of unit 169.
Tendrilled ones are in the limbs and joints (unit 169).
questions.explain: Hollow ones are in the bladder, the two seats and the intestines.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 170 in the line's order.
questions.explain: In the bladder, the seats of the raw and the cooked, and the intestines: hollow ones.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 170 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Hollow ones in the bladder, the seats of the raw and the cooked, and the intestines.
questions.teaches: आमाशय and पक्वाशय = seats of the raw and of the cooked, probably the stomach and the large intestine.

questions.q: Which split of बस्त्याम in unit 170 is right?
optionExplain: याम is not the word; the word is आम (raw).
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: बस्ति + आम → बस्त्याम.
ए + आ would give बस्त आम or बस्तयाम, not बस्त्याम.
That would keep the इ: बस्तियाम, not बस्त्याम.
questions.explain: बस्ति (bladder) + आम (raw): इ + आ → या.
questions.rule: इ + unlike vowel → य् + that vowel.

questions.q: Why does the English of unit 170 name both āmāśaya and pakvāśaya for the printed आमपक्वाशय?
options: The print repeats one and the same word twice
The Hindi adds a seat not in the line
It may be a short dvandva of both seats
आम and पक्व are two names of one seat
optionExplain: The word is printed once, as आमपक्वाशय.
Both आम and पक्व are printed in the line.
Right: The note: a contracted dvandva for āmāśaya and pakvāśaya.
आम (raw) and पक्व (cooked) are opposite, two seats.
questions.explain: आमपक्वाशय is read as आमाशय + पक्वाशय, a contracted dvandva.
questions.rule: आम-पक्व-आशय = the seats of the raw and the cooked.

questions.q: By the rule of बस्ति + आम, how is अति + आचारः (excess conduct) joined?
optionExplain: ई comes from इ + इ, not from इ + आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + आ.
अय् comes from ए before a vowel, not from इ.
Right: इ before आ becomes य्, as बस्ति + आम → बस्त्याम.
questions.explain: अति + आचारः = अत्याचारः, like बस्ति + आम = बस्त्याम.
questions.teaches: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: बस्ति + आम → बस्त्याम.

questions.q: By unit 171, where are the broad (पृथु) snāyus found?
options: The limbs and the joints of the body
Tongue, gums and the two jaws
optionExplain: Right: पार्श्वपृष्ठोरःशिरःसु पृथूनि.
Those places hold the hollow ones (unit 170).
Those hold the tendrilled ones (unit 169).
Those are counts in units 165-167, not the broad kind.
questions.explain: Broad ones are in the sides, back, chest and head.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 171 in the line's order.
questions.explain: In the sides, back, chest and head: broad ones.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 171 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Broad ones in the sides, back, chest and head.
questions.teaches: पृथु = broad: the kind of snāyu in the sides, back, chest and head.

questions.q: Which split of पृष्ठोरः in unit 171 is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ drops before उ: that gives पृष्ठ उरः, two words.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: पृष्ठ + उरः → पृष्ठोरः.
रः is not a word here; the word is उरः (chest).
ओरः is not a word; the word is उरः.
questions.explain: पृष्ठ (back) + उरः (chest): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: A teacher points to the snāyus of the chest. By unit 171, what kind are they?
optionExplain: Hollow ones are in the bladder and the intestines (unit 170).
Round ones are the large kaṇḍarās (unit 169).
Right: उरः is among the places of पृथूनि.
Tendrilled ones are in the limbs and joints (unit 169).
questions.explain: The chest is a place of the broad ones.

questions.q: By the rule of पृष्ठ + उरः, how is हित + उपदेशः (good advice) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from अ + उ.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel, not from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as पृष्ठ + उरः → पृष्ठोरः.
questions.explain: हित + उपदेशः = हितोपदेशः, like पृष्ठ + उरः = पृष्ठोरः.
questions.teaches: अ + उ gives ओ: पृष्ठ + उरः → पृष्ठोरः.

questions.q: By unit 172, to what is the well-bound body compared?
optionExplain: Right: तनुर्नौरिव: the body, like a boat.
No tree is named in unit 172; the simile is नौः, a boat.
No house is named in unit 172; the simile is a boat.
No chariot is named in unit 172; the simile is a boat.
questions.explain: The body, well bound, acts properly like a boat.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 172 in the line's order.
questions.explain: For by the bonds of sinew, in the joints, well bound, the body like a boat acts properly.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 172 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The body, well bound by the bonds of sinew, acts properly like a boat.
questions.teaches: इव = like: तनुः नौः इव, the body like a boat (a simile).

questions.q: Which split of तनुर्नौरिव in unit 172 is right?
optionExplain: र्नौः is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga of तनुः.
Right: Visarga after उ or औ becomes र् before a voiced sound: तनुर् नौर् इव.
रिव is not a word; the word is इव (like).
नौरि and व are not words here; it is नौः + इव.
questions.explain: तनुः (body) + नौः (boat) + इव (like).
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ → र् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 172?
options: The bonds are made of snāva (sinew)
The body is compared with a chariot
It says the joints are hollow
The body is bound in the joints
optionExplain: Right: स्नावबन्धनैः.
The simile is a boat (नौः), not a chariot.
Hollowness is not named in unit 172.
Right: संधिषु सुबद्धा.
questions.explain: Bound in the joints by the bonds of sinew, the body acts properly like a boat.

questions.q: By the rule of तनुः + नौः → तनुर्नौः, how is गुरुः + गच्छति (the teacher goes) joined?
optionExplain: Before a voiced sound the visarga after उ does not stay.
स् comes from a visarga before त or थ, not before ग.
Right: A visarga after उ becomes र् before the voiced ग, as तनुः + नौः → तनुर्नौः.
The visarga after उ drops only before र, with lengthening.
questions.explain: गुरुः + गच्छति = गुरुर्गच्छति, like तनुः + नौः = तनुर्नौः.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound: तनुः + नौः → तनुर्नौः.

questions.q: By unit 173, what should one do with the sinews?
optionExplain: Nothing is said of cutting; रक्षेत् = should protect.
Nothing is said of binding; रक्षेत् = should protect.
The line asks for effort (यत्नतः) in protecting them.
Right: तानि यत्नतो रक्षेत्: one should protect them with effort.
questions.explain: One should protect them with effort.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of unit 173 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Therefore, even more than the bones, vessels and the rest, one should protect them with effort.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 173 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Therefore one should protect them with effort.
questions.teaches: रक्षेत् is an optative of √रक्ष्: 'one should protect'.

questions.q: Which split of सिरादिभ्योऽपि in unit 173 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः before अ becomes ओ, and the अ is shown by ऽ: सिरादिभ्योऽपि.
सिरादिभ्यो is not the base form; the ओ comes from अः by sandhi.
पि is not a word; the word is अपि (even).
ए + अ would give सिरादिभ्येऽपि, not -भ्योऽपि.
questions.explain: सिरादिभ्यः + अपि: अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: रक्षेत् in unit 173 is an optative (data). What sense does it give?
options: One is being protected by them
optionExplain: That would be a past form, not the optative.
Right: The optative here gives an instruction: one should protect.
That would be a future form, not the optative.
That would be a passive, not this active optative.
questions.explain: रक्षेत् = one should protect.

questions.q: By the rule of सिरादिभ्यः + अपि, how is रामः + अपि (Rāma also) joined?
optionExplain: No rule gives -आपि: अः before अ gives ओऽ, and even after आ the dropped visarga leaves two words.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ, with ऽ for the अ, as सिरादिभ्यः + अपि.
Before अ the visarga after अ does not stay.
questions.explain: रामः + अपि = रामोऽपि, like सिरादिभ्यः + अपि = सिरादिभ्योऽपि.
questions.teaches: A visarga after short अ before अ: अः + अ → ओऽ (सिरादिभ्यः + अपि → सिरादिभ्योऽपि).

questions.q: By unit 174, what can one who knows the sinews well do?
options: Set every broken bone of the limbs
Stop any bleeding of the vessels
Cure every fever of the whole body
Extract even a hidden foreign body
optionExplain: Bones are not named in unit 174.
Bleeding is not named in unit 174.
Fever is not named in unit 174.
Right: गूढमपि शल्यमाहर्तुं समर्थो भवति.
questions.explain: He becomes able to extract even a hidden śalya.

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 174 in the line's order.
questions.explain: He who knows well the sinews, external and internal, becomes able to extract even a hidden śalya.
questions.rule: यश्च स्नावानि → बाह्यान्यभ्यंतराणि च → सम्यग्जानाति → स गूढमपि शल्यमाहर्त्तुं → समर्थो भवति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 174 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Knowing the external and internal sinews, one can extract even a hidden foreign body.
questions.teaches: शल्य = a foreign body such as a dart or splinter (standard); आहर्तुम् = to extract.

questions.q: Which split of बाह्यान्यभ्यंतराणि in unit 174 is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: बाह्यानि + अभ्यन्तराणि.
यभ्यन्तराणि is not a word; the word is अभ्यन्तराणि.
ए + अ would give बाह्यानेऽभ्यन्तराणि.
बाह्यान्य is not a form; the word is बाह्यानि.
questions.explain: बाह्यानि (external) + अभ्यन्तराणि (internal): इ + अ → य.
questions.rule: इ + unlike vowel → य् + that vowel.

questions.q: A healer must remove a splinter buried deep. By unit 174, what knowledge makes one able?
options: Knowing the bones and the joints
Knowing the sinews, outer and inner
Knowing the hollow seats of raw and cooked
optionExplain: Unit 174 names the sinews, not bones and joints.
Right: यश्च स्नावानि बाह्यान्यभ्यन्तराणि च सम्यग्जानाति.
Unit 174 names the sinews, not vessels or muscles.
Unit 174 names the sinews, external and internal.
questions.explain: Knowing the external and internal sinews well.

questions.q: By the pattern of आहर्तुं समर्थः (able to extract), what does पठितुं समर्थः mean in a new example?
optionExplain: -तुम् is not a past form.
-तुम् gives 'to do', not a reason.
Right: -तुम् (infinitive) + समर्थ = able to do it, as आहर्तुं समर्थः.
Wishing would be a desiderative, not -तुम् + समर्थ.
questions.explain: पठितुं समर्थः = able to read, like आहर्तुं समर्थः = able to extract.
questions.teaches: आहर्तुम् is an infinitive (-तुम्): with समर्थ it means 'able to extract'.

questions.q: By unit 175, how many peśī (muscles) are counted?
optionExplain: Nine hundred is the snāyu count (unit 144).
पञ्च शतानि is five hundred, not three hundred.
पञ्च शतानि is five hundred, not seven hundred.
Right: पंच पेशीशतानि: five hundred muscles.
questions.explain: Five hundred muscles.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 175 to its meaning.
questions.explain: पञ्च पेशीशतानि = five hundreds of muscles.

questions.q: In unit 175 the word for muscle is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पेशी = muscle (standard): पञ्च पेशीशतानि, five hundred muscles.

questions.q: What count does unit 175 appear to begin?

questions.q: By the pattern of तासां चत्वारि शतानि (of them, four hundred), what does फलानां त्रीणि mean in a new example?

questions.q: Which split of षष्टिरंतराधौ in unit 177 is right?

No ending is lost; षष्टिः is the normal form.
The data reads nominative singular, not dual.

questions.q: By the rule of षष्टिः + अन्तराधौ, how is हरिः + अपि (Hari also) joined?

questions.teaches: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a vowel: षष्टिः + अन्तराधौ → षष्टिरन्तराधौ.
