questions.q: By unit 214, the body is गवाक्षित. What does that mean?
optionExplain: गवाक्षित comes from गवाक्ष, window-lattice, not a pot.
गवाक्षित comes from गवाक्ष, window-lattice, not layers.
गवाक्षित comes from गवाक्ष, window-lattice, not coils.
Right: गवाक्ष = window, lattice; गवाक्षित = latticed.
questions.explain: गवाक्षितम् = latticed, made like a window-lattice.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put the three things said of the body in unit 214 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Latticed, bound round and stretched out.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 214 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By those this body is latticed, bound round and stretched out.
questions.teaches: पिनद्ध = 'bound round', from अपि-√नह् with the अ of अपि lost.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which split of पिनद्धमाततं in unit 214 is right?
optionExplain: Right: म् before a vowel simply joins it: पिनद्धम् + आततम् → पिनद्धमाततम्.
माततम् is not a word; the word is आततम् (stretched).
पिनद्धमा is not a form; the word is पिनद्धम्.
अः before आ would give पिनद्ध आततम्; and the neuter form is पिनद्धम्.
questions.explain: पिनद्धम् (bound round) + आततम् (stretched out).
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → joined, no change.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: In unit 214, which form is ताभिः?
optionExplain: The feminine accusative plural is ताः.
Right: ताभिः = by those (feminine instrumental plural).
The feminine genitive plural is तासाम्.
The feminine locative plural is तासु.
questions.explain: ताभिः = by those: the body is latticed by those.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the pattern of गवाक्ष → गवाक्षित, what does पुष्पित (from पुष्प, flower) mean in a new example?
options: Given away as a flower gift
optionExplain: -इत does not make a doer; that would be another form.
-इत means furnished with, not deprived of.
Right: -इत on a noun: furnished with it, as गवाक्षित = latticed.
-इत on a noun does not mean given as that thing.
questions.explain: पुष्पित = full of flowers, like गवाक्षित = latticed.
questions.rule: Noun + -इत = furnished with / made into that.
questions.teaches: गवाक्षित is a participle made from the noun गवाक्ष: 'furnished with a lattice', latticed.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 215, which three kinds of hair are named?
optionExplain: Eyebrows and eyelashes are not named; श्मश्रु and लोमन् are.
Eyebrow and nostril hair are not named; केश and लोमन् are.
Eyelash and armpit hair are not named; श्मश्रु and लोमन् are.
Right: केशश्मश्रुलोमानि: केश (head), श्मश्रु (beard), लोमन् (body).
questions.explain: Head-hair (केश), beard-hair (श्मश्रु) and body-hair (लोमन्).
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 215 in the line's order (joined words are shown split).
questions.explain: That many hairs; for their openings are bound to that; therefore those are nourished by those.
questions.rule: तावन्ति → केशश्मश्रुलोमानि → तासां हि मुखानि → तत्प्रतिबद्धानि → अतस्तानि → ताभिराप्यायन्ते.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 215 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Head-, beard- and body-hair; therefore they are nourished.
questions.teaches: आप्यायन्ते (आ-√प्याय्, ātmanepada) = are nourished, swell with fluid.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which split of प्रतिबद्धान्यतस्तानि in unit 215 is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ + अ → य; visarga before त → स्.
A word beginning with य does not fuse with इ; it would stay प्रतिबद्धानि यतः.
ए + अ would give प्रतिबद्धानेऽतः, not -न्यतः.
स्तानि is not a word; the स् is the visarga of अतः.
questions.explain: प्रतिबद्धानि (bound) + अतः (therefore) + तानि (those).
questions.rule: इ + अ → य; visarga + त → स्त.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 215 as the card reads it?
options: It names head-, beard- and body-hair
It states plainly what 'that many' refers to
It names the sirā and dhamanī as 'those'
optionExplain: Right: केशश्मश्रुलोमानि.
It does not; the reference is only probable.
They are not named in the unit; that reading is probable.
Right: आ-√प्याय्, are nourished.
questions.explain: Three kinds of hair are named and said to be nourished; the references stay open.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the pattern of केशश्मश्रुलोमानि, what does फलपुष्पपत्राणि mean in a new example?
optionExplain: A dvandva does not make one member grow from another.
Right: A dvandva lists its members; plural, neuter after the last (पत्र).
A dvandva is a list, not 'X that holds Y'.
पत्र is the last member of the list, not left out.
questions.explain: फलपुष्पपत्राणि = fruits, flowers and leaves, like केशश्मश्रुलोमानि = head-, beard- and body-hairs.
questions.rule: Dvandva = a list joined into one word.
questions.teaches: केशश्मश्रुलोमानि is a dvandva: a list joined into one word, plural, taking the gender of its last member (लोमन्, neuter).
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 216, what do 'those' (ताः) carry?
optionExplain: The line names स्वेद, sweat, not urine.
The line names स्वेद, sweat, not tears.
Right: स्वेदमभिवहन्ति: carry the sweat (स्वेद).
The line names स्वेद, sweat, not ear wax.
questions.explain: Those carry the sweat.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put the words of unit 216 in the line's order (joined words are shown split).
questions.explain: And by those, those carry the sweat.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: In unit 216 the word for 'sweat' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स्वेदम् (sweat, accusative) + अभिवहन्ति (carry).
questions.teaches: स्वेद = sweat.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Why is तैः printed तैश् before च in unit 216?
optionExplain: स् comes from a visarga before त or थ, not before च.
र् comes before a voiced sound; च is unvoiced.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant; here it is ऐः before च.
Right: तैः + च → तैश्च.
questions.explain: तैः (by those) + च (and): visarga before च → श्.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 216 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And by those, those carry the sweat.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the rule of तैः + च, how is रामः + च (and Rāma) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: Visarga before च becomes श्, as तैः + च → तैश्च.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant; च is unvoiced.
स् comes from a visarga before त or थ, not before च.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ; here it is अः.
questions.explain: रामः + च = रामश्च, like तैः + च = तैश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: तैः + च → तैश्च.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 217, whose potency (वीर्य) is carried after it has matured in the skin?
options: Of the food eaten and the water drunk
Of oil massage, paste and the like
Of the semen and the menstrual blood
Of the bones and the joints of the limbs
optionExplain: Food and drink are not named in unit 217; it names massage and paste.
Right: अभ्यङ्गलेपादिवीर्यम्: the potency of abhyaṅga, lepa and the like.
Śukra and rajas are measured in units 223 and 225, not carried here.
Bones and joints are not named in unit 217.
questions.explain: They carry the potency of oil massage (abhyaṅga), paste (lepa) and the like, matured in the skin.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 217 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Likewise the potency of massage, paste and the like, in the skin, matured, they carry; and touch they take up.
questions.rule: तथा … वीर्यम् → त्वचि → विपक्वम् … नयन्ति → स्पर्शं च → गृह्णन्ति.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 217 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The potency of oil massage and paste, matured in the skin, is carried; touch is taken up.
questions.teaches: -आदि at the end of a list means 'and the like': अभ्यङ्गलेपादि = oil massage, paste and the like.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 217, what has happened to that potency in the skin (त्वचि)?
options: It has flowed out there as sweat
It has been bound there to dung
optionExplain: Sweat is carried in unit 216; unit 217 says the potency matured.
'Countless' is said of the srotas in unit 218, not of a potency.
Right: विपक्वम् = fully matured, past participle of वि-√पच्.
Binding to the dung is said in unit 221 of a liquid.
questions.explain: The potency of massage and paste is वीर्यं त्वचि विपक्वम्: fully matured in the skin.
questions.rule: त्वचि विपक्वम् = fully matured in the skin.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which two actions does unit 217 give to its unnamed subject ('they')?
optionExplain: Cooking food is not said in unit 217.
Right: वीर्यं … नयन्ति, they carry the potency.
Covering the joints is said in unit 212 (probably of the peśīs), not in unit 217.
Right: स्पर्शं च गृह्णन्ति, and they take up touch.
questions.explain: They carry the matured potency, and they take up touch.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the rule of स्पर्शं च (स्पर्शम् + च), how is फलम् + च (and the fruit) written inside a sentence?
optionExplain: श् before च comes from a visarga, not from a final म्.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant; च is not voiced, and the word ends in म्.
The म् is not dropped with a long आ; it becomes anusvāra.
Right: A final म् before a consonant inside a sentence is written as anusvāra, as स्पर्शम् + च → स्पर्शं च.
questions.explain: फलम् + च → फलं च, like स्पर्शम् + च → स्पर्शं च.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a consonant inside a sentence is written ं: स्पर्शम् + च → स्पर्शं च.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 218, how many srotas (bodily channels) are there?
options: Ten, like the seats of life
optionExplain: Right: असंख्येयानि एव: indeed countless.
Three hundred and sixty is the count of the bones in unit 100.
Sixteen is the count of the jālas (nets) in unit 93.
Ten is the count of the seats of life in unit 90.
questions.explain: स्रोतांसि पुनः असंख्येयानि एव: the srotas are indeed countless.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put the words of unit 218 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The srotas, however, countless, indeed.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 218 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The srotas (channels), however, are indeed countless.
questions.teaches: असंख्येय = अ (not) + संख्येय (to be counted): what cannot be counted.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which split of पुनरसंख्येयान्येव is right?
optionExplain: पुनर is not a word, and without the अ the meaning would flip to 'countable'.
Right: पुनः (base पुनर्) keeps its र् before a vowel; इ + ए → ये.
न् + ए would give नेव, with no य; the य comes from इ.
ए before ए would give -येय एव, not -यान्येव; the word is असंख्येयानि.
questions.explain: पुनः (पुनर्) + असंख्येयानि + एव → पुनरसंख्येयान्येव.
questions.rule: पुनर् + vowel → पुनर…; इ + a different vowel → य्.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: A student says that unit 218 lists the srotas one by one. What is wrong with that?
options: It lists them, but only in the women
It lists them, but counts only three
It lists none; it calls them countless
It lists them, but under the name sirā
optionExplain: Women are not mentioned in unit 218.
No number at all is given in unit 218.
Right: The line only says the srotas are countless (असंख्येय).
Sirā and the rest are taken up in unit 219, not listed here.
questions.explain: Unit 218 gives no list: स्रोतांसि पुनरसंख्येयान्येव.
questions.rule: स्रोतांसि असंख्येयानि = no count, no list.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the rule of असंख्येयानि + एव → असंख्येयान्येव, how is फलानि + एव (the fruits indeed) joined?
optionExplain: ए from a join comes from अ + इ; here it is इ + ए.
The ए of एव stays ए after य्; it does not become ऐ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए; फलानि ends in इ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as असंख्येयानि + एव.
questions.explain: फलानि + एव = फलान्येव, like असंख्येयानि + एव = असंख्येयान्येव.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: असंख्येयानि + एव → असंख्येयान्येव.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 219, what will be done with the sirā and the rest?
options: They are counted here, one by one
They are left out, never to be taught
They are measured here in handfuls
optionExplain: Right: अन्यत्र उपदेक्ष्यन्ते: they will be taught elsewhere.
No count is given in unit 219; the teaching is put off.
उपदेक्ष्यन्ते says they will be taught.
Handful measures belong to the fluids from unit 222 on.
questions.explain: सिरादीनि … अन्यत्र उपदेक्ष्यन्ते: they will be taught elsewhere.
questions.rule: अन्यत्र उपदेक्ष्यन्ते = will be taught elsewhere.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 219 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Even so, the sirā and the rest, broadly and as use requires, will be taught elsewhere.
questions.rule: तथापि तु → सिरादीनि → यथास्थूलम् → यथोपयोगम् → च अन्यत्र उपदेक्ष्यन्ते.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Match each word of unit 219 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Even so, the sirā and the rest will be taught elsewhere, broadly and as use requires.
questions.teaches: यथा- before a noun means 'according to': यथास्थूलम् = according to the gross (outline), यथोपयोगम् = according to use.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: Which split of यथोपयोगं is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give आ (यथापयोगम्), not ओ.
Right: आ + उ → ओ: यथा + उपयोगम् → यथोपयोगम्.
Neither यथो nor पयोगम् is a word here.
A visarga after आ is dropped before a vowel; no ओ would arise.
questions.explain: यथा (according to) + उपयोगम् (use) → यथोपयोगम्.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: In unit 219, what does the form उपदेक्ष्यन्ते tell about the teaching of the sirā and the rest?
options: It was given in an earlier line
It is being given in this line
It is still to come, later
It is forbidden to give at all
optionExplain: The form is future, not past.
The line gives no teaching on sirā; it points ahead.
Right: उपदेक्ष्यन्ते is a future passive: they will be taught.
Nothing forbids it; the form says it will be done.
questions.explain: उपदेक्ष्यन्ते (3 pl. fut. pass. उप-√दिश्) = they will be taught.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By the rule of यथा + उपयोगम् → यथोपयोगम्, how is महा + उत्सवः (a great festival) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ/आ + ओ or औ, not from आ + उ.
The उ is not lost; आ + उ gives ओ.
The आ is not lost; आ + उ gives ओ.
Right: आ + उ → ओ, as यथा + उपयोगम्.
questions.explain: महा + उत्सवः = महोत्सवः, like यथा + उपयोगम् = यथोपयोगम्.
questions.teaches: आ followed by उ joins as ओ: यथा + उपयोगम् → यथोपयोगम्.
questions.section: सिरा-धमनी के मुख, रोम व स्रोतस्

questions.q: By unit 220, what has been done with the corporeal entities (भाव) in the body?
options: They are said to be countless
optionExplain: Right: परिसंख्याताः: enumerated, counted out.
Teaching elsewhere is said of the sirā and the rest in unit 219.
'Countless' is said of the srotas in unit 218.
The handful measures belong to the fluids of units 222 to 226.
questions.explain: इत्येवं परिसंख्याताः शरीरे मूर्तिमन्तः … भावाः: thus the corporeal entities have been enumerated.

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 220 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Thus enumerated, in the body, the corporeal (firm, as read) entities.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 220 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Thus the corporeal entities in the body have been enumerated.
questions.teaches: -मत् (nominative plural -मन्तः) means 'having': मूर्तिमत् = having form (मूर्ति).

questions.q: Which split of इत्येवं is right?
optionExplain: इत्य is not a word; the य् is the changed इ of इति.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + एवम् → इत्येवम्.
इति has a short इ; ई + ए would also give ये, but इती is not the word.
इ + इ would give ई (इतीवम्), not ये.
questions.explain: इति (thus) + एवम् (so) → इत्येवम्.

questions.q: If मूर्तिमन्तः means 'having form', what kind of entities (भावाः) does unit 220 close?
options: Those with no form at all
optionExplain: That would be अमूर्त; unit 220 says मूर्तिमन्तः.
The mind is not named; the entities are 'in the body', with form.
Right: मूर्ति (form) + -मत् (having): entities that have form.
The liquids (द्रव) are taken up in unit 221, after this close.
questions.explain: मूर्तिमन्तः भावाः = entities having form, in the body.

questions.q: By the pattern of मूर्तिमत् (having form), what does a new example बुद्धिमान् पुरुषः mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would need अ- or निर्-; -मत् means 'having'.
That would be पुरुषस्य बुद्धिः; बुद्धिमान् describes the man.
'Made of' would be -मय; -मत् means 'having'.
Right: -मत् means 'having', as मूर्तिमत् = having form.
questions.explain: बुद्धि + -मत् → बुद्धिमान् (nom. sg. m.): having intellect, like मूर्ति + -मत् = having form.
questions.teaches: -मत् after a noun means 'having it': मूर्तिमत् = having form; nom. pl. मूर्तिमन्तः.

questions.q: After the corporeal entities, which group does unit 221 take up?
optionExplain: Right: द्रवास्तु: as for the liquids.
The srotas were called countless in unit 218.
The hairs are spoken of in unit 215.
The bones were counted much earlier, from unit 100.
questions.explain: द्रवाः तु: as for the liquids.

questions.q: Put the things named in unit 221 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Dung; likewise urine, blood and the other dhātus in the body.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 221 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The liquids; through excess; the dung, urine, blood and other dhātus.
questions.teaches: अनुबध्नाति (अनु-√बन्ध्) = binds on to, attaches; its objects here are in the accusative (-म्, -आन्).

questions.q: Which split of द्रवास्तु is right?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give ओऽ (द्रवोऽस्तु), not आस्.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: द्रवाः + तु → द्रवास्तु.
A visarga after आ is dropped before a vowel (द्रवा अस्तु).
द्रवास्त is not a word; the word is द्रवाः.
questions.explain: द्रवाः (liquids) + तु (as for) → द्रवास्तु.

questions.q: Which of these does unit 221 name?
optionExplain: Right: तथा मूत्रम्, likewise the urine.
Head-hair is named in unit 215, not in unit 221.
The brain is named in unit 224, not in unit 221.
Right: रुधिरम् follows मूत्रम्.
questions.explain: Unit 221 names the dung, urine, blood and the other dhātus.

questions.q: By the rule of द्रवाः + तु → द्रवास्तु, how is नराः + तत्र (the men there) joined?
optionExplain: The visarga after आ is dropped only before a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
आ does not turn into ओ; only the visarga changes.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, as द्रवाः + तु.
श् stands before च/छ/श; before त the visarga becomes स्.
questions.explain: नराः + तत्र = नरास्तत्र, like द्रवाः + तु = द्रवास्तु.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: द्रवाः + तु → द्रवास्तु.

questions.q: By unit 222, what is the fluid called that, bound with heat, flows out of the hair-pores?
optionExplain: Lasīkā is the name of the fluid in a wound, within the skin.
Rasa is the essence of food, the first measured after udaka.
Urine is one of the fluids measured; it does not come from the pores.
Right: स्वेदवाच्यम्: called sweat.
questions.explain: यच्चोष्मणाऽनुबद्धं रोमकूपेभ्योऽभिनिष्पतत् स्वेदवाच्यम्: bound with heat, flowing from the hair-pores, called sweat.

questions.q: Put the first six fluids measured in unit 222 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Water, rasa (essence of food), blood, dung, śleṣman, pitta; then urine, vasā, medas and marrow follow.
questions.rule: उदक → रस → रक्त → शकृत् → श्लेष्मन् → पित्त.

questions.q: Match each term of unit 222 to what the line says of it.
pairs: the name of the fluid in a wound
questions.explain: Lasīkā is the wound fluid, sweat flows from the pores, rasa is the essence of food; dung and urine are measured too.
questions.teaches: -आख्य at the end of a compound means 'named': रसाख्य = named rasa; -वाच्य = to be called: स्वेदवाच्य.

questions.q: Unit 222 speaks of 'an increase of number beginning with one'. Which fluid's own number does it print?
options: None: no fluid's number is printed
Rasa's, printed as half an añjali
optionExplain: Right: The data: the measure of each substance is not stated numerically.
Sweat is a form of udaka; no number is printed for it or any fluid.
The line speaks of an increase, so they are not all alike.
Half an añjali is said of śukra in unit 223, not here.
questions.explain: Only 'each by its own añjali measure ... an increase of number beginning with one' is printed.
questions.rule: No numbers are printed in unit 222.

questions.q: By unit 222, which of these are called udaka (water)?
optionExplain: Rasa, the essence of food, is measured next to udaka; it is not one of its forms.
Right: the fluid from the hair-pores called sweat is udaka.
Marrow (majjan) is the last fluid measured, not a form of udaka.
Right: the fluid in a wound called lasīkā is udaka.
questions.explain: The three 'yat' clauses (through the whole body, held by the outer skin; lasīkā; sweat) together are udaka.

questions.q: By the pattern of व्रणगतम् (gone to a wound), what does a new example हृदयगतम् mean?
optionExplain: 'Made of' would be -मय; -गत means gone to, situated in.
Right: -गत = gone to, situated in, as व्रणगत = gone to a wound.
-गत makes no comparison.
A measure would be -प्रमाण, as in अञ्जलिप्रमाण.
questions.explain: हृदय + -गत = gone into, situated in the heart, like व्रण + -गत = gone to a wound.
questions.rule: X-गत = gone to / situated in X.
questions.teaches: -गत at the end of a compound means 'gone to, situated in': सर्वशरीरगत, व्रणगत.

questions.q: By unit 223, how much śukra (semen) is there?
optionExplain: Four añjali is said of rajas in women, in unit 225.
Two is said of breast milk, in unit 226.
Right: अर्द्धंजलिः शुक्रस्य (read अर्ध-अञ्जलिः): half an añjali of śukra.
No such measure is given for śukra.
questions.explain: Half a cupped handful (añjali) of śukra.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 223 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Half a cupped handful of śukra (semen).

questions.q: Unit 223 measures śukra by half a cupped handful. Type its Sanskrit word for 'half': ____ (Devanagari or English letters, e.g. veda).
questions.explain: अर्ध (half) + अञ्जलिः (cupped handful); the print doubles the द (अर्द्ध).
questions.teaches: अर्ध = half; अर्ध-अञ्जलि = half a cupped handful.

questions.q: Unit 223 has no verb. Which rendering of it is right?
options: Half of the śukra fills a hand
A handful of śukra is halved
Śukra is half of the body
Half a cupped handful of śukra
optionExplain: The half is of the añjali, not of the śukra.
Nothing is said to be halved; अर्ध is part of the measure.
The body is not mentioned; the line gives a handful measure.
Right: A measure in the series: 'is' is understood.
questions.explain: अर्ध-अञ्जलिः (half a cupped handful) + शुक्रस्य (of śukra).
questions.rule: अर्ध-अञ्जलिः शुक्रस्य = half an añjali of śukra.

questions.q: Unit 223 continues the series of unit 222. In what unit of measure is śukra given?
optionExplain: Right: अञ्जलि, the measure of each fluid in unit 222.
Finger-breadths are not the measure used for these fluids.
Drops are not mentioned; the measure is the añjali.
No weight is given; the measure is the añjali.
questions.explain: Each fluid is measured by its own añjali; śukra by half an añjali.
questions.rule: अञ्जलि = the measure of the fluids.

questions.q: By the pattern of अर्ध-अञ्जलिः शुक्रस्य, what does a new example अर्धाञ्जलिस्तैलस्य mean?
options: Half a cupped handful of oil
Half the oil kept in a hand
optionExplain: The body is not named; अर्धाञ्जलि is a handful measure.
Right: The genitive names what is measured, as शुक्रस्य.
अर्ध means half, not two.
The half goes with the handful (अर्ध-अञ्जलि), not with the oil.
questions.explain: अर्धाञ्जलिः + तैलस्य → अर्धाञ्जलिस्तैलस्य (visarga + त → स्): half a cupped handful of oil.
questions.rule: Measure (nom.) + substance (gen.) = so much of it.
questions.teaches: A measure word with a genitive gives 'so much of X': अर्ध-अञ्जलिः शुक्रस्य = half an añjali of śukra.

questions.q: By unit 224, which two are given 'that much only' (तावदेव)?
optionExplain: Rajas and breast milk come in units 225 and 226.
Urine and blood are among the fluids of unit 222.
Right: मस्तिष्कम् ओजश्च: the brain and ojas.
Sweat and lasīkā are forms of udaka in unit 222.
questions.explain: तावदेव मस्तिष्कमोजश्च: that much only, the brain and ojas.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 224 in the line's order.
questions.explain: That much only: the brain and ojas.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 224 to its meaning.
questions.explain: That much only: the brain and ojas.
questions.teaches: तावत् = so much, pointing back to a measure already given; with एव: that much only.

questions.q: Which split of the printed मस्तिष्क मोजश्च is right?
optionExplain: मोजः is not a word; the म् belongs to मस्तिष्कम्.
श्च is not a word; श् is the changed visarga of ओजः.
अश्च is not a word here; the line ends in च, and.
Right: The म् of मस्तिष्कम् is printed with the next word; ओजः + च → ओजश्च.
questions.explain: मस्तिष्कम् (brain) + ओजः (ojas) + च (and); visarga + च → श्.

questions.q: In तावदेव, what does एव add to तावत् (so much)?
options: Not that much, none at all
optionExplain: Right: एव = only, exactly: that much and no other.
Nothing doubles the amount; एव only stresses it.
एव does not reduce the amount.
एव is not a negation.
questions.explain: तावत् एव = that much only.

questions.q: By the rule of तावत् + एव → तावदेव, how is यावत् + एव (as much as) joined?
optionExplain: The त् does not stay unvoiced before a vowel; it becomes द्.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्, as तावत् + एव.
न्न् comes (optionally) from त् before a nasal, not before a vowel.
च्च् comes from त् before च, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: यावत् + एव = यावदेव, like तावत् + एव = तावदेव.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: तावत् + एव → तावदेव.

questions.q: By unit 225, how many cupped handfuls of rajas are there in women?
optionExplain: Two is said of breast milk in unit 226.
Half is said of śukra in unit 223.
Right: अञ्जल्यश्चतस्रः: four cupped handfuls.
Eight is not the measure given for rajas.
questions.explain: स्त्रीणां रजसः अञ्जल्यः चतस्रः: four añjali of rajas in women.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 225 to its meaning.
questions.explain: In women, four cupped handfuls of rajas.

questions.q: Complete unit 225: रजसोऽजल्यः (read …ञ्जल्यः) ____ (four, feminine). Type it in Devanagari or English letters (e.g. tri).
questions.explain: अञ्जल्यः चतस्रः: four cupped handfuls; चतस्रः is the feminine of 'four'.
questions.teaches: चतस्रः = four, feminine nominative plural, agreeing with अञ्जल्यः.

questions.q: Why is the numeral चतस्रः (four) feminine in unit 225?
optionExplain: स्त्रीणाम् is genitive; चतस्रः is nominative, so they do not agree.
रजसः is neuter genitive singular; it cannot agree with चतस्रः.
द्वौ in unit 226 is masculine, so not all are feminine.
Right: Both are feminine nominative plural; añjali is read feminine here.
questions.explain: चतस्रः (f. nom. pl.) agrees with अञ्जल्यः (f. nom. pl.).
questions.rule: A numeral agrees with its noun in gender, case and number.

questions.q: A learner renders unit 225 as: In women, four handfuls of semen. Which word of it is wrong?
optionExplain: Right: रजस् is rajas (menstrual blood, probably); semen is śukra (unit 223).
स्त्रीणाम् = of women, in women: right.
चतस्रः = four: right.
अञ्जल्यः = cupped handfuls: right.
questions.explain: The line is about rajas, not śukra.

questions.q: By the rule of रजसः + अ… → रजसोऽ…, how is शिष्यः + अयम् (this pupil) joined?
optionExplain: अः does not give आ; before अ it gives ओऽ.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked by ऽ, as रजसः + अ… → रजसोऽ….
The visarga is dropped like this only before vowels other than अ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: शिष्यः + अयम् = शिष्योऽयम्, like रजसः + अ… = रजसोऽ….
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ drops, marked ऽ: रजसः + अञ्जल्यः → रजसोऽञ्जल्यः.

questions.q: By unit 226, what number is given for breast milk (स्तन्य)?
optionExplain: Four is said of rajas in unit 225.
Half is said of śukra in unit 223.
Right: स्तन्यस्य द्वौ: of breast milk, two.
Countless is said of the srotas in unit 218.
questions.explain: स्तन्यस्य द्वौ: two of breast milk.

questions.q: What does स्तन्य mean in unit 226?
optionExplain: The breast is स्तन; स्तन्य is the milk of it.
That is rajas, in unit 225.
That is śukra, in unit 223.
Right: स्तन्य = what belongs to the breast (स्तन): breast milk.
questions.explain: स्तन्य = breast milk.

questions.q: Complete unit 226: स्तन्यस्य ____ (two). Type it in Devanagari or English letters (e.g. eka).
questions.explain: स्तन्यस्य द्वौ: of breast milk, two.
questions.teaches: द्वौ = two (masculine nominative dual).

questions.q: In unit 226, why is स्तन्यस्य in the genitive (-स्य)?
options: It names whose measure is given
It is the subject that acts
It names the place of the milk
It names who receives the milk
optionExplain: Right: स्तन्यस्य द्वौ: two (handfuls) of breast milk.
No verb and no action: the genitive names the substance.
A place would be locative (-ए); -स्य is genitive.
A receiver would be dative (-आय); -स्य is genitive.
questions.explain: The genitive names what the number measures: of breast milk.

questions.q: Which of these are true of unit 226?
options: It has a verb of its own
optionExplain: There is no verb in the line.
Right: स्तन्यस्य, of breast milk.
Right: द्वौ, two.
No measure word is printed; the data takes it as understood.
questions.explain: Unit 226 is only स्तन्यस्य द्वौ: breast milk, two.

questions.q: By the pattern of द्वौ (two, masculine dual), which new phrase means two hands (हस्त, masculine)?
optionExplain: द्वे is the feminine/neuter form; हस्त is masculine.
Right: Masculine द्वौ with the dual हस्तौ.
हस्ताः is plural; with two the noun is dual.
हस्तः is singular; with two the noun is dual.
questions.explain: द्वौ हस्तौ: two hands, masculine dual.
questions.teaches: द्वौ is the masculine nominative dual of 'two'; its noun is also dual: द्वौ हस्तौ.

questions.q: By unit 227, of what nature are 'both of these'?
options: Of the waste part of rasa
Of the heat of the body
Of the clear essence of rasa
optionExplain: प्रसाद is the clear essence, not a waste.
Heat (ऊष्मन्) is named in unit 222, not here.
Right: रसप्रसादात्मकम्: of the nature of rasa's clear essence.
Marrow is not named in unit 227; the line names rasa.
questions.explain: उभयमपि चैतद्रसप्रसादात्मकम्: both are of the nature of rasa's clear essence.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 227 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Both, as well, this, of the nature of rasa's clear essence, thus.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 227 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Both of these as well are of the nature of the clear essence of rasa.
questions.teaches: -आत्मक at the end of a compound means 'having X as its nature': रसप्रसादात्मक.

questions.q: Which split of चैतद्रसप्रसादात्मकम् is right?
optionExplain: अ + इ gives ए, not ऐ; and इतत् is not a word.
Neither चैत nor द्रस- is a word here.
An अ- here would give चैतदरस-, which is not printed.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ (चैतत्); त् before the voiced र becomes द्.
questions.explain: च (and) + एतत् (this) + रसप्रसादात्मकम् → चैतद्रसप्रसादात्मकम्.
questions.rule: अ + ए → ऐ; त् + voiced consonant → द्.

questions.q: A learner renders unit 227 as: Both of these are of the nature of the waste of rasa. Which word is wrong?
optionExplain: Right: प्रसाद is the clear essence, the refined part, not waste.
उभयम् = both: right.
-आत्मकम् = having the nature of: right.
रस is named in the compound: right.
questions.explain: रसप्रसाद = the clear essence of rasa.

questions.q: By the rule of च + एतत् → चैतत्, how is तत्र + एव (right there) joined?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ; अ + ए gives ऐ.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as च + एतत् → चैतत्.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + ए.
The ए is not lost; अ + ए gives ऐ.
questions.explain: तत्र + एव = तत्रैव, like च + एतत् = चैतत्.
questions.teaches: अ followed by ए joins as ऐ: च + एतत् → चैतत्.

questions.q: By unit 228, for whom is this measure given?
options: One who is still in the womb
optionExplain: Increase is not the state named; सम means balanced.
Wasting is not the state named; सम means balanced.
Right: समधातोः: of one with balanced dhātus.
The fetus is not named in unit 228.
questions.explain: समधातोः परिमाणमिदम्: this is the measure for one with balanced dhātus.
questions.rule: समधातु = one whose dhātus are balanced.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 228 to its meaning.
questions.explain: This is the measure for one whose dhātus are balanced.

questions.q: What kind of compound is समधातु in unit 228?
options: A dvandva: 'the even and the dhātu'
A tatpuruṣa: 'the dhātu of the even'
A bahuvrīhi: one whose dhātus are even
optionExplain: A dvandva would join two things as 'and'; here सम describes धातु.
No genitive link 'of the even' is meant; it describes a person.
समधातोः is one word with one ending.
Right: It describes a person by his dhātus: सम + धातु.
questions.explain: समधातु = he whose dhātus are सम (balanced): a bahuvrīhi.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi names someone by what he has: समधातु = one whose dhātus are balanced.

questions.q: In unit 228, what does इदम् (this) stand for?
optionExplain: Right: इदम् (n. nom. sg.) goes with परिमाणम् (n. nom. sg.).
No man is named; इदम् agrees with परिमाणम्.
शरीर is not in unit 228; इदम् goes with परिमाणम्.
धातु is masculine here; इदम् is neuter like परिमाणम्.
questions.explain: परिमाणम् इदम्: this (is) the measure.

questions.q: Which of these are true of unit 228?
options: It gives a new añjali number
optionExplain: No disease is named in unit 228.
No number is given in unit 228.
Right: परिमाणमिदम्, this is the measure.
Right: समधातोः, of one with balanced dhātus.
questions.explain: Unit 228 says only: this is the measure for one with balanced dhātus.

questions.q: By the pattern of परिमाणम् + इदम् → परिमाणमिदम्, how is वचनम् + इदम् (this word) joined?
optionExplain: The anusvāra stands for म् only before a consonant.
Right: A final म् before a vowel joins that vowel, as परिमाणम् + इदम्.
The म् is not lost; अ + इ → ए does not apply across म्.
म् + इ keeps the short इ; nothing lengthens it.
questions.explain: वचनम् + इदम् = वचनमिदम्, like परिमाणम् + इदम् = परिमाणमिदम्.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → the म् joins the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel joins it: परिमाणम् + इदम् → परिमाणमिदम्.

questions.q: By unit 229, by what should increase and decrease be discerned?
options: By the season of the year
optionExplain: The line names signs (लक्षणैः), not a bone count.
No season is named; the line says by signs.
Right: यथास्वं लक्षणैः: each by its own signs.
The line says by signs (लक्षणैः), not by a report.
questions.explain: Increase and decrease are discerned, each by its own signs.
questions.rule: यथास्वं लक्षणैः = each by its own signs.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 229 (split out of sandhi) in the line's order.
questions.explain: Therefore increase and decrease, each by its own signs, one should discern; and corporeal and non-corporeal entities. The doubtful word is left out.
questions.rule: अतः → वृद्धिक्षयौ → यथास्वम् → लक्षणैः → विभावयेत् → मूर्तामूर्तान् भावान्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 229 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Increase and decrease are judged by signs; the entities are corporeal and non-corporeal.
questions.teaches: मूर्त = having form, अमूर्त = formless: the line joins them in one compound, मूर्तामूर्त (अ + अ → आ).

questions.q: Which split of लक्षणैर्विभावयेत् in unit 229 is right?
optionExplain: ए before व stays: that would print लक्षणे विभावयेत्, with no ऐर्.
लक्षणैर is not a form; the र् comes from the visarga of लक्षणैः.
र्विभावयेत् is not a word; the verb is विभावयेत्.
Right: Visarga after ऐ, before the voiced व, becomes र्: लक्षणैर्विभावयेत्.
questions.explain: लक्षणैः (by signs) + विभावयेत् (one should discern): ऐः before a voiced sound → ऐर्.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ, before a voiced sound → र्.

questions.q: A student reads unit 229. Which statements fit the line?
options: Increase and decrease are each judged by their own signs
It gives a new measure for each liquid
It also speaks of corporeal and non-corporeal entities
It names the doṣa that increases first
optionExplain: Right: यथास्वं लक्षणैः.
No measure is given; the line speaks of signs.
Right: मूर्तामूर्तान् भावान्.
No doṣa is named in the line.
questions.explain: Increase and decrease by their own signs; also corporeal and non-corporeal entities.

questions.q: By the rule of अतः + वृद्धिक्षयौ → अतो वृद्धिक्षयौ, how is ततः + वदति (then he speaks, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant (व) becomes ओ, as अतः → अतो before वृद्धि.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
Losing the visarga and keeping आ belongs to आः, not to अः.
Visarga becomes श् before च or छ, not before व.
questions.explain: ततः + वदति = ततो वदति, like अतः + वृद्धिक्षयौ = अतो वृद्धिक्षयौ.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: अतः + वृद्धिक्षयौ → अतो वृद्धिक्षयौ.

questions.q: What does तद्यथा (unit 230) do?
optionExplain: The chapter closes at unit 241, not here.
Right: The data: a formula introducing examples.
No teacher is named in it.
No measure is given; it has two words only.
questions.explain: तद्यथा = namely: examples follow.

questions.q: What does तद्यथा mean?
options: Thus ends, so it is said
optionExplain: Therefore would be अतः or तस्मात्.
In the same way would be तथा.
Right: तत् (that) + यथा (as): that is as follows.
A closing 'thus' is इति.
questions.explain: तद्यथा = namely, as follows.

questions.q: तद्यथा = तत् + ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तद्यथा = तत् (that) + यथा (as).
questions.teaches: यथा = as; with तत् it means 'that (is) as follows', namely.

questions.q: Which split of तद्यथा is right?
optionExplain: There is no word तद with a final अ here; the pronoun is तत्.
That would join as तदथा, with no य.
तद्य and था are not the words of this line.
Right: त् before the voiced य becomes द्.
questions.explain: तत् (that) + यथा (as): त् → द् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 230 are right?
options: It is a prose formula, not a verse
Its तत् is the neuter pronoun 'that'
optionExplain: No verb occurs in it.
Right: the unit is prose.
Right: the data gives तत् n. nom. sg.
The examples follow; this line names none.
questions.explain: A two-word prose formula: तत् (that) + यथा (as).
questions.rule: तद्यथा = तत् + यथा, prose, no verb.

questions.q: By the rule of तत् + यथा → तद्यथा, how is भगवत् + गीता joined (a new example)?
optionExplain: Right: त् before the voiced ग becomes द्, as in तत् + यथा.
त् must become द् before the voiced ग.
न् would come before a nasal, not before ग.
त् does not copy the next consonant here.
questions.explain: भगवत् + गीता = भगवद्गीता, like तत् + यथा = तद्यथा.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a voiced sound becomes द्: तत् + यथा → तद्यथा.

questions.q: By unit 231, which of these is named in the second list, with vāyu?
optionExplain: Not named; the list is वायु, बुद्धि, स्मृति.
Right: वायुबुद्धिस्मृत्यादीन्: wind, intellect, memory and the like.
Not named; the list is वायु, बुद्धि, स्मृति.
Not named; the list is वायु, बुद्धि, स्मृति.
questions.explain: The second list: wind, intellect, memory and the like.

questions.q: Put these items of unit 231 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Flesh, ear and the like, malas; then wind, intellect, memory and the like.
questions.rule: मांस → कर्ण → मल → वायु → बुद्धि → स्मृति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 231 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The malas of flesh, ear and the like; wind, intellect, memory and the like.
questions.teaches: आदि at the end of a list = 'and the like': the list is left open.

questions.q: Which split of स्मृत्यादींश्च in unit 231 is right?
optionExplain: स्मृत्य is not a word; the य् comes from the इ of स्मृति.
आदीः + च would give आदीश्च, with no anusvāra.
Right: इ + आ → या; न् before च → ंश्च.
आदीम् + च would give आदीं च, with no श्.
questions.explain: स्मृति (memory) + आदीन् (and the like) + च (and).
questions.rule: इ + unlike vowel → य्; न् + च → ंश्च.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 231 as the data reads it?
options: The line has its own main verb
The listed items are in the accusative plural
It says vāyu here is the doṣa Vāta
optionExplain: No verb is printed; the data takes the items as objects of विभावयेत् in unit 229.
Right: both compounds end in -आन्/-ईन्, acc. pl.
The data: whether doṣa or plain wind is not stated.
Right: मांसकर्णादि..., स्मृत्यादीन्: 'and the like'.
questions.explain: Two open lists in the accusative plural; no verb in the line.
questions.rule: -आदि = and the like; -आन्/-ईन् = m. acc. pl.

questions.q: By the rule of आदीन् + च → आदींश्च, how is देवान् + च (and the gods, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: न् before च is not left as it is; it takes ंश्.
The nasal is not lost; it stays as anusvāra.
A श् is added between the anusvāra and च.
Right: न् before च becomes anusvāra with श् added, as आदीन् + च → आदींश्च.
questions.explain: देवान् + च = देवांश्च, like आदीन् + च = आदींश्च.
questions.teaches: A final न् before च becomes anusvāra and a श् is added: आदीन् + च → आदींश्च.

questions.q: By unit 232, who read (recite)?
options: The author, in his own words
optionExplain: Right: धान्वन्तरीयाः: those belonging to or following Dhanvantari.
The line names one group, the Dhanvantari followers.
The verb is plural and names others: धान्वन्तरीयाः.
No grammarians are named.
questions.explain: The followers of Dhanvantari read (recite).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 232 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The followers of Dhanvantari, on the other hand, read.

questions.q: In धान्वन्तरीय, what does the ending -ईय add to the name Dhanvantari?
optionExplain: -ईय does not mean opposed.
Right: The data: belonging to or following Dhanvantari.
-ईय says nothing of time.
-ईय does not mean teacher.
questions.explain: धान्वन्तरीय = belonging to or following Dhanvantari.
questions.teaches: -ईय after a name = belonging to, following; the first vowel is lengthened: धन्वन्तरि → धान्वन्तरीय.

questions.q: What form is पठन्ति in unit 232?
optionExplain: That would be पठति; -अन्ति is the plural.
That would be पठन्तु.
Right: The data: 3 pl. present of √पठ्.
That would be अपठन्.
questions.explain: पठन्ति = they read (3 pl. present), agreeing with धान्वन्तरीयाः.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 232 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The followers of Dhanvantari, on the other hand, read.

questions.q: By the pattern of धान्वन्तरीयाः, what does पाणिनीयाः mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: -ईय does not name a teacher.
-ईय does not mean opposed.
-ईय says nothing of time.
Right: Name + -ईय = belonging to, following, as धन्वन्तरि → धान्वन्तरीय.
questions.explain: पाणिनीयाः = followers of Pāṇini, like धान्वन्तरीयाः = followers of Dhanvantari.
questions.teaches: -ईय makes 'belonging to, following': धान्वन्तरीयाः = the followers of Dhanvantari.

questions.q: By unit 233, how are the doṣas, dhātus and malas described?
optionExplain: Right: नित्यमेव च चला दोषधातुमलाः: always unsteady.
The line says चलाः, unsteady, not fixed.
Bodies are called विलक्षण, dissimilar.
Nothing is said of sight; they are unsteady.
questions.explain: The doṣas, dhātus and malas are always unsteady.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 233 in the line's order.
questions.explain: For bodies are dissimilar, and always unsteady are the doṣas, dhātus and malas.
questions.rule: विलक्षणानि हि → शरीराणि → नित्यमेव च → चला → दोषधातुमलाः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 233 to its meaning.
questions.explain: For bodies are dissimilar, and the doṣas, dhātus and malas always unsteady.
questions.teaches: हि = for: it marks the line as a reason.

questions.q: Why is चलाः printed चला before दोषधातुमलाः in unit 233?
options: The print lost its visarga by a slip of the press
Regular sandhi: आः loses ः before द
The word is a feminine singular, not a plural
Visarga turns into र् before द
optionExplain: The data: regular sandhi before द, not a print slip.
Right: आः drops its visarga before a voiced sound (the data: regular sandhi).
The data: m. nom. pl., agreeing with दोषधातुमलाः.
र् comes after vowels other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: चलाः + दोष... → चला दोष...: आः before a voiced sound drops the visarga.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 233?
options: Bodies are all alike in their signs
The doṣas, dhātus and malas are always unsteady
हि gives the line as a reason
The dhātus are said to be fixed in amount
optionExplain: विलक्षणानि: bodies are dissimilar.
Right: नित्यमेव च चलाः.
Right: हि = for.
The line calls them unsteady (चलाः).
questions.explain: Bodies are dissimilar; the doṣas, dhātus and malas are always unsteady; हि = for.

questions.q: By the rule of चलाः + दोष... → चला दोष..., how is देवाः + गच्छन्ति (the gods go, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः, not from आः.
र् comes after vowels other than अ/आ.
Right: आः before a voiced sound drops the visarga, as चलाः → चला.
श् comes before च or छ, not before ग.
questions.explain: देवाः + गच्छन्ति = देवा गच्छन्ति, like चलाः + दोष... = चला दोष....
questions.teaches: आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga: चलाः + दोषधातुमलाः → चला दोषधातुमलाः.

questions.q: By unit 234, the evenness of what cannot be specified by measure?
options: Of the bones and joints alone
Of the pores of the body hair
optionExplain: Flesh is the model whose measure is given (मांसादिवत्).
Bones are not named; the line names water (उदक) and the others.
Not named in this line.
Right: उदकादीनामपि समत्वम्: the evenness even of water and the others.
questions.explain: The evenness of water and the others cannot be given by measure.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 234 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Therefore the evenness even of water and the others, as for flesh and the rest, by measure, is impossible to specify.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 234 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Therefore the evenness of water and the others is impossible to specify by measure.
questions.teaches: -तुम् makes the infinitive 'to ...': निर्देष्टुम् = to specify; with अशक्यम्, 'impossible to specify'.

questions.q: In unit 234, how does मांसादिवत् (like flesh and the rest) work?
options: Flesh and the rest are the model whose measure is given
Flesh and the rest also cannot be given by any measure
Water is measured in the very same way as the flesh
Flesh is named as the cause of the evenness of water
optionExplain: Right: The data: in the way of flesh and the rest, whose measure is given.
-वत् compares with flesh, whose measure is given (data note).
The line says this is impossible (अशक्यम्).
-वत् means like; no cause is named.
questions.explain: मांसादिवत् = as for flesh and the rest, whose measure is given; for water and the others it is impossible.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 234?
options: तस्मात् marks it as a consequence
The evenness of the liquids can be stated by measure
It names the bones as the thing measured
optionExplain: Right: तस्मात् = therefore.
The line says it is impossible (अशक्यम्).
Bones are not named; flesh and water are.
Right: the data gives inf. of निर्-√दिश्.
questions.explain: Therefore it is impossible to specify the evenness of water and the others by measure.

questions.q: By the pattern of निर्देष्टुम् अशक्यम्, what does वक्तुम् अशक्यम् mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: The अ- of अशक्य negates: impossible.
Right: Infinitive -तुम् + अशक्यम् = impossible to ..., as निर्देष्टुम् अशक्यम्.
Having said would be उक्त्वा, a gerund; वक्तुम् is the infinitive.
No agent noun here; वक्तुम् is 'to say'.
questions.explain: वक्तुम् अशक्यम् = impossible to say, like निर्देष्टुम् अशक्यम् = impossible to specify.
questions.teaches: Infinitive -तुम् + अशक्यम् = impossible to ...: निर्देष्टुम् अशक्यम् = impossible to specify.

questions.q: By unit 235, by what means should one judge?
options: By direct measure of each dhātu
By weighing each liquid on a scale
optionExplain: केवलम्: only by inference; no measure is named.
No weighing is named; only inference.
Right: स्वास्थ्यमात्रेणानुमानतो लक्षयेत्: by inference, through mere health.
No one is asked; one judges by inference.
questions.explain: Only by inference through mere health.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 235 (split out of sandhi) in the line's order.
questions.explain: Only through mere health, by inference, one should judge: thus (the reading ends).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 235 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Only through mere health, by inference, one should judge.
questions.teaches: -मात्र at the end of a compound = mere, nothing but: स्वास्थ्यमात्र = mere health.

questions.q: Which split of स्वास्थ्यमात्रेणानुमानतो in unit 235 is right?
optionExplain: नुमानतः is not a word; the word is अनुमानतः.
ए + अ would give मात्रेऽनुमानतः, not मात्रेणा.
अः + अ would give ओऽ: मात्रेणोऽनुमानतः.
Right: अ + अ → आ; अः before the voiced ल → ओ.
questions.explain: स्वास्थ्यमात्रेण (through mere health) + अनुमानतः (by inference): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 235?
options: The object of लक्षयेत् is printed in the line
It gives a measure in cupped handfuls (अञ्जलि)
optionExplain: It is not printed (data note).
Right: अनुमानतः लक्षयेत्.
Right: the data says so.
No measure is given; only inference.
questions.explain: One judges only by inference through mere health; इति closes the reading.

questions.q: By the rule of लक्षयेत् + इति → लक्षयेदिति, how is भवेत् + इति (a new example) joined?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as लक्षयेत् + इति → लक्षयेदिति.
त् before a vowel becomes द्; it does not stay त्.
य् comes from इ before a vowel, not from त्.
द् is not doubled before a vowel.
questions.explain: भवेत् + इति = भवेदिति, like लक्षयेत् + इति = लक्षयेदिति.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: लक्षयेत् + इति → लक्षयेदिति.

questions.q: By unit 236, what do all the parts come to?
optionExplain: Not said; they become countless (असंख्येयता).
Right: असंख्येयतां यान्ति: they go to countlessness.
Not said; division makes them countless.
No number is given; they become countless.
questions.explain: All the parts come to be countless.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 236 (split out of sandhi) in the line's order.
questions.explain: But all the parts, by division into atoms, because of extreme subtlety, go to countlessness.
questions.rule: सर्वे एव → तु अवयवाः → परमाणुभेदेन → अतिसौक्ष्म्यात् → असंख्येयताम् → यान्ति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 236 to its meaning.
questions.explain: All the parts, divided into atoms, through extreme subtlety become countless.
questions.teaches: सौक्ष्म्य = subtlety, the abstract noun of सूक्ष्म (subtle, minute); अति- = extreme.

questions.q: Which split of the printed सर्वएव in unit 236 is right?
optionExplain: अ + ए would join as ऐ: सर्वैव.
म् before a vowel joins it: सर्वमेव.
Right: ए before a vowel becomes अय्; the य् drops, leaving सर्व एव (printed without the gap).
आः before a vowel drops ः but keeps आ: सर्वा एव.
questions.explain: सर्वे (all) + एव (indeed): ए + vowel → अ(य्), य् dropped.
questions.rule: ए + vowel → अय्, य् usually dropped.

questions.q: Which reasons does unit 236 give for the parts becoming countless?
optionExplain: Not said; the line speaks of extreme subtlety.
Right: परमाणुभेदेन.
Right: अतिसौक्ष्म्यात्.
Not given here as the reason.
questions.explain: By division into atoms, because of extreme subtlety, the parts become countless.

questions.q: By the rule of तु + अवयवाः → त्ववयवाः, how is मधु + अत्र (honey here, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel, not from उ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from उ + अ.
Right: उ before अ becomes व्, as तु + अवयवाः → त्ववयवाः.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like तु + अवयवाः = त्ववयवाः.
questions.teaches: उ before an unlike vowel becomes व्: तु + अवयवाः → त्ववयवाः.

questions.q: By unit 237, what is the cause of the union and separation of the atoms?
optionExplain: Right: कर्मप्रेरितो वायुः कारणम्: wind, impelled by action, is the cause.
The line names वायु, not heat.
The line names वायु, not water.
The line names वायु, not earth.
questions.explain: Wind, impelled by action, is the cause.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 237 to its meaning.
questions.explain: In the union and separation of the atoms, wind impelled by action is the cause.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 237 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of those, in the union and separation, of the atoms, impelled by action, wind, the cause.
questions.rule: तेषां → संयोगविभागे → परमाणूनां → कर्मप्रेरितो → वायुः → कारणं.
questions.teaches: कर्मप्रेरितः = impelled by action: a tatpuruṣa whose first part names the agent (by).

questions.q: By unit 237, which pair of opposite events does wind cause?
options: Birth and death of the body
optionExplain: Not named; the line says संयोग and विभाग.
Right: संयोगविभागे: in union and separation.
Not named; the line says संयोग and विभाग.
Not named; the line says संयोग and विभाग.
questions.explain: Wind is the cause in the union and separation of the atoms.

questions.q: By unit 237, what stands first in the chain that ends in union and separation?
options: The atoms, which impel the wind
optionExplain: The atoms are joined and separated; action impels the wind.
The wind is कर्मप्रेरित, impelled by action.
Right: कर्मप्रेरितः: the wind is impelled by action.
Union is the result, not the impeller.
questions.explain: Action → wind → union and separation of the atoms.

questions.q: By the pattern of कर्मप्रेरितः (impelled by action), what does वायुप्रेरितः mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: प्रेरित is a past participle, 'impelled', not 'impelling'.
It is not a dvandva of two things.
Nothing in the compound negates.
Right: The first part names the agent: वायु + प्रेरित = impelled by wind.
questions.explain: वायुप्रेरितः = impelled by wind, like कर्मप्रेरितः = impelled by action.
questions.teaches: In a tatpuruṣa like कर्मप्रेरित, the first part names the agent: impelled by action.

questions.q: By unit 238, which two ends do the two datives of the line (बन्धाय, मोक्षाय) name?
optionExplain: Right: बन्धाय मोक्षाय: for bondage, for liberation.
Not named; the line says बन्धाय and मोक्षाय.
Not named; the line says बन्धाय and मोक्षाय.
Not named; the line says बन्धाय and मोक्षाय.
questions.explain: It leads to bondage or to liberation.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 238 in the line's order (the doubtful last word is left out).
questions.explain: This, by distinction of parts and by division, being understood, for bondage, for liberation.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 238 to its meaning.
questions.explain: This, understood by division, leads to bondage or liberation.
questions.teaches: बन्ध and मोक्ष are a pair of opposites in this line: bondage and liberation.

questions.q: What case is बन्धाय in unit 238?
optionExplain: That would be बन्धेन.
Right: -आय is the dative singular of an अ-stem.
That would be बन्धात्.
That would be बन्धे.
questions.explain: बन्धाय = for bondage (dative), like मोक्षाय = for liberation.

questions.q: What does the form गृह्यमाणम् in unit 238 express?
optionExplain: Active would be गृह्णत्; गृह्यमाण is passive (data).
The past participle would be गृहीत.
Right: The data: pass. pres. part. of √ग्रह्.
That would be a gerundive such as ग्राह्य.
questions.explain: गृह्यमाणम् = being grasped, being understood.

questions.q: By the pattern of बन्धाय (for bondage), which form of the new word सुख (happiness) is its dative?
optionExplain: Instrumental, 'by happiness'.
Ablative, 'from happiness'.
Locative, 'in happiness'.
Right: अ-stem dative singular in -आय, like बन्धाय.
questions.explain: सुखाय = for happiness, like बन्धाय = for bondage.
questions.teaches: The dative singular of an अ-stem ends in -आय and means 'for': बन्धाय, मोक्षाय.

questions.q: What does भवति चात्र (unit 239) do?
optionExplain: Right: The data: a formula introducing a verse.
The colophon comes at unit 241.
No teacher is named.
No measure is given.
questions.explain: The formula introduces a verse.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 239 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And here there is (a verse).

questions.q: चात्र = च + ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चात्र = च (and) + अत्र (here).
questions.teaches: अत्र = here, on this matter.

questions.q: Which split of चात्र is right?
optionExplain: चा is not a word; the word is च.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र = चात्र.
आत्र is not a word.
ए + अ would give चेऽत्र.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 239 are right?
options: It is printed as one run-together word
It is itself a metrical verse
It names what the verse is about
It contains the verb भवति, 'there is'
optionExplain: Right: भवतिचात्र.
It is a prose formula.
It has no stated object.
Right: 3 sg. present of √भू.
questions.explain: A run-together prose formula with the verb भवति.

questions.q: By the rule of च + अत्र → चात्र, how is न + अस्ति (is not, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: Two short अ join as long आ.
ए comes from अ + इ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अत्र → चात्र.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.teaches: अ + अ join as long आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.

questions.q: By unit 240, what is said of one who knows the body part by part?
options: He falls ill in no season of the year
He needs no help from a physician
He can count every single atom
He does not turn to harm by delusion
optionExplain: Illness and seasons are not named.
No physician is named.
Atoms are not named in the verse.
Right: अहितेषु स मोहेन न कदाचित्प्रवर्तते.
questions.explain: He never engages in what is harmful through delusion.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of the verse of unit 240 in order.
questions.explain: Thus who knows the body part by part, he through delusion never engages in harmful things.
questions.rule: इति सर्वावयवशो → यो जानाति कलेवरं → अहितेषु स → मोहेनन → कदाचित्प्रवर्त्तते.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 240 to its meaning.
questions.explain: He who knows the body part by part never engages in the harmful through delusion.
questions.teaches: न कदाचित् = never: न (not) + कदाचित् (ever).

questions.q: Which split of the printed मोहेनन in unit 240 is right?
optionExplain: Right: Two words run together in the print: through delusion + not.
नन is not a word; the negation is न.
अ + अ would join as आ: मोहेनान.
एनन is not a word, and अ + ए would give ऐ.
questions.explain: मोहेन (through delusion) + न (not), printed without a space.

questions.q: Which statements fit the verse of unit 240?
options: It names the harmful things one by one
The first line holds the relative clause with यः
It says knowledge of the body cures every disease
The second line holds the main clause with सः
optionExplain: It does not say which harmful things are meant.
Right: यो जानाति कलेवरम्.
Nothing is said of curing.
Right: स ... न कदाचित्प्रवर्तते.
questions.explain: यः ... जानाति (first line) → सः ... न प्रवर्तते (second line).

questions.q: By the pattern of न कदाचित् in unit 240, what does न कदाचिदनृतं वदेत् mean (a new example)?
options: One should speak untruth only once
No one has ever spoken untruth
optionExplain: कदाचित् with न means never, not sometimes.
Right: न कदाचित् = never; वदेत् = should speak.
Nothing here means once.
वदेत् is optative, 'should speak', not a past fact.
questions.explain: न कदाचिदनृतं वदेत् = one should never speak untruth, like न कदाचित् प्रवर्तते = never engages.
questions.teaches: न with कदाचित् (ever) means never: स मोहेन न कदाचित्प्रवर्तते.

questions.q: By unit 241, what is chapter five named?
optionExplain: That is the name of chapter four.
That is the name of chapter three.
Right: इत्यङ्गविभागो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः.
That is the name of chapter two.
questions.explain: The colophon names the chapter Aṅgavibhāga, division of the parts of the body.
questions.rule: अङ्गविभाग = division of the parts of the body.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 241 (split out of sandhi) in their order.
questions.explain: Thus, Aṅgavibhāga, named, fifth, chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 241 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Thus the fifth chapter, named division of the parts of the body.
questions.teaches: अङ्गविभाग = अङ्ग + विभाग: the division of the parts of the body, the theme of the chapter.

questions.q: Which split of इत्यंगविभागो in unit 241 is right?
optionExplain: इत्य is not a word; the य् comes from the इ of इति.
आ before न stays आ; it would print इत्यङ्गविभागा.
ए + अ would give इतेऽङ्ग..., not इत्यङ्ग.
Right: इ + अ → य; अः before the voiced न of नाम → ओ.
questions.explain: इति (thus) + अङ्गविभागः (division of the parts): इ + अ → य; अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.rule: इ + unlike vowel → य्; अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: In unit 241 the word for 'fifth' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पञ्चमः = fifth; before अध्यायः it is printed पंचमोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: पञ्चम = fifth; ऽ marks the lost अ of अध्यायः.

questions.q: By the rule of पञ्चमः + अध्यायः → पञ्चमोऽध्यायः, how is रामः + अपि (Rāma too, a new example) joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः + अ → ओ, and ऽ marks the lost अ, as पञ्चमः + अध्यायः.
आ with a gap comes from आः before a vowel, not from अः.
अः drops to अ with a gap only before vowels other than अ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: रामः + अपि = रामोऽपि, like पञ्चमः + अध्यायः = पञ्चमोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the following अ is marked ऽ: पञ्चमः + अध्यायः → पञ्चमोऽध्यायः.

questions.q: By unit 1, what will chapter 6 explain?
optionExplain: Bones are not named in unit 1; the line names सिरा (vessel).
Right: सिराविभागं ... व्याख्यास्यामः: we shall explain the division of the sirās.
Marmas are not named in unit 1; the line names सिरा (vessel).
Constitution is not named in unit 1; the line names सिरा.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily division of the sirās.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the words of unit 1 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Now therefore, the division of the sirās, bodily, we shall explain.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily division of the sirās.
questions.teaches: सिरा = vessel (veins and other blood-carrying vessels, probable); the term is kept in Sanskrit.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Which split of अथातः in unit 1 is right?
optionExplain: अः before अ would give अथोऽतः, with ओ and avagraha.
No vowel would merge: अथ + तः would stay अथतः.
Right: अ + अ → आ: अथ + अतः → अथातः.
ए before अ would give अथेऽतः, with ए kept.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore): अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: In unit 1, what form is व्याख्यास्यामः?
options: Past, third person plural: they explained
Command, second person: you must explain
Future, third person singular: he will explain
Future, first person plural: we shall explain
optionExplain: The data labels it future, first person: we shall explain.
The data labels it future, first person: we shall explain.
The ending -आमः is first person plural: we.
Right: The data labels it 1 pl. fut. of vi-ā-√khyā.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain (1 pl. future).
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By the rule of अथातः, how is न + अस्ति (is not) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as अथ + अतः → अथातः.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
The two vowels merge into आ; neither simply drops.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like अथ + अतः = अथातः.
questions.teaches: Two short अ vowels merge into long आ: अथ + अतः → अथातः.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 2, how many root-sirās (mūlasirā) are there?
optionExplain: दश is ten; seven hundred is the count of the branches (unit 4).
Right: दश मूलसिरा: ten root-sirās.
दश is ten, not four.
Sixteen is the count of unit 6, not of the root-sirās.
questions.explain: There are ten root-sirās, bound to the heart.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the words of unit 2 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Ten, root-sirās, bound to the heart, to all limbs and sub-limbs ojas, carry.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word of unit 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Ten root-sirās, bound to the heart, carry ojas to all the limbs and sub-limbs.
questions.teaches: ओजस् is a doctrinal term (vital essence) kept in Sanskrit; नयन्ति takes both what is carried and where.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 2, to what are the ten root-sirās bound?
optionExplain: The head is not named in unit 2; हृदय is the heart.
The back is not named in unit 2; हृदय is the heart.
Right: हृदयप्रतिबद्धाः: bound to the heart.
The thighs are not named in unit 2; हृदय is the heart.
questions.explain: The root-sirās are bound to the heart.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 2 and its data?
options: Ojas goes to all the limbs and sub-limbs
Unit 2 says the sirās number seven hundred
optionExplain: Ojas is kept as a doctrinal term (vital essence), not blood.
Right: ...ओजो नयन्ति: they carry ojas.
Right: सर्वाङ्गप्रत्यङ्गानि are where it is carried.
Seven hundred is the count of unit 4, not unit 2.
questions.explain: Ten root-sirās, bound to the heart, carry ojas to all the limbs and sub-limbs.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By the rule of मूलसिरा before ह, how is बालाः + हसन्ति (the boys laugh) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
स् comes from a visarga before त or थ, not before ह.
Right: After आ, a visarga drops before a voiced sound such as ह, as मूलसिराः → मूलसिरा.
questions.explain: बालाः + हसन्ति = बाला हसन्ति, like मूलसिराः + हृदय... = मूलसिरा हृदय...
questions.rule: आः before a voiced sound: the visarga drops.
questions.teaches: After आ, the visarga drops before a voiced sound: मूलसिराः हृदय... → मूलसिरा हृदय...
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 3, what is bound to those (the root-sirās)?
optionExplain: Right: शारीरचेष्टाः: the activities (चेष्टा) of the body.
Bones are not named in unit 3; चेष्टाः are activities.
Joints are not named in unit 3; चेष्टाः are activities.
Hairs are not named in unit 3; चेष्टाः are activities.
questions.explain: For the activities of the body are bound to those.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the words of unit 3 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Bound to those, for, the activities of the body.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: For the activities of the body are bound to those.
questions.teaches: तत् is understood as the ten root-sirās of unit 2; the referent is not printed in unit 3.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: What does हि add to unit 3?
optionExplain: 'Not' is न, which does not occur in unit 3.
Right: The data glosses हि as 'for': the line gives a reason.
'Also' is अपि, which does not occur in unit 3.
'Among those' is तत्र, which does not occur in unit 3.
questions.explain: हि = for: the activities of the body are bound to them.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Why is तत्प्रतिबद्धा printed without a visarga in unit 3?
options: The word is singular, so it ends without a visarga
Before ह any visarga drops, whatever vowel is before it
After आ, a visarga drops before a voiced sound like ह
The visarga has moved onto हि as its first sound
optionExplain: The data labels it f. nom. pl., like चेष्टाः.
अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ; it does not just drop.
Right: Data note: tatpratibaddhāḥ before h-, regular sandhi.
हि has no visarga; the visarga simply drops after आ.
questions.explain: तत्प्रतिबद्धाः + हि → तत्प्रतिबद्धा हि: आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga.
questions.rule: आः before a voiced sound: the visarga drops.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By the join in तत्प्रतिबद्धा, how is तत् + पुत्रः (his son) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: त् becomes द् before a voiced sound; प is not voiced.
त् becomes च् before च or छ (and च्छ with श), not before प.
त् may become न् before a nasal such as न or म (optional), not before प.
Right: त् stays त् before प, as तत् + प्रतिबद्धाः → तत्प्रतिबद्धाः.
questions.explain: तत् + पुत्रः = तत्पुत्रः, like तत् + प्रतिबद्धाः = तत्प्रतिबद्धाः.
questions.rule: त् before an unvoiced stop like प: no change.
questions.teaches: त् before an unvoiced consonant such as प stays त्: तत् + प्रतिबद्धाः → तत्प्रतिबद्धाः.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 4, how many do the sirās become as they branch?
optionExplain: Right: सप्त शतानि भवन्ति: they become seven hundred.
Four hundred is the share of the limbs (unit 5).
सप्त शतानि is seven hundreds, not one.
शतानि are hundreds: seven hundred, not seventy.
questions.explain: Branching out, the sirās become seven hundred.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the measures of unit 4 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Two aṅgulas, an aṅgula, half an aṅgula, a yava, half a yava: the line's order.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word of unit 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Having gone two aṅgulas ... half a yava, they become seven hundred.
questions.rule: अङ्गुल, यव, गत्वा, सप्त शतानि, भवन्ति.
questions.teaches: अङ्गुल (finger-breadth) and यव (barley-grain) are measures; the data does not convert them.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Which split of तास्तु in unit 4 is right?
optionExplain: त् + त would give तात्तु, with no स्.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: ताः + तु → तास्तु.
ए before अ would give तेऽस्तु, with ए kept.
स्तु is not a word here; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: ताः (those) + तु (but): visarga before त → स्.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 4 and its data?
options: Two aṅgulas comes first among the measures
The data converts the aṅgula into centimetres
The line says the measures are thicknesses
Half a yava is the last measure named
optionExplain: Right: द्व्यङ्गुलम् opens the list.
The measures are not converted.
The line does not say whether length or thickness.
Right: यवार्द्धं च closes the list.
questions.explain: Two aṅgulas, an aṅgula, half an aṅgula, a yava, half a yava; the measures are not converted.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By the pattern of गत्वा (having gone, from √गम्), which form of √कृ means having done?
optionExplain: करोति is a present verb: he does.
कृतम् is a past participle: done.
Right: -त्वा forms the absolutive, 'having ...ed', as √गम् → गत्वा.
कर्तुम् is an infinitive: to do.
questions.explain: √कृ → कृत्वा (having done), like √गम् → गत्वा (having gone).
questions.teaches: -त्वा forms the absolutive: an action finished before the main verb (गत्वा ... भवन्ति).
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 5, how many sirās are in the limbs (śākhā)?
optionExplain: Seven hundred is the whole count (unit 4).
चतुःशती is a set of four hundreds, not forty.
Ten is the count of the root-sirās (unit 2).
Right: चतुःशती शाखासु: four hundred in the limbs.
questions.explain: Of the seven hundred, four hundred are in the limbs.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the words of unit 5 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of them, four hundred, in the limbs.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of them, four hundred are in the limbs.
questions.teaches: शाखा, literally 'branch', means the four limbs (arms and legs) in this body-division (standard).
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: What does the ending of शाखासु in unit 5 show?
optionExplain: Right: -आसु is the locative plural of an आ-stem: in the limbs.
Of the limbs would be शाखानाम्.
By the limbs would be शाखाभिः.
In the limb would be शाखायाम्.
questions.explain: शाखासु = in the limbs.
questions.section: आरंभ: मूल सिराएँ व सात सौ सिराएँ

questions.q: By units 4 and 5, how many of the seven hundred are outside the limbs?
optionExplain: Four hundred are in the limbs, not outside them.
Right: 700 − 400 = 300; the data later splits them as 136 + 164.
