questions.explain: Sixteen are in the two sides.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 12 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Two each in the groins, and in the kaṭīkataruṇas, thus eight; sixteen in the sides; named pārśvasandhi.
questions.rule: वंक्षणयोः → कटीकतरुणयोश्च → इत्यष्टौ → षोडश पार्श्वयोः → पार्श्वसंधिसंज्ञां.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: How does unit 12 reach eight (अष्टौ)?
options: Two each in both groins and both kaṭīkataruṇas
Four in the two groins and four in the two sides
Eight in each one of the two groins
Two each in the two sides and in the back as well
optionExplain: Right: द्वे द्वे वङ्क्षणयोः कटीकतरुणयोश्च: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.
The sides are counted apart: sixteen.
द्वे द्वे is two each, not eight each.
The back is not named in unit 12.
questions.explain: Two each in the two groins and in the two kaṭīkataruṇas: eight.
questions.teaches: इति closes a list and the total follows: द्वे द्वे ... इत्यष्टौ = thus eight.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which split of इत्यष्टौ in unit 12 is right?
optionExplain: अः before अ would give इतोऽष्टौ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + अष्टौ → इत्यष्टौ.
ए before अ would give इतेऽष्टौ.
अ + अ would give इत्याष्टौ, with आ.
questions.explain: इति (thus) + अष्टौ (eight): इ + अ → य.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 12 and its data?
options: Printed शखतो is a clear Sanskrit word
The second line prints its own verb
Sixteen are in the two sides
In each side one goes upward, named pārśvasandhi
optionExplain: It is not a word; शस्त्रतः is only conjectural.
It is elliptical: no verb is printed.
Right: षोडश पार्श्वयोः.
Right: ऊर्ध्वगाम् एकैकां पार्श्वसंधिसंज्ञां.
questions.explain: Sixteen in the sides, one upward in each named pārśvasandhi; शखतो is unclear; no verb in line two.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the join in कटीकतरुणयोश्चेति, how is न + इति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ई comes from इ + इ, not from अ + इ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + इ.
Right: अ + इ → ए, as च + इति → चेति.
य् comes from इ before a different vowel; here अ meets इ.
questions.explain: न + इति = नेति, like च + इति = चेति.
questions.teaches: अ + इ → ए: च + इति → चेति (in कटीकतरुणयोश्चेत्यष्टौ).
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 13, how many (sirās, understood) are in the back?
optionExplain: Thirty-two is the śroṇi's count (unit 11).
Sixteen is the count of the sides (unit 12).
चतुर्विंशति is four and twenty: twenty-four.
Right: चतुर्विंशतिः पृष्ठे: twenty-four in the back.
questions.explain: Twenty-four are in the back.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 13 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four + twenty = twenty-four, in the back.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 13, twenty-four are ____ (in the back). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पृष्ठे = in the back: चतुर्विंशतिः पृष्ठे.
questions.teaches: पृष्ठ (back) + -े (locative singular) = in the back.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which meaning fits the form पृष्ठे in unit 13?
optionExplain: Right: The data labels it n. loc. sg.: in the back.
Of the back would be पृष्ठस्य.
By the back would be पृष्ठेन.
The backs would be पृष्ठानि.
questions.explain: पृष्ठे = in the back.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By units 11 to 13, which region has the most (sirās, understood)?
optionExplain: The back has 24 (unit 13), fewer than the śroṇi's 32.
Right: Śroṇi 32 (unit 11) is more than back 24 or sides 16.
The sides have 16 (unit 12), fewer than 32.
The groins have two each (unit 12), fewer than 32.
questions.explain: Śroṇi 32, back 24, sides 16, groins 2 + 2.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the pattern of चतुर्विंशतिः (24), what does चतुस्त्रिंशत् mean in a new example?
optionExplain: The unit comes first in the word, but its value is added: 30 + 4.
The parts are added, not multiplied: 30 + 4.
Right: चतुर् (four) + त्रिंशत् (thirty) = 34, as चतुर् + विंशति = 24.
त्रिंशत् is thirty, not three: 30 + 4.
questions.teaches: A unit placed before a tens word is added to it: चतुर् + विंशति = 24.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 14, where do the two and two upward-going ones (sirās, understood) lie?
options: In the two groins and the hips
Above the meḍhra, in the belly
Within the heart, in the chest
On both sides of the spine
optionExplain: The groins belong to unit 12, not to the back's list.
Above the meḍhra is the belly's list (unit 16).
The heart is in the chest's list (unit 18).
Right: पृष्ठवंशमुभयतः: on both sides of the pṛṣṭhavaṃśa (spine).
questions.explain: Of the back's sirās, two and two go upward on both sides of the spine.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 14 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of them, on both sides of the spine, two and two, going upward; those are four.
questions.rule: तासां → पृष्ठवंशमुभयतो → द्वे द्वे → ऊर्ध्वगामिन्यौ → ताश्चतस्रः.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word of unit 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of them, on both sides of the spine, two going upward each; four in all.
questions.teaches: पृष्ठ (back) + वंश (ridge, bamboo) = पृष्ठवंश, the spine (standard); उभयतः takes it in the accusative.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which split of ताश्चतस्रः in unit 14 is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: ताः + चतस्रः → ताश्चतस्रः.
त् before च becomes च्: it would give ताच्चतस्रः.
श्चतस्रः is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
शतस्रः is not a word; the word is चतस्रः (four).
questions.explain: ताः (those) + चतस्रः (four): visarga before च → श्.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 14?
options: Two lie on each side of the spine
All four lie on one side of the spine
द्वे stays unjoined before ऊर्ध्व- because a dual in -ए does not join with a vowel
The unit says the four must not be pierced
optionExplain: Right: द्वे द्वे with उभयतः gives two on each side.
उभयतः means on both sides.
Right: a dual ending in ए is not joined with a following vowel.
The unit gives no such rule; that is only an inference of the data (unit 8).
questions.explain: Two and two on both sides, four in all; the dual द्वे stays unjoined before a vowel.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: In a new example, which form of 'four' agrees with the feminine plural नद्यः (rivers)?
optionExplain: चत्वारः is masculine: it goes with masculine nouns.
Right: चतस्रः is the feminine nominative plural of 'four', as with the sirās in unit 14.
चत्वारि is neuter: it goes with neuter nouns.
चतुरः is the masculine accusative plural.
questions.explain: चतस्रो नद्यः: four rivers, as ताश्चतस्रः: those (sirās) are four.
questions.teaches: 'Four' agrees in gender: masculine चत्वारः, neuter चत्वारि, feminine चतस्रः (सिरा is feminine).
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 15, how many (sirās, understood) are in the belly (udara)?
optionExplain: Forty is the chest's number (unit 17).
Thirty-two is the hip region's number (unit 11).
Right: चतुर्विंशतिरुदरे: twenty-four in the belly.
Sixteen is the number of the sides (unit 12).
questions.explain: Twenty-four in the belly.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 15 to its meaning.
questions.explain: चतुर् + विंशति = twenty-four; उदरे = in the belly.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: In unit 15 'in the belly' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: उदरे = in the belly, the locative singular of उदर.
questions.teaches: An अ-stem such as उदर takes -ए in the locative singular: उदर → उदरे.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which split of चतुर्विंशतिरुदरे in unit 15 is right?
optionExplain: रुदरे is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
म् before a vowel would give चतुर्विंशतिमुदरे.
ए before उ would not give र्.
Right: After इ, a visarga before a vowel becomes र्.
questions.explain: चतुर्विंशतिः (twenty-four) + उदरे (in the belly): इः + vowel → इर्.
questions.rule: A visarga after इ → र् before a vowel.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which part of the trunk was given the same number as the belly, in unit 13?
optionExplain: Right: Unit 13: चतुर्विंशतिः पृष्ठे, twenty-four in the back.
The chest has forty (unit 17).
The sides have sixteen (unit 12).
The hip region has thirty-two (unit 11).
questions.explain: Back and belly both have twenty-four.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्विंशतिरुदरे, how is हरिः + आगच्छति (Hari comes) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: इ → य् happens only with no visarga; here the visarga gives र्.
Right: After इ, a visarga before a vowel becomes र्, as चतुर्विंशतिः + उदरे.
Visarga → स् happens before त or थ, not before a vowel.
Visarga → श् happens before च, छ or श, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: हरिः + आगच्छति = हरिरागच्छति, like चतुर्विंशतिः + उदरे = चतुर्विंशतिरुदरे.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a vowel: चतुर्विंशतिः + उदरे → चतुर्विंशतिरुदरे.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 16, the belly's four lie above which part?
optionExplain: The heart belongs to the chest's list (unit 18).
The groins belong to unit 12.
Right: मेढ्रस्योपरि: above the meḍhra (penis).
The spine is the back's place (unit 14).
questions.explain: Of the belly's sirās, two and two lie above the meḍhra, on both sides.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 16 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of them, above the meḍhra on both sides of the romarājī (line of body hair), two and two; those also, four.
questions.rule: तासां → मेंढ्रस्योपरिोमराजीमुभयतो → द्वे द्वे → ताअपि → चतस्रः.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word of unit 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Above the meḍhra, on both sides, two and two; those also are four.
questions.teaches: उपरि (above) takes the genitive: मेढ्रस्य उपरि = above the meḍhra.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which split of मेंढ्रस्योपरि in unit 16 is right?
optionExplain: अः before a vowel other than अ would give मेढ्रस्य उपरि, unjoined.
मेढ्रस्यो is not a word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
ए before उ would not give ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: मेढ्रस्य + उपरि → मेढ्रस्योपरि.
questions.explain: मेढ्रस्य (of the meḍhra) + उपरि (above): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 16?
options: The two and two lie on both sides
All four lie below the meḍhra
optionExplain: That is said of the back's four (unit 14), not here.
Right: आः before a vowel drops its visarga; the data calls it regular.
Right: उभयतो द्वे द्वे.
उपरि means above, not below.
questions.explain: Above the meḍhra, on both sides, two and two; ता अपि = ताः अपि.
questions.rule: तासां मेंढ्रस्योपरि ... उभयतो द्वे द्वे ताअपि चतस्रः.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the rule of ताः + अपि → ता अपि, how is देवाः + अत्र (the gods here) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: आः before a vowel drops its visarga and no further join is made, as ताः + अपि → ता अपि.
आ + अ → आ only when there is no visarga; the gap stays.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
questions.explain: देवाः + अत्र = देवा अत्र, like ताः + अपि = ता अपि.
questions.rule: आः + vowel → आ, with a gap.
questions.teaches: After आ the visarga drops before a vowel, and the two vowels are not joined: ताः + अपि → ता अपि.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 17, how many (sirās, understood) are in the chest (vakṣas)?
optionExplain: Twenty-four is the number of the back and of the belly.
Right: चत्वारिंशद्वक्षसि: forty in the chest.
Thirty-two is the hip region's number (unit 11).
Fourteen is a part of the forty (unit 21), not the whole.
questions.explain: Forty in the chest.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Put the trunk places of units 11-17 in the order the text gives them.
questions.explain: Hip region (11), sides (12), back (13), belly (15), chest (17).
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: In unit 17 'in the chest' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: वक्षसि = in the chest, the locative singular of वक्षस्.
questions.teaches: An s-stem such as वक्षस् takes -इ in the locative singular: वक्षस् → वक्षसि.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which split of चत्वारिंशद्वक्षसि in unit 17 is right?
optionExplain: अः before व would give चत्वारिंशो वक्षसि.
द्वक्षसि is not a word; the द् comes from त्.
Right: त् before a voiced consonant (व) becomes द्.
म् before a consonant would be written चत्वारिंशं वक्षसि.
questions.explain: चत्वारिंशत् (forty) + वक्षसि (in the chest): त् → द् before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: त् before a voiced sound → द्.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Add the printed trunk numbers 32, 16, 24, 24 and 40 (units 11-17). Which total of the chapter do they make?
optionExplain: 164 is the upper part's number (unit 9); the sum is 136.
400 is the limbs' number (unit 5); the sum is 136.
700 is the whole (unit 4); the sum is 136.
Right: 32 + 16 + 24 + 24 + 40 = 136: the antarādhi's number in unit 7.
questions.explain: 32 + 16 + 24 + 24 + 40 = 136, the trunk's total.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the rule of चत्वारिंशद्वक्षसि, how is मरुत् + वहति (the wind blows) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a voiced consonant becomes द्, as चत्वारिंशत् + वक्षसि.
त् stays त् only before an unvoiced sound; व is voiced.
त् may become न् before a nasal such as न or म (optional), not before व.
त् becomes च् before च or छ (and before श, giving च्श or optionally च्छ), not before व.
questions.explain: मरुत् + वहति = मरुद्वहति, like चत्वारिंशत् + वक्षसि = चत्वारिंशद्वक्षसि.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: चत्वारिंशत् + वक्षसि → चत्वारिंशद्वक्षसि.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 18, how many of the chest's (sirās, understood) are in the heart?
optionExplain: Four is not the heart's number; द्वे is two.
Right: तासां द्वे हृदये: of them, two in the heart.
Fourteen is the total of units 18-20, given in unit 21.
Forty is the whole chest (unit 17).
questions.explain: Of them, two in the heart.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word of unit 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of them, two in the heart.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: In unit 18, what does the case of हृदये (locative) tell?
options: Whose the two are: of the heart
Where they come from: from the heart
Where the two lie: in the heart
What they serve: for the heart
optionExplain: The genitive would be हृदयस्य.
The ablative would be हृदयात्.
Right: -ए of an अ-stem is the locative singular: in the heart.
The dative would be हृदयाय.
questions.explain: हृदये = in the heart: the place of the two.
questions.teaches: The locative names the place: हृदये = in the heart, as उदरे, वक्षसि.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By units 17-18, which statement is right?
options: The heart has forty of its own as well
The two are added on top of the forty
The two in the heart are said to go upward
Two of the forty lie in the heart
optionExplain: Forty is the chest's count; the heart has two of them.

questions.q: In unit 18 'in the heart' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).

questions.q: तासाम् is the feminine 'of them'. In a new example, which form means 'of them' for masculine nouns?

तासु is the feminine locative plural: in them.
ताभिः is the feminine instrumental plural: by them.
तस्याः is a feminine singular form: of her.
questions.explain: तेषाम् (masc.) : तासाम् (fem.) = of them.
questions.teaches: तद् in the genitive plural: masculine/neuter तेषाम्, feminine तासाम् (सिरा is feminine).
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 19, where do the 'two and two' lie?
optionExplain: These are the neck's names (unit 24).

questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And two and two in the breast-roots and stanarohitas.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: What kind of compound is स्तनमूलस्तनरोहितेषु, by the data?
optionExplain: It is not 'having ...'; and -एषु is not a nominative ending.
A nominative plural would end in -आः or -आनि, not -एषु.
Right: Data: dvandva, loc. pl.: in the stanamūlas and the stanarohitas.
-एषु is no genitive ending; the two names stand side by side.
questions.explain: Two place names joined as 'X and Y', in the locative plural.
questions.rule: स्तनमूल + स्तनरोहित, -एषु: in the X and the Y.
questions.teaches: A dvandva joins names as 'X and Y'; the ending -एषु, put once at the end, gives 'in the X and the Y'.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the data, which statement about स्तनमूल and स्तनरोहित is right?

They are the two sides of the chest
They are kept as names of places

The data does not identify them with the sides.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 19?
options: The line gives a verb of guarding
The line itself gives the total fourteen
The two names stand in the locative plural
optionExplain: No verb is printed; the copula is understood.
The total fourteen is unit 21.
Right: स्तन (breast) + मूल (root).
Right: -एषु, in the ...

questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Like स्तनमूलस्तनरोहितेषु, how are हस्त (hand) and पाद (foot) made one dvandva meaning in the hands and feet, in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva takes one ending at the end: -एषु, locative plural.
-आनि is a nominative/accusative plural, not 'in'.
-ऐः is the instrumental plural: by the hands and feet.
-अस्य is the genitive singular: of the ...
questions.explain: हस्तपादेषु = in the hands and feet, like स्तनमूलस्तनरोहितेषु.
questions.rule: Dvandva of अ-stems, locative plural: -एषु at the end.
questions.teaches: A dvandva puts one case ending on the last member: स्तनमूल-स्तनरोहित-एषु, हस्त-पाद-एषु.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 20, how many lie in each of the named places?
optionExplain: Two and two is unit 19 (द्वे द्वे).
Right: एकैका: one each.
No four is printed in unit 20.
No six is printed in unit 20.

questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each sure word of unit 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: One each in the apastambhas ...; thus.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: How is एकैका (one each) built?
optionExplain: ऐका is not a word; the second part is एका.
अः before a vowel other than अ drops to अ and stays unjoined: एक एका.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ: एक + एका → एकैका.
आ + ए gives ऐ, not आ; and the first part is एक.
questions.explain: एक + एका = एकैका, one each (repeated 'one').
questions.teaches: Repeating एक makes 'one each'; अ + ए joins as ऐ: एक + एका → एकैका.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: The printed line ends -एष्विति. Which split of that ending is right?
optionExplain: इ + इ would give ई: -एषीति.
अ + इ would give ए: -एष्वेति.
अः before इ would give -एष इति, unjoined.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: -एषु + इति → -एष्विति.
questions.explain: -एषु (in the ...) + इति (thus): उ + इ → वि.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 20 and its data?
options: The avagraha after एकैका is a print habit (आ + अ → आ)
Here the avagraha follows ए or ओ
अपस्तम्भ is kept as the name of a place

'One each' is एकैका; इति means thus.
The vowel before the ऽ is आ, not ए or ओ.
Right: a marma name in this tradition (probable).
questions.explain: Print-habit ऽ after आ; अपस्तम्भ kept as a name; इति = thus.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the rule of -एषु + इति → -एष्विति, how is मधु + इति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as -एषु + इति → -एष्विति.
ऊ comes from उ + उ; here उ meets इ.
ए would need अ + इ; there is no अ here.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel; there is no ओ.
questions.explain: मधु + इति = मध्विति, like -एषु + इति = -एष्विति.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: -एषु + इति → -एष्विति.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By unit 21, how many are 'those' (ताः)?
optionExplain: Forty is the chest's whole count (unit 17).
Right: ताश्चतुर्दश: those are fourteen.
चतुर्दश is fourteen; twenty-four is चतुर्विंशति.
दश alone is ten; चतुर्दश is four plus ten.
questions.explain: Those are fourteen.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Those (are) four-ten: fourteen.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the data, how does the fourteen of unit 21 stand to the forty of unit 17?
options: It is added to the forty
It is a part of the forty

The data keeps the forty; nothing is corrected.
Right: Data: the chest total of forty is in unit 17; fourteen is a part.

questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Which of these number words of the chapter means fourteen?
optionExplain: चतुर् + विंशति (twenty) = twenty-four.
चत्वारिंशत् = forty.

questions.explain: चतुर्दश = 14; चतुर्विंशति = 24; चत्वारिंशत् = 40; चतस्रः = 4.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: Put the printed lines of the chest's list (units 18-21) in the text's order.

questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: By the pattern of चतुर्दश (4 + 10), what does पञ्चदश mean in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: पञ्च (five) + दश (ten) = fifteen.
Fifty is पञ्चाशत्; दश adds ten, it does not multiply.
Twenty-five is पञ्चविंशति; दश is ten, not twenty.
पञ्च alone is five; दश adds ten.
questions.explain: पञ्चदश = 5 + 10 = 15, like चतुर्दश = 4 + 10 = 14.
questions.rule: Unit + दश = that unit plus ten.
questions.teaches: A unit before दश adds ten: चतुर्दश = 14, पञ्चदश = 15.
questions.section: सिराएँ: श्रोणि, पार्श्व, पीठ, उदर, वक्ष

questions.q: How is ग्रीवायाम् (in the neck) formed from ग्रीवा?

questions.q: Which split of चतुर्विंशतिर्ग्रीवायां in unit 22 is right?

optionExplain: Here आः before च gives श्, not र्.

Here अः before a voiced consonant gives ओ.

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्विंशतिर्ग्रीवायां, how is मुनिः + गच्छति (the sage goes) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: After इ, a visarga before a voiced consonant becomes र्.
A visarga drops before a voiced consonant after आ; after इ it becomes र्.

questions.teaches: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced consonant: चतुर्विंशतिः + ग्रीवायाम् → चतुर्विंशतिर्ग्रीवायाम्.

questions.q: Which split of चतस्रोऽष्टौ in unit 23 is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would keep ए: चतस्रेऽष्टौ.

questions.q: By unit 23, how many in all are named marma?
optionExplain: The two numbers are joined by च (and), not multiplied.
च joins the four and the eight; both are named marma.
च joins the four and the eight; both are named marma.

questions.q: By the rule of चतस्रोऽष्टौ, how is रामः + अत्र (Rāma here) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the अ drops (ऽ), as चतस्रः + अष्टौ → चतस्रोऽष्टौ.
अ + अ → आ only when there is no visarga.
अः drops to अ before vowels other than अ; before अ it gives ओऽ.

questions.q: By the data, which count makes the sixteen of unit 24?

That would be twenty; unit 23 gives four and eight.

questions.q: What form is स्पृशेत् in न स्पृशेत्?

questions.q: By the rule of विधुरयोरिति, how is हस्तयोः + इति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: After ओ, a visarga before a vowel becomes र्, as विधुरयोः + इति.

questions.teaches: A visarga after ओ becomes र् before a vowel or voiced consonant: विधुरयोः + इति → विधुरयोरिति.

questions.q: By unit 25, how many (sirās, understood) are in the two jaws (hanu)?

questions.q: In the printed तासांसंधिसंबंधिन्यौ, what is the ं of तासां?

optionExplain: तासाम् is a genitive plural; there is no word तासा.
Nothing is lost; ं stands for the final म्.

questions.q: Why is सन्धिसम्बन्धिन्यौ in the feminine dual?

Grammar, not anatomy, sets the ending: it agrees with द्वे.
-इन्यौ is a dual ending (data: f. nom. du.).
Right: Data: f. nom. du., going with द्वे, the two (sirās, understood), a feminine noun.
questions.explain: द्वे ... सन्धिसम्बन्धिन्यौ: two (sirās) connected with the joint.

questions.q: By the pattern of सम्बन्धिन्यौ, which form of वासिन् (dwelling) goes with two feminine nouns in a new example?

वासिनौ is the masculine dual.
वासिन्यः is the feminine plural.
वासी is the masculine nominative singular.

questions.q: By unit 26, how many (sirās, understood) are in the tongue (jihvā)?

Right: षोडश जिह्वायाम्: sixteen in the tongue.
Forty is the chest's number (unit 17).
Fifty-six is the eyes' number (unit 30).
questions.explain: Sixteen in the tongue.

questions.q: In unit 26 'in the tongue' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: जिह्वायाम् = in the tongue; printed जिव्हायां.
questions.teaches: जिह्वा → जिह्वायाम्, locative singular.

questions.q: What does the data say about the printed जिव्हा in unit 26?
options: A dual form of the tongue
optionExplain: No such word; the data reads जिह्वा, tongue.
The data does not flag it as doubtful; it is a plain reversal.
Right: Data: printed jivhā is a letter reversal of jihvā, normalised.
-आयाम् is singular; the data reads loc. sg.
questions.explain: जिव्हा (print) = जिह्वा (tongue), with ह and व swapped.
questions.teaches: Some printed spellings swap letters (व्ह for ह्व); the data records the print and reads the true word.

questions.q: By units 25-26, which pair of parts both have sixteen?
optionExplain: The neck has twenty-four (unit 22).
The nose has twenty-four (unit 28).
The eyes have fifty-six (unit 30).
Right: हन्वोः षोडश (25), षोडश जिह्वायाम् (26).
questions.explain: Jaws sixteen, tongue sixteen.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 26?
options: The unit names two taste-perceiving sirās
The data reads the printed जिव्हा as जिह्वा
No verb is printed; 'are' is understood
optionExplain: Those come in unit 27, not here.
Right: a letter reversal, normalised.
The number is षोडश, sixteen.
Right: copula understood.
questions.explain: Sixteen in the tongue; जिव्हा = जिह्वा; copula understood.

questions.q: By the pattern of जिह्वायाम्, how is शाला (hall) put in the locative singular in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: A feminine आ-stem takes -आयाम् in the locative singular, as जिह्वा → जिह्वायाम्.
-ए is the locative of अ-stems (उदरे), not of feminine आ-stems.
शालासु is plural: in the halls.
शालायाः is genitive or ablative: of / from the hall.
questions.explain: शालायाम् = in the hall, like जिह्वायाम् = in the tongue.
questions.teaches: Feminine आ-stems take -आयाम् in the locative singular: जिह्वा → जिह्वायाम्, शाला → शालायाम्.

questions.q: By unit 27, two sirās (understood) perceive taste; what do the other two named with them do?
options: They move food to the throat
optionExplain: Perceiving smell belongs to two of the nose's sirās (unit 29), not the tongue's.
Right: द्वे वाक्प्रवर्तिन्यौ: two setting speech (वाक्) in motion.
No such task is printed in unit 27.
No such task is printed in unit 27.
questions.explain: Below them: two perceive taste, two set speech in motion.

questions.q: Put the printed phrases of unit 27 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Below them; two taste-perceiving; two speech-moving; those are four.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: रस-वेदिनी = taste-perceiving; वाक्-प्रवर्तिनी = speech-moving; अधः = below.
questions.teaches: Each pair is named by a tat-puruṣa in the feminine dual (-इन्यौ): what it perceives or sets going.

questions.q: Why is अधः printed अधो before द्वे in unit 27?
options: अः before every consonant becomes ओ
ओ is a case ending of the word अधः
अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ
द्वे begins with a vowel, so अः → ओ
optionExplain: Not every consonant: before त the visarga becomes स्, before च श्.
अधः is an indeclinable (gram: ind.); it takes no case ending.
Right: द is a voiced consonant: अधः + द्वे → अधो द्वे.
द्वे begins with the consonant द, not a vowel.
questions.explain: अधः + द्वे: अः before the voiced consonant द → ओ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 27?
options: Two sirās set speech in motion
The line says why the four are counted apart
Those named are four in all
optionExplain: Right: द्वे रसवेदिन्यौ.
Right: द्वे वाक्प्रवर्तिन्यौ.
No reason is printed; the card leaves it open.
Right: ताश्चतस्रः, those are four.
questions.explain: Two perceive taste, two set speech going: four; no reason is given for counting them apart.

questions.q: By the rule of ताश्चतस्रः, how is बालाः + च (and the boys) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: स् comes before त or थ, not before च.
After आ the visarga drops before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
Right: Visarga before च becomes श्, as ताः + चतस्रः → ताश्चतस्रः.
questions.explain: बालाः + च = बालाश्च, like ताः + चतस्रः = ताश्चतस्रः.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: ताः + चतस्रः → ताश्चतस्रः.

questions.q: By unit 28, how many (sirās, understood) are in the nose?
optionExplain: Right: चतुर्विंशतिः = twenty-four, नासायाम् = in the nose.
चतुर्विंशति is four and twenty, not eight and twenty.
Sixteen is the count of the tongue (unit 26), not the nose.
Fifty-six is the count of the two eyes (unit 30).
questions.explain: Twenty-four in the nose.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 28 to its meaning.
Unit 28: चतुर्विंशतिः ____ (in the nose). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नासायाम् (in the nose): चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायां.
questions.teaches: नासायाम् is the locative singular of the ā-stem नासा: 'in the nose'.

questions.q: Which split of चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायां in unit 28 is right?
optionExplain: A word ending in ई with no visarga would not produce र्.
Right: इ + visarga before the voiced न → र्.
रनासायाम् is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
म् before न would be written ं or न्, never र्.
questions.explain: चतुर्विंशतिः (twenty-four) + नासायाम् (in the nose): इः before न → इर्.
questions.rule: इ/उ + visarga before a voiced sound → र्.

questions.q: In चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायां, why does the visarga become र्?
options: It follows अ and stands before a voiced न
Every visarga becomes र् before any consonant
It follows इ and stands before a voiced न
It is the last word of the sentence
optionExplain: The vowel before the visarga is इ (-ति), not अ; अः would give ओ.
Before त it becomes स्, before च श्; so not every consonant.
Right: After a vowel other than अ/आ, visarga + voiced sound → र्.
At a pause the visarga stays ः; here the next word follows.
questions.explain: चतुर्विंशतिः ends in इः; before the voiced न it becomes इर्.
questions.rule: इः / उः + voiced sound → इर् / उर्.

questions.q: By the rule of चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायां, how is हरिः + गच्छति (Hari goes) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: स् comes before त or थ, not before ग.
The visarga drops before a voiced sound after आ, not after इ.
श् comes before च, छ or श, not before ग.
Right: इ + visarga before the voiced ग → र्, as in चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायाम्.
questions.explain: हरिः + गच्छति = हरिर्गच्छति, like चतुर्विंशतिः + नासायाम्.
questions.teaches: After इ or उ a visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound: चतुर्विंशतिः + नासायाम् → चतुर्विंशतिर्नासायाम्.

questions.q: By unit 29, what do the two sirās (understood) named first perceive?
optionExplain: Right: द्वे गन्धवेदिन्यौ: two perceiving smell.
Taste is perceived by two sirās below the tongue (unit 27).
Sound is carried by two sirās of the ears (unit 34).
Touch is not named in unit 29.
questions.explain: Of them, two perceive smell.

questions.q: Put the printed phrases of unit 29 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of them; two smell-perceiving; and of those very ones; one in the palate, thus three.
questions.rule: तासां → द्वे गंधवेदिन्यौ → तासामेव च → तालुन्येकामिति तिस्रः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 29 to its meaning.
questions.explain: गन्ध-वेदिनी = smell-perceiving; तालु = palate; तासामेव = of those very ones; तिस्रः = three.
questions.teaches: तिस्रः is the feminine of 'three', agreeing with the feminine सिरा understood.

questions.q: Which split of तालुन्येकामिति in unit 29 is right?
optionExplain: न्येकाम् is not a word; the न्य् comes from तालुनि.
Right: इ before ए → य्: तालुन्ये-; एकाम् + इति → एकामिति.
एकम् + इति would give एकमिति; the print has -कामिति.
मिति is not a word; the म् belongs to एकाम्.
questions.explain: तालुनि (in the palate) + एकाम् (one) + इति (thus).
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य्; म् joins a following vowel.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 29?
options: The line supplies a verb for एकाम्
Two of the sirās perceive smell
One of them is in the palate (tālu)
optionExplain: No verb is printed or supplied for एकाम्.
Right: द्वे गन्धवेदिन्यौ.
Taste is not named in unit 29.
Right: तालुनि ... एकाम्.
questions.explain: Two perceive smell, one is in the palate: three; एकाम् has no verb.

questions.q: By the rule of तालुन्येकाम्, how is अस्ति + एव (it is indeed) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The इ does not simply drop before ए.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from इ + ए.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as तालुनि + एकाम् → तालुन्येकाम्.
ई comes from इ + इ, not from इ + ए.
questions.explain: अस्ति + एव = अस्त्येव, like तालुनि + एकाम् = तालुन्येकाम्.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: तालुनि + एकाम् → तालुन्येकाम्.

questions.q: By unit 30, how many (sirās, understood) are in the two eyes?
optionExplain: षट् is six and पञ्चाशत् fifty: 56, not 65.
पञ्चाशत् is fifty, not twenty.
पञ्चाशत् is fifty, not thirty.
Right: षट्पञ्चाशत् = six and fifty = 56.
questions.explain: Fifty-six in the two eyes.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each part of unit 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: षट्-पञ्चाशत् = 6 + 50 = 56; नेत्रयोः = in the two eyes.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Unit 30: षट्पञ्चाशत् ____ (in the two eyes). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नेत्रयोः (in the two eyes): षट्पञ्चाशन्नेत्रयोः.
questions.teaches: -योः is the genitive/locative dual; here the data reads it as locative: in the two eyes.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Which split of षट्पंचाशन्नेत्रयोः in unit 30 is right?
optionExplain: Right: The numeral is षट्पञ्चाशत्; its त् is written न् before न (optional; द् is also correct).
There is no numeral पञ्चाशन्; the न् comes from the त् of पञ्चाशत्.
आशन्नेत्रयोः is not a word; पञ्चाशत् is one numeral.
A visarga before न would not give न्न.
questions.explain: षट्पञ्चाशत् (fifty-six) + नेत्रयोः (in the two eyes).
questions.rule: त् before न may become न् (optional; द् is also correct); the print has न्.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: In षट्पंचाशन्नेत्रयोः, what does the print do with the त् of षट्पञ्चाशत्?
optionExplain: Nothing is dropped: the print shows two न (-न्ने-).
Right: The print shows -शन्ने-: त् is written न् before the न of नेत्रयोः.
च् comes from त् before च or छ, not before न.
स् does not come from त् in this place.
questions.explain: षट्पञ्चाशत् + नेत्रयोः → षट्पञ्चाशन्नेत्रयोः: the त् is written न् before न.
questions.rule: त् + न → न्न (optional; द् is also correct; as printed).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By the pattern of नेत्रयोः, which form of हस्त (hand) means in the two hands, in a new example?
optionExplain: -एषु is the locative plural: in the hands (more than two).
हस्ते is singular: in the hand.
Right: -योः is the locative dual of an a-stem, as नेत्र → नेत्रयोः.
हस्तौ is the nominative/accusative dual: the two hands.
questions.explain: हस्तयोः = in the two hands, like नेत्रयोः = in the two eyes.
questions.teaches: -योः gives the locative (and genitive) dual of a-stems: नेत्र → नेत्रयोः, कर्ण → कर्णयोः (unit 34).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 31, which two actions are linked with six of the eyes' sirās (understood)?
optionExplain: Neither seeing nor weeping is named in unit 31.
Neither moving nor turning is named in unit 31.
Colour and form are not named in unit 31.
Right: उन्मेष-निमेष-क्रिये: the actions of opening and closing.
questions.explain: उन्मेष = opening, निमेष = closing (of the eyes).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 31 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of those two; the actions of opening and closing; two, two, two; and in the apāṅgas, thus; six.
questions.rule: तयोः → उन्मेषनिमेषक्रिये → द्वे द्वे द्वे → चापांगयोरिति → षट्.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word of unit 31 to its meaning.
questions.explain: उन्मेष-निमेष-क्रिया = the action of opening and closing; अपाङ्ग = outer corner of the eye.
questions.teaches: उन्मेष and निमेष are a pair of opposites joined in one dvandva, then tied to क्रिया (action).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Which split of चापांगयोरिति in unit 31 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ (चा-); ओः before इ → ओर् (-योरिति).
अः before इ would give अपाङ्गय इति, with no र्.
Neither चा nor पाङ्गयोः is a word here.
रिति is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: च (and) + अपाङ्गयोः (in the two apāṅgas) + इति (thus).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; ओः + vowel → ओर्.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 31, where are the last two sirās of the six?
options: In the pupils of the eyes
optionExplain: No eyelid is named in unit 31.
Right: द्वे चापाङ्गयोः: two in the two apāṅgas.
The temples are not named in unit 31.
No pupil is named in unit 31.
questions.explain: The last two are in the two apāṅgas, the outer corners of the eye.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By the rule of चापांगयोः (च + अपाङ्गयोः), how is न + अस्ति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Two अ do not merge into a short अ; they give आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अपाङ्गयोः → चापाङ्गयोः.
No य् comes between two अ.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like च + अपाङ्गयोः = चापाङ्गयोः.
questions.teaches: Two like vowels merge into the long one: अ + अ → आ (च + अपाङ्गयोः → चापाङ्गयोः).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 32, how many (sirās, understood) are in the forehead (lalāṭa)?
optionExplain: Sixteen is षोडश; the line has षष्टिः, sixty.
Six is षट्; षष्टि is sixty.
Seventy is सप्तति; the line has षष्टिः.
Right: ललाटे षष्टिः: sixty in the forehead.
questions.explain: Sixty in the forehead.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 32 to its meaning.
questions.explain: नासा-नेत्र-गताः = gone to the nose and eyes; ललाटे षष्टिः = sixty in the forehead.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the words of unit 32 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Those going to the nose and eyes, however, in the forehead, sixty.
questions.teaches: नासानेत्रगताः is a tat-puruṣa: the dvandva नासा-नेत्र + गत (gone to), feminine plural for the sirās.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Which split of नासानेत्रगतास्तु in unit 32 is right?
optionExplain: Right: आः before त: the visarga becomes स्, giving -गतास्तु.
त् + त would give -गतात्तु, not -गतास्तु.
म् before त would be written ं or न्, not स्.
स्तु is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: नासानेत्रगताः (gone to the nose and eyes) + तु (however).
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 32, which sirās are the sixty in the forehead?
options: Those going to the ears and temples
Those going to the nose and eyes
Those going to the tongue and palate
Those going to the lips and chin
optionExplain: Ears and temples are not named in unit 32.
Right: नासानेत्रगताः: gone to the nose and eyes.
Tongue and palate are not named in unit 32.
Lips and chin are not named in unit 32.
questions.explain: The sixty in the forehead are those going to the nose and eyes.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By the rule of नासानेत्रगतास्तु, how is जनाः + तत्र (the people there) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: श् comes before च, छ or श, not before त.
After आ the visarga drops before a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
Right: Visarga before त becomes स्, as नासानेत्रगताः + तु → नासानेत्रगतास्तु.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
questions.explain: जनाः + तत्र = जनास्तत्र, like नासानेत्रगताः + तु.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: नासानेत्रगताः + तु → नासानेत्रगतास्तु.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: By unit 33, how many sirās (understood) are in the sthapanī?
optionExplain: Two are in the two āvartas, not in the sthapanī.
Four go along to the keśānta (hair-line, probable).
No group of three is named in unit 33.
Right: एका च स्थपन्याम्: and one in the sthapanī.
questions.explain: One in the sthapanī.
questions.section: सिराएँ: नेत्र, ललाट, कर्ण, सिर; अवेध्य सिराएँ

questions.q: Put the printed phrases of unit 33 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of them; four going to the keśānta; two in the āvartas, and one; in the sthapanī, thus seven.
questions.rule: तासां → केशांतनुगताश्चतस्रो → द्वे आवर्तयोरेका च → स्थपन्यामिति सप्त.
