optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ; here उ meets अ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as रक्तेषु + अपि → रक्तेष्वपि.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel; मधु ends in उ.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like रक्तेषु + अपि = रक्तेष्वपि.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: रक्तेषु + अपि → रक्तेष्वपि.

questions.q: By unit 40, what do they do by reversal (vyatyaya)?
optionExplain: Supporting the body is said of the doṣas remaining thus (unit 39), not by reversal.
Carrying is not said in unit 40.
Becoming threefold is not said in unit 40.
Right: व्यत्ययेन तु पीडयंति: but by reversal they afflict.
questions.explain: But by reversal they afflict.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 40 to its meaning.
questions.explain: But by reversal they afflict.

questions.q: In unit 40 no subject is printed. By the data, who are 'they'?
optionExplain: Right: Data note: the subject, the doṣas of unit 39, is carried over.
The dhamanīs come later; the subject is carried over from unit 39.
The prāṇas come later; the subject is carried over from unit 39.
Unit 37 speaks of ones not to be dealt with by the knife; the subject here is carried over from unit 39.
questions.explain: They = the doṣas of unit 39, carried over.
questions.teaches: An elliptical line can take its subject from the line before: here the doṣas of unit 39.

questions.q: What does तु do in unit 40?
optionExplain: 'Also' is अपि (unit 39), not तु.
Right: तु marks a contrast: but by reversal they afflict.
'Thus' is एवम् (unit 39), not तु.
'Indeed, for' is हि (unit 39), not तु.
questions.explain: तु = but: it sets unit 40 against unit 39.

questions.q: In unit 40 'they afflict' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पीडयन्ति = they afflict (printed पीडयंति).
questions.teaches: पीडयन्ति = they afflict, 3rd person plural present.

questions.q: By the pattern of व्यत्यय → व्यत्ययेन (by reversal), how is हस्त (hand) put in the instrumental singular?
optionExplain: हस्ताय is the dative singular: for the hand.
हस्तात् is the ablative singular: from the hand.
Right: An अ-stem takes -एन in the instrumental singular, as व्यत्यय → व्यत्ययेन.
हस्ते is the locative singular: in the hand.
questions.explain: हस्तेन = by the hand, like व्यत्ययेन = by reversal.
questions.teaches: -एन marks the instrumental singular of अ-stems: व्यत्यय → व्यत्ययेन (by, through).

questions.q: By unit 41, what do the dusky-brown, reddish, throbbing ones carry?
optionExplain: Pitta-blood goes with blue, yellow, warm ones (unit 42).
Kapha-blood goes with fair, cold, itching ones (unit 42).
Pure blood goes with even, hidden ones (unit 43).
Right: ...वातरक्तं वहंति: they carry Vāta-blood.
questions.explain: The dusky-brown, reddish, throbbing, fine, momentarily full and empty ones carry Vāta-blood.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 41 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Dusky-brown and reddish, throbbing, fine, momentarily full and empty: they carry Vāta-blood.
questions.rule: श्यावारुणाः → प्रस्पंदिन्यः → सूक्ष्माः → क्षणपूर्णरिक्ता → वातरक्तं वहंति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 41 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five marks of the ones that carry Vāta-blood.
questions.teaches: क्षण-पूर्ण-रिक्त: for a moment full, (for a moment) empty: filling and emptying by turns.

questions.q: Which sign is NOT given in unit 41 for the ones that carry Vāta-blood?
optionExplain: Right: Warm to the touch (स्पर्शोष्ण) marks the Pitta-blood ones of unit 42.
Right in unit 41: प्रस्पन्दिन्यः.
Right in unit 41: सूक्ष्माः.
Right in unit 41: क्षणपूर्णरिक्ताः.
questions.explain: Unit 41: dusky-brown and reddish, throbbing, fine, momentarily full and empty; warmth is unit 42.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 41 and its data?
options: The noun these adjectives describe is printed
Vāta-blood here is certainly the disease vātarakta
They are momentarily full and momentarily empty
optionExplain: It is not printed; none is supplied.
Right: e.g. प्रस्पन्दिन्यः, f. nom. pl.
The data reads it as blood of the Vāta type, probably not the disease.
Right: क्षणपूर्णरिक्ताः.
questions.explain: Feminine plural adjectives for an unstated noun; momentarily full and empty; Vāta-blood, probably not the disease.
questions.rule: श्यावारुणाः प्रस्पंदिन्यः सूक्ष्माः क्षणपूर्णरिक्ता वातरक्तं वहंति.

questions.q: By the rule of श्याव + अरुणाः → श्यावारुणाः, how is न + अस्ति (is not) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as श्याव + अरुणाः → श्यावारुणाः.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
The two अ merge into a long आ; neither simply drops.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like श्याव + अरुणाः = श्यावारुणाः.
questions.teaches: Two short अ merge into long आ: श्याव + अरुणाः → श्यावारुणाः.

questions.q: By unit 42, which signs go with the Pitta-blood ones?
options: Cold to the touch, steady and itching
Throbbing, fine, momentarily full and empty
Warm to the touch, quickly discharging
optionExplain: Cold, steady, itching mark the Kapha-blood ones.
These mark the Vāta-blood ones of unit 41.
Right: स्पर्शोष्णाः क्षिप्रस्राविण्यः पित्तरक्तं.
These mark the pure-blood ones of unit 43.
questions.explain: Blue, yellow and dark, warm to the touch, quickly discharging: Pitta-blood.

questions.q: Put the signs of the Kapha-blood ones in the order of unit 42.
questions.explain: Fair, unctuous, steady, cold, itching: Kapha-blood.

questions.q: Match each word of the Pitta-blood line of unit 42 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Blue, yellow and dark, warm to the touch, quickly discharging.
questions.rule: नील, पीत, असित, स्पर्श, उष्ण, क्षिप्रस्राविन्.
questions.teaches: स्पर्शोष्ण = warm (उष्ण) to the touch (स्पर्श): the first member says in what respect.

questions.q: Which split of स्पर्शोष्णाः in unit 42 is right?
optionExplain: अः before a vowel other than अ gives अ with no join: स्पर्श उष्णाः.
ए before उ becomes अय् (or अ), never ओ.
ष्णाः is not a word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: स्पर्श + उष्णाः → स्पर्शोष्णाः.
questions.explain: स्पर्श (touch) + उष्णाः (warm): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: By unit 42, the ones that are cold, steady and itching carry what?
optionExplain: Right: गौर्यः स्निग्धाः स्थिराः शीताः कंडूमत्यः कफरक्तं.
Pitta-blood ones are warm, not cold.
Vāta-blood ones are throbbing and fine (unit 41).
Pure-blood ones are even and hidden (unit 43).
questions.explain: Fair, unctuous, steady, cold, itching: Kapha-blood.

questions.q: By the pattern of गौर्यः (fair ones, from गौरी), what is the nominative plural of नदी (river) in a new example?
optionExplain: नदीः is the accusative plural.
Right: A feminine ई-stem takes -यः in the nominative plural, as गौरी → गौर्यः.
नद्यौ is a dual: two rivers.
नद्याः is the genitive or ablative singular.
questions.explain: नद्यः = rivers, like गौर्यः = fair ones.
questions.teaches: Feminine ई-stems take -यः in the nominative plural: गौरी → गौर्यः, कण्डूमती → कण्डूमत्यः.

questions.q: By unit 43, which blood goes with a mixture of the signs (lakṣaṇa-saṅkara)?
optionExplain: Pure blood has its own signs; it is not the mixture.
Kapha-blood has its own signs (unit 42).
Right: लक्षणसंकरे संसर्गसन्निपातरक्तं.
Vāta-blood has its own signs (unit 41).
questions.explain: In a mixture of the signs: blood of saṃsarga and sannipāta.

questions.q: Put the five kinds of blood in the order of units 41-43.
questions.explain: Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, the mixed (saṃsarga, sannipāta), then pure blood; iti closes the list.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 43 to its meaning.
questions.explain: In a mixture of signs: saṃsarga and sannipāta blood; even, hidden ... ones: pure blood.
questions.rule: लक्षण, सङ्कर, संसर्ग, सन्निपात, शुद्ध, गूढ.
questions.teaches: लक्षणसङ्करे is a locative of circumstance: 'when the signs are mixed'.

questions.q: Which sign is shared by the Kapha-blood ones (unit 42) and the pure-blood ones (unit 43)?
optionExplain: समाः is only in the pure-blood list.
कण्डूमत्यः is only in the Kapha-blood list.
शीताः is only in the Kapha-blood list.
Right: स्निग्धाः is in both lists.
questions.explain: स्निग्ध (unctuous) marks both the Kapha-blood and the pure-blood ones.
questions.rule: कफ: गौर्यः स्निग्धाः ...; शुद्ध: समा गूढाः स्निग्धा ....

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 43 and its data?
options: The closing इति ends the five-fold list
The verb 'carry' is printed in unit 43
The line counts the doṣas in saṃsarga
Pure blood is the last kind named
optionExplain: Right: iti closes the list of units 41-43.
It is not printed; it is carried from unit 41.
The line does not count the doṣas.
Right: शुद्धरक्तमिति ends the list.
questions.explain: Mixed signs: saṃsarga and sannipāta blood; pure blood last; iti closes the list.

questions.q: By the rule of समाः + गूढाः → समा गूढाः, how is देवाः + गच्छन्ति (the gods go) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: आः before a voiced consonant drops its visarga, as समाः + गूढाः → समा गूढाः.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
श् comes from a visarga before च, छ or श, not before ग.
questions.explain: देवाः + गच्छन्ति = देवा गच्छन्ति, like समाः + गूढाः = समा गूढाः.
questions.teaches: आः drops its visarga before a voiced sound: समाः गूढाः → समा गूढाः, स्निग्धाः रोहिण्यः → स्निग्धा रोहिण्यः.

questions.q: By unit 44, how many dhamanīs are there?
optionExplain: Seven hundred is the count of the sirās (unit 4), not of the dhamanīs.
Right: धमन्यस्तु चतुर्विंशतिः: the dhamanīs are twenty-four.
चतुर्विंशति is four and twenty, not forty-two.
Fourteen would be चतुर्दश.
questions.explain: The dhamanīs, however, are twenty-four.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 44 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The dhamanīs, however, are four-and-twenty.

questions.q: By unit 44 the vessels counted as twenty-four are the ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: धमन्यः (dhamanīs), nominative plural of धमनी.
questions.teaches: धमनी = vessel, channel (probably a blood vessel, probable); 24 of them.

questions.q: Which split of धमन्यस्तु in unit 44 is right?
optionExplain: That would give धमन्यास्तु, with a long आ.
औ stays before a consonant: धमन्यौ तु.
Right: Visarga before त becomes स्: धमन्यः + तु → धमन्यस्तु.
स्तु is not a word here; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: धमन्यः (dhamanīs) + तु (however): visarga before त → स्.

questions.q: By unit 44 and its data, what is a dhamanī?
options: A bone that forms a joint
A sense organ of the head
A part of the large intestine
A vessel, probably a blood vessel
optionExplain: Bones and joints are not meant; dhamanī is a vessel.
No sense organ is meant; dhamanī is a vessel.
No organ is meant; dhamanī is a vessel.
Right: Data: dhamanī = vessel or channel; blood vessel is probable.
questions.explain: धमनी = a vessel or channel, probably a blood vessel (probable).

questions.q: By the pattern of चतुर्विंशतिः (four + twenty), what does पञ्चविंशतिः mean in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: पञ्च (five) + विंशति (twenty) = 25, as चतुर् + विंशति = 24.
Fifteen is पञ्चदश; विंशति is twenty.
The unit number comes first and is added to twenty.
The parts are added, not multiplied.
questions.explain: पञ्चविंशतिः = 25, as चतुर्विंशतिः = 24.
questions.rule: unit number + विंशति = that number plus twenty.
questions.teaches: A unit number before विंशति is added to twenty: चतुर्विंशतिः = 4 + 20 = 24.

questions.q: In the simile of unit 45, by what is a field (kedāra) moistened?
optionExplain: No clouds are named; the field is moistened by canals.
Right: केदार इव कुल्याभिः: like a field by canals.
No wells are named; the field is moistened by canals.
No rivers are named; the field is moistened by canals.
questions.explain: Like a field by canals (kulyā).

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 45 in the line's order.
questions.explain: By them this body, like a garden by water-carrying ones, like a field by canals, is moistened.
questions.rule: ताभिः → कायोऽयम् → आराम इव जलहारिणीभिः → केदार इव कुल्याभिः → उपस्निह्यति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 45 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By them the body is moistened, like a garden by water-carriers, like a field by canals.
questions.rule: कायः, आरामः, जलहारिणी, केदारः, कुल्या, उपस्निह्यति.
questions.teaches: इव (like) follows the thing compared: आराम इव = like a garden; the instrumentals say by what.

questions.q: Which split of कायोऽयम् in unit 45 is right?
optionExplain: यम् is not the word here; the word is अयम् (this).
कायो is not a word; the ओ comes from the visarga of कायः.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked ऽ: कायः + अयम् → कायोऽयम्.
म् before a vowel would give कायमयम्.
questions.explain: कायः (body) + अयम् (this): अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: In the simile of unit 45, what is to the body as the canals are to the field?
optionExplain: The garden is another thing moistened, like the body.
The field is moistened by the canals; it is not the means.
The body is what is moistened, not the means.
Right: ताभिः = by them, the dhamanīs of unit 44: they moisten the body.
questions.explain: Canals : field = dhamanīs : body.

questions.q: By the rule of कायः + अयम् → कायोऽयम्, how is रामः + अयम् (this Rāma) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked ऽ, as कायः + अयम् → कायोऽयम्.
The gap comes before vowels other than अ; before अ it is ओऽ.
No long आ arises; the visarga gives ओ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
questions.explain: रामः + अयम् = रामोऽयम्, like कायः + अयम् = कायोऽयम्.
questions.teaches: अः before अ gives ओ, and the अ is dropped and marked with ऽ: कायः + अयम् → कायोऽयम्.

questions.q: By unit 46, what is surrounded by them (the dhamanīs)?
optionExplain: The heart is not named in unit 46.
Right: ताभिश्च नाभिः ... आवृता: and by them the navel is surrounded.
The head is not named in unit 46.
The breasts are not named in unit 46.
questions.explain: And by them the navel is surrounded.

questions.q: Match each sure word of unit 46 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And by them the navel is surrounded; cakranābhi = hub of a wheel (the simile rests on a conjectural reading).

questions.q: By unit 46 the ____ (navel) is surrounded by the dhamanīs (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नाभिः = the navel (f. nom. sg.).
questions.teaches: नाभि = navel; चक्रनाभि = hub of a wheel.

questions.q: Which split of ताभिश्च in unit 46 is right?
optionExplain: That would give ताभ्यश्च.
A visarga before च becomes श्, not र्.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: ताभिः + च → ताभिश्च.
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: ताभिः (by them) + च (and): visarga before च → श्.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 46 and its data?
options: आवृता agrees with the feminine नाभिः
The line says the navel is moistened
चक्रनाभि is the hub of a wheel
optionExplain: Right: data note: āvṛtā agrees with nābhiḥ (feminine).
Moistening is said of the body in unit 45, not here.
Right: cakranābhi is taken as the hub of a wheel.
No number is printed in unit 46.
questions.explain: By them the navel is surrounded (आवृता, f.); cakranābhi = hub of a wheel (the simile is a conjectural reading).

questions.q: By the rule of ताभिः + च → ताभिश्च, how is रामः + च (and Rāma) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant; च is not voiced.
The visarga does not drop before च; it becomes श्.
स् comes before त or थ; before च it is श्.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as ताभिः + च → ताभिश्च.
questions.explain: रामः + च = रामश्च, like ताभिः + च = ताभिश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: ताभिः + च → ताभिश्च, नाभिः + चक्र... → नाभिश्चक्र....

questions.q: By unit 47, where are the prāṇas (vital breaths) especially established?
optionExplain: Right: तस्मान्नाभ्यां विशेषेण प्राणा व्यवस्थिताः.
The joints are not named in unit 47.
The eyes are not named in unit 47.
The feet are not named in unit 47.
questions.explain: Therefore the prāṇas are established especially in the navel.

questions.q: Put the words of the first clause of unit 47 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Therefore, in the navel, especially, the prāṇas, are established.

questions.q: Match each sure word of unit 47 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The prāṇas are established especially in the navel; ten go downward, four crosswise.
questions.rule: नाभ्याम्, विशेषेण, प्राणाः, व्यवस्थिताः, अधः, तिर्यक्.
questions.teaches: नाभ्याम् is the locative singular of the feminine नाभि (in the navel).

questions.q: By unit 47, how many of the dhamanīs run crosswise (tiryak)?
optionExplain: Ten is the number going downward (दशाधः).
Right: चतस्रस्तिर्यक्: four crosswise.
चतस्रः is four, not two.
Twenty-four is the total of unit 44.
questions.explain: Ten downward, four crosswise.

questions.q: Which statements fit the sure parts of unit 47?
options: The prāṇas are especially in the navel
optionExplain: Right: दशाधः = दश + अधः.
The heart is not named in unit 47.
Right: चतस्रस्तिर्यक्.
Right: नाभ्यां विशेषेण प्राणा व्यवस्थिताः.
questions.explain: Prāṇas especially in the navel; ten downward, four crosswise.

questions.q: By the pattern of चतस्रः (four, with the feminine dhamanīs), how are four rivers (नदी, f.) named in a new example?
optionExplain: चत्वारः is the masculine 'four'; नदी is feminine.
चत्वारि is the neuter 'four'; नदी is feminine.
Right: चतस्रः is the feminine 'four'; अः before the voiced न becomes ओ.
चतुरः is the masculine accusative 'four'.
questions.explain: चतस्रो नद्यः = four rivers, as चतस्रः (धमन्यः) = four (dhamanīs).
questions.rule: 'Four' agrees in gender: m. चत्वारः, f. चतस्रः, n. चत्वारि.
questions.teaches: The numeral 'four' takes the gender of its noun: चतस्रः goes with the feminine dhamanīs.

questions.q: By unit 48, what do the upward-going ones reach?
optionExplain: The joints are not named in unit 48.
The soles are not named in unit 48.
The large intestine is not named in unit 48.
Right: तासामूर्ध्वगा हृदयमभिप्रपन्नाः: the upward ones reach the heart.
questions.explain: The upward-going ones, having reached the heart, each become threefold.

questions.q: Put these words of the second line of unit 48 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The upward-going, the heart, having reached, each, become threefold.
questions.rule: ऊर्ध्वगा → हृदयम् → अभिप्रपन्नाः → प्रत्येकं → त्रिधा जायंते.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line of unit 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By them the limbs and parts, each according to its own, are held and nourished.
questions.teaches: धार्यन्ते and आप्याय्यन्ते are passive: the limbs are held and nourished; ताभिः (by them) is the agent.

questions.q: Which verb of unit 48 is NOT passive?
optionExplain: धार्यन्ते is passive (3 pl. pres. pass. √धृ).
आप्याय्यन्ते is passive (causative passive of आ-√प्याय्).
Right: जायन्ते is a middle form of √जन्: an -यन्ते form that is not passive.
questions.explain: -यन्ते is not always passive: जायन्ते is middle; धार्यन्ते and आप्याय्यन्ते are passive.
questions.rule: Check the grammar label: जायते is middle, not passive.

questions.q: By unit 48, what happens to each upward-going one after it reaches the heart?
options: It joins the others in one
It turns back to the navel
optionExplain: Nothing is said of joining; each becomes threefold.
Right: प्रत्येकं त्रिधा जायंते: each becomes threefold.
Nothing is said of turning back; each becomes threefold.
Nothing is said of running crosswise; each becomes threefold.
questions.explain: Each upward-going one, having reached the heart, becomes threefold.

questions.q: By the pattern of त्रिधा (threefold), what does पञ्चधा mean in a new example?
optionExplain: The fifth is पञ्चम.
Fifty is पञ्चाशत्.
Right: -धा on a number = in so many ways: त्रिधा threefold, पञ्चधा fivefold.
Fifteen is पञ्चदश.
questions.explain: पञ्चधा = fivefold, as त्रिधा = threefold.
questions.rule: number + -धा = in so many ways, so-many-fold.
questions.teaches: -धा added to a number means 'in so many ways': त्रिधा = threefold.

questions.q: By unit 49, how many of the thirty carry each of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood and rasa?
optionExplain: The numeral is द्वे (two), repeated.
The numeral is द्वे (two), not three.
Ten is the sum of all five pairs, not each.
Right: द्वे द्वे: two and two, read as two for each item.
questions.explain: Two and two carry Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood and rasa.

questions.q: Put the five carried things in the order of unit 49.
questions.explain: Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood, rasa.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Then, among the thirty, two and two carry Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood and rasa.
questions.rule: त्रिंशतः, मध्ये, द्वे द्वे, रक्त, रस.
questions.teaches: त्रिंशतः मध्ये: a genitive with मध्ये = among (the thirty).

questions.q: In unit 49, what does रस mean?
options: A juice pressed out of a plant
The sweat that comes on the skin
optionExplain: Right: Data: rasa here is the nutrient fluid (dhātu), not taste.
Rasa as taste is unit 50; here it is the nutrient fluid.
No plant is meant; rasa here is the nutrient fluid.
Sweat is not meant; rasa here is the nutrient fluid.
questions.explain: रस in unit 49 = the nutrient fluid (dhātu), not taste.
questions.rule: रस with वात, पित्त, कफ, रक्त = the nutrient fluid.

questions.q: On the data's reading of द्वे द्वे, how many of the thirty go to these five things?
optionExplain: Each item has two, not one.
Right: Two for each of five items: 2 × 5 = 10 (data note: 10 + 8 + 8 + 4 = 30).
द्वे द्वे is repeated: two for each item.
Thirty is the whole; the five pairs make ten of it.
questions.explain: Two each for five items = ten of the thirty.

questions.q: By the rule of त्रिंशतः + मध्ये → त्रिंशतो मध्ये, how is नरः + गच्छति (the man goes) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The visarga after अ does not just drop before a voiced consonant; it gives ओ.
आ comes from आः losing its visarga; here it is अः.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as त्रिंशतः + मध्ये → त्रिंशतो मध्ये.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
questions.explain: नरः + गच्छति = नरो गच्छति, like त्रिंशतः + मध्ये = त्रिंशतो मध्ये.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: त्रिंशतः + मध्ये → त्रिंशतो मध्ये.

questions.q: By unit 50, what is grasped by eight?
optionExplain: Touch is not named in unit 50.
Sleep and speech are not in unit 50.
Tears and milk are not in unit 50.
Right: अष्टाभिः शब्दरूपरसगंधा गृह्यंते.
questions.explain: By eight, sound, form, taste and smell are grasped.

questions.q: Put the sense-objects in the order of unit 50.
questions.explain: Sound, form, taste, smell.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By eight, sound, form, taste and smell are grasped.
questions.teaches: गृह्यन्ते is passive of √ग्रह्: the objects are grasped; अष्टाभिः (by eight) is the agent.

questions.q: Which sense-object is NOT named in unit 50?
optionExplain: Right: Data note: touch is not named in this line.
शब्द is the first item of the list.
रूप is the second item of the list.
गन्ध is the last item of the list.
questions.explain: Sound, form, taste, smell are named; touch is not.

questions.q: In unit 50 'smell' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: गन्ध = smell, the last member of शब्दरूपरसगन्धाः.
questions.teaches: गन्ध = smell.

questions.q: By the pattern of गृह्यन्ते (are grasped, passive), what does दृश्यन्ते mean in a new example?
optionExplain: 'They see' is पश्यन्ति, an active form.
Right: दृश्यन्ते is the passive of √दृश्, as गृह्यन्ते of √ग्रह्.
'Having seen' is दृष्ट्वा.
'They will see' is द्रक्ष्यन्ति.
questions.explain: दृश्यन्ते = they are seen, like गृह्यन्ते = they are grasped.
questions.teaches: गृह्यन्ते is a passive (3 pl. pres.): are grasped, perceived.

questions.q: By unit 51, what do the two resting on the breasts carry?
options: Tears in both woman and man
Food and water for the gut
A woman's milk; a man's semen
Sweat and urine of the body
optionExplain: Tears are carried by another two (द्वे चाश्रु वहतः).
Food and water are not in unit 51.
Right: नार्याः स्तन्यं नरस्य शुक्रं.
Sweat and urine are not in unit 51.
questions.explain: Two, resting on the breasts: a woman's milk (stanya), a man's semen (śukra).
questions.rule: द्वे च स्तनाश्रिते नार्याः स्तन्यं नरस्य शुक्रं.

questions.q: Put the four acts of the first line of unit 51 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Speaks, makes a sound, sleeps, wakes.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Speaks, makes a sound, sleeps, wakes; tears; breast-milk.
questions.rule: भाषते, घोषम्, स्वपिति, प्रतिबुध्यते, अश्रु, स्तन्य.
questions.teaches: भाषते and प्रतिबुध्यते are middle (ātmanepada) present forms: speaks, wakes.

questions.q: Which split of चाश्रु in unit 51 is right?
optionExplain: श्रु is not the word here; the word is अश्रु (tears).
ए + अ would give चेऽश्रु, with ए kept.
With no vowel added, च + श्रु would give चश्रु, not चाश्रु.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अश्रु → चाश्रु.
questions.explain: च (and) + अश्रु (tears): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: On the data's reading of the repeated द्वाभ्याम्, how many serve speaking, sounding, sleeping and waking?
optionExplain: Right: Data note: distributive, two for each of the four acts = eight.
द्वाभ्याम् is 'by two', not 'by one'.
Ten is the count of unit 49, not of these four acts.
Four acts are named: speaks, sounds, sleeps, wakes.
questions.explain: Two for each of the four acts = eight.

questions.q: By the pattern of वहतः (the two carry), what form of √वद् means the two speak, in a new example?
optionExplain: वदन्ति is plural: they (all) speak.
Right: -अतः marks the 3rd person dual present, as वहतः (the two carry).
वदति is singular: he speaks.
वदथः is 2nd person dual: you two speak.
questions.explain: वदतः = the two speak, like वहतः = the two carry.
questions.teaches: वहतः is 3rd person dual present: the two carry; so वद् → वदतः.

questions.q: By unit 52, where are the downward-going ones situated?
options: In the hṛdaya (the heart of the body)
In the śiras (the head of the body)
In the grīvā (the neck of the body)
optionExplain: The heart is reached by the upward-going ones (card 48), not these.
No head is named in unit 52; the place is the pakvāśaya.
Right: पक्वाशयस्थाः: situated in the pakvāśaya.
No neck is named in unit 52; the place is the pakvāśaya.
questions.explain: The downward-going ones are situated in the pakvāśaya (probably the large-intestine region).

questions.q: Put the words of unit 52 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Downward-going, situated in the pakvāśaya, likewise, threefold, come to be.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 52 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अधः-गमाः = downward-going; पक्व-आशय-स्थाः = situated in the seat of the digested; त्रिधा = threefold.
questions.rule: अधः, गम, पक्व, आशय, स्थ, त्रिधा.
questions.teaches: पक्वाशय = पक्व (digested) + आशय (seat), with अ + आ → आ.

questions.q: Which split of अधोगमाः in unit 52 is right?
optionExplain: म् before a consonant would be written ं: अधंगमाः.
ए before a consonant stays ए: अधेगमाः.
औ before a consonant stays औ: अधौगमाः.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant (ग) becomes ओ: अधः + गमाः → अधोगमाः.
questions.explain: अधः (downward) + गमाः (going): अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 52?
options: The line itself names them as dhamanīs
They are situated in the pakvāśaya
जायन्ते here is a passive form
optionExplain: The line does not name them; dhamanīs is a presumption from card 47.
Right: पक्वाशयस्थाः.
जायन्ते is a middle present of √जन्: 'come to be', not passive.
Right: एवं त्रिधा जायन्ते.
questions.explain: In the pakvāśaya, likewise threefold; the line does not name the 'ones'.

questions.q: By the rule of अधः + गमाः → अधोगमाः, how is मनः + हरम् (charming) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant (ह) becomes ओ, as अधः + गमाः → अधोगमाः.
आ does not come from अः before a consonant.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ, not after अ.
Before a voiced consonant this visarga does not stay; अः → ओ.
questions.explain: मनः + हरम् = मनोहरम्, like अधः + गमाः = अधोगमाः.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: अधः + गमाः → अधोगमाः.

questions.q: In unit 53, what does पूर्ववत् mean?
optionExplain: After this would be ततः or अनन्तरम्; पूर्ववत् is as before.
Right: पूर्ववत् = as before (data gloss).
From below would be अधस्तात्; पूर्ववत् is as before.
Not so would be न तथा; पूर्ववत् is as before.
questions.explain: पूर्ववत् = as before.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 53 in the line's order.
questions.explain: There, the first ten, as before.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: तत्र = there; दश-आद्याः = the first ten (or 'ten and so on'); पूर्ववत् = as before.
questions.teaches: -वत् after a word as an indeclinable means 'like, as': पूर्ववत् = as before.

questions.q: Which split of दशाद्याः in unit 53 is right?
optionExplain: अः before a vowel other than अ becomes अ with no join: दश आद्याः.
ए before आ would give दशयाद्याः or दश आद्याः, not दशाद्याः.
Right: अ + आ → आ: दश + आद्याः → दशाद्याः.
औ before आ would give दशावाद्याः.
questions.explain: दश (ten) + आद्याः (first): अ + आ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 53 and its data?
options: No verb is printed in the line
The line names what the ten are
दशाद्याः may also mean 'ten and so on'
पूर्ववत् names the passage it points to
optionExplain: Right: the line is elliptical; no verb is supplied.
It does not; the referent is only presumed.
Right: the data notes this second reading.
It does not; what 'before' refers to is not stated.
questions.explain: Elliptical: no verb, no stated referents; दशाद्याः can be read two ways.

questions.q: By the rule of दश + आद्याः → दशाद्याः, how is न + आगच्छति (does not come) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + आ.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ, as दश + आद्याः → दशाद्याः.
questions.explain: न + आगच्छति = नागच्छति, like दश + आद्याः = दशाद्याः.
questions.teaches: अ before आ merges into आ: दश + आद्याः → दशाद्याः.

questions.q: By unit 54, what does the first pair carry?
optionExplain: Right: द्वे वहतोऽन्नम्: two carry food.
Water is carried by the second pair.
Urine is carried by the third pair.
Śukra is carried by the fourth pair.
questions.explain: The first pair carries food, with the intestines as resting-place.

questions.q: Put the items of unit 54 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Food, water, urine, semen; and two release.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two carry food, water, urine, śukra; and two release.
questions.rule: अन्न, तोय, मूत्र, शुक्र; वहतः, मुञ्चतः.
questions.teaches: वहतः and मुञ्चतः are 3rd person dual present: 'the two carry / release', agreeing with द्वे.

questions.q: Which split of वहतोऽन्नम् in unit 54 is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: वहतान्नम्.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ drops (ऽ): वहतोऽन्नम्.
ए + अ would give वहतेऽन्नम्, with ए kept.
औ + अ would give आव्: वहतावन्नम्.
questions.explain: वहतः (the two carry) + अन्नम् (food): अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.rule: अः before अ → ओ, with the अ shown as ऽ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 54?
options: The line states what is released
optionExplain: Right: द्वे तोयम्.
The object of मुञ्चतः is not stated.
Water is carried by two (द्वे तोयम्), not eight.
Right: every item has द्वे (two).
questions.explain: Pairs for food, water, urine, śukra, and a releasing pair; what is released is unstated.

questions.q: By the rule of वहतः + अन्नम् → वहतोऽन्नम्, how is नरः + अयम् (this man) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: आ comes from अ + अ with no visarga; here अः meets अ.
अः drops to अ only before vowels other than अ.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ drops (ऽ), as वहतः + अन्नम् → वहतोऽन्नम्.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: नरः + अयम् = नरोऽयम्, like वहतः + अन्नम् = वहतोऽन्नम्.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is elided (ऽ): वहतः + अन्नम् → वहतोऽन्नम्.

questions.q: By unit 55, what is named for women?
optionExplain: Śukra is named for a man (नरस्य, card 51), not for women; unit 55 names ārtava.
Sveda is not named in unit 55.
Mūtra is not named in unit 55.
Right: नारीणामार्तवम्: of women, ārtava.
questions.explain: Those very two: of women, ārtava.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 55 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Those two, very, of women, ārtava.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Those very two: of women, ārtava.
questions.teaches: नारीणाम् is the genitive plural of नारी: 'of women'.

questions.q: Why are ते and एव not joined in unit 55?
options: ते is a dual in ए, which takes no sandhi
Sandhi is never made before the word एव
ते ends in a consonant, so no vowel joins
The print dropped a letter between the two
optionExplain: Right: Dual endings in ए stay unjoined before a vowel (data: ते = f. nom. du.).
Sandhi is made before एव (तत्र + एव → तत्रैव).
ते ends in the vowel ए.
No flag is noted; the separation is regular.
questions.explain: ते (dual) + एव: a dual in ए stays unjoined.
questions.rule: A dual ending in ई, ऊ or ए takes no sandhi before a vowel.

questions.q: Which verb is understood in unit 55?
options: Are grasped, taken over from unit 50
optionExplain: अभितर्पयन्ति belongs to the remaining eight of unit 56.
Right: Data: the verb (carry) is carried from unit 54 and not supplied.
गृह्यन्ते is said of the sense-objects in unit 50.
स्वपिति is one of the acts of unit 51.
questions.explain: Those very two (carry) ārtava in women.

questions.q: By the rule of ते एव, how is फले + अत्र (the two fruits here) written in a new example?
optionExplain: ए + अ → एऽ is for an ए that is not a dual ending.
अय् comes from ए before a vowel, but not from a dual ए.
Right: The dual in ए stays unjoined, as ते एव.
The dual ए does not turn into आ; it stays: फले अत्र.
questions.explain: फले (two fruits) + अत्र stays फले अत्र, like ते एव.
questions.rule: Dual -ए before a vowel: no sandhi.
questions.teaches: Dual forms ending in ई, ऊ or ए take no sandhi before a vowel: ते एव, फले अत्र.

questions.q: By unit 56, what do the remaining eight do?
optionExplain: Tears are not named in unit 56.
Urine is not named in unit 56.
Food is carried by two (unit 54), not by the remaining eight.
Right: शेषास्त्वष्टौ ... स्वेदमभितर्पयन्ति.
questions.explain: The remaining eight, running crosswise, satiate the sweat.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 56 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Two, (expelling, conjectural), bound to the large intestine; the remaining eight, crosswise, satiate the sweat.
questions.rule: द्वे → वज्र्रोनिरसन्यौ → स्थूलांत्रप्रतिबद्धे → शेषास्त्वष्टौ → तिरश्चीनाः → स्वेदमभितर्पयंति.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: स्थूल-अन्त्र-प्रतिबद्धे = bound to the large intestine; शेषाः तिरश्चीनाः = the remaining, crosswise; स्वेद = sweat.
questions.rule: स्थूल, अन्त्र, प्रतिबद्ध, शेष, तिरश्चीन, स्वेद.
questions.teaches: स्थूलान्त्र = स्थूल (large) + अन्त्र (intestine), with अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which split of शेषास्त्वष्टौ in unit 56 is right?
optionExplain: Right: Visarga before त → स्; उ before अ → व्: शेषास्त्वष्टौ.
त् + त would give शेषात्तु, not शेषास्तु.
औ before अ would give आव्: तावष्टौ.
आ + अ would give आ: त्वाष्टौ.
questions.explain: शेषाः (remaining) + तु (but) + अष्टौ (eight).
questions.rule: Visarga before त → स्; उ + a different vowel → व्.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 56?
options: Two are bound to the large intestine
optionExplain: It is conjectural: the printed word gives no sense.
Right: स्थूलान्त्रप्रतिबद्धे (f. nom. du.).
Śukra is not named in unit 56; they satiate the sweat.
Right: तिरश्चीनाः.
questions.explain: Two bound to the large intestine; eight crosswise that satiate the sweat.

questions.q: By the rule of तु + अष्टौ → त्वष्टौ, how is तु + अत्र (but here) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as तु + अष्टौ → त्वष्टौ.
त्वा- would need आ; here उ meets a short अ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ; here उ meets अ.
questions.explain: तु + अत्र = त्वत्र, like तु + अष्टौ = त्वष्टौ.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तु + अष्टौ → त्वष्टौ.

questions.q: By unit 57, what happens to the four that go crosswise?
options: Reaching the heart, they become three
They stay single and are not divided
They carry the food and the water
optionExplain: That is said of the upward-going ones (card 48).
भिद्यमानाः says they are being divided.
Right: भिद्यमानाः सुबहुधा: being divided, very manifold.
Food and water pairs are in unit 54, not these four.
questions.explain: The four crosswise ones, being divided, become very manifold.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 57 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Crosswise-going four, being divided, very manifold, become: thus said, before.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four crosswise-going ones, dividing, become very manifold; said before.
questions.rule: तिर्यक्, गामिनी, चतस्रः, भिद्यमान, सुबहुधा, प्राक्.
questions.teaches: भिद्यमान is a present passive participle of √भिद्: 'being split'.

questions.q: Which split of तिर्यग्गामिन्यः in unit 57 is right?
optionExplain: त् before ग would give द्: तिर्यद्गामिन्यः.
म् before a consonant would be written ं: तिर्यंगामिन्यः.
अः before a voiced consonant would give ओ: तिर्योगामिन्यः.
Right: क् before a voiced consonant (ग) becomes ग्: तिर्यग्गामिन्यः.
questions.explain: तिर्यक् (crosswise) + गामिन्यः (going): क् → ग् before ग.
questions.rule: A final क् before a voiced consonant → ग्.

questions.q: In unit 57, how are चतस्रः + भिद्यमानाः joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant (भ) becomes ओ.
आ does not come from अः before a consonant.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
स् comes from a visarga before त/थ, not before भ.
questions.explain: चतस्रः + भिद्यमानाः = चतस्रो भिद्यमानाः.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: By the rule of तिर्यक् + गामिन्यः → तिर्यग्गामिन्यः, how is वाक् + देवी joined in a new example?
optionExplain: क् does not stay before a voiced consonant.
Right: क् before a voiced consonant (द) becomes ग्, as in तिर्यग्गामिन्यः.
च् is not the sandhi form of क् before द.
ख् is not voiced; before द the क् becomes ग्.
questions.explain: वाक् + देवी = वाग्देवी, like तिर्यक् + गामिन्यः = तिर्यग्गामिन्यः.
questions.rule: Final क् before a voiced consonant → ग्.
questions.teaches: A final क् becomes ग् before a voiced consonant: तिर्यक् + गामिन्यः → तिर्यग्गामिन्यः.

questions.q: By unit 58, how many srotas (openings) do men have?
optionExplain: Three are the others added for women.
Nine for men; twelve would add the women's three.
Right: स्रोतांसि पुंसां नव: the srotas of men are nine.
Thirteen is the count of the inner srotas (unit 59).
questions.explain: The srotas of men are nine.

questions.q: Put the men's openings in the order of unit 58.
questions.explain: Ears, eyes, nostrils, mouth, anus, urinary passage.
questions.rule: कर्णौ → नेत्रे → नासापुटौ → मुखं → पायुः → मूत्रपथः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Ears, eyes, nostrils, mouth, anus; the breasts for women.
questions.rule: कर्णौ, नेत्रे, नासापुटौ, मुखम्, पायुः, स्तनौ.
questions.teaches: The duals count two each: कर्णौ, नासापुटौ, स्तनौ (m. -औ) and नेत्रे (n. -ए).

questions.q: By unit 58, which is one of the women's three others, not of the men's nine?
optionExplain: The mouth is among the men's nine.
The anus is among the men's nine.
The urinary passage is among the men's nine.
Right: स्त्रीणां स्तनौ: the breasts are among the women's three.
questions.explain: Women's three others: two breasts and the blood-passage.
questions.rule: अन्यानि च त्रीणि स्त्रीणां स्तनौ रक्तपथश्च.

questions.q: Which are among the men's nine by unit 58?
optionExplain: Right: नासापुटौ.
रक्तपथ is among the women's three others.
Right: मूत्रपथः.
स्तनौ are among the women's three others.
questions.explain: Men's nine: ears, eyes, nostrils, mouth, anus, urinary passage.

questions.q: By the pattern of कर्ण → कर्णौ (the two ears), what is the nominative dual of the masculine हस्त (hand)?
optionExplain: Right: A masculine अ-stem takes -औ in the nominative dual, as कर्ण → कर्णौ.
हस्ताः is the nominative plural: hands, more than two.
For masculine हस्त, हस्ते is the locative singular: in the hand.
हस्तम् is the accusative singular: the hand.
questions.explain: हस्तौ = the two hands, like कर्णौ = the two ears.
questions.teaches: A masculine अ-stem takes -औ in the nominative dual: कर्ण → कर्णौ, नासापुट → नासापुटौ.

questions.q: By unit 59, how many are the other inner srotas?
optionExplain: Nine are the men's outer openings (unit 58).
Right: त्रयोदश: thirteen.
Three are the women's added openings (unit 58).
Twenty-four is not the count of the inner srotas.
questions.explain: The other inner srotas, seats of life, are thirteen.

questions.q: Put the five of whom the srotas are seats in the order of unit 59.
questions.explain: Prāṇa, water, food, dhātu, mala.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Other inner srotas: seats of life, thirteen; seats of prāṇa, water ...
questions.rule: अपर, अन्तः, जीवित, आयतन, त्रयोदश, उदक.
questions.teaches: आयतन = seat, abode: the srotas are called seats of life and of prāṇa, water, food, dhātu, mala.

questions.q: Which split of प्राणोदक in unit 59 is right?
optionExplain: अः before a vowel other than अ becomes अ with no join: प्राण उदक.
ए before उ would give अयु or अ उ, not ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: प्राण + उदक → प्राणोदक.
औ before उ would give आवु: प्राणावुदक.
questions.explain: प्राण (vital breath) + उदक (water): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: What does unit 59 leave unlisted?
options: The number of the inner srotas
That the srotas are seats of life
That the srotas are seats of food
optionExplain: The number is printed: त्रयोदश.
Printed: जीवितायतनानि.
Printed: अन्न is among the five.
Right: The line gives the count, not the list (cards 60 to 73 name some).
questions.explain: Count and function are given; the thirteen are not listed here.

questions.q: By the rule of प्राण + उदक → प्राणोदक, how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as प्राण + उदक → प्राणोदक.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + उ.
अ does not drop before उ; the two merge into ओ.
आ comes from अ + अ/आ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like प्राण + उदक = प्राणोदक.
questions.teaches: अ before उ merges into ओ: प्राण + उदक → प्राणोदक.

questions.q: By unit 60, what is the root of the prāṇa-carrying (srotas)?
options: The palate and the kloma organ
The heart and the great channel
The navel and the large intestine
The neck and the two nostrils
optionExplain: Palate and kloma are the roots of the water-carrying ones (unit 64).
Right: हृदयं मूलं महास्रोतश्च.
Navel and intestine are not named in unit 60.
Neck and nostrils are not named in unit 60.
questions.explain: Of the prāṇa-carrying ones, the root is the heart and the great channel.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: There, of the prāṇa-carrying ones, the root is the heart ...

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 60 in the line's order.
questions.explain: There, of the prāṇa-carrying, the heart the root, and the great channel.
questions.teaches: Each srotas entry names its carriers in the genitive plural (-वाहिनाम्), then its root (मूलम्).

questions.q: Which split of महास्रोतश्च in unit 60 is right?
optionExplain: म् before a consonant would be written ं: महास्रोतं च.
त् before च would give च्: महास्रोतच्च.
Right: Visarga before च → श्: महास्रोतश्च.
ए before a consonant stays ए: महास्रोते च.
questions.explain: महास्रोतः (great channel) + च (and): visarga → श् before च.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 60?
options: The line identifies the great channel
The palate is named as a root
The heart is named as a root
The root is given for the prāṇa-carrying ones
optionExplain: It does not; the identity of mahāsrotas is disputed.
The palate is the root of the water-carrying ones (unit 64).
Right: हृदयं मूलम्.
Right: प्राणवाहिनाम्.
questions.explain: Of the prāṇa-carrying ones: heart and great channel; the great channel is not identified.

questions.q: By the pattern of प्राणवाहिन् → प्राणवाहिनाम् (of the carrying ones), what is the genitive plural of बलिन् (strong)?
optionExplain: बलिनः is nominative/accusative plural or genitive/ablative singular, not genitive plural.
बलिभिः is the instrumental plural: by the strong.
बलिने is the dative singular: for the strong one.
Right: An इन्-stem takes -इनाम् in the genitive plural, as वाहिन् → वाहिनाम्.
questions.explain: बलिनाम् = of the strong, like प्राणवाहिनाम् = of the prāṇa-carrying.
questions.teaches: An इन्-stem takes -इनाम् in the genitive plural: प्राणवाहिन् → प्राणवाहिनाम्.

questions.q: By unit 61, what happens to the prāṇa-carrying srotas through these causes?
optionExplain: Right: दुष्यन्ति: they become vitiated, spoiled.
Becoming manifold is said of the crosswise four (unit 57).
Nourishing is not what unit 61 says; दुष्यन्ति = vitiated.
Bound is said in unit 56; unit 61 says दुष्यन्ति.
questions.explain: By these causes they become vitiated.

questions.q: Put the causes in the order of unit 61.
questions.explain: Wasting, dryness, thirst, hunger, exertion, holding back of urges.
questions.rule: क्षय → रौक्ष्य → पिपासा → क्षुद् → व्यायाम → वेगधारण.

questions.q: Match each cause of unit 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Wasting, dryness, thirst, hunger, exertion, holding back of urges.
questions.rule: क्षय, रौक्ष्य, पिपासा, क्षुध्, व्यायाम, वेगधारण.
questions.teaches: वेगधारण = वेग (natural urge) + धारण (holding back).

questions.q: In unit 61, which word means thirst, not hunger?
optionExplain: क्षुध् = hunger.
Right: पिपासा = thirst.
क्षय = wasting, loss.
रौक्ष्य = dryness.
questions.explain: पिपासा is thirst; क्षुध् is hunger.

questions.q: Which split of आदिभिर्दुष्यंति in unit 61 is right?
optionExplain: म् before a consonant would be written ं: आदिभिं दुष्यन्ति.
-भ्यः before द would give आदिभ्यो दुष्यन्ति.
Right: After इ, a visarga before a voiced consonant (द) becomes र्.
ए before a consonant stays ए: आदिभे दुष्यन्ति.
questions.explain: आदिभिः (by ... and the like) + दुष्यन्ति (become vitiated): इः → इर् before द.
questions.rule: A visarga after इ before a voiced sound → र्.

questions.q: By the rule of आदिभिः + दुष्यन्ति → आदिभिर्दुष्यन्ति, how is हरिः + गच्छति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The visarga after इ does not drop here; it becomes र्.
स् comes from a visarga before त/थ, not before ग.
Lengthening with loss of र् happens only before र, not before ग.
Right: After इ, a visarga before a voiced consonant becomes र्.
questions.explain: हरिः + गच्छति = हरिर्गच्छति, like आदिभिः + दुष्यन्ति = आदिभिर्दुष्यन्ति.
questions.rule: इः before a voiced sound → इर्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced sound: आदिभिः + दुष्यन्ति → आदिभिर्दुष्यन्ति.

questions.q: By unit 62, what does the list of features describe?
optionExplain: Right: All the adjectives agree with उच्छ्वसनम्, breathing.
Thirst is a cause in unit 61, not what unit 62 describes.
Holding back urges is a cause in unit 61, not what unit 62 describes.
Sweat is not named in unit 62.
questions.explain: Unit 62 describes the breathing.

questions.q: Put the features of the breathing in the order of unit 62.
questions.explain: Excessively released, obstructed, agitated, scanty, frequent, with sound and pain.
questions.rule: अतिसृष्टं → प्रतिबद्धं → कुपितम् → अल्पाल्पम् → अभीक्ष्णं → सशब्दशूलम्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The breathing: excessively released, obstructed, agitated, scanty or frequent.
questions.rule: अतिसृष्ट, प्रतिबद्ध, कुपित, अल्पाल्प, अभीक्ष्ण, उच्छ्वसन.
questions.teaches: All the adjectives are neuter, agreeing with उच्छ्वसनम् (breathing).

questions.q: In unit 62, which word means 'obstructed, checked'?
optionExplain: अतिसृष्ट = excessively released.
Right: प्रतिबद्ध = obstructed, checked.
कुपित = agitated, disturbed.
अभीक्ष्ण = frequent.
questions.explain: प्रतिबद्ध = obstructed; अतिसृष्ट = excessively released.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 62?
options: The line names the disease śvāsa
optionExplain: Right: the line has adjectives and a noun only.
Śvāsa is named in unit 63, not here.
Not settled: वा follows only the last pair.
Right: they are neuter, like उच्छ्वसनम्.
questions.explain: No verb; the neuter adjectives describe the breathing; the reach of वा is open.

questions.q: By the rule of अल्प + अल्प → अल्पाल्प, how is न + अस्ति (is not) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as अल्प + अल्प → अल्पाल्प.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like अल्प + अल्प = अल्पाल्प.
questions.teaches: अ before अ merges into आ: अल्प + अल्प → अल्पाल्प.

questions.q: By unit 63, the treatment is as in which disorder?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in unit 63.
Thirst is not named in unit 63.
Cough is not named in unit 63.
Right: श्वासवत्साधनम्: treatment as in śvāsa.
questions.explain: There, the treatment is as in śvāsa.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: There, the treatment is as in śvāsa.

questions.q: What does unit 63 leave unsaid about the treatment?
options: Its details: it points to śvāsa's treatment
Whether there is any treatment at all
In which case the treatment is applied
optionExplain: Right: The treatment is given elsewhere and not repeated.
A treatment is named: साधनम्, as in śvāsa.
The disorder is named: श्वासवत्, as in śvāsa.
तत्र (there) ties it to the case of the prāṇa-carrying srotas.
questions.explain: The line names the model (śvāsa) but gives no details.
questions.teaches: -वत् after a noun as an indeclinable means 'as in, like': श्वासवत् = as in śvāsa.

questions.q: Which split of श्वासवत्साधनं in unit 63 is right?
optionExplain: A visarga before स stays ः or becomes स्: श्वासवः साधनम्.
Right: त् before स stays त्: श्वासवत्साधनम्.
न् before स stays न्; it does not become त्.
ए before a consonant stays ए: श्वासवते साधनम्.
questions.explain: श्वासवत् (as in śvāsa) + साधनम् (treatment).
questions.rule: Final त् before स stays त्.

questions.q: In unit 63 the treatment follows that of ____ (breathlessness). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: श्वास = breathlessness: श्वासवत्साधनम्.
questions.teaches: श्वास = breathlessness (probably dyspnoea of the asthma type).

questions.q: By the pattern of श्वासवत् (as in śvāsa), what does ज्वरवत् mean in a new example?
optionExplain: -वत् does not mean after.
-वत् does not mean without.
Right: -वत् = like, as in: ज्वरवत् = as in fever.
-वत् does not mean caused by.
questions.explain: ज्वरवत् = as in fever, like श्वासवत् = as in śvāsa.
questions.rule: Noun + वत् = as in, like that noun.
questions.teaches: -वत् after a noun as an indeclinable means 'as in, like': श्वासवत्, ज्वरवत्.

questions.q: By unit 64, what is the root of the water-carrying (srotas)?
options: The heart and the great channel
The tongue and the two jaws
The navel and the large bowel
optionExplain: Those are the roots of the prāṇa-carrying ones (unit 60).
Tongue and jaws are not named in unit 64.
Navel and bowel are not named in unit 64.
Right: उदकवाहिनां तालु मूलं क्लोम च.
questions.explain: Of the water-carrying ones, the root is the palate and the kloma.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 64 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of the water-carrying, the palate, the root, and the kloma.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of the water-carrying ones, the root is the palate ...
questions.teaches: उदकवाहिनाम् = उदक (water) + वाहिन् (carrying), genitive plural: of the water-carrying ones.

questions.q: In unit 64, which word means 'palate'?
optionExplain: Right: तालु = palate.
मूल = root, origin.
उदक = water.
वाहिन् = carrying; वाहिनाम् = of the carrying ones.
questions.explain: तालु is the palate; मूलम् is the root.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 64?
options: The palate is named as a root
क्लोमच is printed run together for क्लोम च
The heart is named as a root
optionExplain: It is not printed; the 'ones' are understood.
Right: तालु मूलम्.
Right: data note.
The heart is the root of the prāṇa-carrying ones (unit 60).
questions.explain: Palate and kloma are the roots; 'srotas' is understood; क्लोम च is printed joined.

questions.q: By the rule of मूलम् + क्लोम → मूलं क्लोम, how is फलम् + खादति (eats the fruit) written in a new example?
optionExplain: The म् does not drop; it is written as ं.
Right: Final म् before a consonant in a sentence is written ं, as मूलं क्लोम.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from अम्.
फलः changes the word; the ending -म् stays as ं.
questions.explain: फलम् + खादति = फलं खादति, like मूलम् + क्लोम = मूलं क्लोम.
questions.teaches: Final म् before a consonant inside a sentence is written as anusvāra: मूलं क्लोम, फलं खादति.

questions.q: By unit 65, which is a sign once the water-carrying srotas are vitiated?
optionExplain: The left side is a root of the food-carrying ones (unit 67), not a sign here.
Noisy breathing belongs to the prāṇa-carrying ones (unit 62).
Right: ततोऽतितृष्णा: then excessive thirst.
No yellow colour is named in unit 65.
questions.explain: Then come excessive thirst, dry mouth, ringing in the ears and seeing darkness.

questions.q: Put the signs in the order of unit 65.
questions.explain: Excessive thirst, dryness of the mouth, ringing in the ears, seeing darkness.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Causes include fear and excessive drinking; the signs are thirst, dry mouth, ear-ringing, darkness.
questions.rule: अतितृष्णा, मुखशोष, कर्णक्ष्वेडन, तमोदर्शन, भय, अतिपान.
questions.teaches: मुखशोष = मुख (mouth) + शोष (drying): a tatpuruṣa, 'drying of the mouth'.

questions.q: Which split of तमोदर्शनं in unit 65 is right?
optionExplain: आ before a consonant stays आ: तमादर्शनम्.
म् before a consonant would be written ं: तमंदर्शनम्.
औ before a consonant stays औ: तमौदर्शनम्.
Right: अस् before a voiced consonant (द) becomes ओ: तमोदर्शनम्.
questions.explain: तमस् (darkness) + दर्शनम् (seeing): अस् → ओ before a voiced consonant.
questions.rule: अस् / अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 65?
options: A verb is printed with the signs
Fear is named among the causes
Seeing darkness is named among the signs
The line says what is drunk to excess
optionExplain: The signs have no verb (data note).
Right: भय.
Right: तमोदर्शनम्.
अतिपान does not say what is drunk.
questions.explain: Fear is a cause and seeing darkness a sign; āma and the drink are left unclear.

questions.q: By the rule of अतिपान + उष्ण → अतिपानोष्ण, how is हित + उपदेशः joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as अतिपान + उष्ण → अतिपानोष्ण.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + उ.
अ does not drop before उ; the two merge into ओ.
आ comes from अ + अ/आ, not from अ + उ.

questions.section: रसादि स्रोतस् के मूल, दुष्टि व वेध

questions.q: Match each word of unit 80 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Having refused, one should treat; the one whose dart is extracted, as a fresh wound.
questions.teaches: प्रत्याख्याय is an absolutive in -य (with a prefix): done before the main verb उपाचरेत्.
questions.section: रसादि स्रोतस् के मूल, दुष्टि व वेध

questions.q: Which split of प्रत्याख्यायोपाचरेत् in unit 80 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: प्रत्याख्याय + उपाचरेत् → प्रत्याख्यायोपाचरेत्.
अः before उ would lose its visarga with no join: ...य उपाचरेत्.
The verb is उपाचरेत्; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
ए before उ gives अय् or अ, not ओ.
questions.explain: प्रत्याख्याय (having refused) + उपाचरेत् (one should treat): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: रसादि स्रोतस् के मूल, दुष्टि व वेध

questions.q: By unit 80, what is done with one pierced in a srotas before he is treated?
optionExplain: Unit 80 says nothing about leaving a dart in; line 2 is about one whose dart is extracted.
Right: प्रत्याख्यायोपाचरेत्: having refused, one should treat.
No purge is named in unit 80.
No fasting is named in unit 80.
questions.explain: Having refused (declined the case as hopeless), one should treat him.
questions.section: रसादि स्रोतस् के मूल, दुष्टि व वेध

questions.q: By the rule of सद्यः + व्रण → सद्योव्रण, how is मनः + बलम् joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अः before a voiced consonant gives ओ, not आ.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ or आ.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as सद्यः + व्रण → सद्योव्रण.
स् comes before त or थ, not before ब.
questions.explain: मनः + बलम् = मनोबलम्, like सद्यः + व्रण = सद्योव्रण.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: सद्यः + व्रण → सद्योव्रण.
questions.section: रसादि स्रोतस् के मूल, दुष्टि व वेध

questions.q: By unit 81, what are sirā and dhamanī?
optionExplain: The doṣas are not named in unit 81.
The malas are not named in unit 81.
The heart is not named in unit 81.
Right: स्रोतसामेव विशेषाः: particular forms of the srotas only.
questions.explain: Sirā and dhamanī are particular forms of the srotas.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 81 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Among these, of the srotas only, particular kinds: sirā and dhamanī.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 81 'particular kinds' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: विशेषाः = particular kinds, special forms (m. nom. pl.).
questions.teaches: विशेष = a particular kind; sirā and dhamanī are विशेषाः of the srotas.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Why is सिरा printed without a visarga in unit 81?
options: आः loses its visarga before the voiced ध
अः turned to ओ before the voiced ध
The visarga turned to र् before ध
The visarga turned to स् before ध
optionExplain: Right: सिराः + धमन्यः → सिरा धमन्यः (data note).
ओ comes from अः; सिराः ends in आः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ or आ.
स् comes before त or थ, not before ध.
questions.explain: सिराः (vessels) + धमन्यः: आः before a voiced sound drops the visarga.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 81?
options: Sirā and dhamanī are called forms of the srotas
The line gives a reason for this view
The verb 'are' is printed in the line
optionExplain: Right: स्रोतसामेव विशेषाः.
No reason is given in unit 81.
Right: the data labels this probable.
The copula is understood, not printed.
questions.explain: Sirā and dhamanī are forms of the srotas; vein and artery are probable equivalents; no verb.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of स्रोतसाम् + एव → स्रोतसामेव, how is गृहम् + एव joined in a new example?
optionExplain: म् becomes ं only before a consonant, not before a vowel.
Right: Final म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it, as स्रोतसाम् + एव → स्रोतसामेव.
म् does not drop; ऐ would need अ + ए.
ऐ needs अ + ए; here म् meets ए directly.
questions.explain: गृहम् + एव = गृहमेव, like स्रोतसाम् + एव = स्रोतसामेव.
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → म joined to the vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it: स्रोतसाम् + एव → स्रोतसामेव.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 82, what do the 'others' (anye) maintain?
optionExplain: Sameness is the opposite of अन्यत्व.
No root is named in unit 82.
Right: अन्यत्वमिच्छन्ति: they maintain a difference (otherness).
No number is given in unit 82.
questions.explain: Others maintain a difference (अन्यत्वम्).
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: But others maintain a difference.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: How is the word अन्यत्व built?
optionExplain: अन्न (food) has no य; the word is अन्य, other.
त्वम् (you) makes no sense here; -त्व is the suffix.
The word is अन्य (other) with -त्व, not अन + यत्व.
Right: -त्व makes an abstract noun: otherness, difference.
questions.explain: अन्यत्व = अन्य (other) + -त्व (-ness).
questions.rule: -त्व on a word = the state of being that.
questions.teaches: -त्व makes an abstract noun: अन्य (other) → अन्यत्व (otherness).
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of त्वन्यत्वम् in unit 82 is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तु + अन्यत्वम् → त्वन्यत्वम्.
अ + अ would give आ: त्वान्यत्वम्.
ए before अ would give तेऽन्यत्वम्, with ए kept.
म् before a vowel would give तुमन्यत्वम्.
questions.explain: तु (but) + अन्यत्वम् (difference): उ + अ → व.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Put the words of unit 82 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Others, but, a difference, maintain: अन्येत्वन्यत्वमिच्छंति.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of तु + अन्यत्वम् → त्वन्यत्वम्, how is मधु + अत्र joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, with अ first; here उ comes first.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as तु + अन्यत्वम् → त्वन्यत्वम्.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not उ + अ.
The अ does not vanish; the उ becomes व्.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like तु + अन्यत्वम् = त्वन्यत्वम्.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तु + अन्यत्वम् → त्वन्यत्वम्.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 83, which is one reason the three seem alike?
optionExplain: Colour is not named in unit 83.
Length is not named in unit 83.
Right: सौक्ष्म्याच्च: and from fineness.
Number is not named in unit 83.
questions.explain: Proximity, similar function and fineness make them seem alike.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 83 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Of the three, merely; from proximity, similar function and fineness; non-distinction as it were; is seen.
questions.rule: सिराधमनीस्रोतसां केवलं → परस्परसन्निकर्षात् → सदृशकर्मत्वात् → सौक्ष्म्याच्च → विभक्तकर्मणामप्यविभागइव → लक्ष्यते.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 83 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Mutual proximity, similar function, fineness; distinct functions, yet a non-distinction as it were.
questions.rule: परस्पर, सन्निकर्ष, सदृश, सौक्ष्म्य, विभक्त, अविभाग.
questions.teaches: The three reasons stand in the ablative (-आत्), 'from, because of'.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of सौक्ष्म्याच्च in unit 83 is right?
optionExplain: च्च is not a word; the first च् comes from त्.
आः before च would give सौक्ष्म्याश्च.
म् before च would give सौक्ष्म्यं च.
Right: त् before च becomes च्: सौक्ष्म्यात् + च → सौक्ष्म्याच्च.
questions.explain: सौक्ष्म्यात् (from fineness) + च (and): त् + च → च्च.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which does unit 83 state?
options: The three lie far from one another
The three are truly one channel
optionExplain: No: परस्परसन्निकर्ष is mutual proximity.
No: the non-distinction is only 'as it were' (इव).
Right: विभक्तकर्मणाम्, of distinct functions.
Right: अविभाग इव लक्ष्यते, seen as it were.
questions.explain: Their functions are distinct; they only seem undivided.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of सौक्ष्म्यात् + च → सौक्ष्म्याच्च, how is तस्मात् + च joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: त् before च becomes च्, as सौक्ष्म्यात् + च → सौक्ष्म्याच्च.
द् comes before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
त् does not stay before च; it becomes च्.
श् comes from a visarga, not from त्.
questions.explain: तस्मात् + च = तस्माच्च, like सौक्ष्म्यात् + च = सौक्ष्म्याच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: सौक्ष्म्यात् + च → सौक्ष्म्याच्च.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 84, what does आहुः mean?
optionExplain: Seeing would be from √दृश्, not आहुः.
Right: आहुः = they say (√अह्).
Going would be from √गम्, not आहुः.
Eating would be from √भुज्, not आहुः.
questions.explain: आहुः = they say.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 84 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Others, again, say.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 84 'again' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पुनः (again) stands for पुनर्; before a vowel the र् shows: पुनराहुः.
questions.teaches: पुनः = again; its र् shows before a vowel or a voiced sound.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of पुनराहुः in unit 84 is right?
optionExplain: राहुः is not 'they say'; the र् belongs to पुनर्.
म् before a vowel would give पुनमाहुः.
Right: पुनः stands for पुनर्; its र् shows before the vowel आ.
इ + आ would give पुन्याहुः.
questions.explain: पुनः (again) + आहुः (they say) → पुनराहुः.
questions.rule: पुनः = पुनर्; र् shows before a vowel.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 84?
optionExplain: No: आहुः (they say) is the verb.
Right: अपरे पुनराहुः.
Right: पुनः = again.
No names are given in unit 84.
questions.explain: Others, again, say; पुनः = again; the others are not named.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of पुनः + आहुः → पुनराहुः, how is पुनः + अपि (again too) joined?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः of an अस् ending; पुनः stands for पुनर्.
The र् of पुनर् does not drop before a vowel.
The अ of अपि does not vanish after र्.
Right: पुनः stands for पुनर्; its र् shows before a vowel, as in पुनराहुः.
questions.explain: पुनः + अपि = पुनरपि, like पुनः + आहुः = पुनराहुः.
questions.teaches: पुनः stands for पुनर्, whose र् shows before a vowel: पुनः + आहुः → पुनराहुः.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 85, what are srotas, sirā, dhamanī and the rest?
options: Names of the spaces of the dhātus
Names of the kinds of the doṣas
Names of the seats of the agni
Names of the parts of the heart
optionExplain: Right: धात्ववकाशानां ... नामानि: names of the spaces of the dhātus.
The doṣas are not the subject of unit 85.
Agni is not named in unit 85.
The heart is not named in unit 85.
questions.explain: All are names, in the body, of the spaces of the dhātus.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Put the first five names of unit 85 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Srotas, sirā, dhamanī, carriers of rasa, nāḍī.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 85 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Openings closed and open; spaces perceptible and imperceptible.
questions.rule: संवृत, असंवृत, लक्ष्य, अलक्ष्य, अवकाश, छिद्र.
questions.teaches: अ- before a word negates it: संवृत / असंवृत, लक्ष्य / अलक्ष्य.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of पंथानोऽयनानि in unit 85 is right?
optionExplain: यनानि is not a word; the word is अयनानि (routes).
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is elided (ऽ): पन्थानोऽयनानि.
औ before a vowel would give पन्थानावयनानि.
ए before अ would give पन्थानेऽयनानि, with ए.
questions.explain: पन्थानः (paths) + अयनानि (routes): अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.rule: अः before अ → ओ, and the अ is elided (ऽ).
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which are among the names listed in unit 85?
optionExplain: Right: नाड्यः is in the list.
Marma is not in the list of unit 85.
Kaṇḍarā is not in the list of unit 85.
Right: निकेताश्च, and dwellings.
questions.explain: Nāḍī and dwellings (निकेत) are among the names; marma and kaṇḍarā are not.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of स्थानानि + आशयाः → स्थानान्याशयाः, how is अस्ति + आत्मा joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The इ is not lost; it becomes य्.
ई comes from इ + इ, not इ + आ.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as स्थानानि + आशयाः → स्थानान्याशयाः.
The vowel after य् stays long: आ.
questions.explain: अस्ति + आत्मा = अस्त्यात्मा, like स्थानानि + आशयाः = स्थानान्याशयाः.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: स्थानानि + आशयाः → स्थानान्याशयाः.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 86, what does अवकाशाः mean?
optionExplain: Signs would be लक्षणानि; अवकाश is space.
Roots would be मूलानि; अवकाश is space.
Seasons would be ऋतवः; अवकाश is space.
Right: अवकाशाः = spaces (m. nom. pl.).
questions.explain: अवकाशाः = spaces.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 86 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And these spaces.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 86, what case and number is अवकाशाः?
optionExplain: Right: -आः on a masculine अ-stem: nominative plural, the subject.
That would be अवकाशम्.
That would be अवकाशानाम्.
That would be अवकाशे.
questions.explain: अवकाशाः = nominative plural: 'the spaces', the subject.
questions.teaches: -आः on a masculine अ-stem marks the nominative plural: अवकाश → अवकाशाः.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of तेचावकाशाः in unit 86 is right?
optionExplain: वकाशाः is not a word; the word is अवकाशाः.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अवकाशाः → चावकाशाः.
आकाश is another word (sky); the print has व: चावकाशाः.
Neither तेच nor वकाशाः is a word here.
questions.explain: ते (these) + च (and) + अवकाशाः (spaces): अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 86?
options: The line has a printed verb
optionExplain: Right: अवकाशाः.
No verb is printed in unit 86.
-आः here is plural.
Right: ते च, and these.
questions.explain: The line names the spaces; च = and; no verb; plural.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of च + अवकाशाः → चावकाशाः, how is न + अस्ति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अवकाशाः → चावकाशाः.
The two अ give a long आ, not a short अ.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like च + अवकाशाः = चावकाशाः.
questions.teaches: Two short अ merge into a long आ: च + अवकाशाः → चावकाशाः.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 87, what do the agitated ones do to the dhātus?
optionExplain: Nourishing is not said; the verb is प्रकोपयन्ति.
Cleansing is not said; the verb is प्रकोपयन्ति.
Drying is not said; the verb is प्रकोपयन्ति.
Right: धातून् प्रकोपयन्ति: they agitate the dhātus.
questions.explain: Agitated, they agitate the dhātus.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 87 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Agitated, they agitate the dhātus.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: How are प्रकुपित and प्रकोपयन्ति related?
options: Both are past participles of one root
Both are nouns that mean 'anger' itself
They come from two different roots
optionExplain: Right: प्रकुपित is the past participle; प्रकोपयन्ति the causative.
प्रकोपयन्ति is a present verb, not a participle.
Neither is a noun here: one participle, one verb.
Both come from the one root √कुप् with प्र.
questions.explain: प्रकुपित = agitated; प्रकोपयन्ति = they make agitated: one root, two forms.
questions.teaches: प्रकुपित is the past participle (agitated); प्रकोपयन्ति is the causative present, 'they make agitated'.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of ...मार्गस्थांश्च in unit 87 is right?
optionExplain: आः before च would give ...स्थाश्च, with no anusvāra.
Right: न् before च becomes ंश्: ...स्थान् + च → ...स्थांश्च.
म् before च would give ...स्थां च, with no श्.
ए stays before च: ...स्थे च.
questions.explain: ...मार्गस्थान् (those on the paths, acc. pl.) + च: न् + च → ंश्च.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 87?
options: The dhātus are the object of the verb
The verb is printed in this line
optionExplain: No dhātu is named.
Right: धातून्, accusative plural.
Right: प्रकोपयन्ति.
प्रकुपिताः is nominative plural, with the subject.
questions.explain: धातून् is the object of the printed verb प्रकोपयन्ति; no dhātu is named.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of ...स्थान् + च → ...स्थांश्च, how is तान् + च joined in a new example?
optionExplain: न् does not stay plain before च.
न् before च gives ंश्, not ञ्.
Right: न् before च becomes ंश्, as ...स्थान् + च → ...स्थांश्च.
No vowel is added; न् gives ंश्.
questions.explain: तान् + च = तांश्च, like ...स्थान् + च = ...स्थांश्च.
questions.teaches: A final न् before च becomes ंश्: मार्गस्थान् + च → मार्गस्थांश्च.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 88, which verb is understood from unit 87?
optionExplain: No nourishing verb is in unit 87.
The verb of unit 87 is प्रकोपयन्ति, not 'carry'.
No cleansing verb is in unit 87.
Right: The data carries प्रकोपयन्ति (they agitate) from unit 87.
questions.explain: They too (agitate) those and the srotas.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each word of unit 88 to its meaning.
questions.explain: They too (agitate) those and the srotas.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: In unit 88 the word for too or also is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अपि = also, too; printed तेऽपि with its अ elided after ए.
questions.teaches: अपि = also; after ए its अ is elided (ऽ).
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of तेऽपि in unit 88 is right?
optionExplain: Right: ए before अ stays, and the अ is elided (ऽ): तेऽपि.
पि is not a word; ऽ marks a lost अ.
औ before a vowel would give तावपि.
म् before a vowel would give तमपि.
questions.explain: ते (they) + अपि (too): ए + अ → एऽ.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which are printed in unit 88?
optionExplain: No verb is printed; 'agitate' is understood.
Right: स्रोतांसि.
Right: तान्.
No doṣa is named in unit 88.
questions.explain: स्रोतांसि and तान् are printed; the verb is understood.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of ते + अपि → तेऽपि, how is वने + अस्मिन् joined in a new example?
optionExplain: आ comes from अ + अ; here ए meets अ.
Right: ए before अ stays and the अ is elided, as ते + अपि → तेऽपि.
अय् comes from ए before vowels other than अ.
ओ comes from अः, not from ए.
questions.explain: वने + अस्मिन् = वनेऽस्मिन्, like ते + अपि = तेऽपि.
questions.teaches: ए before अ stays, and the अ is elided (marked ऽ): ते + अपि → तेऽपि.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 89, what do the srotas and the dhātus (agitate)?
optionExplain: No doṣa is named in unit 89.
No mala is named in unit 89.
Right: धातून्: the dhātus (acc. pl.).
No sense organ is named in unit 89.
questions.explain: The srotas and the dhātus (agitate) the dhātus.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Put the words of unit 89 in the printed order.
questions.explain: The srotas, and the dhātus, (agitate) the dhātus.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Match each form in unit 89 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The srotas and the dhātus (agitate) the dhātus.
questions.teaches: धातु: -अवः marks the nominative plural (subject), -ऊन् the accusative plural (object).
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which form of धातु in unit 89 is the accusative plural (the object)?
optionExplain: धातवः is the nominative plural, the subject.
धातूनाम् is the genitive plural, and not printed here.
धातौ is the locative singular, and not printed here.
Right: -ऊन्: accusative plural of the masculine उ-stem.
questions.explain: धातून् = the dhātus as object; धातवः = the dhātus as subject.
questions.rule: Masculine उ-stem: nom. pl. -अवः, acc. pl. -ऊन्.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: Which split of धातवश्च in unit 89 is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: धातवश्च.
म् before च would give धातवं च.
ए stays before च: धातवे च.
त् before च would give धातवच्च.
questions.explain: धातवः (the dhātus) + च (and): visarga before च → श्.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By the rule of धातवः + च → धातवश्च, how is वृक्षाः + च joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The visarga after आ drops before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as धातवः + च → धातवश्च.
स् comes before त or थ, not before च.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
questions.explain: वृक्षाः + च = वृक्षाश्च, like धातवः + च = धातवश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: धातवः + च → धातवश्च.
questions.section: सिरा, धमनी व स्रोतस् का भेद

questions.q: By unit 90, what are the vitiators of all these?
optionExplain: Seasons are not named in unit 90.
Pierced srotas are not named in unit 90.
Right: दूषयितारो दुष्टा दोषाः: the vitiated doṣas.
Sense organs are not named in unit 90.
questions.explain: The vitiators of all these are the vitiated doṣas.
questions.rule: तेषां सर्वेषाम् एव दूषयितारो दुष्टा दोषाः.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 90 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Of these, of all indeed, the vitiators, vitiated, the doṣas.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 90 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of all these, the vitiators are the vitiated doṣas.
questions.teaches: दुष्ट (vitiated) and दूषयितृ (vitiator) both come from √दुष्: the doṣas are spoiled and they spoil.

questions.q: Which split of दूषयितारो दुष्टा in unit 90 is right?
optionExplain: औ stays औ before a consonant; the print has ओ.
म् before द would be written ं: दूषयितारं.
ए stays ए before a consonant; the print has ओ.
Right: अः before the voiced द becomes ओ: दूषयितारो दुष्टाः.
questions.explain: दूषयितारः (vitiators) + दुष्टाः (vitiated): अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 90?
options: The doṣas are named one by one
The line has a printed verb
The doṣas are called the vitiators
The vitiating doṣas are themselves vitiated
optionExplain: No: only दोषाः, with no names.
No: the copula is understood.
Right: दूषयितारो ... दोषाः.
Right: दुष्टाः दोषाः.
questions.explain: The vitiated doṣas are the vitiators; no names and no verb are printed.

questions.q: By the rule of दूषयितारः + दुष्टाः → दूषयितारो दुष्टाः, how is बालः + गच्छति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as दूषयितारः + दुष्टाः → दूषयितारो दुष्टाः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ or आ.
स् comes before त or थ, not before ग.
श् comes before च, छ or श, not before ग.
questions.explain: बालः + गच्छति = बालो गच्छति, like दूषयितारः + दुष्टाः = दूषयितारो दुष्टाः.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: दूषयितारः + दुष्टाः → दूषयितारो दुष्टाः.

questions.q: By unit 91, through what do they mostly become vitiated?
