optionExplain: No season is named in unit 91; the cause is agni's fault.
Right: अग्निदोषात्: through a fault of agni, the digestive fire.
The mind is not named in unit 91; the cause is agni's fault.
Blood is not named in unit 91; the cause is agni's fault.
questions.explain: They mostly become vitiated through a fault of agni.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 91 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And they mostly become vitiated through a fault of agni.

questions.q: In unit 91, what does the ablative ending -आत् of अग्निदोषात् express?
optionExplain: A place would need the locative (-ए), not the ablative -आत्.
Ownership would need the genitive (-स्य), not the ablative -आत्.
Right: The ablative here gives the source or cause: from, through a fault of agni.
A goal would need the accusative or dative, not the ablative -आत्.
questions.explain: अग्निदोषात् = from, through a fault of agni: the cause of the vitiation.
questions.rule: Ablative -आत् of an अ-stem: from, because of.
questions.teaches: The ablative singular -आत् of अ-stems can state a cause: अग्निदोषात् = through a fault of agni.

questions.q: Which split of दुष्यंत्यग्निदोषात् in unit 91 is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give दुष्यन्तेऽग्नि, with ए kept and ऽ.
अः + अ would give दुष्यन्तोऽग्नि.
यग्नि is not a word; the य् comes from the इ of दुष्यन्ति.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: दुष्यन्ति + अग्नि → दुष्यन्त्यग्नि.
questions.explain: दुष्यन्ति (become vitiated) + अग्निदोषात् (through agni's fault): इ + अ → य.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 91?
options: Agni here means the digestive fire
The unit describes the kind of fault of agni
प्रायशः (mostly) does not make agni the only cause
optionExplain: Right: the data reads agni as the digestive fire.
No kind of fault is described.
Right: 'mostly' leaves room; no other cause is named.
दुष्यन्ति is third person plural: they become vitiated.
questions.explain: Agni = digestive fire; 'mostly' does not make it the only cause.

questions.q: By the rule of दुष्यन्त्यग्नि, how is पतन्ति + अधः (they fall down) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as दुष्यन्ति + अग्नि → दुष्यन्त्यग्नि.
ई comes from इ + इ; here इ meets अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
The इ does not simply drop; it becomes य्.
questions.explain: पतन्ति + अधः = पतन्त्यधः, like दुष्यन्ति + अग्नि = दुष्यन्त्यग्नि.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: दुष्यन्ति + अग्निदोषात् → दुष्यन्त्यग्निदोषात्.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the six things listed in unit 92?
optionExplain: निद्रा is not in the compound of unit 92.
Right: वर्ण (complexion) is the fifth member of the compound.
स्मृति is not in the compound of unit 92.
क्षुधा is not in the compound of unit 92.
questions.explain: The six: lifespan, health, strength, growth, complexion, ojas.

questions.q: Put the six members of the compound of unit 92 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Lifespan, health, strength, growth, complexion, ojas.
questions.rule: आयुः → आरोग्य → बल → उपचय → वर्ण → ओजस्.

questions.q: Match each member of the compound of unit 92 to its meaning.
questions.explain: आयु, आरोग्य, बल, उपचय, वर्ण, ओजस्: lifespan, health, strength, growth, complexion, ojas.
questions.rule: आयुः, आरोग्य, बल, उपचय, वर्ण, ओजस्.
questions.teaches: The six form one dvandva compound; its last member takes the neuter plural ending: -ओजांसि.

questions.q: Which split of वर्णौजांसि in unit 92 is right?
optionExplain: अः before a vowel other than अ loses its visarga with no join: वर्ण ओजांसि.
ए before ओ does not give औ; ए becomes अय् (or अ).
Right: अ + ओ → औ: वर्ण + ओजांसि → वर्णौजांसि.
जांसि is not a word; the word is ओजांसि (ojas, plural).
questions.explain: वर्ण (complexion) + ओजांसि (ojas): अ + ओ → औ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 92 are certain from the data?
options: The six words form one compound in the neuter plural
The unit prints a verb for the sentence
optionExplain: It has six: आयुः, आरोग्य, बल, उपचय, वर्ण, ओजस्.
Right: one dvandva, neuter nominative plural.
No verb is printed; the statement is incomplete.
Right: उपचय = growth.
questions.explain: Sure: the compound and its meanings. Open: what the six are causes of.

questions.q: By the rule of बलोपचय (बल + उपचय), how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
अ + उ does not give ऊ; the two vowels merge into ओ.
Inside a compound the vowels are joined, not left side by side.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as बल + उपचय → बलोपचय.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like बल + उपचय = बलोपचय.
questions.teaches: अ + उ → ओ: बल + उपचय → बलोपचय.

questions.q: By unit 93, what state does food attain when it is digested by agni?
optionExplain: Right: पक्वम् अमृततां याति: digested, it attains the state of nectar.
Poison is the state of undigested (अपक्व) food.
Food does not become fire; agni digests it.
Water is not named in unit 93.
questions.explain: Digested food attains the state of nectar; undigested, of poison.

questions.q: Put the parts of the second line of unit 93 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Likewise food too, digested by that very agni, attains nectar-state; undigested, poison-state.

questions.q: Match each term of unit 93 to its meaning.
pairs: a kind of Pitta that colours
questions.explain: Rañjaka, bhūtāgni, dhātvagni depend on agni; digested food → nectar, undigested → poison.
questions.teaches: -ता makes a noun of state: अमृत → अमृतता (nectar-state), विष → विषता (poison-state).

questions.q: Which split of धात्वग्नयश्च in unit 93 is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give धाताग्नयः, with a long आ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्; अग्नयः + च → अग्नयश्च.
ओ + अ would give धातोऽग्नयः, with ओ kept.
A visarga after उ before a vowel becomes र्: धातुरग्नयः.
questions.explain: धातु (dhātu) + अग्नयः (fires) + च (and): उ + अ → व.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.

questions.q: By unit 93, what happens to food that is not digested (अपक्व)?
options: It attains the state of nectar
It attains the state of poison
It is turned into a dhātvagni
optionExplain: Nectar is the state of digested food.
Rañjaka depends on agni; food does not become it.
Right: अपक्वं च विषताम्: undigested, it attains the state of poison.
The dhātvagnis depend on agni; food does not become one.
questions.explain: Undigested food attains the state of poison.

questions.q: By the rule of रञ्जकादीनि (रञ्जक + आदीनि), how is देव + आलयः (temple) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The long आ of आलयः is not lost; अ + आ gives आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ, as रञ्जक + आदीनि → रञ्जकादीनि.
questions.explain: देव + आलयः = देवालयः, like रञ्जक + आदीनि = रञ्जकादीनि.
questions.teaches: अ + आ → आ: रञ्जक + आदीनि → रञ्जकादीनि.

questions.q: By unit 94, agni is a special kind of which doṣa?
optionExplain: Right: पित्तविशेषः ... अग्निः: agni is a special kind of Pitta.
Kapha is not named in unit 94; agni is a kind of Pitta.
Vāta is not named in unit 94; agni is a kind of Pitta.
Ojas is not a doṣa and is not named in unit 94.
questions.explain: A special kind of Pitta, named pācaka, is agni.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 94 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Among these, a special kind of Pitta named pācaka is agni: so it was stated earlier.

questions.q: By unit 94, the Pitta that is agni is named ____ (the digesting one). Type it in Devanagari or English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पाचक (the digesting one): पाचकसंज्ञोऽग्निः.
questions.teaches: पाचक, from √पच् (to cook, to digest), is the name of the Pitta that is agni.

questions.q: Which split of पाचकसंज्ञोऽग्निरिति in unit 94 is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give पाचकसंज्ञाग्निः, with no ओ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ; the visarga of अग्निः after इ before a vowel → र्.
ए + अ would give पाचकसंज्ञेऽग्निः, with ए kept.
रिति is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga of अग्निः.
questions.explain: पाचकसंज्ञः + अग्निः + इति → पाचकसंज्ञोऽग्निरिति.
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओऽ; इः + vowel → इर्.

questions.q: What does प्रागभिहितः tell the reader in unit 94?
options: That this will be taught later
That this is quoted from a Veda
That this is a new, own view
optionExplain: प्राक् means earlier, not later.
No Veda is named; प्राक् अभिहितः = stated earlier.
Right: प्राक् (earlier) + अभिहितः (stated): it was said before in the work.
It is a repeated statement, not a new one.
questions.explain: प्रागभिहितः = stated earlier.

questions.q: By the rule of प्रागभिहितः (प्राक् + अभिहितः), how is वाक् + ईशः joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The क् does not stay voiceless before a vowel; it becomes ग्.
ङ् comes before a nasal, not before a vowel.
च् does not come from क् here; क् becomes ग्.
Right: A final क् before a vowel (a voiced sound) becomes ग्, as प्राक् + अभिहितः → प्रागभिहितः.
questions.explain: वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः, like प्राक् + अभिहितः = प्रागभिहितः.
questions.teaches: A final क् before a vowel (a voiced sound) becomes ग्: प्राक् + अभिहितः → प्रागभिहितः.

questions.q: What does अन्ये पुनराचक्षते mean?
optionExplain: Right: अन्ये (others), पुनः (again), आचक्षते (they say).
आचक्षते means they say, not they ask.
आचक्षते is from आ-√चक्ष्, to say, not from a verb of coming.
आचक्षते is active in sense, 'they say'; it is not a passive.
questions.explain: Others, again, say.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 95 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Others, again, say.

questions.q: Complete unit 95: ____ पुनराचक्षते (others, again, say). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अन्ये = others: अन्ये पुनराचक्षते.
questions.teaches: अन्ये (nominative plural of अन्य) = others: the unnamed authorities whose view follows.

questions.q: Which split of पुनराचक्षते in unit 95 is right?
optionExplain: राचक्षते is not a word; the र् belongs to पुनर्.
Right: पुनः is पुनर् at heart; before the vowel आ its र् shows: पुनराचक्षते.
With a short अ the join would be पुनरचक्षते, not पुनराचक्षते.
ए before आ becomes अय् (or अ), not र्.
questions.explain: पुनः (again) + आचक्षते (they say) → पुनराचक्षते.

questions.q: In unit 95, what kind of form is आचक्षते?
optionExplain: Not passive: the others do the saying; -अते is a middle ending here.
A past participle would end in -त; आचक्षते is a finite verb.
Right: आ-√चक्ष् is used in the middle: आचक्षते = they say.
The optative would show -एत् or -यात्; this is present plural.
questions.explain: आचक्षते: present tense, third person plural, middle voice: they say.

questions.q: By the pattern of पुनराचक्षते, how is पुनः + अपि (again too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओऽ would come from a plain अः before अ; पुनः is पुनर्.
The र् of पुनर् does not drop before a vowel.
श् comes from a visarga before च, छ or श, not before a vowel.
Right: पुनः is पुनर् at heart; before a vowel its र् shows, as in पुनराचक्षते.
questions.explain: पुनः + अपि = पुनरपि, like पुनः + आचक्षते = पुनराचक्षते.
questions.teaches: पुनः is पुनर् at heart: before a vowel its र् shows (पुनराचक्षते, पुनरपि).

questions.q: By the view in unit 96, agni is the inner heat produced by what?
options: Doṣa, dhātu and mala coming together
Blood, flesh and fat coming together
The sun's heat entering the body
Food and water mixed in the stomach
optionExplain: Right: दोषधातुमलसन्निपातजनितः: produced by their coming together.
Blood, flesh and fat are not named in unit 96.
The sun is not named; the heat is produced within.
Food and water are not named in unit 96.
questions.explain: Agni = the inner heat produced by the coming together of doṣa, dhātu and mala.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 96 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Doṣa-dhātu-mala, produced by their coming together, the inner heat, whose seat and function are as indicated, is agni.
questions.rule: दोषधातुमल → सन्निपातजनितः → अन्तरूष्मा → यथानिर्दिष्ट → अधिष्ठानकर्मा → अग्निरिति.

questions.q: Match each word part of unit 96 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Produced by the coming together (of doṣa, dhātu, mala), the inner heat, with its seat and function as indicated.
questions.rule: सन्निपात, जनित, अन्तर्, ऊष्मा, अधिष्ठान, कर्म.
questions.teaches: यथानिर्दिष्टाधिष्ठानकर्मा is a bahuvrīhi: 'whose seat and function are as indicated', describing agni.

questions.q: Which split of जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा in unit 96 is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give जनितान्तरूष्मा, with no ओ.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the अ is dropped (ऽ): जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा.
ए + अ would give जनितेऽन्तरूष्मा, with ए kept.
न्तरूष्मा is not a word; the word is अन्तरूष्मा (inner heat).
questions.explain: जनितः (produced) + अन्तरूष्मा (inner heat): अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 96?
options: It names the seat of agni
It reports the view of the others of card 95
Mala here means a waste product
It calls agni a kind of Kapha
optionExplain: The seat is 'as indicated' earlier; it is not named here.
Right: the closing इति ends that reported view.
Right: mala = waste product (data).
Kapha is not named; agni is called the inner heat.
questions.explain: The view of others; agni = inner heat from doṣa, dhātu and mala (waste).

questions.q: By the rule of जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा, how is बालः + अपि (the boy too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: आ comes from आ + अ; here it is अः + अ.
र् comes from a visarga after other vowels (इ, उ ...), not after अ.
Right: अः + अ → ओ and the अ drops (ऽ), as जनितः + अन्तरूष्मा → जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा.
Before अ, अः becomes ओ with ऽ; the visarga is not simply dropped.
questions.explain: बालः + अपि = बालोऽपि, like जनितः + अन्तरूष्मा = जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped, marked ऽ: जनितः + अन्तरूष्मा → जनितोऽन्तरूष्मा.

questions.q: In the simile of unit 97, the food in the āmāśaya is like what?
options: Oil and ghee in a lamp
Milk and sugar in a churn
Wood and fire in a stove
Water and rice in a pot
optionExplain: No lamp is named; the simile is water and rice in a pot.
No churn is named; the simile is water and rice in a pot.
No stove is named; the simile is water and rice in a pot.
Right: स्थालीस्थमिवाम्बुतण्डुलम्: like water and rice in a pot.
questions.explain: The agni cooks the food as water and rice are cooked in a pot.

questions.q: Put the states of the food in the order printed in unit 97.
questions.explain: Eaten by rule → drawn into the koṣṭha by prāṇa → mass broken by liquids → softened by sneha → lying in the āmāśaya.

questions.q: Match each helper in unit 97 to what it does.
pairs: draws the food into the koṣṭha
questions.explain: Prāṇa draws in, liquids break apart, sneha softens, samāna kindles the agni.
questions.teaches: Each helper stands in the instrumental (-एन, -ऐः, -उना): प्राणेन वायुना, द्रवैः, स्नेहेन, समानेन.

questions.q: By unit 97, what does samāna do?
options: It draws the food into the koṣṭha
optionExplain: Right: अभिसन्धुक्षितः समानेन: agni is kindled by samāna.
That is prāṇa: प्राणेन वायुना कोष्ठमाकृष्टम्.
That is sneha: स्नेहेन मृदूकृतम्.
That is the liquids: द्रवैर्विभिन्नसंघातम्.
questions.explain: Samāna kindles agni; prāṇa draws in; liquids break; sneha softens.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 97?
options: Prāṇa draws the food into the koṣṭha
The unit says how long the cooking lasts
The agni cooks food lying in the āmāśaya
optionExplain: Right: प्राणेन वायुना कोष्ठमाकृष्टम्.
The liquids break its mass; sneha softens it.
No time is given in unit 97.
Right: आमाशयस्थम् ... पचति.
questions.explain: Prāṇa draws in; liquids break; sneha softens; agni cooks the food in the āmāśaya.

questions.q: By the rule of विधिवदभ्यवहृतम् (विधिवत् + अभ्यवहृतम्), how is जगत् + ईशः joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The त् does not stay voiceless before a vowel; it becomes द्.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्, as विधिवत् + अभ्यवहृतम् → विधिवदभ्यवहृतम्.
न् comes (optionally) from त् before a nasal, not before a vowel.
च्छ comes (optionally) from त् + श, not from त् + ई.
questions.explain: जगत् + ईशः = जगदीशः, like विधिवत् + अभ्यवहृतम् = विधिवदभ्यवहृतम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: विधिवत् + अभ्यवहृतम् → विधिवदभ्यवहृतम्.

questions.q: By unit 98, which doṣa does the food stir up first, as it is being cooked?
optionExplain: Pitta is stirred later, when the food has turned sour (unit 99).
Vāta is stirred later, in the pakvāśaya (unit 100).
Right: मधुरीभूतं कफं फेनीभूतम् उदीरयति: it stirs up Kapha.
Ojas is not a doṣa and is not named in unit 98.
questions.explain: First the food becomes sweet and stirs up Kapha, become foamy.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 98 in the printed order (after the first word).
questions.explain: Though of all tastes, being cooked, at first, become sweet, Kapha, become foamy, it stirs up.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 98 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Though of all tastes, being cooked, at first become sweet, it stirs up Kapha, become foamy.
questions.rule: सर्वरसम्, पच्यमानम्, आदौ, मधुरीभूतम्, फेनीभूतम्, उदीरयति.
questions.teaches: -ई-भूत means 'become X' (what it was not before): मधुर → मधुरीभूत, फेन → फेनीभूत.

questions.q: By unit 98, what taste does the food take on first while being cooked?
optionExplain: Sour comes later, with Pitta (unit 99).
Pungent comes later, in the pakvāśaya (unit 100).
Salty is not named in unit 98.
Right: आदौ मधुरीभूतम्: at first it becomes sweet.
questions.explain: At first the food becomes sweet.

questions.q: In unit 98, what does सर्वरसम् अपि add?
options: Even food of all tastes turns sweet first
Only food that is sweet stirs up Kapha
The food loses all its tastes in cooking
Each taste stirs up Kapha in its own turn
optionExplain: Right: सर्वरसम् अपि: though it has all tastes, it first becomes sweet.
The point is the reverse: even food of all tastes becomes sweet.
Losing tastes is not said; it becomes sweet at first.
No such turn-taking is stated; the food as a whole turns sweet.
questions.explain: Whatever its tastes, the food first turns sweet in cooking.

questions.q: By the pattern of मधुरीभूतम् (become sweet, from मधुर), what does शीतीभूतम् mean in a new example?
optionExplain: -ई-भूत does not mean 'very'; it means 'become'.
Right: -ई-भूत = has become X (what it was not): शीत → शीतीभूत, as मधुर → मधुरीभूत.
-ई-भूत marks a change into the state, not a natural one.
-ई-भूत says the change has happened, not that it is pending.
questions.explain: शीतीभूतम् = become cold, like मधुरीभूतम् = become sweet.
questions.teaches: An अ-stem with -ई-भूत means 'become X': मधुर → मधुरीभूत (become sweet).

questions.q: By unit 99, from where is the food falling away as it turns sour?
optionExplain: The pakvāśaya is reached later (unit 100); the food falls from the āmāśaya.
The mouth is not named in unit 99.
Right: आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्: falling away from the āmāśaya.
The heart is not named in unit 99.
questions.explain: Turned sour, the food falls away from the āmāśaya.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 99 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Then, burnt, turned sour, falling away from the āmāśaya, clear Pitta.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 99 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Burnt, turned sour, falling away (from the āmāśaya), (it stirs up) clear Pitta.
questions.teaches: The food's states are neuter nominatives (विदग्धम्, अम्लीभूतम्, च्यवमानम्); अच्छं पित्तम् is the object of the understood verb.

questions.q: By unit 99, which doṣa does the sour food stir up?
optionExplain: Kapha is stirred at the sweet stage (unit 98).
Vāta is stirred at the pungent stage (unit 100).
Rasa is not a doṣa; it is the essence made later (unit 103).
Right: अच्छं पित्तम् (उदीरयति): it stirs up clear Pitta.
questions.explain: Sour food stirs up clear Pitta.

questions.q: Which split of आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम् in unit 99 is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् before च becomes च्: आमाशयात् + च्यवमानम् → आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्.
A visarga before च becomes श्: आमाशयाश्च्यवमानम्.
ए stays before a consonant: आमाशये च्यवमानम्.
म् before च would give ं: आमाशयं च्यवमानम्.
questions.explain: आमाशयात् (from the āmāśaya) + च्यवमानम् (falling away): त् + च → च्च.

questions.q: By the rule of आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्, how is तत् + च (and that) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: द् does not come before च; त् becomes च्.
Right: त् before च becomes च्, as आमाशयात् + च्यवमानम् → आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्.
ज् comes before a voiced palatal (ज, झ), not before च.
श् comes from a visarga before च, not from त्.
questions.explain: तत् + च = तच्च, like आमाशयात् + च्यवमानम् = आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: आमाशयात् + च्यवमानम् → आमाशयाच्च्यवमानम्.

questions.q: By unit 100, which doṣa does the food stir up when it has turned pungent?
optionExplain: Kapha is stirred at the sweet stage (unit 98).
Pitta is stirred at the sour stage (unit 99).
Right: कटुकीभूतमनिलम्: it stirs up anila, that is Vāta.
Ojas is not a doṣa and is not named in unit 100.
questions.explain: Turned pungent in the pakvāśaya, the food stirs up anila (Vāta).

questions.q: Put the words of unit 100 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Having reached, and, the pakvāśaya, turned pungent, the wind.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 100 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Having reached the pakvāśaya, turned pungent, (it stirs up) the wind.
questions.teaches: प्राप्य is an absolutive in -य (prefix प्र + √आप्): having reached.

questions.q: By unit 100, where has the food arrived when it turns pungent?
optionExplain: The food falls away from the āmāśaya (unit 99); it does not arrive there now.
The heart is not named in unit 100.
The mouth is not named in unit 100.
Right: प्राप्य च पक्वाशयम्: having reached the pakvāśaya.
questions.explain: Having reached the pakvāśaya, the food turns pungent.

questions.q: Why does प्राप्य in unit 100 end in -य and not -त्वा?
options: The prefix प्र stands before the root
The sentence has a plural subject
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य: प्र + √आप् → प्राप्य.
Without a prefix आप् takes -त्वा: आप्त्वा.
-य here is the absolutive ending, not a passive marker.
The subject (the food) is singular; number does not decide -य.
questions.explain: Prefix + root → absolutive in -य: प्राप्य = having reached.
questions.rule: Absolutive: -त्वा without a prefix, -य with one.

questions.q: By the pattern of प्राप्य, what is the absolutive of प्र + √विश् (to enter) in a new example?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix; with प्र the ending is -य.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य, as प्र + √आप् → प्राप्य.
प्रविष्टः is a past participle, 'entered', not 'having entered'.
प्रविशति is the present tense, 'enters'.
questions.explain: प्र + √विश् → प्रविश्य (having entered), like प्र + √आप् → प्राप्य.
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its absolutive with -य: प्राप्य, प्रविश्य.

questions.q: In unit 101, what does यथास्वम् mean?
options: All of them at one and the same time
optionExplain: यथा- means 'according to', not 'against'.
यथास्वम् is about each one's own, not about time.
Right: यथास्वम् (ind.) = each according to its own.
No place is meant by यथास्वम्.
questions.explain: यथास्वम् = each according to its own.

questions.q: Put these readable parts of unit 101 in the printed order (the damaged middle is left out).
questions.explain: Then thus, the food moistened, ... by wind, scattered, each according to its own, only the five element-qualities lying in the food, cook.
questions.rule: ततश्चैवं → विक्लिन्नआहारे → वायुना → व्यस्तान्यथास्वं → पंचैवभूतगुणानाहारस्थान् → पचंति.

questions.q: Match each readable word of unit 101 to its meaning.
questions.explain: By wind ... each according to its own ... the element-qualities lying in the food ... cook.
questions.teaches: आहारस्थ = आहार + स्थ ('standing in'): the element-qualities that lie in the food.

questions.q: Which split of ततश्चैवं in unit 101 is right?
optionExplain: त् + च would give तच्चैवम्, with च्च.
अ + इ would give ए: ततश्चेवम्.
ऐवम् is not a word; the ऐ comes from च + एवम्.
Right: Visarga before च → श्; अ + ए → ऐ: ततश्चैवम्.
questions.explain: ततः (then) + च (and) + एवम् (thus) → ततश्चैवम्.
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च; अ + ए → ऐ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 101 does the data support?
options: विक्लिन्नआहारे is printed with its vowels joined
पंचातमक महाभूतन मयो is unclear in print
पचन्ति is a plural verb: they cook
optionExplain: It says five: पञ्चैव भूतगुणान्.
Not merged: the print keeps विक्लिन्न and आहारे side by side.
Right: damaged print, kept unsplit as unclear.
Right: पचन्ति, third person plural.
questions.explain: The middle words are unclear; पचन्ति is plural; who cooks is not certain.
questions.rule: पंचातमक महाभूतन मयो: unclear; पचंति: they cook.

questions.q: By the rule of पंचैव (पञ्च + एव), how is अत्र + एव (here indeed) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as पञ्च + एव → पञ्चैव.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + ए.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + ए.
य् is not inserted; अ + ए merge into ऐ.
questions.explain: अत्र + एव = अत्रैव, like पञ्च + एव = पञ्चैव.
questions.teaches: अ + ए → ऐ: पञ्च + एव → पञ्चैव, च + एवम् → चैवम्.

questions.q: By unit 102, what do the cooked ones nourish?
options: The doṣas that were stirred up in cooking
The element-qualities resting in the body
The digestive fire in the āmāśaya
The bones and the marrow of the body
optionExplain: The doṣas are not named in unit 102.
Right: देहाश्रितान् ... भूतगुणान् आप्याययन्ति.
Agni is not named in unit 102.
Bones and marrow are not named in unit 102.
questions.explain: Cooked, they nourish the element-qualities that rest in the body.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 102 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Those, cooked, again each according to its own, resting in the body, of their own nature, the element-qualities, nourish.
questions.rule: ते पक्काः → पुनर्यथास्वमेव → देहाश्रितांश्च → स्वाविकारभूतान् → भूतगुणानाप्याययंति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 102 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Cooked, again, they nourish the element-qualities resting in the body.
questions.teaches: आप्याययन्ति: causative of आ-√प्याय्, 'make grow, nourish', third person plural.

questions.q: Which split of देहाश्रितांश्च in unit 102 is right?
optionExplain: A visarga before च gives श्च with no ं: देहाश्रिताश्च.
म् before च gives ं with no श्: देहाश्रितं च.
Right: A final न् before च becomes ंश्: देहाश्रितान् + च → देहाश्रितांश्च.
ए stays before a consonant: देहाश्रिते च.
questions.explain: देहाश्रितान् (resting in the body) + च (and): न् + च → ंश्च.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 102 fit the data?
options: ते is taken as the element-qualities of card 101
The unit names the doṣas as what is nourished
The nourished qualities lie in the food
optionExplain: Right: the data's note reads te so.
Right: causative of आ-√प्याय्, make grow.
The doṣas are not named; the element-qualities resting in the body are.
They rest in the body (देहाश्रितान्).
questions.explain: ते = the element-qualities; they nourish those resting in the body; स्वाविकारभूतान् stays two-way.

questions.q: By the rule of देहाश्रितांश्च, how is तान् + च (and them) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The न् does not stay unchanged before च.
The nasal sound does not vanish; it stays as ं.
An श् stands between the ं and च.
Right: A final न् before च becomes ंश्, as देहाश्रितान् + च → देहाश्रितांश्च.
questions.explain: तान् + च = तांश्च, like देहाश्रितान् + च = देहाश्रितांश्च.
questions.teaches: A final न् before च becomes ंश्: देहाश्रितान् + च → देहाश्रितांश्च.

questions.q: By unit 103, what is the clear essence from digested food called?
optionExplain: Right: अच्छः सारभूतो रसाख्यः: a clear essence named rasa.
Kiṭṭa is the waste (mala), not the essence.
Ojas is not named in unit 103.
Sneha (oil) belongs to the simile, not to the products.
questions.explain: The clear essence is rasa; the waste is kiṭṭa.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 103 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the digested food, as from an oil ..., rasa (essence) and kiṭṭa (waste) are produced.
questions.rule: रस, किट्ट, पक्वात् आहारात्, स्नेहात्, अभिनिर्वर्तते.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 103 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Thus, from the digested food, as if from an oil with medicines inside, a clear essence named rasa, and a waste named kiṭṭa, is produced.
questions.teaches: The sentence runs: source (ablatives with a simile) → two products (rasa, kiṭṭa) → one singular verb.

questions.q: By unit 103, which product of the digested food is called mala?
options: Sneha, the oil of the simile
optionExplain: Rasa is the essence (सार), the opposite of the waste.
Right: किट्टाख्यश्च मलः: the waste named kiṭṭa.
Sneha belongs to the simile; it is not a product.
Ojas is not named in unit 103.
questions.explain: Mala = kiṭṭa; sāra = rasa.

questions.q: Why is सारभूतः printed सारभूतो before रसाख्यः in unit 103?
options: अः before every consonant becomes ओ
ओ marks the vocative case in this unit
अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ
ओ is a dual ending of the word here
optionExplain: Not before voiceless ones: before क, त, प ... it is not ओ.
सारभूतः is nominative; the ओ comes from sandhi.
Right: र is voiced: सारभूतः + रसाख्यः → सारभूतो रसाख्यः.
The word is singular; the ओ comes from sandhi.
questions.explain: अः + voiced consonant → ओ: सारभूतो रसाख्यः.

questions.q: By the rule of विविधौषध (विविध + औषध), how is वन + औषधिः (forest herb) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + औ.
आव् comes from औ before a vowel; here औ follows अ.
Inside a compound the vowels are joined, not left side by side.
Right: अ + औ → औ, as विविध + औषध → विविधौषध.
questions.explain: वन + औषधिः = वनौषधिः, like विविध + औषध = विविधौषध.
questions.teaches: अ + औ → औ: विविध + औषध → विविधौषध.

questions.q: By unit 104, what is filled by the essence and the waste?
options: The pores of the skin only
optionExplain: Right: स्रोतांसि ... आपूर्यन्ते: the srotas of the dhātus are filled.
The skin pores are not named in unit 104.
Unit 104 speaks of the srotas of the dhātus, not the stomach.
Neither is named in unit 104.
questions.explain: By the essence and the waste the srotas of the dhātus are filled.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 104 in the line's order.
questions.explain: By those two, of the same nature, of the bodily qualities, each its own, the srotas are filled in succession, unbroken.
questions.rule: ताभ्यां च सारमलाभ्यां → तदात्मकानामेव → शारीरगुणानां → यथास्वं → स्रोतांसि → पारंपर्येणाव्यवच्छिन्नसंतानमापूर्यंते.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 104 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Essence and waste fill the srotas in succession, unbroken.
questions.teaches: अ- negates: व्यवच्छिन्न 'cut off' → अव्यवच्छिन्न 'unbroken'; the stream of filling is never cut.

questions.q: By unit 104, how are the srotas filled?
options: All at once, in one single flood
In succession, in an unbroken stream
In breaks, the stream being cut off
Only during sleep, at night, in a trickle
optionExplain: पारम्पर्येण says in succession, not all at once.
Right: पारम्पर्येणाव्यवच्छिन्नसन्तानम्: in succession, unbroken.
अव्यवच्छिन्न means unbroken, not cut off.
No time of day is named in unit 104.
questions.explain: The filling goes in succession and in an unbroken stream.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 104?
options: ताभ्याम्, by those two, takes up the essence and the waste
The srotas are filled by the waste alone
The filling goes each according to its own, यथास्वम्
The unit names each dhātu one by one
optionExplain: Right: ताभ्यां च सारमलाभ्यां.
Both the essence and the waste are named (सारमलाभ्याम्).
Right: यथास्वं स्रोतांसि.
No dhātu is named one by one here; the lists come in units 109-114.
questions.explain: By essence and waste together the srotas are filled, each according to its own.
questions.rule: ताभ्यां च सारमलाभ्यां ... यथास्वं स्रोतांसि ... आपूर्यंते.

questions.q: By the rule of तत् + आत्मक → तदात्मक, how is सत् + आचार (good conduct) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् does not stay; it becomes द्.
The आ of आचार is kept long; nothing shortens it.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्, as तत् + आत्मक → तदात्मक.
त् may become न् (optionally) only before a nasal, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: सत् + आचार = सदाचार, like तत् + आत्मक = तदात्मक.
questions.rule: Final त् before a vowel → द्.
questions.teaches: A word-final त् becomes द् before a vowel: तत् + आत्मक → तदात्मक.

questions.q: By unit 105, what are nourished from the srotas?
optionExplain: The senses are not named in unit 105.
The mind is not named in unit 105.
No wind is named in unit 105.
Right: धातवः पुष्यन्ति: the dhātus are nourished.
questions.explain: From the srotas the dhātus are nourished.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 105 in the line's order.
questions.explain: From the srotas, according to division, the dhātus are nourished.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 105 to its meaning.
questions.explain: From the srotas, according to division, the dhātus thrive.
questions.teaches: पुष्यन्ति is a 3rd plural present of √पुष् (to thrive); its subject is the plural धातवः.

questions.q: Which split of स्त्रोतोभ्यश्च (printed for स्रोतोभ्यश्च) in unit 105 is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: स्रोतोभ्यः + च → स्रोतोभ्यश्च.
अश्च is not a word here; and अ + अ would give आ.
भ्यश्च is not a word; -भ्यः is the case ending of स्रोतस्.
म् before च would be written ं: स्रोतोभ्यां च.
questions.explain: स्रोतोभ्यः (from the srotas) + च (and): visarga before च → श्.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 105?
options: The srotas are nourished from the dhātus
The dhātus are nourished from the srotas
The unit explains what the division is
पुष्यन्ति is plural, agreeing with धातवः
optionExplain: The other way round: the dhātus from the srotas.
Right: स्रोतोभ्यश्च ... धातवः पुष्यन्ति.
The division is not explained in unit 105.
Right: both are plural.
questions.explain: From the srotas the dhātus (plural) are nourished; the division is not explained.

questions.q: By the rule of स्रोतोभ्यश्च, how is देवाः + च (and the gods) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: स् is the form before त/थ, not before च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as स्रोतोभ्यः + च → स्रोतोभ्यश्च.
After आ the visarga drops before a voiced sound or a vowel; च is not voiced.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
questions.explain: देवाः + च = देवाश्च, like स्रोतोभ्यः + च = स्रोतोभ्यश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: स्रोतोभ्यः + च → स्रोतोभ्यश्च.

questions.q: By unit 106, what is denied (न ... भवति) for the earlier srotas?
optionExplain: They are nourished (आप्यायमानानाम्); that is affirmed.
Only wasting (अपचय) is denied: नापचयो भवति. Nothing else is denied.
Right: नापचयो भवति: there is no wasting (apacaya).
They are kept up by the proper use of food; that is affirmed.
questions.explain: There is no wasting of the earlier srotas.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 106 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Even with the later ones entering, of the earlier srotas, in due time, by proper food, nourished, no wasting.
questions.rule: उत्तरोत्तरानुप्रवेशेऽपि च → पूर्वेषां स्रोतसां → यथाकालं → सम्यगाहारोपयोगेन → परिणामवताप्यायमानानां → नापचयो भवति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 106 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of the earlier ones, nourished properly in due time, there is no wasting.
questions.teaches: उत्तर 'later' and पूर्व 'earlier' are this unit's pair: the later ones enter, yet the earlier do not waste.

questions.q: Which split of नापचयो in unit 106 is right?
optionExplain: पचयः is not the word here; the word is अपचयः (wasting).
अ + उ would give ओ: नोपचयो; उपचय means growth, the opposite.
अः before अ would give नोऽपचयो, not नापचयो.
Right: अ + अ → आ; अपचयः before the voiced भ of भवति becomes अपचयो.
questions.explain: न (not) + अपचयः (wasting): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: By unit 106, by what are the earlier srotas nourished?
options: By the proper use of food, in due time
By fasting, at long and irregular intervals
By medicines, taken only at night
By sleep and the rest of the body
optionExplain: Right: यथाकालं सम्यगाहारोपयोगेन: in due time, by the proper use of food.
Fasting is not named; proper use of food is.
No medicine is named in unit 106.
Sleep is not named in unit 106.
questions.explain: They are nourished in due time by the proper use of food.

questions.q: By the rule of नापचयो, how is न + अस्ति (is not) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as न + अपचयः → नापचयः.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Two अ merge into a long आ, not a short अ.
questions.explain: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, like न + अपचयः = नापचयः.
questions.teaches: Two short अ merge into long आ: न + अपचयः → नापचयः.

questions.q: By unit 107, the measure of the essences and wastes goes according to what?
optionExplain: Season and land are not named in unit 107.
Food and drink are not named in unit 107.
Right: यथावयःशरीरम्: according to age and body.
Day and night are not named in unit 107.
questions.explain: They follow their own measure according to age and body.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 107 in the line's order.
questions.explain: And then, called dhātus, the essences and wastes, each its own, follow the measure, by age and body.
questions.rule: ततश्च → धात्वाख्याः → प्रसादमलाः → स्वंस्वमेव → मानमनुवर्तंते → यथावयःशरीरं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 107 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The clear essences and wastes follow their measure by age and body.
questions.rule: प्रसाद, मल, मानम्, अनुवर्तन्ते, वयः, शरीर.
questions.teaches: यथा + a noun makes 'according to': यथावयःशरीरम् = according to age and body.

questions.q: In unit 107, what does the repeated स्वं स्वम् (एव) mean?
optionExplain: The repetition gives 'each its own', not one shared.
The repetition is distributive, not a doubling.
Each follows its own measure; a measure is affirmed.
Right: स्वं स्वम् एव: each its own, only.
questions.explain: स्वं स्वम् = each its own: every essence and waste keeps its own measure.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 107?
options: The unit gives a figure for each measure
The measure goes by age and body
Only the essences follow a measure, not the wastes
optionExplain: No figure is printed in unit 107.
Right: यथावयःशरीरम्.
Right: visarga before च → श्.
Both are named: प्रसादमलाः.
questions.explain: Essences and wastes each follow their own measure, by age and body; no figures are given.

questions.q: By the pattern of यथावयःशरीरम् (according to age and body), what does यथाशक्ति mean in a new example?
options: Beyond the limit of one's strength
optionExplain: Right: यथा + शक्ति = according to strength, as यथा + वयःशरीर.
यथा means according to, not against.
यथा does not negate.
यथा keeps within, it does not exceed.
questions.explain: यथाशक्ति = according to one's strength, like यथावयःशरीरम् = according to age and body.
questions.rule: यथा + noun = according to that noun.
questions.teaches: यथा- + a noun gives an indeclinable 'according to X': यथावयःशरीरम्, यथाकालम्, यथास्वम्.

questions.q: By unit 108, by which wind is the food-rasa scattered?
optionExplain: Unit 108 names vyāna as the scatterer, not prāṇa.
Right: व्यानविक्षिप्तः: scattered by vyāna.
Unit 108 names vyāna as the scatterer, not samāna.
Apāna is not named in unit 108.
questions.explain: The food-rasa is scattered by vyāna.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 108 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The food-rasa, scattered by vyāna, cooked in the dhātu-fires, nourishes.

questions.q: Put these printed words of unit 108 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The rasa, scattered by vyāna, in the dhātu-fires, cooked in order, having invigorated the body, nourishes.
questions.rule: तत्राहाररसो → व्यानविक्षिप्तो → धात्वग्निषु → क्रमात्पच्यमानः → देहमूर्जयित्वा → धातून्धातुमलांश्च पुष्णाति.
questions.teaches: The line moves from the rasa, to its cooking in the dhātu-fires, to what it nourishes.

questions.q: By unit 108, what does the food-rasa nourish?
options: The dhātus only, not their wastes
The wastes only, not the dhātus
The doṣas only, not the dhātus
optionExplain: The wastes of the dhātus are named too (धातुमलान्).
The dhātus are named first (धातून्).
Right: धातून्धातुमलांश्च पुष्णाति: the dhātus and the wastes of the dhātus.
The doṣas are not named in unit 108.
questions.explain: It nourishes both the dhātus and the dhātu-wastes.

questions.q: Which split of धात्वग्निषु in unit 108 is right?
optionExplain: धात्व is not a stem; the stem is धातु.
औ before a vowel becomes आव्: धाताव् अग्निषु.
वग्निषु is not a word; the व् comes from the उ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: धातु + अग्निषु → धात्वग्निषु.
questions.explain: धातु (dhātu) + अग्निषु (in the fires): उ + अ → व.
questions.rule: उ + a different vowel → व् + that vowel.

questions.q: By the rule of धात्वग्निषु, how is सु + अस्ति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as धातु + अग्निषु → धात्वग्निषु.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ; here उ meets अ.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel; here the उ simply becomes व्.
questions.explain: सु + अस्ति = स्वस्ति, like धातु + अग्निषु = धात्वग्निषु.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: धातु + अग्निषु → धात्वग्निषु.

questions.q: By unit 109, what is the essence (सार) of rasa?
optionExplain: Flesh is the essence of blood (unit 110).
Right: रसस्य सारो रक्तम्: the essence of rasa is blood.
Fat is the essence of flesh (unit 111).
Marrow is the essence of bone (unit 112).
questions.explain: Of rasa the essence is blood.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line of unit 109 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The refuse of food: clear urine, thick dung.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of unit 109 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of rasa, the essence, blood; the waste, Kapha and lasīkā.
questions.rule: रसस्य → सारो → रक्तं → मलः → कफ़ो → लसीका च.
questions.teaches: Each statement runs: the dhātu in the genitive, सारः and its essence, then मलः and its waste.

questions.q: By unit 109, which is clear and which is thick in the refuse of food?
options: Urine is thick; dung is clear
Both urine and dung are clear
Urine is clear; dung is thick
Both urine and dung are thick
optionExplain: The other way round: अच्छं goes with मूत्रं.
घनं (thick) goes with शकृत्.
Right: अच्छं मूत्रं घनं शकृत्: clear urine, thick dung.
अच्छं (clear) goes with मूत्रं.
questions.explain: Clear urine and thick dung.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 109?
options: Kapha is named as a waste of rasa
Blood is named as the waste of rasa
Lasīkā is named as the essence of rasa
Urine and dung are the refuse of food
optionExplain: Right: मलः कफो लसीका च.
Blood is the essence of rasa, not its waste.
Lasīkā is named with Kapha as the waste.
Right: अन्नकिट्टम् ... मूत्रं ... शकृत्.
questions.explain: Food refuse: urine and dung; rasa: essence blood, waste Kapha and lasīkā.
questions.rule: अथान्नकिट्टमच्छं मूत्रं घनं शकृत् · रसस्य सारो रक्तं मलः कफो लसीका च.

questions.q: By the rule of सारः + रक्तम् → सारो रक्तम्, how is नरः + गच्छति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अः drops to अ before vowels other than अ, not before a consonant.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
स् is the form before त or थ, not before ग.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as सारः + रक्तम् → सारो रक्तम्.
questions.explain: नरः + गच्छति = नरो गच्छति, like सारः + रक्तम् = सारो रक्तम्.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: सारः + रक्तम् → सारो रक्तम्.

questions.q: By unit 110, what is the waste (मल) of blood?
optionExplain: Right: मलः पित्तम्: the waste of blood is Pitta.
Kapha is a waste of rasa (unit 109).
Sweat is the waste of fat (unit 112).
Urine is the refuse of food (unit 109).
questions.explain: The waste of blood is Pitta.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 110 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of blood, the essence, flesh; kaṇḍarās and sirās; the waste, Pitta.
questions.rule: रक्तस्य → सारो → मांसं → कंडराः → सिराश्च → मलः पित्तं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 110 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of blood the essence is flesh; the waste is Pitta.
questions.teaches: The genitive -स्य names the dhātu whose essence and waste follow: रक्तस्य = of blood.

questions.q: By unit 110, which is the essence (सार) of blood?
optionExplain: Blood is the essence of rasa (unit 109), not of itself.
Right: रक्तस्य सारो मांसम्: the essence of blood is flesh.
Pitta is the waste of blood, not its essence.
Fat is the essence of flesh (unit 111).
questions.explain: Of blood the essence is flesh.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 110?
options: Kapha is the waste of blood
Pitta is the waste of blood
Blood is the essence of flesh
Flesh is the essence of blood
optionExplain: Kapha is a waste of rasa (unit 109); blood's waste is Pitta.
Right: मलः पित्तम्.
The other way round: flesh is the essence of blood.
Right: रक्तस्य सारो मांसम्.
questions.explain: Of blood: essence flesh, waste Pitta.

questions.q: By the pattern of रक्त → रक्तस्य (of blood), which form of वृक्ष (tree) means of the tree in a new example?
optionExplain: वृक्षाय is the dative: for the tree.
वृक्षेण is the instrumental: by the tree.
Right: An अ-stem takes -स्य in the genitive singular, as रक्त → रक्तस्य.
वृक्षात् is the ablative: from the tree.
questions.explain: वृक्षस्य = of the tree, like रक्तस्य = of blood.
questions.teaches: An अ-stem forms its genitive singular in -स्य: रक्त → रक्तस्य, रस → रसस्य.

questions.q: By unit 111, which is an essence of flesh?
optionExplain: Bone is not named in unit 111; it first comes in unit 112.
Blood is the essence of rasa (unit 109).
Marrow is the essence of bone (unit 112).
Right: मांसस्य सारो मेदः: fat is an essence of flesh.
questions.explain: Of flesh the essence is fat, the skins and vasā.

questions.q: Put the places of the wastes of flesh in the order of unit 111.
questions.explain: Ear, eye, nose, mouth, hair-pores, genital organ.
questions.rule: कर्ण → अक्षि → नासिका → आस्य → रोमकूप → प्रजनन.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 111 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Essence: fat, skins, vasā; refuse: wastes of the mouth, hair-pores, genital organ and others.
questions.rule: मेदः, त्वचः, वसा; आस्य, रोमकूप, प्रजनन.
questions.teaches: किट्ट (refuse) here is a list of six places in one compound that ends in मलाः (wastes).

questions.q: Which split of मेदस्त्वचो in unit 111 is right?
optionExplain: Right: Visarga before त → स्; त्वचः before the voiced व of वसा becomes त्वचो.
स्त्वचः is not a word; the स् is the visarga of मेदः.
म् before त would be written ं: मेदं त्वचः.
त् + त would give त्त: मेदत्त्वचः.
questions.explain: मेदः (fat) + त्वचः (skins): visarga before त → स्.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 111?
options: The wastes of the eye are part of the refuse of flesh
Sweat is named as the refuse of flesh
Fat is named as the refuse of flesh
The wastes of the hair-pores are named
optionExplain: Right: अक्षि is in the compound before मलाः.
Sweat is the refuse of fat (unit 112).
Fat is the essence of flesh, not its refuse.
Right: रोमकूप is in the compound.
questions.explain: Refuse of flesh: the wastes of ear, eye, nose, mouth, hair-pores, genital organ.

questions.q: By the rule of नासिका + आस्य → नासिकास्य, how is विद्या + आलय (house of learning) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ/आ + इ, not from आ + आ.
Right: आ + आ → आ, as नासिका + आस्य → नासिकास्य.
The two आ merge into one आ; they are not both kept.
ओ comes from अ/आ + उ, not from आ + आ.
questions.explain: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय, like नासिका + आस्य = नासिकास्य.
questions.teaches: Two like vowels merge into one long vowel: नासिका + आस्य → नासिकास्य.

questions.q: By unit 112, what is the waste (किट्ट) of fat (medas)?
optionExplain: Pitta is the waste of blood (unit 110).
Urine is the refuse of food (unit 109).
Right: मेदसः ... किट्टं स्वेदः: the waste of fat is sweat.
Kapha is a waste of rasa (unit 109).
questions.explain: The waste of fat is sweat.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 112 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Sweat; marrow; head hair, body hair, nails; waste.
questions.rule: स्वेदः, मज्जा, केश, लोमन्, नखाः, किट्टम्.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 112 in their order over the two lines.
questions.explain: Of fat ... sweat; of bone ... marrow ... hair and body hair, nails.
questions.rule: मेदसः → स्वेदः → अस्थ्नः → मज्जा → केशलोमानि → नखाः.
questions.teaches: Each line runs: the dhātu in the genitive (मेदसः, अस्थ्नः), its essence, then its waste.

questions.q: Which split of सारोऽस्थि in unit 112 is right?
optionExplain: स्थि is not a word; ऽ marks a dropped अ of अस्थि.
अ + अ would give आ: सारास्थि.
म् before a vowel stays: सारमस्थि.
Right: अः before अ → ओ, and the अ is dropped (ऽ): सारोऽस्थि.
questions.explain: सारः (essence) + अस्थि (bone): अः + अ → ओऽ.

questions.q: By unit 112, whose essence is marrow (majjā)?
optionExplain: Right: अस्थ्नः सारो मज्जा: the essence of bone is marrow.
Marrow is named after अस्थ्नः (of bone), not after मेदसः (of fat).
The essence of flesh is fat (unit 111).
The essence of blood is flesh (unit 110).
questions.explain: Of bone the essence is marrow.

questions.q: By the rule of सारोऽस्थि, how is रामः + अपि (Rāma too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अ + अ → आ is for a bare अ; here the अ has a visarga.
Right: अः before अ → ओ, the अ dropped (ऽ), as सारः + अस्थि → सारोऽस्थि.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ and आ.
अः drops to अ before vowels other than अ; before अ it gives ओऽ.
questions.explain: रामः + अपि = रामोऽपि, like सारः + अस्थि = सारोऽस्थि.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped (ऽ): सारः + अस्थि → सारोऽस्थि.

questions.q: By unit 113, what is the essence of marrow?
optionExplain: Ojas is the essence of śukra (unit 114).
Bone is not named in unit 113; marrow is the essence of bone (unit 112).
Right: मज्ज्ञस्तु सारः शुक्रम्: the essence of marrow is śukra.
Fat is an essence of flesh (unit 111).
questions.explain: Of marrow the essence is śukra.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 113 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of marrow the essence is śukra; the waste, eye-excrement and the oiliness of the skins.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 113 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of marrow, however, the essence, śukra; the waste, eye-excrement, of the skins the oiliness.
questions.rule: मज्ज्ञस्तु → सारः → शुक्रं → मलोऽक्षिविट् → त्वचां → स्नेहः.
questions.teaches: तु (however) follows the first word: मज्ज्ञः + तु → मज्ज्ञस्तु.

questions.q: By unit 113, which is a waste of marrow, not its essence?
optionExplain: Śukra is the essence of marrow, not its waste.
Ojas is the essence of śukra (unit 114).
Sweat is the waste of fat (unit 112).
Right: त्वचां स्नेहः is named after मलः, as a waste.
questions.explain: Wastes of marrow: eye-excrement and the oiliness of the skins.

questions.q: By unit 113, the essence of marrow is ____ (semen). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शुक्रम् (śukra, semen): मज्ज्ञस्तु सारः शुक्रम्.
questions.teaches: शुक्र = semen: the essence of marrow.

questions.q: By the rule of मज्ज्ञः + तु → मज्ज्ञस्तु, how is बालाः + तिष्ठन्ति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, as मज्ज्ञः + तु → मज्ज्ञस्तु.
After आ the visarga drops before a voiced sound or a vowel; त is not voiced.
ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
श् is the form before च or छ; before त it is स्.
questions.explain: बालाः + तिष्ठन्ति = बालास्तिष्ठन्ति, like मज्ज्ञः + तु = मज्ज्ञस्तु.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: मज्ज्ञः + तु → मज्ज्ञस्तु.

questions.q: By unit 114, what is the essence of śukra?
optionExplain: Marrow is the essence of bone (unit 112).
Right: शुक्रस्य सारमोजः: the essence of śukra is ojas.
Blood is the essence of rasa (unit 109).
Pitta is the waste of blood (unit 110).
questions.explain: Of śukra the essence is ojas.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 114 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Of śukra the essence is ojas.

questions.q: Put these in the order in which units 110-114 first name them.
questions.explain: Flesh (110), fat (111), bone (112, as read: the essence of fat may instead be the joints), marrow (112), śukra (113), ojas (114).
questions.rule: मांस → मेदस् → अस्थि → मज्जा → शुक्र → ओजस्.
questions.teaches: Units 110-114 go dhātu by dhātu: each line opens with a dhātu in the genitive, then its essence and waste.

questions.q: In unit 114, what is the relation of ojas to śukra?
options: Śukra is the essence of ojas
Ojas is the waste of śukra
Ojas is the essence of śukra
Ojas is the source of śukra
optionExplain: The other way round: शुक्रस्य is the genitive.
सारम् is essence; no waste is named here.
Right: शुक्रस्य सारम् ओजः: ojas is the essence of śukra.
Ojas comes from śukra as its essence.
questions.explain: Ojas is the essence of śukra.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 114?
options: Unit 114 names a waste of śukra
ओजः is the essence named in this unit
optionExplain: No waste is named in unit 114.
No verb is printed; the copula is understood.
Right: the genitive -स्य names whose essence ojas is.
Right: शुक्रस्य सारमोजः.
questions.explain: Of śukra (genitive) the essence is ojas; no verb and no waste are printed.

questions.q: By the rule of सारम् + ओजः → सारमोजः, how is फलम् + अस्ति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ं is written for म् before a consonant, not before a vowel.
म् does not drop, and अ + अ would not give ओ.
म् does not drop before a vowel.
Right: A final म् before a vowel stays and joins it, as सारम् + ओजः → सारमोजः.
questions.explain: फलम् + अस्ति = फलमस्ति, like सारम् + ओजः = सारमोजः.
questions.rule: Final म् before a vowel stays: म् + vowel.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel stays and joins it: सारम् + ओजः → सारमोजः.

questions.q: By unit 115, why is there no waste (mala) in this?
optionExplain: Right: अत्यन्तशुद्धतया: through extreme purity.
Heat is not named in unit 115.
Cooking is named only as what others deny.
No wind is named in unit 115.
questions.explain: Through extreme purity there is no waste in this.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 115 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Extreme purity, absence of waste; others deny cooking.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 115 in their order over the two lines.
questions.explain: Through extreme purity, and in this no waste; others for this very reason do not accept its cooking.
questions.rule: अत्यंतशुद्धतया → चास्मिन्मलाभावः → अन्येपुनरतएव → तस्य → नेच्छंति → पाकं.
questions.teaches: The first line gives the fact and its reason; the second gives the others' view, on the same ground (अत एव).

questions.q: By unit 115, what do the others (अन्ये) not accept?
optionExplain: Purity is the reason given, not what is denied.
Right: तस्य नेच्छन्ति पाकम्: they do not accept its cooking.
No place is named in unit 115.
Strength is not named in unit 115.
questions.explain: Others do not accept its cooking (pāka).

questions.q: Which split of नेच्छंति in unit 115 is right?
optionExplain: च्छन्ति is not a word; the verb is इच्छन्ति.
एच्छन्ति is not a word; and अ + ए would give ऐ.
Right: अ + इ → ए: न + इच्छन्ति → नेच्छन्ति.
अः before इ drops its visarga with no join: न इच्छन्ति.
questions.explain: न (not) + इच्छन्ति (wish, accept): अ + इ → ए.

questions.q: By the rule of नेच्छन्ति, how is न + इति (not, thus) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + इ.
आ comes from अ + अ, not from अ + इ.
अय् comes from ए before a vowel; here there is no ए.
Right: अ + इ → ए, as न + इच्छन्ति → नेच्छन्ति.
questions.explain: न + इति = नेति, like न + इच्छन्ति = नेच्छन्ति.
questions.teaches: अ + इ → ए: न + इच्छन्ति → नेच्छन्ति.

questions.q: By unit 116, what do the others hold the essence of śukra (semen) to be?
optionExplain: Right: शुक्रस्य सारं गर्भमेव आमनन्ति: the essence of śukra is held to be the garbha itself.
Marrow is not the essence of śukra; card 113 makes śukra the essence of marrow.
Blood is not named in unit 116 or as the essence of śukra.
Fat is not named in unit 116 or as the essence of śukra.
questions.explain: Others hold the essence of śukra to be the garbha (embryo) itself.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 116 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Others, however; of śukra; the essence; the garbha itself they hold.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 116 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अपरे = others; पुनः = however; सार = essence; गर्भ = embryo; आमनन्ति = they hold.
questions.teaches: आमनन्ति (ā-√mnā, 3rd plural present) takes two accusatives here: 'they hold X to be Y'.

questions.q: Which split of गर्भमेवामनंति in unit 116 is right?
optionExplain: मेव is not a word; the म् belongs to गर्भम्.
Right: म् joins the vowel ए; अ + आ → आ: एव + आमनन्ति → एवामनन्ति.
म् + इ would give गर्भमिवा-, not गर्भमेवा-.
एव + म- would give एवमनन्ति, with a short अ.
questions.explain: गर्भम् (the embryo) + एव (itself) + आमनन्ति (they hold).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; म् joins a following vowel.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 116?
options: The line gives a reason for the view
The view is given as that of others (अपरे)
It names the garbha the waste (mala) of śukra
The essence of śukra is held to be the garbha
optionExplain: No reason is printed in unit 116.
Right: अपरे पुनः, others, however.
The garbha is named the essence (सार), not a waste.
Right: शुक्रस्य सारं गर्भमेव आमनन्ति.
questions.explain: Others hold the essence of śukra to be the garbha; no reason is given.

questions.q: By the rule of एवामनन्ति (एव + आमनन्ति), how is न + आगच्छति (he does not come) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अ + आ does not give a short अ; it gives आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ, as एव + आमनन्ति → एवामनन्ति.
No य् comes between अ and आ.
questions.explain: न + आगच्छति = नागच्छति, like एव + आमनन्ति = एवामनन्ति.
questions.teaches: अ before आ merges into one long आ: एव + आमनन्ति → एवामनन्ति.

questions.q: By unit 117, where does vāyu (wind) appear (prādurbhavati)?
optionExplain: No bone is named in unit 117.
No skin is named in unit 117.
No eye is named in unit 117.
Right: कोष्ठे प्रादुर्भवति: it appears in the koṣṭha.
questions.explain: Vāyu appears in the koṣṭha.

questions.q: Put these printed phrases of unit 117 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Wind; however, of fire and food; through abundance and scarcity; appears in the koṣṭha.
questions.rule: वायुः → पुनरग्नेराहारस्य च → बह्वल्पतया → कोष्ठे प्रादुर्भवति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 117 to its meaning.
questions.explain: वायु = wind; अग्नि = fire; आहार = food; अमूर्त = non-corporeal; कोष्ठ = belly cavity.
questions.teaches: बह्वल्पता = बहु + अल्प + ता: a dvandva of 'much' and 'little' made abstract, 'abundance and scarcity'.

questions.q: Which split of पुनरग्नेराहारस्य in unit 117 is right?
optionExplain: Right: एः before the vowel आ → एर्: अग्नेः + आहारस्य → अग्नेराहारस्य.
राहारस्य is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
ए + आ would give अग्नयाहारस्य or अग्न आहारस्य, never अग्नेरा-.
इः + आ would give अग्निराहारस्य, not अग्नेरा-.
questions.explain: पुनर् (however) + अग्नेः (of the fire) + आहारस्य (of the food).
questions.rule: A vowel other than अ/आ + visarga before a voiced sound → र्.

questions.q: By unit 117, through what does vāyu appear in the koṣṭha?
options: Abundance and scarcity of water and sleep
Abundance and scarcity of fire and food
Abundance and scarcity of blood and fat
Abundance and scarcity of heat and cold
optionExplain: Neither water nor sleep is named in unit 117.
Right: अग्नेराहारस्य च बह्वल्पतया: by the much-and-little of fire and food.
Neither blood nor fat is named in unit 117.
Neither heat nor cold is named in unit 117.
questions.explain: Through the abundance and scarcity of the fire and of the food.

questions.q: By the rule of बह्वल्प (बहु + अल्प), how is मधु + अत्र (honey here) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from उ + अ.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from उ + अ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as बहु + अल्प → बह्वल्प.
The अ is not simply lost after उ.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, like बहु + अल्प = बह्वल्प.
questions.teaches: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: बहु + अल्प → बह्वल्प.

questions.q: By unit 118, what are all the bhāvas in the body made of?
optionExplain: Unit 118 says अन्नमय, made of food, not of fire.
Unit 118 says अन्नमय, made of food, not of wind.
Unit 118 says अन्नमय, made of food, not of water.
Right: अन्नमया एव: made of food alone.
questions.explain: All bhāvas in the body are made of food alone.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 118 in the line's order.
questions.explain: This being so; in the body made of food; alone; all bhāvas.
questions.rule: एवं च कृत्वा → देहेऽन्नमया → एव → सर्वे भावाः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 118 to its meaning.
questions.explain: एवम् = thus; कृत्वा = having done; देह = body; अन्नमय = made of food; भाव = state.
questions.teaches: -मय added to a noun means 'made of': अन्न (food) → अन्नमय (made of food).

questions.q: Why is देहे + अन्नमयाः printed देहेऽन्नमयाः in unit 118?
options: After ए, the अ is dropped, marked ऽ
The ए becomes अय् before the following अ
The ए and the अ merge into ऐ
The ए is dropped before the अ
optionExplain: Right: ए + अ: the ए stays and the अ is dropped, marked by ऽ.
ए + अ does not give अय् here; the print keeps ए and marks ऽ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from ए + अ.
The ए stays (देहे-); it is the अ that is dropped.
questions.explain: देहे (in the body) + अन्नमयाः: after ए the अ is dropped, written ऽ.

questions.q: Why is अन्नमयाः printed अन्नमया before एव in unit 118?
options: आः becomes ओ before a vowel
आः drops its visarga before a vowel
आः becomes आर् before a vowel
आः becomes आस् before a vowel
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः before a voiced consonant, not from आः.
Right: After आ the visarga is lost before a voiced sound, vowels included.
र् comes after vowels other than अ/आ, not after आ.
स् comes before त or थ, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: अन्नमयाः + एव → अन्नमया एव: आः loses its visarga before a voiced sound.

questions.q: By the pattern of अन्नमय (made of food), what does सुवर्णमय mean in a new example?
optionExplain: -मय does not mean fond of.
-मय does not mean free of.
Right: -मय = made of: सुवर्ण (gold) → सुवर्णमय, like अन्न → अन्नमय.
-मय does not mean giver of.
questions.explain: सुवर्णमय = made of gold, like अन्नमय = made of food.
questions.teaches: -मय forms adjectives meaning 'made of': अन्नमय (unit 118).

questions.q: By unit 119, the body is called a kind of what?
optionExplain: No chariot is named in unit 119.
No house is named in unit 119.
No river is named in unit 119.
Right: शरीरयन्त्रम्: the body-machine.
questions.explain: The body is called a machine: शरीर-यन्त्र.

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 119 in the line's order.
questions.explain: By that alone, and this, thus, for long; the body-machine with unbroken flow; endowed with health, strength and growth; is kept going.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 119 to its meaning.
questions.explain: स्वास्थ्य-बल-उपचय-युक्त = endowed with health, strength and growth; अनवरत-प्रवाह = unbroken flow.
questions.teaches: स्वास्थ्य-बल-उपचय is a dvandva of three nouns, then tied to युक्त: 'endowed with health, strength and growth'.

questions.q: Which split of तेनैव in unit 119 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ: तेन + एव → तेनैव.
अ + इ would give तेनेव, with ए, not ऐ.
There is no form तेनः; a visarga would leave तेन एव.
ए + ए would not give ऐ.
questions.explain: तेन (by that) + एव (alone).

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 119?
options: It is kept going for a long time (चिरेण)
It is said to lack growth (उपचय)
It runs with an unbroken flow
It is endowed with health, strength and growth
optionExplain: Right: चिरेण, for a long time.
No: it is endowed with growth, स्वास्थ्यबलोपचययुक्तम्.
Right: अनवरतप्रवाहेण.
Right: स्वास्थ्यबलोपचययुक्तम्.
questions.explain: Kept going long, with unbroken flow, endowed with health, strength and growth.

questions.q: By the rule of तेनैव (तेन + एव), how is अत्र + एव (here indeed) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + ए.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as तेन + एव → तेनैव.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + ए.
No य् comes between अ and ए.
questions.explain: अत्र + एव = अत्रैव, like तेन + एव = तेनैव.
questions.teaches: अ before ए gives ऐ (vṛddhi): तेन + एव → तेनैव.

questions.q: By unit 120, what are the two outcomes when things go otherwise (anyathā)?
options: It grows, or gains in strength
It is cooked, or it changes into food
It is cut off, or falls into disease
It dries up, or turns into waste
optionExplain: Growth and strength belong to unit 119, not to 'otherwise'.
Neither is named in unit 120.
Right: व्यवच्छिद्यते ... व्याधिभाजनं वा भवति.
Neither is named in unit 120.
questions.explain: Either it is cut off, or it becomes a vessel of disease.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of unit 120 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Otherwise ... (the srotas phrase); in the midst of the not duly joined dhātu-flow; is cut off; or becomes a vessel of disease.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 120 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अन्यथा = otherwise; व्याधि-भाजन = vessel of disease; व्यवच्छिद्यते = is cut off; यथावत् = duly.
questions.teaches: वा ... वा, with one वा in each clause, means 'either ... or'.

questions.q: Which split of the printed यथावदनभिसंधीयमान- in unit 120 is right?
optionExplain: वदन् + अ- would give वदन्नभि-, with two न.
अः before अ would give यथावोऽनभि-.
त् + न would give यथावन्नभि- (or, optionally, यथावद्नभि-).
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: यथावत् + अ- → यथावदनभि-.
questions.explain: यथावत् (duly) + अनभिसन्धीयमान (not being joined).

questions.q: In unit 120, what do the two वा (vā) mark?
options: A cause and then its effect
A question and then its answer
optionExplain: Right: वा ... वा: either it is cut off, or it becomes a vessel of disease.
वा does not mark cause and effect.
वा does not mark a sequence.
वा does not mark question and answer.
questions.explain: वा ... वा = either ... or: two outcomes.

questions.q: By the rule of यथावदनभि- (यथावत् + अ-), how is जगत् + अपि (the world too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: A final त् does not stay त् before a vowel.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्, as यथावत् + अनभि- → यथावदनभि-.
न्न comes (optionally) from त् + न, not from त् + अ.
च्च comes from त् + च, not from त् + अ.
questions.explain: जगत् + अपि = जगदपि, like यथावत् + अनभि- = यथावदनभि-.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: यथावत् + अनभिसन्धीयमान → यथावदनभिसन्धीयमान.

questions.q: By unit 121, what do the others (anye) do?
optionExplain: The verb printed is वर्णयन्ति, not गायन्ति.
The verb printed is वर्णयन्ति, not गणयन्ति.
Right: वर्णयन्ति = they describe.
The verb printed is वर्णयन्ति, not पृच्छन्ति.
questions.explain: But others describe.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 121 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अन्ये = others; तु = but; वर्णयन्ति = they describe.

questions.q: Unit 121: अन्ये तु ____ (they describe). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: वर्णयन्ति (they describe), printed वर्णयंति.
questions.teaches: वर्णयन्ति is the 3rd person plural present of √वर्ण् (10th class, stem वर्णय-).

questions.q: In unit 121, what form is वर्णयन्ति?
optionExplain: He describes would be वर्णयति.
Let them describe would be वर्णयन्तु.
They should describe would be वर्णयेयुः.
Right: The data labels it 3 pl. pres.: they describe.
questions.explain: वर्णयन्ति = present, third person plural: they describe.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 121?
options: The line states what is described
optionExplain: Right: अन्ये, others.
Right: -न्ति, third person plural.
No object is printed or supplied.
Right: तु = but.
questions.explain: Others (plural) describe; but (तु); what they describe is not printed here.

questions.q: By the pattern of वर्णयन्ति, which form of √चुर् (चोरयति, he steals) means they steal, in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: Stem चोरय- + -न्ति (3rd plural), as वर्णय- + -न्ति → वर्णयन्ति.
चोरयति is singular: he steals.
चोरयन्तु is imperative: let them steal.
चोरयामि is first person: I steal.
questions.explain: चोरयन्ति = they steal, like वर्णयन्ति = they describe.
questions.teaches: 10th-class verbs take the stem -अय-: वर्णय- → वर्णयन्ति, they describe.

questions.q: By unit 122, through what does food rush as soon as it is swallowed?
optionExplain: No nose is named in unit 122.
Right: कण्ठनाडीप्लुतिः: the rush through the throat-tube (probably the gullet).
No palate is named in unit 122.
No heart is named in unit 122.
questions.explain: Swallowed food rushes through the throat-tube (kaṇṭha-nāḍī, probably the gullet).

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 122 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Of food just swallowed; the rush through the throat-tube; having descended into the great hollow; is brought to cooking; named prasāda; equally into all dhātus.
questions.rule: swallowed → कण्ठनाडी → महानिम्न → पाक → प्रसाद → सब धातु.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 122 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अभ्यवहृत = swallowed; महानिम्न = great hollow; कायाग्नि = bodily fire; प्रसाद = clear essence; स्रोतस् = channel.
questions.teaches: कायाग्नि = काय (body) + अग्नि (fire), a tat-puruṣa: the fire of the body.

questions.q: Which split of पाकमुपनीयते in unit 122 is right?
optionExplain: मुपनीयते is not a word; the म् belongs to पाकम्.
अः before उ would give पाक उपनीयते, with no म्.
Right: म् joins the vowel उ: पाकम् + उपनीयते → पाकमुपनीयते.
म् + अ would give पाकमपनीयते, not -मुप-.
questions.explain: पाकम् (to cooking) + उपनीयते (is brought).
questions.rule: म् + vowel: the म् joins the vowel.

questions.q: By unit 122, into what does the swallowed food descend (avatīrṇa)?
optionExplain: No head is named in unit 122.
No nose is named in unit 122.
No heart is named in unit 122.
Right: महानिम्न मवतीर्णस्य: having descended into the great hollow (probably the abdominal cavity).
questions.explain: Swallowed food descends into the mahānimna (great hollow, probably the abdominal cavity).

questions.q: By the rule of चान्वेति (च + अन्वेति), how is अत्र + अपि (here too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अन्वेति → चान्वेति.
Two अ do not merge into a short अ; they give आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: अत्र + अपि = अत्रापि, like च + अन्वेति = चान्वेति.
questions.teaches: Two short अ merge into आ: च + अन्वेति → चान्वेति.

questions.q: By unit 123, what is nourished directly (sākṣāt)?
optionExplain: सर्वधातून्: all the dhātus, not the doṣas.
Right: साक्षात्सर्वधातून् पुष्णाति: it directly nourishes all the dhātus.
सर्वधातून्: all the dhātus, not the srotas.
सर्वधातून्: all the dhātus, not the wastes.
questions.explain: All the dhātus are nourished directly.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 123 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Thus the rasa itself; directly all the dhātus; by just some difference of time; nourishes.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 123 to its meaning.
questions.explain: साक्षात् = directly; सर्व = all; काल-भेद = difference of time; पुष्णाति = nourishes.
questions.teaches: पुष्णाति is the 3rd singular present of √पुष् (9th class, -णा-): nourishes.

questions.q: Which split of केनचिदेव in unit 123 is right?
optionExplain: त् + इ would give केनचिदिव, not -देव.
अ + ए would give केनचिदैव, with ऐ.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: केनचित् + एव → केनचिदेव.
There is no form केनचिः; the द् comes from त्.
questions.explain: केनचित् (by some) + एव (just).

questions.q: By unit 123, with what difference does the nourishing of all dhātus happen?
optionExplain: देश (place) is not named; the line has काल, time.
रस-भेद is not named; the line has काल, time.
ऋतु is not named; the line has काल, time.
Right: केनचिदेव कालभेदेन: by just some difference of time.
questions.explain: By just some difference of time (kāla-bheda).

questions.q: By the pattern of कालभेदेन (by difference of time), what does देशभेदेन mean in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: -एन is the instrumental: by, through, as कालभेदेन = by difference of time.
Of would be the genitive, देशभेदस्य.
From would be the ablative, देशभेदात्.
In would be the locative, देशभेदे.
questions.explain: देशभेदेन = by difference of place, like कालभेदेन = by difference of time.
questions.teaches: -एन marks the instrumental singular of a-stems: कालभेदेन, by difference of time.

questions.q: By unit 124, into what do the dhātus not pass by crushing their own form?
optionExplain: No doṣa is named in unit 124.
Right: धात्वन्तरतां न प्रतिपद्यन्ते: they do not pass into another dhātu's state.
No srotas is named in unit 124.
No food is named in unit 124.
questions.explain: The dhātus do not pass into the state of another dhātu.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 124 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Not, however, the dhātus; into another-dhātu-state; by crushing of own form; pass, thus.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 124 to its meaning.
questions.explain: धात्वन्तरता = another-dhātu-ness; स्वरूप-उपमर्द = crushing of own form; प्रतिपद्यन्ते = pass into.
questions.teaches: -ता makes an abstract noun: धातु + अन्तर + ता = the state of being another dhātu.

questions.q: Which split of स्वरूपोपमर्देन in unit 124 is right?
optionExplain: अः before उ would give स्वरूप उपमर्देन, unjoined.
पमर्देन is not a word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: स्वरूप + उपमर्देन → स्वरूपोपमर्देन.
म् + उ would give स्वरूपमुपमर्देन.
questions.explain: स्वरूप (own form) + उपमर्देन (by crushing).

questions.q: Why is धातवः printed धातवो before धात्वंतरतां in unit 124?
options: अः before every consonant becomes ओ
ओ is the case ending of धातु
ध begins with a vowel, so अः → ओ
अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ
optionExplain: Not every consonant: before त the visarga becomes स्.
The ending is -अः (nom. pl. धातवः); ओ comes from sandhi.
ध is a consonant, not a vowel.
Right: ध is a voiced consonant: धातवः + धात्व- → धातवो धात्व-.
questions.explain: धातवः + धात्वन्तरताम्: अः before the voiced consonant ध → ओ.

questions.q: By the rule of स्वरूपोपमर्देन (स्वरूप + उपमर्देन), how is सूर्य + उदयः (sunrise) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as स्वरूप + उपमर्देन → स्वरूपोपमर्देन.
ऊ comes from उ + उ, not from अ + उ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
व् comes from उ before a vowel, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, like स्वरूप + उपमर्देन.
questions.teaches: अ before उ gives ओ (guṇa): स्वरूप + उपमर्देन → स्वरूपोपमर्देन.

questions.q: By unit 125, by what difference is agni of four kinds?
optionExplain: No season is named in unit 125.
Right: बलभेदेन चतुर्विधो भवति: fourfold by difference of strength.
No place is named in unit 125.
No age is named in unit 125.
questions.explain: Agni is fourfold by difference of strength.

questions.q: Put the four kinds of agni in the order printed in unit 125.
questions.explain: समो विषमस्तीक्ष्णो मन्दश्च: sama, viṣama, tīkṣṇa, manda.

questions.q: Match each kind of agni in unit 125 to its meaning.
questions.explain: सम = even; विषम = uneven; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; मन्द = slow.
questions.teaches: विषम = वि + सम with स → ष after इ: 'uneven', the opposite of सम.

questions.q: Why is विषमः printed विषमस् before तीक्ष्णो in unit 125?
options: Visarga before every consonant becomes स्
स् is part of the stem of विषम
Visarga before a voiced sound becomes स्
optionExplain: Not every consonant: before a voiced one अः gives ओ (समो विषमः).
The stem is विषम; the स् comes from the visarga.
Right: विषमः + तीक्ष्णः → विषमस्तीक्ष्णः, as in अग्निः + तु → अग्निस्तु.
त is not voiced; before a voiced consonant अः gives ओ.
questions.explain: Visarga + त → स्त: विषमस्तीक्ष्णो, अग्निस्तु.

questions.q: Which are among the four kinds of agni named in unit 125?
optionExplain: Sthira is not one of the four printed kinds.
Right: समो.
Right: तीक्ष्णो.
Right: मंदश्च.
questions.explain: The four are sama, viṣama, tīkṣṇa and manda; sthira is not among them.

questions.q: By the rule of समो विषमः (समः + विषमः), how is रामः + गच्छति (Rāma goes) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: र् comes after vowels other than अ/आ, not after अ.
अः never becomes आ; before a voiced consonant it gives ओ.
स् comes before त or थ, not before ग.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as समः + विषमः → समो विषमः.
questions.explain: रामः + गच्छति = रामो गच्छति, like समः + विषमः = समो विषमः.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: समः + विषमः → समो विषमः.

questions.q: By unit 126, what does the sama (even) agni do?
options: Digests properly what is taken properly
Digests quickly what is taken wrongly
Digests slowly what is taken properly
Fails to digest even what is taken properly
optionExplain: Right: सम्यगेवोपयुक्तमन्नं सम्यक् पचति.
That is the tīkṣṇa (sharp) agni of unit 128, not sama.
Slow digestion is the manda agni (unit 129), not sama.
That is said of the viṣama agni (unit 127), not sama.
questions.explain: The sama agni properly digests food properly taken.
questions.rule: तत्र समो यः सम्यगेवोपयुक्तमन्नं सम्यक् पचति.

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 126 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Among these, the even one which; food taken properly alone; properly; digests.
questions.rule: तत्र समो यः → सम्यगेवोपयुक्तमन्नं → सम्यक् → पचति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 126 to its meaning.
questions.explain: तत्र = among these; सम्यक् = properly; उपयुक्त = taken; अन्न = food; पचति = digests.
questions.teaches: उपयुक्त is the past participle of उप-√युज्: 'used, taken', here of food eaten.

questions.q: Which split of सम्यगेवोपयुक्तम् in unit 126 is right?
optionExplain: क् + इ would give सम्यगिव-, not सम्यगेव-.
Right: क् → ग् before ए; अ + उ → ओ: एव + उपयुक्तम् → एवोपयुक्तम्.
एवम् + उ would give एवमुपयुक्तम्.
अ + अ would give एवापयुक्तम्.
questions.explain: सम्यक् (properly) + एव (only) + उपयुक्तम् (taken).
questions.rule: क् + vowel → ग्; अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Why is सम्यक् printed सम्यग् before एव in unit 126?
options: क् before a vowel becomes च्
क् before a vowel is dropped
क् before a vowel becomes ग्
The word always ends in ग्
optionExplain: च् does not come from क् here.
Nothing is dropped: the print shows ग्.
Right: A final क् becomes ग् before a vowel: सम्यक् + एव → सम्यगेव.
The same line prints सम्यक् before पचति.
questions.explain: सम्यक् + एव → सम्यगेव: क् before a vowel → ग्.

questions.q: By the rule of सम्यगेव (सम्यक् + एव), how is वाक् + ईशः (lord of speech) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: A final क् does not stay क् before a vowel.
च् does not come from a final क् before a vowel.
ङ् comes from क् before a nasal, not before a vowel.
Right: क् before a vowel becomes ग्, as सम्यक् + एव → सम्यगेव.
questions.explain: वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः, like सम्यक् + एव = सम्यगेव.
questions.teaches: A final क् before a vowel becomes ग्: सम्यक् + एव → सम्यगेव.

questions.q: By unit 127, what does the viṣama agni do with food taken properly?
options: Even then, it does not digest it
It digests it quickly and well
It digests it, after a long time
optionExplain: Right: सम्यगपि च न पचति: even when properly taken, it does not digest.
Quick digestion is said of the tīkṣṇa agni (unit 128).
Proper digestion of proper food is the sama agni (unit 126).
Late digestion is the manda agni (unit 129), not viṣama.
questions.explain: The viṣama agni, even with food properly taken, does not digest.
