questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 127 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The uneven one; digests even what is improperly taken; and even properly; does not digest.
questions.rule: विषमो → ऽसम्यगप्युपयुक्तं पचति → सम्यगपिच → न पचति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 127 to its meaning.
questions.explain: विषम = uneven; असम्यक् = improperly; सम्यक् = properly; अपि = even; न = not.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates: सम्यक् (properly) → असम्यक् (improperly).

questions.q: Which split of असम्यगप्युपयुक्तं in unit 127 is right?
optionExplain: इ + अ would give अप्यपयुक्तम्, not -प्युप-.
Right: क् → ग् before अ; इ + उ → यु: अपि + उपयुक्तम् → अप्युपयुक्तम्.
अप्य is not a word; अ + उ would also give -प्योप-.
अपु is not a word; उ + उ would give -पूप-.
questions.explain: असम्यक् (improperly) + अपि (even) + उपयुक्तम् (taken).
questions.rule: क् + vowel → ग्; इ + a different vowel → य्.

questions.q: In विषमो ऽसम्यक् (विषमः + असम्यक्) of unit 127, what does the sandhi do?
options: अः + अ → अर्, and the अ stays
अः + अ → अ, with a gap left between
अः + अ → ओ, and the अ is dropped
अः + अ → आ, and the two merge
optionExplain: र् does not come after अ; that is for other vowels.
The gap (अः → अ) is before vowels other than अ.
Right: विषमः + असम्यक् → विषमोऽसम्यक्.
अः + अ does not merge into आ.
questions.explain: अः before अ: ओ, and the following अ is dropped (ऽ).

questions.q: By the rule of विषमो ऽसम्यक्, how is रामः + अपि (Rāma too) joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The gap (अः → अ) is before vowels other than अ.
र् does not come after अ; it comes after other vowels.
अः + अ does not merge into आ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ, as विषमः + असम्यक् → विषमोऽसम्यक्.
questions.explain: रामः + अपि = रामोऽपि, like विषमः + असम्यक् = विषमोऽसम्यक्.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped (ऽ): विषमः + असम्यक् → विषमोऽसम्यक्.

questions.q: By unit 128, what does the tīkṣṇa agni become when it increases?
optionExplain: Right: स एव वर्धमानोऽत्यग्निर्भवति: increasing, it becomes atyagni.
Manda is a separate kind (unit 125), not what tīkṣṇa becomes.
Sama is a separate kind (unit 125), not what tīkṣṇa becomes.
Viṣama is a separate kind (unit 125), not what tīkṣṇa becomes.
questions.explain: That very one, increasing, becomes atyagni.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of unit 128 in the line's order.
questions.explain: The sharp one, even what is improperly taken; digests quickly; that very one; increasing becomes atyagni.
questions.rule: तीक्ष्णो ... → आशु पचति → स एव → वर्धमानोऽत्यग्निर्भवति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 128 to its meaning.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्ण = sharp; आशु = quickly; वर्धमान = increasing; अत्यग्नि = excessive fire; भवति = becomes.
questions.teaches: वर्धमान is a present participle (√वृध्, -मान): 'increasing', still going on.

questions.q: Which split of अत्यग्निर्भवति in unit 128 is right?
optionExplain: र्भवति is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
Right: इः before the voiced भ → इर्: अत्यग्निर्भवति.
म् before भ would be written ं, not र्.
एः before भ would give अत्यग्नेर्भवति.
questions.explain: अत्यग्निः (excessive fire) + भवति (becomes).

questions.q: How is अति + अग्निः joined in अत्यग्निः of unit 128?
options: इ and अ merge into ए
इ and अ merge into ई
The इ is dropped before अ
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
ई comes from इ + इ, not from इ + अ.
Right: अति + अग्निः → अत्यग्निः: इ before a different vowel → य्.
The इ is not dropped; it becomes य्.
questions.explain: अति + अग्निः → अत्यग्निः: इ + अ → य.

questions.q: By the rule of अत्यग्नि (अति + अग्नि), how is प्रति + अक्षम् joined in a new example?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
The इ does not drop and lengthen the अ.
The अ is not simply lost after इ.
Right: इ before अ becomes य्, as अति + अग्नि → अत्यग्नि.
questions.explain: प्रति + अक्षम् = प्रत्यक्षम्, like अति + अग्नि = अत्यग्नि.
questions.teaches: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: अति + अग्नि → अत्यग्नि.

questions.q: By unit 129, what does the manda (slow) agni do with food that was taken properly?
options: It shows signs of āma, then digests late
It digests it fast and turns into atyagni
It digests it properly at the due time
It leaves properly taken food undigested
optionExplain: Right: आमलिङ्गानि दर्शयित्वा चिरात्पचति: shows the signs of āma, digests after a long time.
Growing into atyagni is said of the tīkṣṇa agni (unit 128).
Proper digestion of properly taken food is the sama agni (unit 126).
Not digesting properly taken food is said of the viṣama agni (unit 127).
questions.explain: Even properly taken food: signs of āma first, digestion after a long time.

questions.q: Put these signs of āma in the order unit 129 prints them.
questions.explain: Heaviness of the belly, distension, constipation, gurgling, intestinal murmuring, dryness of the mouth (then stiffness of the anus and the like).
questions.rule: उदरगौरव → आध्मान → विबंध → आटोप → आंत्रकूजन → मुखशोष.

questions.q: Match each sign of āma in unit 129 to its meaning.
questions.explain: आध्मान distension, विबन्ध constipation, आटोप gurgling, मुखशोष dry mouth, पायुस्तम्भ stiff anus.
questions.teaches: These are the printed signs (लिङ्ग) of āma, raw undigested matter, that the manda agni shows before it digests.

questions.q: Which split of सम्यगप्युपयुक्तम् in unit 129 is right?
optionExplain: That would give सम्यगपियुक्तम्; the print has -प्युप-.
Right: क् before a vowel → ग्; इ before the unlike vowel उ → य्.
अप्यु is not a word; the य् comes from the इ of अपि.
ए before उ would not give य्; the word is अपि, 'even'.
questions.explain: सम्यक् (properly) + अपि (even) + उपयुक्तम् (taken).
questions.rule: क् + vowel → ग्; इ + unlike vowel → य्.

questions.q: Which statements fit the manda agni of unit 129?
options: It digests improperly taken food quickly
Even properly taken food is digested after a long time
It shows the signs of āma before digesting
optionExplain: That is the tīkṣṇa agni (unit 128).
Right: सम्यगप्युपयुक्तं ... चिरात्पचति.
Right: आमलिङ्गानि दर्शयित्वा.
Becoming atyagni is said of the tīkṣṇa agni (unit 128).
questions.explain: Manda: signs of āma, then late digestion, even of properly taken food.

questions.q: By the rule of सम्यक् + अपि → सम्यगपि, how is वाक् + ईशः joined in a new example?
optionExplain: क् does not stay क् before a vowel when words are joined.
ङ् comes from क् before a nasal, not before a vowel.
Right: क् before a vowel becomes ग्, as in सम्यक् + अपि → सम्यगपि.
The ग् is right, but the long ई of ईशः must stay long.
questions.explain: वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः, like सम्यक् + अपि = सम्यगपि.
questions.teaches: A final क् becomes ग् before a vowel: सम्यक् + अपि → सम्यगपि.

questions.q: By unit 130, what is said of cooking with outer fire of flame and embers?
options: It is always even and steady
It is the same as inner heat
It cooks only raw grain well
It is not always of one form
optionExplain: The line denies this: न एकाकारः सर्वदा.
The line sets outer fire against the heat within.
No grain or kind of food is named.
Right: नैकाकारः सर्वदा पाकोभवति: the cooking is not always one-formed.
questions.explain: Even outer fire does not always cook in one way.

questions.q: Put these printed phrases of unit 130 in the line's order.
questions.explain: Even by outer fire of flame and embers, cooking is not always one-formed ... even when even ... so guard it with effort.
questions.rule: बाह्येनापि च → ज्वालांगारात्मकेनाग्निना → नैकाकारः सर्वदा पाकोभवति → समेनापि → तस्मात्तं प्रयत्नतो रक्षेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 130 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Outer fire of flame and embers; cooking not of one form; guard with effort.
questions.teaches: किमुत means 'how much more, what to say of': from the outer fire it argues to the heat within.

questions.q: Which split of नैकाकारः in unit 130 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ: न + एकाकारः → नैकाकारः, 'not of one form'.
अ + इ gives ए, not ऐ; and इकाकार is not a word.
नै and काकार are not words here.
That would print नैकाकरः; the print has -कारः.
questions.explain: न (not) + एक (one) + आकारः (form).

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 130?
options: The outer fire is made of flame and embers
Outer fire always cooks in one way
It ends: guard it with effort
It says inner heat cooks faster than outer fire
optionExplain: Right: ज्वालाङ्गारात्मकेन अग्निना.
The line says the opposite: न एकाकारः सर्वदा.
Right: तस्मात्तं प्रयत्नतो रक्षेत्.
No such comparison of speed is printed.
questions.explain: Outer fire of flame and embers is uneven; so guard the inner one with effort.

questions.q: By the use of किमुत in unit 130, what does बालोऽपि जानाति किमुत वृद्धः mean (a new example)?
options: A boy knows it, but an elder does not
Even a boy knows; how much more an elder
Neither the boy nor the elder knows
The elder knows more slowly than a boy
optionExplain: किमुत does not deny; it argues to the greater case.
Right: किमुत argues from the lesser case to the greater, as in unit 130.
जानाति is affirmative; nothing is denied.
Nothing is said about speed of knowing.
questions.explain: बालोऽपि जानाति, किमुत वृद्धः = even a boy knows, what to say of an elder.
questions.rule: X अपि ..., किमुत Y = even X ..., how much more Y.
questions.teaches: किमुत (how much more): even outer fire is uneven, how much more the heat within.

questions.q: In unit 131, what does क्रमशः साम्यमापाद्य mean?
options: Having first measured all the doṣas
Having given up every kind of food
optionExplain: क्रमशः is gradual, and साम्य is reached, not broken.
No measuring is printed.
Right: क्रमशः = gradually; साम्यम् आपाद्य = having brought to equality.
No giving up of food is printed.
questions.explain: Gradually bringing to equality, then keeping by the best.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 131 in the line's order.
questions.explain: With the best sātmya; by the lesser the others; gradually to equality; by the Vāta-and-other remedy; by medicine-exercise combinations.
questions.rule: तत्र प्रवरेण सात्म्येन समं → यथास्वमवरेणेतरान् → क्रमशः साम्यमापाद्य → वातादिसाधनेन → ग्रहणीरोगविहितैश्चौषधव्यायामयोगैरिति.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 131 to its meaning.
questions.explain: प्रवर best, अवर lesser, सात्म्य what suits, साम्य equality, व्यायाम exercise.
questions.teaches: प्रवर and अवर are a pair (best and lesser); this line does not say what each refers to.

questions.q: Which split of विहितैश्चौषध in unit 131 is right?
optionExplain: ए before च stays ए: it would print विहिते च.
चः is not a word; the word is च, 'and'.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ; the print has चौ.
Right: ऐः before च → ऐश्; अ + औ → औ: विहितैश्चौषध.
questions.explain: विहितैः (prescribed) + च (and) + औषध (medicine).
questions.rule: Visarga + च → श्च; अ + औ → औ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 131?
options: The line gives a dose for each medicine
Remedies for Vāta and the like come from the doṣa-treatment section
The line says what the lesser (avara) refers to
Medicine-and-exercise combinations are those prescribed in grahaṇī
optionExplain: No dose is printed.
Right: दोषोपक्रमणीयोक्तेन वातादिसाधनेन (probably a chapter title).
What अवर refers to is not stated.
Right: ग्रहणीरोगविहितैः औषधव्यायामयोगैः (probably a digestive disorder).
questions.explain: Two named sources of means; no doses, and no referents for प्रवर / अवर.

questions.q: By the rule of अवरेण + इतरान् → अवरेणेतरान्, how is रामेण + इति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Right: अ + इ → ए, as अवरेण + इतरान् → अवरेणेतरान्.
अ + इ does not give a long ई.
ऐ comes from अ + ए or ऐ, not from अ + इ.
य् comes from इ before a different vowel, not from अ.
questions.explain: रामेण + इति = रामेणेति, like अवरेण + इतरान् = अवरेणेतरान्.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial इ join as ए: अवरेण + इतरान् → अवरेणेतरान्.

questions.q: What does भवति चात्र (unit 132) do?
options: It closes the sixth chapter at this point
It leads in to the verses that follow
It names the four kinds of agni here
It gives a cure for the manda agni
optionExplain: The chapter's closing line is unit 141.
Right: A lead-in formula; the verses from unit 133 appear to be its content.
The four kinds are named in unit 125.
No cure is printed in these two words.
questions.explain: A formula that brings in the verses after it.
questions.rule: भवति चात्र = and on this there are (verses).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 132 to its meaning.
questions.explain: And on this matter there are (verses).

questions.q: In the lead-in formula of unit 132, the verb meaning there is / are is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: भवति = there is / are (3 sg. present of √भू).
questions.teaches: भवति, from √भू (be), opens the lead-in formula.

questions.q: Which split of चात्र in unit 132 is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would print चेऽत्र, not चात्र.
आत्र is not a word.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र = चात्र.
चा and त्र are not words here.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (on this matter): अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Which statements about unit 132 are right?
options: It is itself a metrical verse
It states what the coming verses are about
The verses from unit 133 appear to be its content
optionExplain: Right: 3 sg. present of √भू, 'there is'.
It is a prose formula.
It has no stated object.
Right: the data reads them so ('appear').
questions.explain: A prose lead-in with the verb भवति; the verses after it appear to be its content.

questions.q: By the rule of च + अत्र → चात्र, how is तत्र + अपि joined in a new example?
optionExplain: Two short अ join as a long आ, not a short अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as च + अत्र → चात्र.
questions.explain: तत्र + अपि = तत्रापि, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial अ join as a long आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.

questions.q: By unit 133, what colour are the srotas (channels)?
options: The colour of their own dhātu
optionExplain: Right: स्वधातुसमवर्णानि: equal in colour to their own dhātu.
No one colour is given; each has its own dhātu's colour.
No such colour is printed.
No such colour is printed.
questions.explain: Each srotas has the colour of its own dhātu.

questions.q: Put these printed parts of the verse of unit 133 in order.
questions.explain: Own-dhātu-coloured; round, thick and fine; the srotas; long in form; like tendrils.
questions.rule: स्वधातुसमवर्णांनि → वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि च → स्रोतांसि → दीर्घाण्याकृत्या → प्रतानसदृशानि च.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 133 to its meaning.
questions.explain: वृत्त round, स्थूल thick, अणु fine, दीर्घ long, आकृति form.
questions.teaches: स्रोतस् (neuter, plural स्रोतांसि) are the body's channels; the verse gives their colour and shape.

questions.q: Which pair of opposite words does unit 133 print side by side for the srotas?
optionExplain: दीर्घ is printed, but ह्रस्व is not.
Right: वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि: thick and fine are both printed.
वृत्त is printed, but चतुरस्र is not.
No colour words are printed; colour follows the dhātu.
questions.explain: Thick (स्थूल) and fine (अणु) stand together in the first line.

questions.q: Which split of वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि in unit 133 is right?
optionExplain: यणूनि is not a word; the य् comes from the इ of -आनि.
ए + अ would print -लानेऽणूनि.
Right: इ before the unlike vowel अ → य्: -लान्यणूनि.
अ + अ would give आ: -न्याणूनि.
questions.explain: वृत्तस्थूलानि (round, thick) + अणूनि (fine).

questions.q: By the rule of वृत्तस्थूलानि + अणूनि, how is फलानि + अत्र joined in a new example?
optionExplain: The इ does not stay and add a य्; it becomes य्.
ए with ऽ comes from ए + अ, not from इ + अ.
आ comes from अ + अ, not from इ + अ.
Right: इ before the unlike vowel अ → य्, as in वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि.
questions.explain: फलानि + अत्र = फलान्यत्र, like वृत्तस्थूलानि + अणूनि = वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि.
questions.teaches: A final इ before अ becomes य्: वृत्तस्थूलानि + अणूनि → वृत्तस्थूलान्यणूनि.

questions.q: By unit 134, how does food or conduct that defiles the srotas stand to the doṣas?
options: It is equal to them in qualities
It is equal to the dhātus in qualities
It is opposite to all of the doṣas
It has no bearing on the doṣas at all
optionExplain: Right: दोषगुणैः समः: equal to the doṣas in qualities.
Toward the dhātus it is विगुण, not equal.
The verse says equal (सम), not opposite.
The verse links it to the doṣas' qualities.
questions.explain: Equal to the doṣas in qualities, unlike the dhātus: that defiles the srotas.

questions.q: Put the printed quarter-lines of unit 134 in order.
questions.explain: Food and conduct, which is equal to the doṣas in qualities, and which is unlike the dhātus: that defiles the srotas.
questions.rule: आहारश्च विहारश्च → यः स्याद्दोषगुणैः समः → धातुभिर्विगुणो यश्च → स्रोतसां स प्रदूषकः.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 134 to its meaning.
questions.explain: आहार food, विहार conduct, गुण quality, सम equal, प्रदूषक defiler.
questions.teaches: यः ... सः (which ... that): a relative clause in the first lines, the main clause स प्रदूषकः at the end.

questions.q: In धातुभिर्विगुणो of unit 134, why is the visarga of धातुभिः written र्?
options: Every visarga becomes र् before a consonant
It follows इ and stands before the voiced व
It follows अ and stands before the voiced व
र् is part of the stem of the word
optionExplain: Before त it becomes स्, before च श्; not every consonant.
Right: After a vowel other than अ/आ, visarga before a voiced sound → र्.
The vowel before it is इ (-भिः); अः would give ओ.
The stem is धातु; -भिः is the ending, and its visarga becomes र्.
questions.explain: धातुभिः + विगुणः: इः before the voiced व → इर्.
questions.rule: इः / उः + voiced sound → इर् / उर्.

questions.q: Which statements fit the verse of unit 134?
options: It names the doṣa that does the harm
Both food and conduct can defile the srotas
Equality with the doṣas' qualities is named as a cause
Likeness to the dhātus defiles the srotas
optionExplain: No single doṣa is named.
Right: आहारश्च विहारश्च.
Right: दोषगुणैः समः.
Toward the dhātus it is विगुण, not alike.
questions.explain: Food or conduct like the doṣas and unlike the dhātus defiles the srotas.

questions.q: By the rule of विगुणः + यः → विगुणो यः, how is रामः + याति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
The vowel is not lengthened; अः before a voiced consonant gives ओ.
Right: अः before the voiced consonant य → ओ, as विगुणो यः.
अः drops to अ only before vowels other than अ, not before य.
questions.explain: रामः + याति = रामो याति, like विगुणः + यः = विगुणो यः.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: विगुणः + यश्च → विगुणो यश्च.

questions.q: Which of these does unit 135 print as a sign of vitiated srotas?
options: A change in the colour of the skin
Loss of sleep through the night
optionExplain: Skin colour is not printed in unit 135.
Sleep is not printed in unit 135.
Joints are not printed in unit 135.
Right: अतिप्रवृत्तिः is the first printed sign.
questions.explain: Excessive flow, obstruction, knots of the sirās ...: signs of vitiated srotas.

questions.q: Put these printed parts of unit 135 in order (the damaged phrase is left out).
questions.explain: Excessive flow, or obstruction, or also knots of the sirās, ... the sign of vitiated srotas.
questions.rule: अतिप्रवृत्तिः → संगो वा → सिराणांग्रंथयोऽपि वा → स्रोतसां दुष्टिलक्षणं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 135 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अतिप्रवृत्ति excessive flow, सङ्ग obstruction, ग्रन्थि knot, दुष्टि vitiation, लक्षण sign.
questions.teaches: वा ... वा (or ... or): each printed item alone is a sign of vitiated srotas.

questions.q: Which split of संगो वा in unit 135 is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः before the voiced व → ओ; ं in the print stands for ङ्.
ए before व stays ए: it would print सङ्गे वा.
म् before व is written ं: it would print सङ्गं वा.
आ before व stays आ: it would print सङ्गा वा.
questions.explain: सङ्गः (obstruction) + वा (or): अः + voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Which statements fit unit 135?
options: Obstruction (saṅga) is one of the signs
The verse says which doṣa causes each sign
The verse gives a cure for vitiated srotas
Knots of the sirās are one of the signs
optionExplain: Right: सङ्गो वा.
No doṣa is named.
No cure is printed.
Right: सिराणां ग्रन्थयोऽपि वा (sirā, probably veins).
questions.explain: Signs only: excessive flow, obstruction, knots of the sirās, and a damaged fourth item.
questions.rule: अतिप्रवृत्तिः सङ्गो वा सिराणां ग्रन्थयोऽपि वा.

questions.q: By the rule of ग्रन्थयः + अपि → ग्रन्थयोऽपि, how is बालः + अत्र joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अः becomes अ only before vowels other than अ.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and ऽ marks the lost अ, as in ग्रन्थयोऽपि.
आ with a gap comes from आः, not from अः.
र् comes from a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: बालः + अत्र = बालोऽत्र, like ग्रन्थयः + अपि = ग्रन्थयोऽपि.
questions.teaches: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked ऽ: ग्रन्थयः + अपि → ग्रन्थयोऽपि.

questions.q: By unit 136, what are the openings of the srotas compared to?
options: The hairs of the head, for number
Threads of a web, for their pattern
Grains of sand, for their dryness
optionExplain: Hair is not named in unit 136.
No web is named in unit 136.
Right: बिसानामिव सूक्ष्माणि: fine like those of lotus stalks.
No sand is named in unit 136.
questions.explain: Fine like lotus stalks and spread far.

questions.q: Put the printed quarter-lines of unit 136 in order.
questions.explain: Fine like lotus stalks, and spread far: the openings of the srotas in the body, through which rasa is built up.
questions.rule: बिसानामिव सूक्ष्माणि → दूरं विप्रसृतानि च → द्वाराणि स्रोतसां देहे → रसोयैरुपचीयते.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 136 to its meaning.
questions.explain: बिस lotus stalk, सूक्ष्म fine, विप्रसृत spread out, द्वार opening, उपचीयते is built up.
questions.teaches: इव (like) follows the thing compared: बिसानाम् इव = like (those) of lotus stalks.

questions.q: Which split of रसोयैरुपचीयते in unit 136 is right?
optionExplain: ए before य stays ए: it would print रसे यैः.
That would print यैरप-; the print has यैरुप-.
म् before य is written ं: it would print रसं यैः.
Right: अः before the voiced य → ओ; ऐः before a vowel → ऐर्.
questions.explain: रसः (rasa) + यैः (by which) + उपचीयते (is built up).
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ; ऐः + vowel → ऐर्.

questions.q: Which statements fit the verse of unit 136?
options: The openings are fine like lotus stalks
Through the openings rasa is built up
The verse gives the number of openings
optionExplain: Right: बिसानामिव सूक्ष्माणि.
Right: रसो यैरुपचीयते.
No number is printed.
Right: दूरं विप्रसृतानि.
questions.explain: Fine, far-spread openings through which rasa is built up; no number is given.

questions.q: उपचीयते in unit 136 is passive (is built up). What does अन्नं पच्यते mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: Right: पच्यते is the passive of √पच्, like उपचीयते of उप-√चि.
The passive does not take an object here.
पच्यते is present, not future.
पच्यते is present, not past.
questions.explain: अन्नं पच्यते = food is (being) cooked; रसो यैरुपचीयते = by which rasa is built up.
questions.rule: Passive present (as here): -यते with the doer, if any, in the instrumental; not every -यते is passive.
questions.teaches: उपचीयते is the present passive (gram: pass.) of उप-√चि; not every -यते is passive, but this one is.

questions.q: By unit 137, what do the different views disagree about?
options: How many dhātus the body holds
How long food takes to become śukra
Which season best suits a meal
optionExplain: No count of dhātus is printed in unit 137.
Right: प्रयाति शुक्रत्वमन्नं: when food reaches the state of śukra.
No season is printed in unit 137.
The verse takes the sequence of cooking for granted.
questions.explain: The views differ on the time food takes to reach the state of śukra.
questions.rule: केचित् ... अपरे ... परे ... प्रयाति शुक्रत्वम् अन्नम्.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of the verse of unit 137 in order.
questions.explain: Some say from a day and night, others from six days, others ...; from a month food reaches śukra, by the sequence of cooking.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 137 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अहोरात्र a day and night, षडह six days, मास a month, शुक्रत्व state of śukra, पाकक्रम sequence of cooking.
questions.teaches: केचित् ... अपरे ... परे (some ... others ... still others) is the frame for listing views.

questions.q: By unit 137, which period do the others (अपरे) give?
optionExplain: A day and night is the view of केचित्, 'some'.
The month is not printed with अपरे.
Right: षडहादपरे: others, from six days.
No fortnight is printed in unit 137.
questions.explain: केचित्: a day and night; अपरे: six days.

questions.q: Which statements fit the verse of unit 137?
options: A month (मास) is printed as a period
The verse decides which view is right
Food reaches śukra by the sequence of cooking
The verse names three dhātus in the chain
optionExplain: Right: मासात् प्रयाति ... is printed.
No view is chosen.
Right: पाकक्रमात्.
No dhātu besides śukra is named.
questions.explain: Several periods are reported; the change is by the sequence of cooking; no view is chosen.

questions.q: By the rule of केचित् + आहुः → केचिदाहुः, how is कश्चित् + आगच्छति joined in a new example?
optionExplain: त् does not stay त् before a vowel when words are joined.
न् comes (optionally) from त् before a nasal, not before a vowel.
च्च comes from त् before च, not before a vowel.
Right: त् before a vowel → द्, as केचित् + आहुः → केचिदाहुः.
questions.explain: कश्चित् + आगच्छति = कश्चिदागच्छति, like केचित् + आहुः = केचिदाहुः.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: केचित् + आहुः → केचिदाहुः.

questions.q: By unit 138, how soon do vṛṣya things make śukra, and by what?
optionExplain: Right: प्रभावात्तु सद्यः शुक्रादि कुर्वन्ते.
A month and the sequence of cooking belong to food (unit 137).
Six days is a view about food (unit 137); taste is not named.
The verse says they make śukra and the like.
questions.explain: Vṛṣya things make śukra and the like at once, by prabhāva.

questions.q: Put these printed words of unit 138 in order (one long joined word is left out).
questions.explain: Vṛṣya and the like, but by prabhāva, at once make śukra and the like; generally ... medicine.
questions.rule: वृष्यादीनि → प्रभावात्तु → सद्यः → शुक्रादिकुर्वंते → प्रायः → भेषजं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 138 to its meaning.
questions.explain: वृष्य virility-promoting, प्रभाव special potency, सद्यः at once, प्रायः generally, भेषज medicine.
questions.teaches: प्रभाव is a special potency whose action is not reasoned out from the other properties.

questions.q: Which split of प्रभावात्तु in unit 138 is right?
optionExplain: त्तु is not a word; the word is तु, 'but'.
Right: त् before त stays त्: प्रभावात् + तु = प्रभावात्तु.
अ + उ would give ओ: -त्तो, not -त्तु.
म् before त is written ं: it would print प्रभावं तु.
questions.explain: प्रभावात् (through prabhāva) + तु (but).

questions.q: Unit 137 has food reach śukra over time. Which word of unit 138 marks its contrast with that?
optionExplain: सद्यः gives the time, not the contrast.
प्रायः belongs to the second line, 'generally'.
Right: प्रभावात्तु: तु, 'but', sets vṛṣya things against the food views of unit 137.
अपि means 'also', not 'but'.
questions.explain: तु (but) marks the contrast: vṛṣya things act at once (सद्यः) by prabhāva.

questions.q: By the rule of शुक्र + आदि → शुक्रादि, how is अन्न + आदि joined in a new example?
optionExplain: अ + आ gives a long आ, not a short अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए or ऐ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ, as शुक्र + आदि → शुक्रादि.
questions.explain: अन्न + आदि = अन्नादि, like शुक्र + आदि = शुक्रादि.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial आ join as आ: शुक्र + आदि → शुक्रादि; वृष्य + आदीनि → वृष्यादीनि.

questions.q: By unit 139, which doṣa is named in the condition for the manda (slow) agni?
optionExplain: Right: मन्दोऽस्मिन्कफपीडिते: slow when afflicted by Kapha.
Being overcome by Pitta makes the agni tīkṣṇa (sharp).
Rakta is not named in unit 139.
Vāta is not named for the manda agni; the verse names Kapha.
questions.explain: Kapha-afflicted: manda.

questions.q: Match each state of agni to its cause in unit 139.
questions.explain: Sama: Samāna in place; viṣama: wrong path; tīkṣṇa: Pitta; manda: Kapha.

questions.q: Put the four states of agni in the order of the verse of unit 139.
questions.explain: Sama, viṣama, tīkṣṇa, manda: the same order as the list of unit 125.
questions.teaches: The verse keeps the order of unit 125 (sama, viṣama, tīkṣṇa, manda) and gives each state its cause.

questions.q: Which split of पित्ताभिमूर्च्छिते in unit 139 is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would print पित्तेऽभि-.
Right: अ + अ → आ: पित्त + अभिमूर्च्छिते → पित्ताभिमूर्च्छिते.
म् would join the vowel: पित्तमभि-.
इ + अ would give य: पित्त्यभि-.
questions.explain: पित्त (Pitta) + अभिमूर्च्छिते (overcome).

questions.q: Unit 128: the tīkṣṇa agni digests even improperly taken food quickly. By unit 139, which condition goes with it?
optionExplain: Kapha goes with manda, the slow one.
That goes with sama, the even one.
Right: पित्ताभिमूर्च्छिते तीक्ष्णः.
A wrong path goes with viṣama, the uneven one.
questions.explain: Tīkṣṇa: overcome by Pitta.

questions.q: कफपीडिते in unit 139 is a locative absolute (when afflicted by Kapha). What does गुरौ गते शिष्यः पठति mean?
options: The pupil reads to the teacher who went
The teacher goes, and the pupil goes too
The pupil goes to the teacher to read
When the teacher has gone, the pupil reads
optionExplain: गुरौ गते is not an object; it sets the time.
शिष्यः पठति: the pupil reads, he does not go.
गते is the teacher's going, in the locative.
Right: गुरौ गते: noun and participle in the locative = 'when ...'.
questions.explain: गुरौ गते = when the teacher has gone, like कफपीडिते = when afflicted by Kapha.
questions.teaches: A noun and a participle both in the locative give 'when ...': स्थानस्थे समाने, कफपीडिते.

questions.q: By unit 140, what follows when the agni is extinguished (śānta)?
optionExplain: Right: शान्तेऽग्नौ म्रियते: when the agni is extinguished, one dies.
Long life goes with the well-ordered (yukta) agni.
Illness goes with the abnormal (vikṛta) agni.
Cold is not named in unit 140.
questions.explain: Extinguished agni: death.

questions.q: Put the printed parts of the verse of unit 140 in order.
questions.explain: Extinguished: dies; well-ordered: lives long, healthy; abnormal: diseased; so protect it with effort.
questions.rule: शांतेऽग्नौ म्रियते → युक्ते चिरं जीवत्यनामयः → रोगीस्याद्विकृते → तस्मात्तं प्रयत्नेन पालयेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 140 to its meaning.
questions.explain: शान्त extinguished, युक्त well-ordered, विकृत abnormal, अनामय free from disease, प्रयत्न effort.
questions.teaches: शान्ते, युक्ते, विकृते are locatives agreeing with अग्नौ: 'when the agni is ...'.

questions.q: Which split of शांतेऽग्नौ in unit 140 is right?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give आ: शान्ताग्नौ.
Right: ए + अ: ए stays and the अ is marked ऽ.
अः + अ would give ओऽ: शान्तोऽग्नौ.
म् would join the vowel: शान्तमग्नौ.
questions.explain: शान्ते (extinguished) + अग्नौ (when the agni): ए + अ → एऽ.

questions.q: Units 130 and 140 both close with advice about the agni. What is it?
optionExplain: No outer fire is advised; unit 130 only compares it.
Kapha makes it manda (unit 139); it is not advised.
Right: तस्मात्तं प्रयत्नतो रक्षेत् (130); तस्मात्तं प्रयत्नेन पालयेत् (140).
Both lines say to protect it with effort.
questions.explain: Both: therefore protect it with effort.

questions.q: पालयेत् in unit 140 is an optative (one should protect). What does सत्यं वदेत् mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: वदेत् is optative, not past.
वदेत् is optative, not future.
वदेत् is optative, not present.
Right: वदेत् is the optative of √वद्, like पालयेत्: 'should'.
questions.explain: सत्यं वदेत् = one should speak the truth, like तं पालयेत् = one should protect it.
questions.teaches: पालयेत् is optative (gram: opt.): 'one should protect'; वदेत् is formed the same way.

questions.q: By unit 141, what is the sixth chapter named?
optionExplain: Right: इति सिराविभागो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः.
That is the name of chapter five.
That is the name of chapter seven.
That is the name of chapter four.
questions.explain: The sixth chapter is Sirāvibhāga, the division of the vessels.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 141 (split out of sandhi) in their order.
questions.explain: Thus, Sirāvibhāga, named, sixth, chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 141 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Thus the sixth chapter, named division of the vessels.
questions.teaches: सिराविभाग = सिरा + विभाग: the division of the vessels, the theme with which the chapter began.

questions.q: Which split of षष्ठोऽध्यायः in unit 141 is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would print षष्ठेऽध्यायः.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and ऽ marks the lost अ.
आ + अ would give आ: षष्ठाध्यायः.
म् would join the vowel: षष्ठमध्यायः.
questions.explain: षष्ठः (sixth) + अध्यायः (chapter).

questions.q: In unit 141 the word for 'sixth' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: षष्ठः = sixth; before अध्यायः it is printed षष्ठोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: षष्ठ = sixth (ordinal of षट्, six).

questions.q: By the pattern of षष्ठोऽध्यायः, what does सप्तमोऽध्यायः mean (a new example)?
optionExplain: सप्तम is the ordinal 'seventh', not the number 'seven'.
Sixth is षष्ठ; सप्तम is seventh.
Right: सप्तमः (seventh) + अध्यायः, joined like षष्ठः + अध्यायः.
Nothing about parts is said; सप्तम is 'seventh'.
questions.explain: सप्तमोऽध्यायः = the seventh chapter, like षष्ठोऽध्यायः = the sixth chapter.
questions.teaches: षष्ठ (sixth) and सप्तम (seventh) are ordinals; joined with अध्यायः they give षष्ठोऽध्यायः, सप्तमोऽध्यायः.
